name: S Gopalakrishnan
profile: Senapathy 'Kris' Gopalakrishnan co-founded Infosys in 1981 and was its CEO/MD (2007-2011) and vice chairman (2011-2014). He now backs startups through Axilor Ventures and family investment arm Pratithi, and funds neuroscience and research through the Pratiksha Trust, while chairing IISc's Council and several Indian government innovation bodies.
interesting_fact: He gave Rs 2.25 billion to build the Centre for Brain Research at IISc, described as the largest individual gift the institute has received, and funds a cellular-level brain-mapping centre at IIT Madras.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a physicist, earning an M.Sc. in Physics (1977) before an M.Tech in Computer Science (1979) at IIT Madras, and his first job was as a software engineer at Patni Computer Systems in Mumbai in 1979, where he met the future Infosys founding team.
current_role: Chairman, Axilor Ventures (Bengaluru seed fund/accelerator); co-founder of Infosys; Chair, IISc Council
public_contact: office_email: accelerator@axilor.com | official_website: https://www.axilor.com | x: https://x.com/Axilor_2025 (Axilor company account)
research_notes: Goes by 'Kris'. Very active public speaker on AI, deep tech and startups (CII, IISc); good podcast fit. Axilor's general inbox is the best published route; the Pratiksha Trust site lists no email.

name: NR Narayana Murthy
profile: N.R. Narayana Murthy (b. 1946) co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues, seeded by Rs 10,000 from his wife Sudha Murty, and built it into one of India's largest IT services companies, serving as CEO and chairman. Often called the father of the Indian IT sector, he is now Chairman Emeritus and invests via Catamaran Ventures.
interesting_fact: He has said being arrested and expelled near the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border in 1974, while hitchhiking back from Europe, turned him from a 'confused leftist' into a 'compassionate capitalist'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and designed a BASIC interpreter for ECIL; his first startup, Softronics, folded after about a year and a half.
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; founder of family investment firm Catamaran Ventures
research_notes: Infosys press email reaches the company, not him directly; Catamaran Ventures (his family office, catamaranventures.com) may be a more direct route but no published email was verified. Gives frequent public lectures and interviews, often on work ethic and entrepreneurship.

name: Peter P Gassner
profile: Software engineer who worked at IBM's Silicon Valley Lab, led PeopleTools at PeopleSoft and ran technology at Salesforce before co-founding Veeva Systems in 2007. Veeva builds cloud software for the life-sciences industry and went public in 2013; Gassner remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Under Gassner, Veeva became a public benefit corporation in 2021, which made it the first public company to convert to a PBC.
deep_cut_fact: Gassner grew up in Portland, Oregon, the son of Swiss immigrants (his father had a machine shop). He earned a computer science degree from Oregon State University in 1989, and his first internship was at IBM.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Veeva Systems
public_contact: press_email: pr@veeva.com | ir_email: ir@veeva.com | official_website: https://www.veeva.com
research_notes: Low public profile but gives occasional founder interviews (Sramana Mitra, SaaStr) on vertical SaaS. The PBC claim is from Wikipedia; check it before using. Best route is Veeva PR.

name: Vince McMahon
education: East Carolina University; Fishburne Military School
profile: Former WWE chairman and CEO. He bought his father's wrestling company in 1982 and built WWE into a global media business, which merged with UFC to form TKO in 2023. He resigned from TKO in January 2024 and in 2025 launched 14TH & I, named for the D.C. intersection where his father's Capitol Wrestling Corp. was based.
interesting_fact: McMahon was behind the 1976 Muhammad Ali vs. Antonio Inoki match, years before he took over his father's promotion.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from East Carolina University in 1968 and working as a traveling salesman, he became a ring announcer in 1969. In 1971 he promoted his first card, in a small territory in Maine.
current_role: Founder of 14TH & I, a private sports, media and entertainment investment firm (Connecticut)
research_notes: Sensitive: he resigned from TKO in January 2024 amid a lawsuit alleging sexual misconduct, and in January 2025 he settled SEC charges over undisclosed payments (>$1.7m). Weigh reputational fit before any outreach. 14TH & I's site published no contact details; reported executives are Brad Blum (president) and David Spingarn (CIO), per https://wrestletalk.com/news/vince-mcmahon-new-company-wwe-exit-revealed/

name: Paul Georges Despature
profile: Paul-Georges Despature is the patriarch of the French Despature family, which controls Somfy, the Cluses-based maker of motors and automation for blinds, shutters and gates. He ran Somfy as chairman of its management board from 1983 until the end of 2014, then moved to head the family investment arm Edify. His son Jean Guillaume Despature now chairs Somfy, which the family took private in 2022-23.
interesting_fact: The Despature family, which already owned the thermal-underwear brand Damart, bought Somfy in 1984 as a diversification into summer-season products; Somfy has since become a world leader in motorised blinds and the connected home.
deep_cut_fact: The name SOMFY is an acronym for 'Société d'Outillage et Mécanique du FaucignY', a 1969 spin-off of the Cluses precision-machining firm Carpano & Pons in the Arve valley, a region known for Swiss-watch part-making.
current_role: Chairman of Edify (Despature family investment company); former chairman of Somfy's management board (1983-2014)
public_contact: press_email: presse.somfy@somfy.com | pr_agency: Agence Shan (Somfy press agency), 30 rue des Mathurins, 75008 Paris
research_notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Edify role per Somfy's December 2014 announcement (https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2014/12/FCECO035465_20141222.pdf); check whether he still holds it. Somfy press route is the corporate one, not a personal office.

name: Raja Bagmane
profile: Bengaluru real-estate developer who founded Bagmane Group in 1996 and built it into one of the city's largest commercial/tech-park landlords (Bagmane Tech Park, Bagmane World Technology Center; ~30 mn sq ft operational). Blackstone took a minority stake in 2024, and the group sponsors Bagmane Prime Office REIT, which has listed in India. His sons Aditya and Shashank are directors.
interesting_fact: Bagmane Tech Park in C V Raman Nagar, launched in 2001, was one of Bengaluru's earliest IT parks; the group's portfolio is now hosted in a Blackstone-backed listed REIT.
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Bagmane Group (Bagmane Developers Pvt Ltd), Bengaluru
public_contact: office_email: enquiries@bagmanegroup.com | contact_form: https://www.bagmanegroup.com/contact-us | official_website: https://www.bagmanegroup.com
research_notes: Low media profile; rarely gives interviews. The published email is a general company enquiries inbox. A data-center/tech-park angle is relevant: Bagmane hosts big tech occupiers in Bengaluru. His sons may be easier to reach for a conversation.

name: Naveen Jindal
profile: Naveen Jindal (b. 1970, Hisar), youngest son of O.P. Jindal, took over the group's Raigarh and Raipur steel operations in 1993 and built Jindal Steel & Power into a major steel, power and mining group. He is founding chancellor of O.P. Jindal Global University and, since 2024, a BJP MP; the group is now expanding Angul steel capacity and investing in nuclear and solar in Jharkhand.
interesting_fact: His 1990s court fight after hoisting the flag at his Raigarh factory led to the 2004 Supreme Court ruling that flying the Indian national flag on any day is part of citizens' freedom of expression.
deep_cut_fact: While earning his MBA at UT Dallas (1992) he served as Student Government VP then president and won Student Leader of the Year; the university's Naveen Jindal School of Management now bears his name. He is also a national-record skeet shooter in India.
current_role: Chairman, Jindal Steel Ltd (formerly Jindal Steel & Power); BJP Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) for Kurukshetra
research_notes: Highly public figure (industrialist + MP); active on X. Also captains the Jindal Panther polo team. Steer clear of the coal-block allocation case.

name: GM Rao
profile: Grandhi Mallikarjuna Rao (b. 1950, Rajam, Andhra Pradesh) is a mechanical engineer who built GMR Group from a single jute mill bought in 1978 into one of India's largest infrastructure developers, running Delhi and Hyderabad airports plus energy and highway assets. He funded the move into power by selling his Vysya Bank stake; sons and family now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: He used the roughly Rs 3.4 billion from selling his entire ING Vysya Bank stake to fund GMR's entry into power and infrastructure; the group is also co-owner of IPL cricket team Delhi Capitals.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked as a shift engineer at a paper mill and then as a junior engineer in the Andhra Pradesh Public Works Department; he moved into commodities trading at his mother's insistence.
current_role: Founder Chairman, GMR Group (infrastructure: airports, energy, highways, urban development)
research_notes: Press email reported from GMR's media page (page returned 503 when re-checked; verify). Philanthropy via GMR Varalakshmi Foundation (est. 1991). Strong energy/infrastructure fit for the podcast.

name: Nirmal Kumar Minda
profile: Second-generation head of UNO Minda (formerly Minda Industries), a Gurugram-based maker of auto switches, lighting, alloy wheels and EV components. He joined his father Shadilal's business in 1977 and ran it on his own after a 1996 split with his brother. He built it through Japanese and European joint ventures and moved from MD to Chairman in April 2025.
interesting_fact: The business goes back to 1958, when his father Shadilal Minda started importing ammeters from Japan. It moved to Delhi in 1962 to serve the tractor and motorcycle aftermarket.
deep_cut_fact: The group's first joint venture (1995) came from a quality push by Maruti. Minda asked the carmaker to help find a Japanese partner for switches, which led to Toyota-group supplier Tokai Rika. Separately, he and his wife Suman run Samarth-Jyoti, which operates two schools, a 100-bed hospital and 18 village centres.
current_role: Chairman (Executive Chairman), UNO Minda Ltd; President of ASSOCHAM for 2025
public_contact: press_email: communicationdesk@unominda.com | ir_email: investor@unominda.com | official_website: https://www.unominda.com
research_notes: The Samarth-Jyoti detail comes from an India CSR profile (https://indiacsr.in/biography-nirmal-kumar-minda-president-assocham-2025/). EV components and ASSOCHAM policy work are possible podcast angles. Sources differ on his exact title (Chairman vs Chairman & MD).

name: Jonathan Burrell
profile: Jonathan C. Burrell is the son of Garmin cofounder Gary Burrell (d. 2019), and his wealth comes from the family's Garmin stake. He formerly helped lead Garmin's engineering department, now runs the Burrell Family Office and sits on Garmin's board. He invests in financial, technology and clean-energy businesses.
interesting_fact: He is named as an inventor on 35 issued and pending U.S. patents, many of them owned by Garmin.
deep_cut_fact: He has a BS in mechanical engineering from Wichita State University and was a hands-on Garmin engineering leader before joining the board. Garmin's 2018 proxy says he invests in clean-energy businesses, which ties in with the podcast's energy theme.
current_role: CEO, Burrell Family Office; director of Garmin Ltd. (since 2018); president of the Burrell family charitable foundation
research_notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Garmin contacts are company-level; he is an independent director, not an executive.

name: Jacob Brunsborg
profile: Son of JYSK founder Lars Larsen; became chairman of Lars Larsen Group (JYSK, ILVA, Actona, investments) in June 2019 shortly before his father's death. Rose through JYSK as head of purchasing and brand director, then did business development, entrepreneurship and board work; now steers the group's strategy, including investments in securities, property and green energy.
interesting_fact: He carries his mother's surname rather than Larsen, and his father reportedly warned him against aiming for the JYSK CEO job, insisting management be chosen on merit while ownership stays in the family.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1993 as a trainee ('elev') in the JYSK store on Grenåvej in Aarhus, and did his military service with the Royal Danish Life Guards (Dronningens Livregiment).
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Lars Larsen Group (owner of JYSK)
public_contact: office_email: contact@larslarsengroup.com (Lars Larsen Group general contact) | press_email: Press contact: Communications Director Lise Brøndum Wemmelund via Lars Larsen Group press room | official_website: https://www.larslarsengroup.com/
research_notes: Rarely gives interviews and says he is less outgoing than his father (lex.dk). Group invests in green energy, a possible hook. Approach via the group's Communications Director.

name: Mette Brunsborg
profile: Daughter of JYSK founder Lars Larsen (d. 2019). She and her brother Jacob Brunsborg (chairman) control Lars Larsen Group, the Silkeborg holding company that owns the JYSK home-furnishings chain plus BOLIA, ILVA, SOFACOMPANY and other investments. She joined the family foundation's board in 2019, taking her mother Kris Brunsborg's seat.
interesting_fact: When she joined the board of Lars Larsens JYSK Fond in 2019, she took the seat of her mother, Kris Brunsborg. The foundation's first gift under the new board was DKK 1m to Børns Vilkår to help children whose parents have mental illness.
deep_cut_fact: Away from the boardroom she runs her own farm (driver sit eget landbrug), according to the Danish encyclopedia Lex.
current_role: Board member, Lars Larsen Group A/S (owner of JYSK) and Lars Larsens JYSK Fond
research_notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Brother Jacob Brunsborg is the family's public face. In July 2026 Lars Larsen Group announced a new renewable-energy agreement, which could be an angle for an energy podcast. Best route is Lars Larsen Group press.

name: Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua
profile: Vajiralongkorn is the reigning King of Thailand, the only son of King Bhumibol Adulyadej; he took the throne in 2016 and was crowned in 2019. Hurun counts his wealth through his holdings in Siam Commercial Bank, assets once managed by the Crown Property Bureau that he took into direct ownership after his accession.
interesting_fact: He is a graduate of Australia's Royal Military College, Duntroon, and qualified as both a military fast-jet pilot and a commercial airline pilot.
deep_cut_fact: He was once known as the 'Football Prince': he played forward and later centre-back at Chitralada School, Millfield School in Somerset and Duntroon. Since 1978 he has personally handed out degrees at Rajabhat University commencements every year, estimated at over 2.1 million degrees.
current_role: King of Thailand (Rama X), since 2016
research_notes: Reigning monarch, not a realistic podcast guest. Thailand's strict lese-majeste laws make any outreach or commentary sensitive. The only channel is formal, via the Bureau of the Royal Household. No personal contacts are published.

name: Madhusudhan Agarwal
profile: Madhusudan Agarwal and his brother Manohar Lal Agarwal, grandsons of founder Ganga Bishan 'Haldiram' Agarwal (sons of Moolchand), built the Delhi-based Haldiram's snacks business. After the 2022-25 merger of the Delhi and Nagpur packaged-snacks units into Haldiram Snacks Food, the Delhi brothers hold ~56%; Temasek bought a ~9% stake in 2025 at a ~$10bn valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to a 1937 bhujia shop in Bikaner, Rajasthan; the merged company was valued at nearly US$10bn when Singapore's Temasek bought in in 2025.
current_role: Co-owner/director, Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd (Delhi branch of the Haldiram's family)
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.haldirams.com/contact-us | office_email: support@haldirams.com (company customer support, not personal)
research_notes: Family is famously interview-shy (Financial Express called the brothers 'elusive'). Most coverage focuses on Manohar Lal; very little on Madhusudan personally. Best route is via the company's corporate communications.

name: Brad Garlinghouse
profile: Kansas-born executive (b. 1971) who held senior roles at @Home, Dialpad, Yahoo (SVP running Homepage, Flickr, Mail, Messenger) and AOL, then ran Hightail (ex-YouSendIt). Joined Ripple as COO in 2015 and became CEO around end-2016; his wealth comes from Ripple equity and XRP. He continues to lead Ripple's global payments, custody and RLUSD stablecoin push.
interesting_fact: As a Yahoo SVP in 2006 he wrote the internal 'Peanut Butter Manifesto' memo, warning Yahoo was spreading itself too thin like peanut butter; it leaked to the Wall Street Journal and became a Silicon Valley strategy classic.
deep_cut_fact: He told Fortune his interest in technology began growing up in Kansas when his dad brought home a Tandy TRS-80 computer.
current_role: CEO, Ripple (Ripple Labs)
public_contact: contact_form: https://ripple.com/contact/press/ (Ripple Press Team) | x: https://x.com/bgarlinghouse
research_notes: Very media-accessible, active on X (@bgarlinghouse) and frequent podcast guest. Best route is Ripple's press team form. Avoid the long SEC-litigation saga as a hook.

name: Dmitry Pumpansky
profile: Russian industrialist (b. 1964, usually spelled Dmitry Pumpyansky), graduate of the Ural Polytechnic Institute. Started as a metals trader, ran pipe plants including Sinarsky, joined TMK in 2002 and by 2006 owned 100% of it, building one of the world's largest makers of oil-and-gas tubulars. Said to have exited TMK in 2022; reported living in Geneva.
interesting_fact: After co-buying TMK with Sergei Popov and Andrey Melnichenko, he bought both partners out in 2006 to become its sole owner.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 he earned a Doctor of Technical Sciences degree with a dissertation on steels, alloys and production technologies for next-generation OCTG and specialty pipes, adding to his earlier engineering candidate degree and economics doctorate.
current_role: Former owner and chairman of TMK (Russian steel-pipe maker); left TMK's board and beneficial ownership in March 2022
research_notes: Name in input is a variant spelling of Pumpyansky. Sanctioned by UK (2022) and named on the US CAATSA list; EU sanctions annulled by the EU General Court on appeal. Outreach carries compliance/reputational risk; no published personal or office contact found.

name: Rajendrakumar Shivkisan Agrawal
name_chinese: 拉金德拉库马尔·希夫基桑·阿格拉瓦尔
profile: Member of the Nagpur branch of the Haldiram's snack-food family; Indian company registries list him as a director of Haldiram Foods International and some 27 related companies. The family's fortune jumped after the Delhi and Nagpur businesses merged in 2025 into Haldiram Snacks Food (Nagpur ~44%) and Temasek, Alpha Wave and IHC bought stakes at a reported ~$10B valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal's bhujia shop in Bikaner; the Nagpur arm was built by Shivkisan Agrawal, who introduced kaju katli to Nagpur. Hurun named Rajendrakumar one of India's biggest wealth gainers in its 2026 Global Rich List.
current_role: Director, Haldiram Foods International (Nagpur Haldiram's) and related family companies; shareholder in merged Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd
research_notes: Almost no public profile, interviews or social accounts found. Sources don't state his exact relation to Nagpur founder-chairman Shivkisan Agrawal (the patronymic suggests he is a son; unverified). The only site email is customer support, so a better route is corporate PR at Haldiram Snacks Food.

name: Allison McCain
profile: Allison D. McCain, nephew of McCain Foods co-founders Harrison and Wallace McCain, joined the Florenceville, N.B. frozen-potato giant in 1975 as an engineer, ran production in Australia and the UK, became deputy chairman in 1999 and chairman in 2004. His wealth is his family stake in privately held McCain Foods.
interesting_fact: As chair of UNB's 'Forging our Futures' campaign from 2003, he helped raise $107 million, then a record for Atlantic Canada; he later served as UNB's chancellor (named 2013) and chaired the Beaverbrook Art Gallery board.
deep_cut_fact: An electrical engineering graduate of UNB (1972), he worked at the New Brunswick Telephone Company before taking an engineering job at McCain's Florenceville plant in 1975 — the first of the family's next generation to join the firm.
current_role: Chairman, McCain Foods Ltd. (chair since 2004; no 2025-26 source found confirming he still holds the title)
research_notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. No death reports found (born c.1949). Best route is McCain Foods corporate communications. Only listed by Hurun 2014-2016.

name: Maurice Greenberg
profile: Maurice 'Hank' Greenberg (b. 1925) ran AIG from 1968 to 2005, building it into one of the world's largest insurers, then led C.V. Starr & Co. (Starr Companies), a global insurance and investment group. In 2025 he handed leadership to his sons and he chaired The Starr Foundation until 2024; he remains active in US-China and medical philanthropy.
interesting_fact: A WWII veteran, he enlisted at 17, landed at Omaha Beach on D-Day and took part in the liberation of Dachau; he later served in Korea, and credits the GI Bill for his college education.
deep_cut_fact: In 1990 he became the first Chairman of Shanghai's International Business Leaders' Advisory Council, later served as Senior Economic Advisor to the Beijing municipal government, and was made an honorary citizen of Shanghai.
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Starr Companies (C.V. Starr & Co.); sons Jeff and Scott Greenberg took over leadership in 2025
public_contact: press_email: media@starr.com | pr_agency: Prosek Partners (listed as Starr's PR adviser, Oct 2025 release) | contact_form: https://starrfoundation.org/contact/ | official_website: https://www.starr.com
research_notes: Aged 101; Hurun-listed wealth via Starr. Best route is Starr media office (media@starr.com). Starr Foundation does not accept unsolicited proposals.

name: Won-Woo Kim
profile: Kim Won-woo (김원우, b. ~1993) is the eldest son of NICE Group founder Kim Kwang-soo, who died in 2018 at 55; he inherited control at age 25 and is the largest shareholder of NICE Holdings, parent of Korea's leading credit bureau NICE Information Service. He has worked in the group's digital strategy unit, becoming executive director in Dec 2024 and president for 2026.
interesting_fact: He became controlling owner of one of Korea's biggest credit-information groups at just 25; day-to-day management has been run by professional CEO Choi Young while he built experience in digital strategy.
current_role: President (사장) and head of Digital Strategy, NICE Holdings (largest shareholder of NICE Group), promoted in the 2026 executive reshuffle
research_notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Korean-language press only. Best route is via NICE Holdings corporate communications.

name: Jacques Bouriez
profile: Member of the Bouriez family that controls Belgian-French retailer Louis Delhaize Group (Cora hypermarkets, Match, Smatch, Delitraiteur). Brother of Cora founder Philippe Bouriez (d. 2014). Moved from CEO to chairman when his sons became joint managing directors. The group has since been unwinding: Cora France sold to Carrefour (2024), Belgian Cora stores closed by early 2026.
interesting_fact: Louis Delhaize Group traces its roots to 1875 in Charleroi; Jacques's brother Philippe Bouriez founded the Cora hypermarket chain, and the family held the group for decades as one of Europe's last big private grocers.
current_role: Chairman (président), Louis Delhaize Group (Charleroi, Belgium); operations run by sons François and Pierre Bouriez
research_notes: Very private, elderly; no death reported in searches (only brother Philippe's, 2014: https://www.lsa-conso.fr/philippe-bouriez-mort-d-un-grand-nom-de-la-distribution-francaise,166753). Group is being dismantled (https://www.retaildetail.eu/news/food/dismantling-of-ldz-louis-delhaize-group-nears-completion/), so poor fit for podcast; any route would be via Louis Delhaize SA corporate office. Shares listing with Philippe Bouriez (deceased).

name: Uma Devi Prasad
profile: Hurun links her to Aristo Pharmaceuticals, the Mumbai-based drugmaker founded in 1971 by Mahendra Prasad, a seven-term Rajya Sabha MP who died in December 2021. Public records name an Uma Devi in disputes over his estate. I could not confirm her role at the company or any public profile.
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2025-26) as a holder of Aristo Pharmaceuticals wealth; no executive role found
research_notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Her link to Aristo is tied up in ongoing estate litigation over Mahendra Prasad's assets, so this is a sensitive family matter: avoid. The only contact is the company's general email. Low priority.

name: Darshan Hiranandani
profile: Son of Mumbai developer Niranjan Hiranandani, named successor to the real-estate group in 2019. He launched Yotta in 2019 as the group's data-center park business (Panvel/Navi Mumbai), now a sovereign AI cloud/GPU provider with NM1 (Mumbai), D1 (Greater Noida) and G1 (GIFT City) and reported IPO plans. He also founded LNG developer H-Energy.
interesting_fact: Yotta says its NM1 campus in Navi Mumbai is Asia's largest Tier IV Gold uptime-certified data center; Yotta has been empanelled under IndiaAI to supply GPU compute.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he went into energy: he founded H-Energy, which began developing India's first floating LNG terminal in 2017; the FSRU Hoegh Giant arrived at H-Energy's Jaigarh terminal in Maharashtra in April 2021, India's first FSRU.
current_role: Co-Founder & Chairman, Yotta Data Services and Nidar; CEO, Hiranandani Group and Nidar Group
public_contact: ir_email: ir@yotta.com | press_email: marketing@yotta.com (general/marketing contact) | x: https://x.com/YottaInfra (company) | official_website: https://yotta.com/
research_notes: Highly relevant to data-center/energy theme. Search results are flooded with SEO/reputation-management pages about him (hackmd, issuu, sites.google) - ignore those as sources. Yotta CEO is Sunil Gupta, who does most media. Avoid political topics (2023 Indian parliamentary 'cash-for-query' controversy) and the later Hoegh FSRU charter termination.

name: Frank Sobey
education: Harvard University
profile: Frank C. Sobey is a grandson of Sobeys founder Frank H. Sobey and a son of Bill Sobey. He spent 36 years at Empire Company, retiring as VP Real Estate in 2014, and chaired Crombie REIT and its predecessor until 2019. The Sobey family's fortune sits mainly in Empire/Sobeys, Canada's No. 2 grocer, and he remains an Empire director.
interesting_fact: He is a founding partner of CDL-Atlantic, the Atlantic Canada site of the Creative Destruction Lab startup program, and sits on the board of the Canada-U.S. Fulbright Program.
deep_cut_fact: When he stepped down as Crombie REIT chair in 2019, he had chaired it for 13 years and its predecessor Crombie Properties for eight, and said he had been 'connected in one way or another with Crombie' for 40 years.
current_role: Director, Empire Company Limited (Sobeys parent); President, ECL Properties; founding partner, Creative Destruction Lab Atlantic
public_contact: office_email: board@empireco.ca | press_email: Media@Sobeys.com | ir_email: investor.relations@empireco.ca
research_notes: The founder Frank H. Sobey died in 1985, so Hurun's 'Frank Sobey' is most likely Frank C. Sobey, possibly standing in for the wider family's Empire stake. board@empireco.ca is Empire's published route to directors and goes through the corporate secretary. CDL-Atlantic offers an entrepreneurship hook.

name: Jacques
profile: Jacques Bouriez (identified via shared_with Philippe Bouriez and source Louis Delhaize) is a member of the Bouriez family that controls Belgian retailer Louis Delhaize, owner of the Cora and Match hypermarkets. He chaired/oversaw the group's supervisory board after his brother Philippe stepped back in 2009. The group sold Cora/Match France to Carrefour (2023-24) and Delitraiteur to Colruyt (2024).
interesting_fact: The family group, founded in 1875 in Charleroi, sold its French Cora and Match chains to Carrefour, closing in July 2024.
current_role: Former chairman / supervisory board president, Louis Delhaize Group (Belgium; now renamed LDz)
research_notes: Input gives only first name 'Jacques'; identity inferred as Jacques Bouriez. No recent public info; current status and age (likely 80s) unconfirmed. Next generation (Pierre and François Bouriez) runs the business. Very low public profile.

name: Neal Aronson
profile: Neal Aronson (b. 1965) founded Atlanta private-equity firm Roark Capital in 2001 and remains its majority owner. Roark specialises in franchised brands and owns Subway, Arby's, Jimmy John's, Sonic, Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins (via Inspire Brands), having done many of the restaurant industry's biggest deals of the past decade.
interesting_fact: Roark Capital is named after Howard Roark, the uncompromising architect-hero of Ayn Rand's The Fountainhead.
deep_cut_fact: Before Roark, he co-founded U.S. Franchise Systems in 1995 with his uncle Mike Leven (ex-Holiday Inn president), growing a 27-hotel regional chain (Microtel) into the 10th-largest US hotel franchisor with 1,100+ properties before selling to Hyatt's Pritzkers in 2000. He began his career in Drexel Burnham Lambert's corporate finance department.
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Roark Capital Group (Atlanta)
public_contact: office_email: contact@roarkcapital.com | ir_email: investorrelations@roarkcapital.com | pr_agency: Joele Frank (Roark-JF@joelefrank.com) | official_website: https://www.roarkcapital.com

name: Ramon Ang
education: Far Eastern University (Bachelor of Engineering)
profile: Tondo-raised mechanical engineer (b. 1954) who rose from fixing and dealing used Japanese engines to running San Miguel, the Philippines' oldest conglomerate. He steered it from beer and food into power, fuel (Petron), cement and infrastructure - including the $15bn New Manila International Airport in Bulacan, the NAIA revamp and a $3.3bn LNG hub in Batangas.
interesting_fact: Per a widely told account, he met San Miguel chairman Danding Cojuangco at a car repair shop: when the mechanics couldn't diagnose Cojuangco's sports car, Ang identified the defect and was hired on the spot as his mechanic - the start of a decades-long partnership.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his mechanical engineering degree from Far Eastern University as a working student while helping in his father's auto repair shop on Jose Abad Santos Street in Tondo; FEU gave him an honorary doctorate in business engineering in 2018. He is also a former racing driver and vintage-car restorer.
current_role: Chairman and CEO, San Miguel Corporation; President and CEO, Top Frontier Investment Holdings
research_notes: Highly relevant to energy (SMC Global Power, LNG, Petron) and infrastructure. Gives frequent press conferences in Manila. No dedicated press email published; SMC Corporate Affairs Office (main line +63 2 8632 3000) is the media route; IR email listed as fallback.

name: Patrice Motsepe
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
education: St Mark's School; University of Eswatini; University of the Witwatersrand
profile: South African lawyer-turned-mining entrepreneur and the first Black African on the Forbes billionaires list (2008). He was the first Black partner at Bowman Gilfillan (1994), then bought marginal gold shafts in 1997 and built African Rainbow Minerals. He also founded African Rainbow Capital, has a stake in Sanlam, owns Mamelodi Sundowns and has led CAF since 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2013 he became the first African to sign the Giving Pledge. His Mamelodi Sundowns have won the South African Premiership every season since 2017-18.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, Future Mining, was a contract-mining outfit that cleaned gold dust from inside the Vaal Reefs mine shafts, paying workers a low base salary plus a profit-sharing bonus. He learned business as a boy in his father's spaza shop, which served mine workers.
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, African Rainbow Minerals; President, Confederation of African Football (CAF, re-elected 2025)
public_contact: press_email: Betty.Maloka@arm.co.za | ir_email: ir.admin@arm.co.za | official_website: https://www.arm.co.za | contact_form: https://www.motsepefoundation.org/contact-us/
research_notes: ARM lists Betty Maloka (Senior Manager: Media Relations and Brand Management) as its media contact. Very high-profile and press-friendly; mining, energy and African-investment angles fit the podcast. He is the subject of 2026 speculation about a run for the ANC presidency.

name: Atul Ruia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
education: University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School (Bachelor of Arts/Science)
profile: Third-generation scion of the Ruia textile family (Phoenix Mills founded 1905). The Wharton-educated Ruia turned the loss-making Lower Parel cotton mill into High Street Phoenix/Palladium, then built a national portfolio of 'Phoenix' and 'Palladium' malls, offices and hotels (St. Regis Mumbai, Courtyard Agra). He remains chairman of the listed company.
interesting_fact: He is not related to the Ruia family of the Essar Group, a frequent mix-up.
deep_cut_fact: The mill's redevelopment started with leisure, not shopping: in 1996 the compound opened what was billed as South Asia's largest 20-lane bowling concourse (Bowling Co., India's first bowling company and sports bar), years before the mall took shape.
current_role: Chairman, The Phoenix Mills Ltd (stepped down as managing director in Dec 2019)
public_contact: ir_email: secretarial@phoenixmills.com (company secretarial, on official letterhead) | official_website: https://www.thephoenixmills.com
research_notes: Low personal media profile; retired from executive duties at 48. Approach via Phoenix Mills corporate/secretarial office. Third-party sites list investorrelations@highstreetphoenix.com, but it is unverified on an official page and not included.

name: Howard Butt III
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
profile: Great-grandson of H-E-B founder Florence Butt and nephew of chairman Charles Butt, Howard Butt III succeeded his uncle as CEO of the family-owned Texas grocer in 2021. H-E-B has 455 stores in Texas and Mexico, about 160,000 employees and roughly $50 billion in sales. In 2025 he picked COO Roxanne Orsak as the company's first female president, starting in 2026.
interesting_fact: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity each year. The company was started in 1905 by his great-grandmother Florence Butt.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming CEO he ran H-E-B's Mexico division (as of 2016). His father, Howard E. Butt Jr., co-created the Laity Lodge retreat center in the Texas Hill Country in 1961.
current_role: CEO and board member, H-E-B (since 2021); board member, H.E. Butt Foundation
research_notes: Keeps a low media profile. The news@heb.com address came from a search snippet of an H-E-B page that loads by JavaScript, so I could not confirm it directly; check before use. H-E-B says media inquiries go to regional Public Affairs offices.

name: Stephen Butt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
profile: Great-grandson of H-E-B founder Florence Butt and nephew of chairman Charles Butt, Stephen Butt is a member of the family that owns privately held Texas grocer H-E-B (Texas and Mexico, roughly $50bn revenue). Based in Dallas, he runs H-E-B's specialty-food Central Market format and shareholder relations and sits on the board.
interesting_fact: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity. The first Central Market opened in Austin on 22 Jan 1994 despite advice that a store without Coke, Pepsi or Tide would fail.
deep_cut_fact: He recalls that in Central Market's second year, shoppers began carpooling from Houston and Dallas with big coolers, taking turns filling friends' shopping lists; by year three customers routinely drove 25 miles to shop there.
current_role: President of Shareholder Relations and of the Central Market division, H-E-B; H-E-B board member
research_notes: Described by PaperCity as a 'low-key billionaire' who 'doesn't want press'. He did give Shelby Report and Dallas Morning News interviews tied to Central Market, so pitching around Central Market/food retail innovation works best via H-E-B public affairs. Note: H-E-B's CEO is not his brother (Forbes bio claim looks outdated/wrong); verify before citing.

name: Mark Davis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
education: California State Chico (Diploma)
profile: Son of Raiders legend Al Davis, Mark Davis spent his whole career inside the team, starting in the equipment room and team retail, and inherited control after his father's death in 2011. He moved the franchise from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020 and Allegiant Stadium; the team is now valued at over $7bn (vs $761m in 2011). He bought the WNBA's Aces in 2021.
interesting_fact: While working in Raiders team retail he is said to have invented the muff-style hand warmer now used across the NFL.
deep_cut_fact: A Chico State alumnus, he long kept driving from Oakland back to Chico to see his favourite barber for his trademark bowl cut, and famously drove a 1997 Dodge Caravan with a VHS player.
current_role: Owner and managing general partner, Las Vegas Raiders (NFL); owner, Las Vegas Aces (WNBA)
research_notes: Approachable, unpretentious reputation but gives few long interviews (ESPN's Tim Keown profile is a rare one). Aces dynasty (WNBA titles) and Las Vegas stadium economics are natural podcast angles. Route via Raiders communications department.

name: Eduard Schleicher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
profile: Fifth-generation member of the Schwenk family behind Ulm-based SCHWENK, a cement maker founded in 1847 that now also spans concrete, sand & gravel and concrete pumps, with ~4,500 staff across Germany and Central/Eastern Europe. Schleicher co-leads the group and drives its international expansion; he formerly sat on Heidelberg Materials' supervisory board.
interesting_fact: SCHWENK's Mergelstetten cement plant hosts catch4climate, a >EUR120M oxyfuel carbon-capture pilot run jointly with rivals Heidelberg Materials, Buzzi/Dyckerhoff and Vicat; it captured its first high-purity CO2 (as dry ice) in July 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Today the group has subsidiaries in Austria, Hungary and Czech Republic, among other countries, and employs 4,500 people.
current_role: Managing partner / co-managing director, SCHWENK Zement GmbH & Co. KG (Ulm); supervisory board member at PAUL HARTMANN AG and Wieland-Werke AG
research_notes: Very low public profile; little personal coverage. catch4climate CO2 capture is a strong energy/decarbonisation angle; route via SCHWENK corporate communications. Board roles per https://de.marketscreener.com/insider/EDUARD-SCHLEICHER-A09UUA/ (aggregator).

name: Ursula Hutter-Schleicher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
profile: Forbes says her fortune comes from SCHWENK, a family-owned Ulm building-materials group founded in 1847 that makes cement, concrete, sand and gravel and employs about 4,500 people. Her brother Eduard Schleicher, the fifth generation, runs the company. I found no public statements, interviews or a separate profile for her. She is not the late CSU politician Ursula Schleicher.
interesting_fact: SCHWENK is one of Germany's oldest family firms: Carl Schwenk founded it in Ulm in 1847, and the family has run it for five generations.
current_role: Family shareholder in SCHWENK Zement (Ulm), per Forbes; no public operating role found
research_notes: Very private: only Forbes mentions her. The only route is the SCHWENK corporate contact (general company email), probably via the company's management, which her brother Eduard Schleicher leads. Cement links to the energy and decarbonisation angle.

name: Zhang Lei
profile: Henan-born investor who studied at Renmin University and Yale SOM (MBA 2002) and worked in Yale's Investments Office under David Swensen. He founded Hillhouse in 2005 with seed capital from Yale's endowment and built it into one of Asia's largest investment firms, with early stakes in Tencent, JD.com and BeiGene and buyouts such as Belle International.
interesting_fact: Hillhouse began in 2005 with a startup investment from Yale's endowment, after Zhang had worked under endowment pioneer David Swensen; he later set out his long-term philosophy in the 2020 book 'Value'.
deep_cut_fact: In 2010, less than 10 years after graduating, he pledged exactly $8,888,888 to Yale SOM for its new campus - reportedly the largest gift ever by a SOM graduate - choosing the number because eight signifies fortune in Chinese.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Hillhouse Investment (Hillhouse Capital)
public_contact: office_email: contactus@hillhouseinvestment.com (Hillhouse general contact) | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hillhouse-capital-management (firm) | official_website: https://www.hillhouseinvestment.com/
research_notes: Rarely does English-language podcasts; firm communications go through Hillhouse. Best route is the firm's published general contact.

name: Charles R. Bronfman
profile: Charles Bronfman, born 1931, is a son of Seagram founder Samuel Bronfman. He spent 50 years at Seagram, retiring as co-chairman in 2001, and owned the Montreal Expos from 1968 to 1991. He chaired the Andrea and Charles Bronfman Philanthropies for 30 years and co-founded Birthright Israel.
interesting_fact: He brought Major League Baseball to Canada as the founding principal owner of the Montreal Expos, the first MLB franchise outside the U.S., and owned the team for about 22 years.
deep_cut_fact: His CRB Foundation came up with the Heritage Minutes, the 60-second Canadian history shorts that first aired on CBC on 31 March 1991. He later co-founded Historica Canada, which still produces them.
current_role: Retired co-chairman of Seagram; philanthropist (honoree of The Charles Bronfman Prize)
research_notes: He is 95, so an interview may be difficult. There is no published personal or office email. The Charles Bronfman Prize (founded by his children) is the nearest official channel. His 2016 memoir 'Distilled' covers Seagram, the Expos and the Heritage Minutes and is a good hook.

name: Akira
profile: Kyoto-born (1936) Tokyo property developer, son of Mori Building founder Taikichiro Mori. He and brother Minoru inherited the family business in 1993 and split it in 1999; Akira built Mori Trust (Marunouchi Trust City, Tokyo Shiodome Building, Conrad Tokyo and ~30 hotels). In 2016 he handed the CEO role to his daughter Miwako Date and became chairman.
interesting_fact: Mori Trust helped create Japan's REIT market and listed Mori Trust Sogo REIT; the group also brought Conrad and Shangri-La hotels to Japan and turned around the historic Karuizawa Manpei Hotel.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent 12 years as a banker: after graduating in economics from Keio in 1960 he joined Yasuda Trust and Banking, only joining Mori Building in 1972; in 1973 he founded Mori Trust Hotels & Resorts.
current_role: Chairman, Mori Trust Co., Ltd.; founder and chairman, MA Platform
research_notes: Input record listed only 'Akira' (shared with Minoru Mori, Forbes 1996-98); this is Akira Mori of Mori Trust. Age ~90; daughter Miwako Date runs day-to-day operations. Route via Mori Trust corporate contact.

name: David Zalik
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
education: Auburn University (Drop Out)
profile: David Zalik is the cofounder and former CEO of financial technology company GreenSky, which Goldman Sachs acquired in an all-stock transaction worth about $2.2 billion in 2022. Goldman sold GreenSky to a consortium of investors in 2024, and Zalik left the company.
interesting_fact: Zalik started his first business at the age of 14, buying computer parts from distributors and assembling them himself.
deep_cut_fact: Zalik didn't attend high school and never graduated from college.

name: Richard Chang
profile: Richard H.P. Chang co-founded Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) in Kaohsiung in 1984 with his elder brother Jason; it is now ASE Technology Holding, the world's largest provider of chip assembly, packaging and test services, a key beneficiary of advanced packaging demand for AI chips. He is vice chairman/president, and with Jason a main investor in developer Sino Horizon.
interesting_fact: In the early 1980s the Chang family was already successful in property, but Richard argued Taiwan's nascent electronics industry was the bigger long-term bet; their mother sold properties to cover ASE's losses in its first three years.
deep_cut_fact: He was ASE's founding President from March 1984 (when the first Kaohsiung plant started with about 200 people) until becoming Vice Chairman in 1999, and holds an industrial engineering degree from Chung Yuan Christian University in Taiwan.
current_role: Vice Chairman and President, ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. (Taiwan)
public_contact: press_email: ASEH_PR@aseglobal.com | ir_email: ir@aseglobal.com | official_website: https://www.aseglobal.com
research_notes: Taiwanese family but Forbes lists him under Hong Kong. Low public profile; brother Jason Chang (chairman) is the public face. Best route is ASE corporate PR. ASE is highly relevant to AI/data-center chip packaging (CoWoS-type capacity).

name: Qiu Guanghe
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
profile: Qiu Guanghe is chairman and founder of Semir Group, the parent of Zhejiang Semir Garment, which makes and sells apparel. Semir Garment was founded in 2002, focusing on casual wear and children's clothing and now boasts nearly 8,000 stores across China (including franchises).
interesting_fact: Qiu founded the fashion retailing group in 1996 in his hometown of Wenzhou, a trading mecca in Zhejiang Province.
deep_cut_fact: Qiu Jianqiang, Qiu's son, chairs Zhejiang Semir Garment.

name: Lina Tombolato
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
profile: Lina Tombolato is the widow of Ennio Doris, the former chairman of Italian bank Banca Mediolanum, who died at 81 in November 2021. She and her two children, Mediolanum CEO Massimo and vice president Annalisa, own 41% of the bank, which has 104 billion euros in assets under management.
interesting_fact: She and Ennio were both born in the small northern Italian town of Tombolo and were married for 55 years.

name: Hsieh Wen-Ta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
sec_insider_companies: Amprius Technologies, Inc. (AMPX) - Director; Ambiq Micro, Inc. (AMBQ) - Director; Desktop Metal, Inc. (DM) - Director
profile: Hsieh Wen-Ta (謝旼達) founded Hon. Precision's predecessor in 1999 to build IC test handlers; the company now holds about a third of that market and adds active thermal control and liquid-cooling plates, supplying TSMC, Nvidia and ASE. AI/HPC orders drive about 70% of sales. He took it public on the Taiwan Stock Exchange on Nov 27, 2025.
interesting_fact: Hon. Precision's Nov 2025 TWSE debut set Taiwan listing records: it opened at NT$1,495 (an all-time high listing price) and jumped NT$1,445 on its first day, briefly pushing its market cap near UMC's.
deep_cut_fact: A machine-design graduate of Taipei Institute of Technology (台北工專機械設計科), Hsieh came out of Taiwan's machine-tool trade. Commentator Hsieh Chin-ho noted he wears work clothes on the floor of his Taichung factory, tucked in a lane off Daya Road, so visitors may not realise he's the boss.
current_role: Chairman, Hon. Precision Inc. (鴻勁精密, TWSE: 7769), Taichung, Taiwan
public_contact: ir_email: ir@honprec.com | contact_form: https://www.honprec.com/contact/ | official_website: https://www.honprec.com
research_notes: Very low-profile engineer-founder; rarely interviewed. Hon Precision is unrelated to Hon Hai/Foxconn despite the name. The SEC insider roles listed (Amprius, Ambiq, Desktop Metal director) belong to a different person, Wen Hsieh (a US venture capitalist), not this Hsieh Wen-Ta. Route via company IR.

name: Guenter Herz
profile: Guenter ran his family's Tchibo coffee business for almost 35 years, building it into a retailing force by adding other consumer goods and services. In 2003, he and sister Daniela sold their combined 40% interest in the family holding company, maxingvest ag, for an estimated $5 billion.
interesting_fact: Max Herz, who passed away in 1965, came up the idea of opening stores where coffee could be both sipped and sold over the counter -- a forerunner to Starbucks.
deep_cut_fact: Guenter, an avid fan of race horses and competitive sailing, has enjoyed success as a breeder of trotters.

name: Udo Schütz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
profile: Udo Schütz is the founder of Schütz-Werke, a German industrial packaging company that he founded in 1958. Today the company manufactures products in packaging, recycling, energy systems and the aerospace industry.
interesting_fact: A former race car driver, Schütz won several championships in the 1960s.
deep_cut_fact: Schütz has given 25.5% of the company's shares to the family's charitable foundation Else Schütz Stiftung.

name: Marina Berlusconi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
education: University of Milan
profile: Marina Berlusconi is the eldest daughter of Silvio Berlusconi, the media mogul and longest-serving Italian prime minister in the post-war era, who died at age 86 in June 2023. She is the president of media group Fininvest, which her father started in the late 1970s and built into a national force, importing American shows like 'Baywatch' to Italy.
interesting_fact: Her younger son and her father, both named Silvio, share the same birthday, September 29.
deep_cut_fact: She is the eldest daughter of businessman and former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.

name: Pier Silvio Berlusconi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
profile: Pier Silvio Berlusconi is the son of Silvio Berlusconi, the media mogul and longest-serving Italian prime minister in the post-war era. He died at age 86 in June 2023. He is one of five heirs and, with his older sister Marina, inherited the majority of his father's empire which includes stakes in media, publishing and banking firms.
interesting_fact: He was made an honorary citizen of Portofino in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: As a shareholder of Fininvest, the Berlusconi family's holding company, Pier Silvio Berlusconi plays a significant role in the management of the Mediaset Group, now known as MFE - MediaForEurope, where he serves as Executive Vice President and managing director.

profile: Alan Howard cofounded Brevan Howard Asset Management, a European hedge fund specializing in macro trading, in 2002. The firm was once one of the world's top macro hedge funds, with assets under management peaking at $40 billion in 2013.
interesting_fact: A streak of uninspiring returns led to billions in investor withdrawals, but assets have rebounded to $36 billion after solid returns in recent years.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019, Howard stepped down as CEO to focus solely on investing and to give portfolio managers more autonomy.

name: Shiv Kishan Agrawal
profile: Shiv Kishan Agrawal, who was running Nagpur-based Haldiram Foods International, merged his company with Delhi-based Haldiram Foods in 2023 to create Haldiram Snacks Food. A consortium of investors led by Singapore's Temasek, acquired a 20% stake in the merged company in 2025 at an estimated valuation of $10 billion.
interesting_fact: Agrawal is the grandson of the founder Ganga Bishan Agarwal, who started selling snacks from a tiny shop in Bikaner in Rajasthan and went on to create the popular Haldiram brand.
deep_cut_fact: The business was eventually divided among the patriarch's grandsons into three separate companies, operating out of Nagpur, Delhi and Kolkata.

interesting_fact: Shen was a successful entrepreneur himself earlier in his career, cofounding travel site Trip.com before joining Sequoia.
deep_cut_fact: He previously co-founded Ctrip.com and Home Inn.

name: Roberto Hartono
profile: Roberto Hartono is the president commissioner of Hartono Istana Teknologi.  He inherited his wealth from his late father Michael "Bambang" Hartono. Michael was among the richest in Indonesia and owned a stake in Bank Central Asia together with his brother R. Budi. Michael died in March 2026 at age 86.

profile: Catheline Perier D'Ieteren and her late brother, Roland, are the great great grandchildren of Jean-Joseph D'Ieteren, who founded the D'Ieteren company in 1805. The Group's portfolio includes five businesses ranging from automobile distribution to real estate and glass repair.

interesting_fact: Paul lives in San Francisco's affluent Pacific Heights neighborhood. He owns two yachts and at least one Picasso painting.

name: Ryan Smith
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2025-2026)
education: Brigham Young University (Bachelor of Science)
profile: Utah tech billionaire who co-founded survey and experience-management software firm Qualtrics with his father and brother while at BYU. SAP bought it for $8B in 2019 and later spun it off, and Silver Lake took it private in 2023. He now runs Smith Entertainment Group, which owns the NBA's Utah Jazz and the NHL's Utah Mammoth, and remains a Qualtrics shareholder.
interesting_fact: He brought the NHL to Utah: in 2024 the league granted him an expansion franchise, and he paid $1.2B for the Arizona Coyotes' hockey assets. The team became the Utah Mammoth.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of BYU's Marriott School in his junior year to build Qualtrics. He went back and finished his degree in 2016, when he was already a billionaire CEO. Before that he served a two-year church mission in Mexico.
current_role: Co-founder and board member of Qualtrics; chairman of Smith Entertainment Group (owner of the Utah Jazz and Utah Mammoth)
research_notes: In Feb 2026 Qualtrics named Jason Maynard CEO, with Jim Whitehurst as executive chairman. Older sources still call Smith executive chairman, so describe him as co-founder. He sold his stake in Real Salt Lake in 2025. X handle @RyanSmith belongs to a different person. For sports or media topics, the best route is probably SEG or Utah Jazz communications.

profile: Akio Nitori founded discount home furnishings chain Nitori Holdings; its shares trade on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. The company has expanded in urban markets like Tokyo and has more than 1,000 stores mostly in Japan.

deep_cut_fact: In 2020, the company acquired home-improvement chain Shimachu in a nearly $2 billion deal.

education: University of Rhode Island (Bachelor of Arts/Economics)
