profile: Organic chemist (PhD) who spent about a decade in pharma, at Ranbaxy and then at Matrix Labs, where he rose to COO. He founded Laurus Labs in Hyderabad in 2005 as an R&D firm. It now supplies APIs and formulations for HIV, cancer, asthma and diabetes drugs and has expanded into CDMO and biotech. He still spends about 25% of his time in the labs.
interesting_fact: He is a named co-inventor on about 145 patents granted to Laurus Labs, and in his spare time he enjoys cooking Indian food and sweets.
deep_cut_fact: As founder and first employee he never held 50% of Laurus Labs. In 2006, a year after founding, he set aside 5% of the company's equity for employee stock options.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Laurus Labs (Hyderabad)
public_contact: ir_email: secretarial@lauruslabs.com (company secretarial / investor contact) | official_website: https://www.lauruslabs.com
research_notes: He won EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2021 (Life Sciences & Healthcare category), and he serves on the USP board of trustees. I found no dedicated press email; the secretarial inbox is the published investor channel.

name: Segolene Gallienne
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
profile: Ségolène Frère-Gallienne is the daughter of the late Albert Frère, Belgium's richest industrialist, and co-heir to the Frère holding with stakes in GBL (run by her husband Ian Gallienne). After PR roles at Belgacom/Proximus and five years leading communications at Dior Fine Jewelry, she sits on several boards and since 2023 runs the family's Lenoble Champagne house.
interesting_fact: She sits on the board of Château Cheval Blanc, the Saint-Émilion first growth co-owned by the Frère family and Bernard Arnault, and has been a director of Christian Dior SE since about 2010.
deep_cut_fact: She has a long-standing passion for gemology, and at Lenoble she has personally joined the grape harvest to understand the terroir; she redesigned the house's HQ with Dior Maison creative director Cordelia de Castellane as a free-to-visit family home.
current_role: Head of Champagne Lenoble (Damery) since 2023; director of Christian Dior SE, Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, Power Corporation of Canada and Château Cheval Blanc
research_notes: Contacts are for Champagne Lenoble (the business she runs), not personal. Private family; GBL press office is an alternative route. Weak fit for energy/data-center themes beyond GBL holdings.

name: Maritsa Lazari
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2021)
profile: Born in Dora, Cyprus in 1943, she moved to London at 16 and married fellow Cypriot Christos (Chris) Lazari in 1965. In 1978 the couple put profits from his Drendie Girl fashion label into London property. Lazari Investments now owns over 3M sq ft, mostly West End offices plus the Brunswick Centre. Since Chris died in 2015 she has stayed on as a director alongside their three children.
interesting_fact: The fortune began with a high-street fashion label: Chris saved money from washing dishes and waiting tables to study fashion design, and Drendie Girl funded the move into property in 1978.
deep_cut_fact: The family's Christos Lazari Foundation, set up in 2017 with Maritsa as trustee, supports Cypriot, Greek Orthodox and medical causes. It gave £3.25m of investment property to the Cypriot children's charity Radiomarathon.
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Lazari Investments (London); trustee, Christos Lazari Foundation
research_notes: Very private, with almost no interviews on record. The foundation's published email is the only route found. Lazari Investments has no verified official website (lazari.co.uk sits behind a bot wall and could not be confirmed). Her sons are also directors. Little obvious energy or data-center fit beyond London office property.

name: Nikhil Kamath
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2019); Hurun Global U40 (2021-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
profile: Bengaluru entrepreneur who co-founded discount brokerage Zerodha with brother Nithin in 2010, disrupting Indian retail broking. Also runs zero-fee asset manager True Beacon, co-founded investment firm Gruhas (2021), and hosts the 'WTF is' podcast, whose guests have included PM Narendra Modi, Bill Gates and Elon Musk.
interesting_fact: In 2023 he became the youngest Indian signatory of the Giving Pledge, committing to give away at least half his wealth.
deep_cut_fact: A school dropout after 10th grade with no formal degree, he started out working in a call centre while trading equities on the side; in 2024 he launched WTFund, a non-dilutive grant fund for founders aged 25 and under.
current_role: Co-founder, Zerodha; founder of True Beacon and Gruhas; host of the 'WTF is' podcast
public_contact: x: https://x.com/nikhilkamathcio | instagram: https://www.instagram.com/nikhilkamathcio/ | linkedin: https://linkedin.com/in/nikhilkamathcio | podcast: WTF is with Nikhil Kamath
research_notes: Fellow podcaster; peer-to-peer pitch (guest swap) is a natural angle. Very active on X/Instagram. Gruhas invests in climate tech. No published press email found.

name: Stephen Lansdown
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
profile: Bristol-born accountant (b. 1952) who co-founded Hargreaves Lansdown with Peter Hargreaves in 1981. It grew into the UK's largest retail investment platform. He left its board in 2012 and moved to Guernsey in 2010, and now concentrates on Bristol Sport and private and impact investments. He co-founded the sustainable PE firm Earth Capital in 2008; it closed in 2024.
interesting_fact: Trained as an accountant, he started Hargreaves Lansdown trading from a bedroom in 1981. He later sold Hargreaves Lansdown shares to help fund Bristol City's redevelopment of Ashton Gate, and rescued Bristol Rugby (now Bristol Bears) when it was close to going under.
deep_cut_fact: He was an early convert to sustainable investing. In 2019 he said he had narrowed his focus to four themes: food security, energy security, clean water and waste management. Earth Capital scored every deal on its own 'Earth Dividend' ESG scorecard, mapped to the UN SDGs.
current_role: Owner, Bristol Sport (Bristol City FC, Bristol Bears, Bristol Flyers); private investor based in Guernsey
research_notes: He received a CBE in 2017. His energy-security and sustainability investing is a natural podcast angle. Bristol Sport is the most direct published route.

name: Fabrizio Di Amato
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
education: La Sapienza University of Rome (Bachelor of Political Science)
profile: Rome-born Di Amato started his business at 19 with three employees. Through acquisitions including Fiat Engineering (2004), Tecnimont (2005), Stamicarbon (2009) and KT (2010) he built MAIRE, now an energy-transition engineering and technology group with 9,800+ staff in 45 countries. He listed it in Milan in 2007, and in 2018 he founded NextChem, its sustainable-technology arm working on hydrogen, ammonia, SAF and circular chemistry.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he founded Federprogetti, the Italian Plant Engineering Federation, and chaired it until 2015. He was made a Cavaliere del Lavoro (Knight of Labour) in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: His degree is in Political Science from La Sapienza, yet the Politecnico di Milano later gave him an honorary degree in Chemical Engineering. His Maire Foundation preserves the group's historic engineering archives and trains 'humanist engineers' for the energy and digital transitions.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, MAIRE S.p.A. (Rome/Milan); Chairman, Maire Foundation
public_contact: press_email: mediarelations@groupmaire.com | ir_email: investor-relations@groupmaire.com | office_email: communications@fondazionemaire.com | official_website: https://www.groupmaire.com
research_notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: MAIRE/NextChem work on hydrogen, ammonia, SAF and nuclear MoUs (e.g. Nuward). The group media relations contact named in releases is Tommaso Verani. The press-release contact block was confirmed via search snippet, not opened directly.

name: Frank Love
profile: Son of Tom and Judy Love, who started Love's in 1964 by leasing a gas station in Watonga, Oklahoma. Frank and Greg have been co-CEOs since 2014 of the Oklahoma City-based, family-owned chain, now 640+ truck stops and stores in 42 states with ~40,000 team members and an estimated $22B in sales.
interesting_fact: Love's is also an alternative-fuels player: in 2016 it bought Trillium, then the second-largest U.S. distributor of compressed natural gas, which became the base of its alternative-energy business.
current_role: Co-CEO, Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores (with brother Greg Love)
research_notes: Low personal media profile; sister Jenny Love Meyer (Chief Culture Officer) is the family's usual public voice. Father Tom Love died 2023. Truck-stop fuel transition (CNG, RNG, hydrogen, EV charging) is the natural energy-podcast angle. Route via Love's media group.

name: Greg Love
profile: Greg Love is co-CEO of Love's, the family-owned truck-stop and convenience chain founded by his parents Tom and Judy Love in 1964, now 600+ locations in 42 states with ~$22bn in estimated sales. He began working at the company in high school and previously held roles including president/COO and VP of real estate. Founder Tom Love died in 2025.
interesting_fact: Love's is a sizable energy-transition player: its Trillium unit (bought 2016, renamed Love's Alternative Energy in 2025) runs 100+ CNG stations, hydrogen stations, EV charging and RNG supply.
deep_cut_fact: Love's opened its first hydrogen fueling station in 2018 at the Orange County Transportation Authority's Santa Ana bus facility, via its then-subsidiary Trillium CNG.
current_role: Co-CEO (with brother Frank Love), Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, Oklahoma City
research_notes: Strong energy-podcast fit (truck fuel, CNG/RNG, hydrogen, EV charging). Low personal media profile; route via Love's media group. Aggregators say he holds a BA from Trinity University (unverified).

name: Jenny Love Meyer
profile: Daughter of Tom and Judy Love, who founded Love's in 1964 with a $5,000 family loan; the Oklahoma City chain now has 600+ truck stops in 42 states and ~$22bn in sales, run by her brothers Frank and Greg as co-CEOs. She joined the company in 1991 and in 2019 became its first-ever Chief Culture Officer; her wealth stems from the family's ownership stake.
interesting_fact: She was the first person to hold the title of chief culture officer at Love's, created in November 2019, and has described culture as being like the water in an aquarium: always present, but it needs nourishing.
deep_cut_fact: She studied political science at Colorado College, began at Love's in 1991 in business and operational roles, and for years led the company's public/media relations, internal communications and charitable giving; she sits on the Greater Oklahoma City Chamber executive committee.
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Culture Officer, Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores
public_contact: press_email: lauren.daniels@loves.com (Lauren Daniels, Media Relations Specialist) | official_website: https://www.loves.com/en/news
research_notes: Speaks at comms/HR conferences (Ragan, NACS), so open to culture/leadership conversations. Route via Love's media relations. Energy angle: truck-stop fueling and alternative fuels (verify Love's current EV/alt-fuel programs before using).

name: Laura Love
profile: One of four children of Tom and Judy Love, who founded Love's in Oklahoma in 1964. The family-owned chain runs 600+ truck stops in 42 states (~$22B est. sales); brothers Greg and Frank are co-CEOs and sister Jenny Love Meyer is chief culture officer. Laura keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Love's began in 1964 when Tom and Judy Love started it with a $5,000 loan from Tom's parents; it remains wholly family-owned with 600+ locations in 42 states.
deep_cut_fact: Sister Jenny Love Meyers is chief culture officer and EVP.
current_role: Co-owner (with siblings Greg, Frank and Jenny) of Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores; no public executive role found
public_contact: press_email: LovesMediaGroup@loves.com (Love's corporate media relations) | official_website: https://www.loves.com
research_notes: Very private; no interviews, personal accounts or individual role found. Parents died 2023 (Tom) and 2024 (Judy) - avoid. A podcast pitch would more realistically go to the co-CEOs via the company media group.

name: Tim Cook
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Wikidata (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
sec_insider_companies: Apple Inc. (AAPL) - Chief Executive Officer; NIKE, Inc. (NKE) - Director
education: Fuqua School of Business (Master of Business Administration)
profile: Alabama-raised industrial engineer who joined Apple in 1998 from Compaq, after 12 years at IBM, to fix its supply chain. As COO he became Steve Jobs's successor and was CEO from 2011 to Aug 2026, taking Apple to record valuations. He is one of the few billionaires who made his fortune as a hired CEO. As executive chairman he now focuses partly on global policy engagement.
interesting_fact: He handed the CEO role to hardware chief John Ternus on Sept 1, 2026 after nearly 15 years. He came from humble roots (his father was a shipyard worker, his mother worked at a pharmacy) and was salutatorian of Robertsdale High School in 1978.
deep_cut_fact: To pay his way through Auburn's industrial-engineering program he did a co-op with Reynolds Aluminum, working in Richmond, Virginia every other quarter. Before Apple he was COO of the computer-reseller division of Intelligent Electronics.
current_role: Executive Chairman, Apple (stepped down as CEO on Sept 1, 2026, succeeded by John Ternus); director, Nike
research_notes: The press contact is Josh Rosenstock, named on Apple's Cook/Ternus transition release. Very hard to book; any request goes through Apple PR. The X handle @tim_cook is widely known, but I didn't confirm it on the leadership page. The Intelligent Electronics detail is sourced to Wikipedia/CNN Fast Facts.

name: Eugene Murtagh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
profile: Born in Kingscourt, Co. Cavan in 1942, Murtagh started out making agricultural trailers and engineering parts in the early 1960s, then built Kingspan into a global leader in insulated panels and building envelopes, with 200+ factories in roughly 80 countries. He was CEO until 2005 and chairman until 2021, and still owns about 15%.
interesting_fact: Kingspan began with him building agricultural trailers behind his family's bar, Murtagh's, in Kingscourt. The group's head office still sits in the same small Cavan town.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2011 local Q&A he said that before going it alone he worked for a company in Carrickmacross and went to England with them for a short while; by the time he came back he had decided to work for himself, at 21, starting in his father's backyard.
current_role: Founder and President Emeritus, Kingspan Group plc (stepped down as chairman in 2021)
public_contact: pr_agency: Murray Consultants (Pat Walsh), Tel +353 (0)1 4980300, Kingspan's listed press contact | official_website: https://www.kingspan.com
research_notes: In his 80s and retired from the board; keeps a low profile in Kingscourt. His son Gene Murtagh is Kingspan CEO. Kingspan is highly relevant to data centers (it supplies data-center building envelopes and raised floors). Route through Kingspan's PR agency Murray. Avoid mentioning his late wife.

name: Sol Daurella i Comadrán
education: ESADE
profile: Barcelona-born (1966) heir to the Daurella family, which became Spain's first Coca-Cola bottler in 1951. After strategy consulting at Mac Group she joined the Coca-Cola system in 1992, led Coca-Cola Iberian Partners, and has chaired CCEP, the world's largest Coca-Cola bottler by revenue, since its 2016 formation; the family holds its stake through Cobega.
interesting_fact: Her family's Cobega has been part of the Coca-Cola system since 1951, when it became the first Spanish Coca-Cola bottler; she has also sat on the boards of Banco Santander, Banco Sabadell, Acciona and Ebro Foods.
deep_cut_fact: She went to an English school in Montreux, Switzerland, holds a finance master's from UC Berkeley as well as an ESADE MBA, and has served as honorary consul general of Iceland in Barcelona.
current_role: Chairman, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP); executive chair of family holding Cobega
research_notes: Very private, rarely interviewed. Iceland consulate role may be historical (Icelandic government now lists a different honorary consul). Route via CCEP media relations.

name: Jamie Dimon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
sec_insider_companies: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO (JPM) - Chairman & CEO
education: Harvard Business School (Master of Business Administration)
profile: Jamie Dimon has run JPMorgan Chase, the largest US bank by assets, as CEO since 2005-06 and chairman since 2006-07, after helping Sandy Weill build Citigroup and leading Bank One. His stake and pay make him one of few bank-CEO billionaires. In June 2026 JPMorgan named Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh co-presidents; Dimon reportedly plans about three more years as CEO before becoming executive chairman.
interesting_fact: His Greek grandfather, a banker in Smyrna and Athens, changed the family name from Papademetriou to Dimon; his father and grandfather were both stockbrokers at Shearson.
deep_cut_fact: His break came from a college paper: at Tufts he wrote about Shearson's mergers, his mother sent it to Sandy Weill, and Weill hired him for a summer job doing budgets at Shearson.
current_role: Chairman & CEO, JPMorgan Chase
public_contact: press_email: Global Communications: Joe Evangelisti (no email listed); IR/HR media: michael.f.fusco@jpmchase.com | official_website: https://www.jpmorganchase.com
research_notes: Go through JPMorgan Global Communications. He publishes an annual shareholder letter, which is a good hook for outreach. Succession source: https://www.foxbusiness.com/business-leaders/jpmorgan-names-2-new-co-presidents-setting-up-race-succeed-jamie-dimon

name: Adam Kwok
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
education: Harvard Business School (Master of Business Administration); Stanford University (Bachelor of Science in Engineering)
profile: Adam Kwok Kai-fai (郭基煇) is a grandson of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng and son of former joint chairman Thomas Kwok. After a stint in investment banking he joined Hong Kong's largest developer in 2008, became an executive director in 2014 and has led its South China (mainland) property business since 2013, acting as project director on major residential and commercial schemes.
interesting_fact: He is part of one of Asia's richest property families: four of his cousins, his father, an uncle and his grandmother have all been billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: A keen cyclist, he donated HK$10 million to a Hong Kong Sports Institute / HKUST joint venture to develop more aerodynamic cycling equipment for Hong Kong riders.
current_role: Executive director, Sun Hung Kai Properties (since 2014); runs SHKP's South China property business
research_notes: Also sits on HK government's Major Sports Events Committee and is a vice president of REDA. Avoid referencing his father's conviction. Route via SHKP corporate communications.

name: Gerald Ford
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
sec_insider_companies: Hilltop Holdings Inc. (HTH) - TenPercentOwner
education: Southern Methodist University (Bachelor of Arts/Science); Southern Methodist University (Doctor of Jurisprudence)
profile: Dallas lawyer-turned-banker (b. 1944, raised in Pampa, Texas; SMU grad) who has bought and turned around distressed banks since 1975. His biggest win was selling Golden State Bancorp (with Ronald Perelman) to Citigroup for ~$6B in 2002. He owns ~25% of Hilltop Holdings (PlainsCapital Bank, PrimeLending, HilltopSecurities) and controls California's Mechanics Bank via Ford Financial Fund.
interesting_fact: He gave his alma mater SMU $20M in 1997 for a new football stadium (Gerald J. Ford Stadium) and $15M in 2013 for a research center.
deep_cut_fact: Ford credits working as a teenager in an auto body shop alongside his dad in Pampa, Texas, with pushing him toward a better career - and he carried around Ayn Rand's 'Atlas Shrugged' in high school.
current_role: Chairman, Hilltop Holdings (NYSE: HTH); co-managing partner, Ford Financial Fund; director, Mechanics Bank
public_contact: ir_email: mdunn@hilltop.com (Matt Dunn, Hilltop Holdings investor relations) | official_website: https://ir.hilltop-holdings.com/
research_notes: Not to be confused with the US president. Son Jeremy Ford is Hilltop CEO. Low media profile; IR contact is a corporate route, not personal.

name: D. Leopoldo Del Pino
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2013-2025)
education: INSEAD (Master of Business Administration); Polytechnic University of Madrid (Bachelor of Engineering)
profile: Leopoldo del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo is a son of Rafael del Pino y Moreno, who founded Ferrovial in 1952, and inherited a stake in the infrastructure group. He sat on Ferrovial's board until early 2016 and has since gradually reduced his holding from over 8% to roughly 4%. His brother Rafael chairs Ferrovial. He invests privately, largely through SICAV vehicles.
interesting_fact: Ferrovial, the company his father founded in 1952, is now one of the world's largest infrastructure operators, with stakes in toll roads such as Toronto's 407 ETR and in Heathrow Airport.
deep_cut_fact: Leopoldo, who owns about 4% of Ferrovial, served as a board member of the company until early 2016.
current_role: Private investor and Ferrovial shareholder; former Ferrovial board member (until early 2016)
research_notes: Very private, with no public role or published contact. He is not an executive at Ferrovial, so the company press office is not a real route to him. Press coverage centres on his SICAVs and stake sales. Low priority.

name: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
title_and_organization: Founder, Chair And Managing Director, Biocon
education: Bangalore University (Bachelor of Arts/Science); Melbourne University (Master of Science)
profile: Trained master brewer who founded Biocon in 1978 and built it into one of India's largest biopharma firms, with one of Asia's largest insulin plants (Johor, Malaysia) and a biosimilars arm that bought Viatris' biosimilars business in 2022. In Dec 2025 Biocon agreed to buy out the rest of Biocon Biologics (valued at $5.5bn). Her philanthropy includes the Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center cancer-care model.
interesting_fact: She wanted to be a doctor but couldn't get into medical school; after qualifying as a master brewer in Australia she was told in India she wouldn't be hired as a brewer because it was 'a man's work', and started Biocon in 1978 in a rented garage with Rs 10,000.
deep_cut_fact: On 5 March 2015 her alma mater, Federation University Australia (formerly Ballarat College of Advanced Education, where she was the only woman in the 1974 brewing course), opened 'Mazumdar Drive' at its Mt Helen campus in her honour; she cut the ribbon herself.
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairperson, Biocon Ltd (Bengaluru)
public_contact: press_email: rumman.ahmed@biocon.com (Head - External Communications, Biocon) | ir_email: Prashant.nair@biocon.com (Head - Investor Relations) | x: https://x.com/kiranshaw | x: @bioconlimited (company) | official_website: https://www.biocon.com/ | https://kiranshaw.blog/ | https://www.instagram.com/realkiranshaws/
research_notes: Very media-accessible and active on X (@kiranshaw); frequently speaks on Bengaluru infrastructure, biotech policy and women in science. Husband John Shaw died in 2022 - be sensitive. Avoid the 2022 CBI bribery case.

name: Sergei Galitsky
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2020)
education: Kuban State University (Bachelor of Arts/Science)
profile: Sergey Galitsky founded Magnit, one of Russia's largest grocery and cosmetics chains, after starting as a perfume/cosmetics wholesaler (Tander) in 1994; he opened the first store in 1998 and took it public in 2006. He sold almost all his stake to VTB in 2018 for $2.4B and now focuses on FC Krasnodar, its academy, a stadium, a 2,500-tree park and a family winery.
interesting_fact: An admirer of Walmart, he advertised his first Magnit store with the slogan 'Always Low Prices'; he later spent ~$460M on FC Krasnodar's stadium (nicknamed the 'Galiseum') and $70M on the adjacent park.
deep_cut_fact: A teenage chess talent, he became a candidate master within two years and won the Sochi championship; he made chess compulsory at the FC Krasnodar academy and in 2013 played a 4-hour simul vs 20 pupils, winning 16.5-3.5.
current_role: Owner and president, FC Krasnodar (football club and academy); founder of Magnit
public_contact: press_email: n.baiburin@fckrasnodar.ru (head of FC Krasnodar press service) | press_email: event@fckrasnodar.ru (FC Krasnodar PR department) | office_email: info@fckrasnodar.ru
research_notes: Russia-based; check current sanctions/compliance status before outreach. Known as outspoken and relatively accessible to press in Russian media (e.g. Novaya Gazeta 2025 interview). Born Sergey Arutyunyan, 1967.

name: Liora Ofer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
education: Hebrew Reali School
profile: Haifa-born (1953) real estate businesswoman who inherited Ofer Investments, cofounded in 1957 by her father Yuli and uncle Sammy Ofer. She has chaired Melisron since 2008, growing it into one of Israel's largest property companies (malls incl. Ramat Aviv Mall, office parks), and now owns 100% of Ofer Investments.
interesting_fact: She is one of only two female billionaires in Israel (the other being Shari Arison); under her chairmanship Melisron acquired 25 shopping malls from British Israel Investments.
deep_cut_fact: She began working alongside her father at Ofer Investments at age 20, and in 1995 became general manager of Coral Beach Eilat Ltd, the Red Sea hotel business, years before taking over Melisron.
current_role: Chairperson, Ofer Investments and Melisron Ltd (TASE)
research_notes: Private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is via Melisron's corporate/IR office (melisron.co.il; site was unreachable during research). Recognized as a donor to Reichman University (IDC Herzliya): https://runi.ac.il/en/about/runifriends/donor-recognition/liora-ofer

name: Gerry Harvey
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
education: All Saints' College, Bathurst; University of Sydney
profile: Gerry Harvey (b. 1939) co-founded Harvey Norman with Ian Norman in 1982 after their first chain, Norman Ross, was sold; it now sells furniture, electricals and bedding across Australia and 100+ overseas stores (NZ, Singapore, Malaysia, Slovenia, Ireland, UK). His wife Katie Page runs the business as CEO, while he remains executive chairman, a vocal media commentator and a major thoroughbred breeder.
interesting_fact: He owns Baramul Stud, has one of the world's largest thoroughbred portfolios (600+ horses) and co-owns the Magic Millions bloodstock auction.
deep_cut_fact: He started out selling vacuum cleaners and fridges door-to-door for Goodwins of Newtown, where he met Ian Norman; the pair opened their first Sydney store in 1961. He dropped out of university and has said: 'I always wanted to be a farmer.'
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Harvey Norman Holdings (Australia)
research_notes: Very media-accessible; frequently gives interviews to Australian business press and radio. No published press email found; company contact page or ASX company secretary are the routes.

name: Jerry Yang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1999-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Wikidata (2015)
education: Stanford University (Bachelor of Arts/Science); Stanford University (Master of Science)
profile: Taiwan-born Jerry Yang co-founded Yahoo with David Filo in 1994-95 while both were Stanford EE PhD students. He was Yahoo's CEO from 2007 to 2009 and left the company in 2012. His bet on Alibaba, a 40% stake in 2005, was one of the most lucrative in tech history. Through AME Cloud Ventures he backs data-driven startups such as Zoom, Wattpad and Evernote, and he chaired Stanford's board of trustees from 2021 to 2025.
interesting_fact: He collects ancient Chinese calligraphy, about 250 works from the Ming and Qing eras. In 2017 he and his wife Akiko Yamazaki gave $25M to San Francisco's Asian Art Museum, the largest gift in its history.
deep_cut_fact: His VC firm's name, AME (pronounced 'ah-meh'), means 'rain' in Japanese, a nod to cloud computing. He met his wife Akiko on a six-month Stanford exchange in Japan in 1992, and he says 'shoe' was the only English word he knew when he arrived in San Jose aged 10.
current_role: Founding Partner, AME Cloud Ventures (Yahoo co-founder; Stanford trustee, board chair 2021-2025)
research_notes: No public email on the AME site. Best route is AME Cloud Ventures (Palo Alto) or a warm intro through Stanford or portfolio founders such as Eric Yuan of Zoom. AME's data and cloud focus fits the data-center theme.

name: Sam Altman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); SEC insider holdings (2024); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
sec_insider_companies: Oklo Inc. (OKLO) - Director
education: John Burroughs School; Stanford University
profile: Stanford dropout who founded Loopt (sold 2012 for $43M), ran Y Combinator as president 2014-2019, then became OpenAI CEO (briefly fired and rehired in 2023). profile: Puthan Naduvakkatt Chenthamaraksha Menon, also known as P.N.C. Menon is an Omani billionaire businessman of Indian origin, born in Palakkad, Kerala.
interesting_fact: He is the founder and chairman of Sobha Ltd & Sobha LLC.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Vadakkencherry; studied at Sree Kerala Varma College.

name: Willis J Johnson
profile: Willis J Johnson — wealth from Copart (United States) Estimated net worth $3.0B (Hurun Global, 2026).

name: Miriam Blocher
profile: Miriam Blocher is a Swiss businesswoman — wealth from EMS Chemie (Switzerland) Estimated net worth $3.0B (Hurun Global, 2026).

name: Rawya Mansour
profile: Rawya Mansour is a Egyptian businessperson — wealth from Mansour Group (Egypt) Estimated net worth $3.0B (Hurun Global, 2026).

name: Henrik Mads Clauson
profile: Born 1953, one of five children of Danfoss founder Mads Clausen and Bitten Clausen. He is listed as a direct owner of Danfoss alongside Clausen Controls A/S and the Bitten & Mads Clausen Foundation (largest shareholder). Danfoss, based in Nordborg, Denmark, makes drives, cooling, heating and power solutions, including for data centers.
interesting_fact: Danfoss was founded by his father Mads Clausen in 1933 in a farmhouse attic on the island of Als; the company now leads in energy-efficient cooling, drives and heat pumps.
current_role: Shareholder of Danfoss A/S (no public executive or board role found)
public_contact: press_email: lars.lohff@danfoss.com (Lars Grubak Lohff, Head of Media Relations, Danfoss) | contact_form: https://www.danfoss.com/en-gb/about-danfoss/news-and-events/media-contacts/ | office_email: info@bmcfond.dk (Bitten & Mads Clausen Foundation)
research_notes: Very private; no public role. Family is represented on the Danfoss board by third-generation Mads Clausen and Mads-Peter Clausen - better interview targets for an energy/data-center podcast. Approach via Danfoss media relations.

name: Arvindkumar Poddar
profile: Arvind Poddar controls and runs Balkrishna Industries (BKT), the Mumbai-listed maker of off-highway tyres for agriculture, mining and earthmoving. BKT opened its first off-highway tyre plant in Aurangabad in 1987 and sells mainly into replacement markets in Europe and North America. It held about 8% of the global off-the-road tyre segment in 2014 and supplies OEMs such as JCB, John Deere and CNH.
interesting_fact: Under Poddar, BKT became a major sports sponsor: the official tyre of Monster Jam since 2014 and title sponsor of Italy's Serie BKT and France's Ligue 2 BKT (extended to 2028). In October 2026 it announced a 50:50 joint venture with Pirelli to make Pirelli-branded premium tyres in India.
current_role: CEO & Managing Director (chairman & MD in earlier filings), Balkrishna Industries Ltd (BKT Tires), Mumbai
research_notes: Web search budget ran out at this point, so research came from Wikipedia and BKT's site only and no sourced deep-cut fact was found. BKT runs a registration-only Press Hub for journalists, which is the logical route. The investor-relations email is in stock-exchange filings but was not verified here.

name: Sandeep Pravinbhai Engineer
profile: Sandeep Engineer is a first-generation entrepreneur and chemical engineer. He spent eight years in pharmaceutical bulk drugs before founding Astral Poly Technik in 1996, now Astral Ltd, a leading Indian maker of plastic pipes and building materials. He has since expanded into adhesives (Resinova, 2014), water tanks (Sarita, 2020) and paints (Gem Paints).
interesting_fact: In 1998 Astral launched CPVC piping in India for the first time. Plastic pipes were then barely accepted against metal, so Engineer spent years educating plumbers and builders to create the category Astral now leads.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a project engineer at a pharmaceuticals company, then became a distributor and later manufactured pharmaceutical remedies. He said he had been fascinated by polymers since his graduation days, which led to the pivot into piping. He also completed Harvard Business School's OPM programme.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Astral Limited (Ahmedabad)
research_notes: Self-made founder story with a strong entrepreneurship angle. His wife Jagruti Engineer is a whole-time director. Contact is through Astral corporate (info@) or company secretary or IR via the investors page.

name: Rafique Abdul Malik
profile: Indian footwear retailer who turned the single Colaba, Mumbai shoe store his father Malik Tejani acquired in 1955 into Metro Brands, one of India's largest and most profitable footwear chains (~800 stores) with Metro Shoes, Mochi and Walkway plus franchises for Crocs, FitFlop, Fila and Foot Locker. Metro Brands is listed; daughter Farah Malik Bhanji is MD and Nissan Joseph CEO.
interesting_fact: Metro started as one standalone shoe shop in Colaba, Mumbai, and over three generations grew into a 'Made in India' footwear house of brands with roughly 800 stores.
deep_cut_fact: He has been chairman since 19 January 1977, the month Metro Shoes was incorporated, giving him nearly five decades at the helm; the company bio also notes he is a Harvard alumnus.
current_role: Chairman, Metro Brands Limited (Mumbai)
public_contact: office_email: info@metrobrands.com (Metro Brands general contact; tel +91-22-6656-0444) | official_website: https://www.metrobrands.com/
research_notes: Low public profile; daughter and MD Farah Malik Bhanji is the usual public face. The company site has a Media section that may list a PR contact.

name: Cecilia Morel
profile: Cecilia Morel Montes is the widow of former Chilean president and billionaire investor Sebastián Piñera (d. 2024), whose fortune came from introducing credit cards to Chile and stakes including LATAM Airlines; Hurun lists her as holder of the family wealth. A trained family and youth counsellor, she chaired social foundations such as Integra and PRODEMU as First Lady.
interesting_fact: She was at the San José mine site with the president throughout the October 2010 rescue of the 33 trapped Copiapó miners, famously moved to tears when the first miner surfaced.
deep_cut_fact: In 1989, with professionals from the Instituto Carlos Casanueva, she founded 'La Casa de la Juventud', running personal-development workshops for young people in Santiago's Conchalí district; the project later spun off the Women Embark Foundation.
current_role: Former First Lady of Chile (2010-14, 2018-22); heir to the Piñera family fortune (family investment group Bancard)
research_notes: Not an entrepreneur in her own right; wealth is inherited from Sebastián Piñera (family vehicle Grupo Bancard). No published personal/office contact verified (search budget exhausted). Recently widowed (2024) - handle sensitively. Weak fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast.

name: Jogi Hendra Atmadja
profile: Jakarta-born (1946) University of Indonesia economics graduate who founded Mayora with his siblings in 1977, starting with a biscuit factory in Tangerang. Mayora now owns 50+ brands including Kopiko, Danisa, Beng-Beng, Torabika and Energen, runs 25 factories and exports to 100+ countries; son Andre Sukendra Atmadja is president director.
interesting_fact: Through its Kopiko brand, Mayora is often described as the world's largest coffee-candy maker; Kopiko is exported to more than 100 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Mayora, he started his career as a banker at Bank Central Asia.
current_role: Founder and President Commissioner (chairman), PT Mayora Indah Tbk
research_notes: Very low public profile, in his late 70s. Deep-cut fact cited via Wikipedia to a Jakarta Post article that was paywalled/403 for me - verify before use. Mayora's published consumer email (consumer@mayora.co.id) is consumer-care only, not a press route.

name: Douglas Hsu Hsu-Tung
profile: Douglas Tong Hsu (徐旭東) is the son of founder Yu-Ziang Hsu and heads Far Eastern Group, a Taiwanese conglomerate of about 250 companies and nine listed firms. Its businesses span petrochemicals and energy (including Chiahui Power), polyester, cement, telecom (Far EasTone), banking, retail (SOGO, Far Eastern Department Stores) and hotels. Son Jeff Hsu debuted as group Chief Innovation Officer at 2026 AGMs.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Far Eastern New Century became the world's third-largest polyester textile maker (2018), and the group's family foundations established leading private universities and a medical-centre hospital in Taiwan.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his BA and MA at the University of Notre Dame, where he is an Emeritus Trustee, followed by postgraduate study at Columbia. His Committee of 100 profile calls him an 'architecture devotee' and collector of modern art and sculpture who enjoys diving and swimming.
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Far Eastern Group (Taipei); re-elected chairman of Asia Cement in 2026
research_notes: No personal or press email published on the FEG site (the only email listed is a mall customer-service address, so it is excluded). Energy and telecom holdings make him a podcast fit; best route is via group corporate communications or Far EasTone/FENC investor relations. Member of the Committee of 100 since 2005.

name: Maria Dolores Mantegazza
profile: Maria Dolores Mantegazza (b. 1956) is the daughter of Sergio Mantegazza (1927-2024), longtime owner-chairman of Lugano-based Globus, the escorted-tour group behind Globus, Cosmos, Avalon Waterways and Monograms. She appeared on Hurun's 2024 global list after inheriting a share of the family fortune on her father's death in February 2024.
interesting_fact: The Globus travel empire traces back to 1928, when her grandfather Antonio Mantegazza started out with a single gondola carrying tourists and goods on Lake Lugano.
deep_cut_fact: She is a trustee, with Fabio and Geo Mantegazza, of the Sergio Mantegazza Charitable Foundation in Canton Ticino, which supports arts, youth sports, education and medical charities.
current_role: Heir and shareholder of the Globus family of travel brands (Globus, Cosmos, Avalon Waterways, Monograms; U.S. arm Group Voyagers); trustee, Sergio Mantegazza Charitable Foundation
research_notes: Extremely private; no interviews or public channels found. Alive status inferred from Hurun 2024 listing, not independently confirmed (web-search budget exhausted). Globus press pages blocked automated access; best route is the Globus/Group Voyagers corporate press office.

name: TS Kalyanaraman
profile: Born in Thrissur, Kerala in 1947, Kalyanaraman came from a family textile business founded by his grandfather in 1909. He opened the first Kalyan Jewellers store in Thrissur in 1993 and built it into one of India's largest jewellery chains, with stores in India and the Gulf. The company listed in 2021. He also runs Kalyan Developers.
interesting_fact: He opened the first Kalyan Jewellers showroom in Thrissur on 18 April 1993, after two decades in the family's textile retail business, Kalyan Silks.
deep_cut_fact: He was named after his grandfather T. S. Kalyanarama Iyer, who started the family business in 1909. He began learning trade at age 12 by helping in his father's shop, and in 2023 he published an autobiography, 'The Golden Touch'.
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd
research_notes: The age-12 detail is from Wikipedia (citing Bloomberg 2013). His autobiography is a good conversation hook. The company's general inbox is the only published email; the IR page lists no separate address.

name: Basudeo Narain Singh
profile: Co-founder of Alkem Laboratories, one of India's largest pharma companies (incorporated 1973, listed on BSE/NSE), which he built with his elder brother Samprada Singh. Samprada, the Chairman Emeritus, has died; Basudeo is now Executive Chairman, and the next generation (e.g. MD Sandeep Singh) sits on the board.
interesting_fact: Alkem's own founders' story compares the two brothers' partnership to the Ramayana: 'a tale of two determined brothers' from Bihar who built a company now employing over 23,000 people.
deep_cut_fact: After the Jehanabad district school in Bihar and a degree from Patna University, he had started work as a professor when his brother called him into the business. In the early years he personally delivered stock to stockists and distributors.
current_role: Executive Chairman, Alkem Laboratories Ltd (Mumbai)
public_contact: office_email: contact@alkem.com (company head office) | ir_email: investors@alkem.com | contact_form: https://www.alkemlabs.com/contact-us/key-contacts | official_website: https://www.alkemlabs.com/media-room/corporate-press-kit (press kit)
research_notes: Listed as Executive Chairman on Alkem's board page (checked Nov 2026). Low media profile. Corporate head-office and IR channels are the published routes.

name: Pritviraj Jindal
profile: Prithavi Raj (P.R.) Jindal is the eldest son of O.P. Jindal, founder of the O.P. Jindal Group. When the group was split among the four brothers, he took Jindal SAW, a leading maker of submerged-arc-welded line pipe for oil, gas and water, and the family cross-holdings give him stakes in JSW Steel and other group companies. His daughters Sminu Jindal (MD) and Shraddha (Joint MD) now help run Jindal SAW.
interesting_fact: Jindal SAW credits him with introducing SAW (submerged-arc-welded) pipe manufacturing in India more than four decades ago, helping make India one of the world's leading line-pipe makers.
deep_cut_fact: Besides steel pipes, he is listed as a director of Sonabheel Tea Limited, a tea company, among his other board seats.
current_role: Chairperson (Non-Executive), Jindal SAW Ltd. (O.P. Jindal Group)
research_notes: Company spells his name 'Prithavi Raj Jindal' (also P.R. Jindal). Listed under UAE by Hurun. Low personal media profile; route through Jindal SAW corporate office (New Delhi). Pipe and energy-infrastructure angle (oil and gas, water) fits the podcast.

name: Patrice Pichet
profile: Bordeaux-born (1959) property developer who started as a salesman for home-builder Maisons Phénix in 1983. He did his first property deal on a Bordeaux plot in 1988 and founded his own developer, Eurobat. Renamed Groupe Pichet in 2004, the family company now develops housing and commercial property across France, especially Île-de-France, and employs about 1,250-1,400 people.
interesting_fact: Groupe Pichet bought Château Les Carmes Haut-Brion (Pessac-Léognan) in 2010; it is the only Bordeaux château with an address inside the city of Bordeaux.
deep_cut_fact: He commissioned Philippe Starck (with architect Luc Arsène-Henry) to design a ship-shaped winery at Les Carmes Haut-Brion. Inaugurated in 2016 at a cost of about €10m, it was the first wine cellar of Starck's career.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO (PDG), Groupe Pichet (Pessac, Gironde)
research_notes: French-language outreach is advisable. The Groupe Pichet press office is the best route; the wine estate (les-carmes-haut-brion.com) is a softer conversational hook.

name: Bhushan Dua
profile: Bhushan Kumar Dua (b. 1977, Delhi), son of T-Series founder Gulshan Kumar, took charge of the music label as a teenager in 1997 with his uncle Krishan Kumar. He built T-Series into India's largest music label and a major Bollywood producer (Aashiqui 2, Hindi Medium, Animal, Bhool Bhulaiyaa franchise), and its YouTube channel became one of the world's most-subscribed.
interesting_fact: He is credited as producer on 100+ films since Tum Bin (2001); T-Series' Hindi Medium won him the Filmfare Award for Best Film.
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, T-Series (Super Cassettes Industries Pvt Ltd), Mumbai/Noida
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.tseries.com/contact-us | x: https://twitter.com/TSeries (company) | instagram: https://instagram.com/tseries.official (company)
research_notes: Listed as Bhushan Dua; publicly known as Bhushan Kumar. T-Series site says to contact exclusively via its contact page. Avoid father's 1997 murder and past allegations/tax probe. No sourced deep-cut fact found beyond widely known film credits.

name: Anand Suresh Deshpande
name_chinese: 阿南德·苏雷什·德什潘德
profile: Anand Deshpande (IIT Kharagpur B.Tech; Indiana University PhD, 1989) founded Persistent Systems in Pune in 1990 with about Rs 2 lakh of own and borrowed money and built it into a listed global software/AI engineering firm (Q2 FY27 revenue $487.6M; 2026 takeover offer for Nagarro). Through the family's deAsra Foundation he supports small 'nano-entrepreneurs'.
interesting_fact: deAsra Foundation, named from his family's initials, has supported more than 750,000 nano-entrepreneurs with free help on registrations, finance and business setup.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Persistent he worked as a Member of Technical Staff at Hewlett-Packard Laboratories in Palo Alto (1989-1990), after a database-systems PhD at Indiana University, which later gave him its School of Informatics Career Achievement Award.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Persistent Systems (Pune); stepped back from CEO role in 2019
research_notes: Accessible, entrepreneurship-focused founder who speaks often at Indian tech/startup events; strong fit for an entrepreneurship podcast. deAsra (deasra.in) is another route.

name: Devi Prasad Shetty
education: Mangalore University; Manipal Academy of Higher Education; St. Aloysius University
profile: Cardiac surgeon from Karnataka, trained at Kasturba Medical College and Guy's Hospital, London. He founded Narayana Hrudayalaya in Bengaluru in 2001 and grew it into a listed hospital chain, including a facility in the Cayman Islands, built on assembly-line economies of scale. That model has pushed bypass surgery prices to a fraction of US costs, and his family holds a majority stake.
interesting_fact: The Wall Street Journal called him 'the Henry Ford of heart surgery'. His hospitals save money with tricks like cross-ventilation instead of air-conditioning, and their surgeons do 30-35 operations a day.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up the eighth of nine children in Kinnigoli village and chose heart surgery as a schoolboy after hearing of Christiaan Barnard's first heart transplant. In 1992 in Kolkata he performed India's first neonatal heart surgery, on a 21-day-old baby. He also co-designed Yeshasvini, Karnataka's low-cost farmers' health insurance scheme.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Narayana Health (Narayana Hrudayalaya Ltd), Bengaluru
research_notes: Padma Shri (2004) and Padma Bhushan (2012). He speaks often about healthcare economics and frugal innovation, which suits an entrepreneurship podcast. No dedicated press email was found; investor relations is the best published route.

name: Hilmi Panigoro
profile: Bandung-born geologist and younger brother of Medco founder Arifin Panigoro. Joined Medco as a director in 1998 and has run or overseen it since (President Director 2001-08 and again from 2015). MedcoEnergi spans oil & gas across Southeast Asia, power (incl. geothermal/solar) and a stake in copper-gold miner Amman Mineral.
interesting_fact: Holds an ITB geological engineering degree (1981), Thunderbird MBA core program (1984) and an MSc from the Colorado School of Mines (1988); he has over four decades in oil and gas and leads a company that has set net-zero targets.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1981 as a wellsite geologist at Huffco/Vico Indonesia, rising to VP & Director of Business Process Reengineering before his brother invited him to join Medco as a director in 1998.
current_role: President Director, PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MedcoEnergi), Jakarta
research_notes: Regular speaker at energy conferences (SPE, Singapore International Energy Week) and has given interviews on energy transition, so reachable via MedcoEnergi corporate communications/IR.

name: Mary Vy Ty
profile: Mary Vy Ty is the widow of Metrobank founder George S.K. Ty (d. 2018) and the matriarch of the Ty family. The family controls GT Capital, the Philippine conglomerate behind Metrobank, Toyota Motor Philippines, Federal Land and stakes in Metro Pacific and AXA Philippines. She was GT Capital's Treasurer from its 2007 incorporation and became a Board Adviser in 2014.
interesting_fact: GT Capital, which takes its name from George Ty, combines Metrobank with the Philippine Toyota franchise. It is one of the country's largest listed conglomerates, with interests in banking, cars, property, infrastructure and insurance.
deep_cut_fact: She has more than 50 years of experience in banking and general business, is a University of Santo Tomas graduate, and served as GT Capital's first Treasurer from its incorporation in 2007.
current_role: Adviser to the Board, GT Capital Holdings and Metrobank; Honorary Chairman, GT Foundation; Trustee, Metrobank Foundation
public_contact: ir_email: ir@gtcapital.com.ph | office_email: gtcap@gtcapital.com.ph | official_website: https://www.gtcapital.com.ph/
research_notes: Elderly (her GT Capital bio gives her age as 85) and private, with an advisory rather than executive role. For a business conversation, GT Capital/Metrobank management are the active leaders. The corporate inbox is the realistic route.

name: Maximilian Rudolph von Finck
profile: Middle son (b. c.1969) of the late Bavarian banker-investor August von Finck Jr. (d. Nov 2021), whose fortune included a large SGS (testing/inspection) stake, mostly sold in 2020 ahead of an equal four-way inheritance. Naturalised Swiss (canton Schwyz); Bilanz reports he is mainly active as an entrepreneur in the USA, e.g. in the seed business.
interesting_fact: The family sold SGS shares worth about CHF 2.3bn in 2020, reportedly to split a holding too big to divide equally among August von Finck Jr.'s four children.
current_role: Heir/investor in the von Finck family fortune; board member of family holding Clair (per Bilanz)
research_notes: Extremely private; almost no public profile and no published contact. Identity matched to the von Finck SGS fortune via Bilanz, but his own business activities are not documented. Hurun listing likely reflects inherited share of the family fortune. Not a realistic podcast target.

name: Diane Goldman
profile: Diane Goldman Kemper (b. 1946) is a daughter of New York real-estate investor Sol Goldman (d. 1987) and one of four siblings who co-own Solil Management. Solil holds roughly 400 mostly Manhattan properties, including the land under Olympic Tower and the Cartier Building and part of the land under the World Trade Center. Her sister Jane runs day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: Solil's portfolio includes the land under Olympic Tower and the Cartier Building, The Peninsula New York hotel, and about 17% of the land under the World Trade Center complex.
deep_cut_fact: She studied at C.W. Post College and the New York School of Interior Design, and once worked in the family company's residential leasing department. Columbia University has a 'Diane Goldman Kemper Family Professor of Epidemiology in Psychiatry' chair.
current_role: Co-owner, Solil Management (Goldman family real estate, New York); philanthropist
research_notes: Known publicly as Diane Goldman Kemper. The family is famously private (Forbes: 'doesn't want you to know who they are'), and there is ongoing family litigation over Solil, so avoid that topic. She has no published personal or office contact. The only published family entity address is the Lillian Goldman Charitable Trust (postal). Low relevance to an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Jami Gertz
profile: Jami Gertz is the actress known for The Lost Boys, Less than Zero, Twister and the CBS sitcom Still Standing. Her listed fortune is shared with her husband Tony Ressler, co-founder of Ares Management. Their group bought majority control of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks in 2015 for about $730M, and the couple give through the Ressler-Gertz Foundation to education, Los Angeles and Jewish causes.
interesting_fact: She was discovered by Norman Lear in a nationwide talent search and reportedly turned down the role of Rachel Green on Friends during pre-production.
deep_cut_fact: Between acting jobs she worked in Paris as a scent designer for the fashion house Lanvin. She grew up in Glenview, Illinois, and graduated from Maine East High School.
current_role: Co-owner, Atlanta Hawks (with husband Tony Ressler); actress; philanthropist (Ressler-Gertz Foundation)
research_notes: Private; rarely appears in public. Wealth is through Tony Ressler (Ares Management), who is the better entrepreneurship or podcast angle. No personal or foundation contact was published; the Atlanta Hawks communications office is the institutional route. Gertz is also a Melanoma Research Alliance board member.

name: Ratan Jindal
profile: Son of O.P. Jindal, founder of the O.P. Jindal Group; brother of Sajjan (JSW), Prithviraj and Naveen Jindal. Ratan heads Jindal Stainless, India's largest stainless-steel producer and a major exporter, and in 2006 set up the group's Dubai (Jindal Stainless FZE) and London arms, which fits Hurun listing him under the UAE.
interesting_fact: He pitches Jindal Stainless as a front-runner in circular, scrap-based stainless production, writing that 'the world is quickly transitioning towards circularity in production processes' and committing to power growth with renewables.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he was put in charge of the group's global foray, heading newly formed subsidiaries in Dubai (Jindal Stainless FZE) and London as their CEO.
current_role: Chairman (and managing director), Jindal Stainless Ltd
public_contact: press_email: sonal.singh@jindalstainless.com (Jindal Stainless media contact; others listed on same page) | ir_email: investorcare@jindalstainless.com | office_email: info@jindalstainless.com
research_notes: Identity 'uncertain' only because Hurun tags his wealth as 'JSW Steel' (brother Sajjan's company) - he is the O.P. Jindal son who chairs Jindal Stainless; the family holdings are intertwined. Green/circular steel and renewable power are good podcast hooks.

name: Lachman Das Mittal
profile: Lachhman (Lakshman) Das Mittal, born 1931 in Hoshiarpur, spent decades at LIC (agent from 1955, retired as deputy zonal manager) before building Sonalika: threshers from 1970, then Sonalika tractors (International Tractors Ltd) from 1995-96, now one of India's largest tractor makers and a big exporter. Sons Amrit Sagar and Deepak Mittal run the business; he is often called India's oldest billionaire.
interesting_fact: He launched his tractor business around age 60 after retiring from LIC, making him one of the world's most striking late-start founders.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an M.A. in English and Urdu from Panjab University, and once quipped: 'Once I applied for dealership of Maruti Udyog but was rejected. Today, I give out dealerships.'
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus/Chairman, Sonalika Group (International Tractors Ltd), Hoshiarpur, Punjab
research_notes: Aged ~95; operational leadership is with sons Amrit Sagar Mittal (Vice Chairman) and Deepak Mittal (MD). For a podcast, the sons may be the realistic guests; Sonalika has a media room with interviews.

name: Gerard Déprez
profile: French executive who took over equipment-rental firm SAM in Brittany in 1986 and built it into Loxam, Europe's No.1 and the world's 4th-largest equipment rental company (~1,120 branches in 30 countries, ~€2.6bn revenue in 2024) through acquisitions such as Lavendon, Cramo Denmark and Finland's Ramirent (2019). He remains chairman, with Stéphane Hénon as managing director.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Loxam grew from a 1967 regional Breton rental outfit into a supplier of equipment for the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games.
deep_cut_fact: Before Loxam he was VP of finance at cement maker Ciments d'Origny (Holderbank group) from 1978-83 and a regional director at building-materials firm SOCIMAT; he is an EM Lyon graduate with law and accounting degrees, and chaired the European Rental Association 2005-2013.
current_role: Chairman (Président) and CEO, Loxam Group
research_notes: Low-profile; rarely gives interviews beyond trade press (KHL, Rental Management). Loxam press releases also route media via FTI Consulting (loxam@fticonsulting.com per search snippets; not verified on a current release). Possible angle: equipment rental for energy/data-center construction and Loxam's carbon trajectory.

name: David C Paul
profile: Mechanical engineer who left Synthes, where he was Director of Product Development, to found spine and musculoskeletal device maker Globus Medical in 2003. He was CEO until 2017, then executive chairman; he remains the largest stockholder after Globus' 2023 merger with NuVasive, and Keith Pfeil has been CEO since July 2025.
interesting_fact: He is named as an inventor on more than 300 patents and published patent applications.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he was a research engineer in biomaterials at Temple University. He earned a mechanical engineering degree from the University of Madras in India and a master's in computer-integrated mechanical engineering systems from Temple.
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Globus Medical (NYSE: GMED)
public_contact: ir_email: investors@globusmedical.com (Brian Kearns, SVP Corporate Development & IR) | official_website: https://www.globusmedical.com
research_notes: Engineer-founder; low media profile. Also sits on boards of Free Flow Medical and Cross Ventures LLC (real estate). Company IR is the published route.

name: Siew Khim Ng
profile: Hurun Global Rich List (2023-2026) attributes about $3B to Siew Khim Ng via Indoritel Makmur Internasional (IDX: DNET), the listed parent of the Indomaret convenience-store chain and a holder of FiberStar. I found no public source that names her role or shareholding. DNET's disclosed major holders are Hannawell Group Ltd (~39%), Anthoni Salim (~25%) and PT Megah Eraraharja (~20%).
interesting_fact: Indomaret, which Indoritel controls, runs more than 21,900 convenience stores across 32 Indonesian provinces.
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun as a billionaire whose wealth derives from Indoritel (Indonesia)
research_notes: Identity unresolved: the only web profiles named 'Siew Khim Ng' are unrelated executives at Malaysia's U Mobile and Singapore's Keong Hong. She may be the beneficial owner behind the offshore holder Hannawell Group, but that is unverified. Very private. If you approach her, go through Indoritel corporate secretary/IR.

name: Dana Azrieli
profile: Montreal-born (1967) daughter of developer David Azrieli, educated at Swarthmore (BA) and Vermont Law School (JD). She took over Azrieli Group, Israel's largest listed real estate company (Azrieli Center towers, malls, offices, hotels, rentals), in 2014. She pushed it into data centers, buying Norway's Green Mountain in 2021 for about NIS 2.8bn, and became permanent CEO in 2026.
interesting_fact: Under her, Azrieli bought Green Mountain, whose flagship Stavanger data center is built inside a mountain in a former NATO ammunition store. She called data centers 'a significant new category of income-producing real estate.'
deep_cut_fact: In 2001 she produced 'One Step Ahead,' her father David Azrieli's memoirs of 1939–1950, published by Yad Vashem. In 2004 she founded the Azrieli Empowerment Program for at-risk middle-schoolers, run with Darca Schools.

name: Timm Oberwelland
profile: Oberwelland's great-grandfather, August Storck founded the business in the Westphalia town of Werther in 1903. At the time, sweets typically were sold unpackaged and without branding. He packaged his individually and gave them snappy names.
interesting_fact: Today, Storck employs over 7,000 people, sells products in more than 100 countries and generates almost $3 billion in estimated annual revenue.
deep_cut_fact: His brother, Axel, became the fourth generation of his family to lead the company after his father, Klaus, retired on Storck's 100th anniversary in 2003.

name: Madeleine Grogg
profile: Madeleine Grogg is the widow of Peter Grogg, founder of Swiss biochemical company Bachem Holding AG. Peter Grogg, who died in 2025, started the business in 1971 and served as CEO until 2002, and chairman until 2012.
interesting_fact: In 1971, Grogg started Bachem with 50,000 Swiss Francs.
deep_cut_fact: The family controls about 58% of Bachem as well as shares in Swiss electrical engineering company Burkhalter Holding and chemical maker Dottikon.

name: Dmitry Mazepin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
education: Moscow Institute of International Relations (Bachelor of Arts/Science)
profile: Minsk-born Mazepin worked in banking and insurance in the 1990s and ran oil and coal companies. He was First Deputy Chairman of the Russian Federal Property Fund in 2002. He then built Uralchem, one of the world's largest nitrogen and potash fertilizer producers, starting with a 2004 privatization purchase. After EU/UK sanctions in 2022 he stepped down as CEO and sold a 52% controlling stake.
interesting_fact: From 2022 to 2024 Uralchem made several humanitarian shipments of fertilizer to African countries.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from the Minsk Suvorov Military School in 1985, Mazepin served as a military interpreter in Afghanistan from 1986 to 1988. He later graduated in economics from MGIMO (1992) and earned a PhD in 2012 with a thesis on managing the stock-market potential of an oil producer.
current_role: Former owner/CEO and remaining minority shareholder of Uralchem; President of the Aquatics Federation of Russia (since 2024)
research_notes: Under EU and UK sanctions since March 2022; check legal and compliance implications before any engagement. He sold control of Uralchem in 2022 (TASS: https://tass.ru/ekonomika/14033745), so the current stake should be verified. The Uralchem general inbox is the only published route.

name: Prem Kumar Arora
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2019)
profile: Prem Kumar (PK) Arora co-founded New Delhi-based Mankind Pharma with his brothers-in-law Ramesh and Rajeev Juneja. The company was incorporated in 1991 and began operations in 1995. It grew into India's fourth-largest drugmaker by domestic sales, selling affordable generics and consumer brands, and listed on NSE/BSE in May 2023. Arora oversees finance, HR and operations.
interesting_fact: Mankind entered consumer healthcare by launching the Manforce and Prega News brands, now household names in India, alongside its generics business.
deep_cut_fact: The company went public in India in May 2023, raising 43.3 billion rupees ($529 million).
current_role: Co-founder and Director - FHA (finance, HR and administration), Mankind Pharma Ltd.
public_contact: ir_email: investors@mankindpharma.com | office_email: contact@mankindpharma.com (general corporate) | official_website: https://www.mankindpharma.com/company/management/

name: F.C. Tseng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
education: National Cheng Kung University (Ph.D)
profile: Fan-Cheng Tseng is one of Morris Chang's longest-serving lieutenants: TSMC president 1998-2001, deputy CEO 2001-05 and vice chairman 2005-18. While Chang chased customers, Tseng consolidated TSMC internally. His TSMC shares made him a billionaire in 2024 amid the AI chip boom; he remains on the board and chairs TSMC China.
interesting_fact: Tseng has sat on TSMC's board since May 1997 and was its president from 1998 to 2001, before becoming vice chairman for 13 years (2005-2018).
deep_cut_fact: In 1976 ITRI sent him, with Shih Chin-tai and Robert Tsao, to RCA in the US for CMOS IC training: part of the first group of Taiwanese engineers to acquire integrated-circuit technology, seen as the spark of Taiwan's chip industry.
current_role: Director, TSMC (board member since 1997); Chairman, TSMC China and TSMC Education & Culture Foundation; Vice Chairman, Vanguard International Semiconductor
research_notes: Low public profile; appears at events in his role as chairman of the TSMC Education and Culture Foundation. TSMC corporate PR (press@tsmc.com) is the official route.

name: Tom Ford
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
education: New York University (Drop Out); Parsons School of Design (Bachelor of Architecture)
profile: Texas-born designer who revived Gucci as creative director (1994-2004) and founded Tom Ford International in 2005. He sold the brand and its beauty business to Estée Lauder for $2.8bn in 2022 and stepped back fully at the end of 2023. He is now focused on film: after A Single Man and Nocturnal Animals, he is directing an adaptation of Anne Rice's Cry to Heaven, which began shooting in January 2026.
interesting_fact: He trained in interior architecture at Parsons rather than fashion. His Santa Fe ranch, Cerro Pelon, was designed by Japanese architect Tadao Ando.
deep_cut_fact: To land his first fashion job, he phoned designer Cathy Hardwick every day for a month. Asked his favourite European designers, he said 'Armani and Chanel', later admitting it was because she was wearing Armani. He worked as her design assistant for two years.
current_role: Film director, writer and producer (Fade to Black); founder of Tom Ford International (sold to Estée Lauder, 2022)
research_notes: No personal channels found; the Tom Ford brand accounts are now owned by Estée Lauder, not by him. The most realistic route is via his film company Fade to Black or his film publicists around the Cry to Heaven release. He is a weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Lirio Parisotto
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
profile: Born in Nova Bassano, Rio Grande do Sul, and trained as a physician (Universidade de Caxias do Sul), Parisotto founded Videolar, a pioneer in Brazilian videocassette manufacturing, and reinvested its profits in dividend-paying Brazilian stocks (banks, power, mining, steel). Videolar later merged with Innova to make petrochemical products; he stepped back from day-to-day management in 2007.
interesting_fact: He has 11 siblings, holds a medical degree and also spent time in a monastery before turning to business.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Videolar reportedly came after he saw a videocassette in a New York store; and as a young man in 1971 he won a monograph contest run by Brazil's Army Ministry, putting the prize (worth about a VW Beetle) into his first stock-market investment.
current_role: Founder and chairman, Videolar-Innova (petrochemicals/plastics, Manaus); private equity investor
research_notes: Sources differ on Videolar's founding year (1980 vs 1988). Sits on the board of Fundacao Amazonas Sustentavel (per MarketScreener). Low media profile; route via Videolar-Innova.

name: Thomas Kwok
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2015)
education: Imperial College London (Bachelor of Engineering); London Business School (Master of Business Administration)
profile: Thomas Kwok Ping-kwong is the second son of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng and, with brothers Raymond and Walter, inherited one of Hong Kong's largest developers in 1990. He was SHKP joint chairman until 2014; since 2020 he has been a senior director of the group's real estate agency arm, while his son Adam serves as an SHKP executive director.
interesting_fact: He and brother Raymond, both devout Christians, built the Noah's Ark theme park on Ma Wan island, Hong Kong, reflecting their evangelical faith.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a civil engineer (BSc, Imperial College London; MBA, London Business School), and in the 1990s set up a church in the 75th-floor pyramid atrium atop SHKP's Central Plaza tower.
current_role: Senior Director, Sun Hung Kai Real Estate Agency (subsidiary of Sun Hung Kai Properties), since 2020
research_notes: Sensitive history (2014 bribery conviction, released 2019); avoid in outreach. Approach via SHKP corporate communications. SHKP also runs data-centre business (SUNeVision/iAdvantage), a possible podcast angle.

name: Alexander Frolov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
education: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology (Ph.D)
profile: A physicist (MIPT PhD) who left Moscow's Kurchatov Institute in 1994 to go into business. With partner Alexander Abramov he built the Evraz steel and coking-coal group, sold 40% of it to Roman Abramovich in 2006 for more than $3B, and was CEO from 2007 to 2021. He left the Evraz board in March 2022 and was sanctioned by the UK in November 2022. He also holds stakes in Norilsk Nickel, Yandex and Ivi.
interesting_fact: He started out as a research fellow at the I.V. Kurchatov Institute of Atomic Energy after earning a doctorate in physics and mathematics, an unusual path into steel and coal.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated with honours from the Department of Molecular and Chemical Physics at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology (1987). He was also one of the sponsors of the restoration of the Valaam Spaso-Preobrazhensky Monastery on Lake Ladoga.
current_role: Investor; former CEO of Evraz (2007-2021) and still a major shareholder (~10%); no current executive role found
research_notes: Under UK sanctions since November 2022 (Russia-related); check legal and reputational exposure before any outreach. Very private, with no published personal or office contacts found. The Valaam fact comes from Forbes facts (https://www.forbes.com/profile/alexander-frolov/).

name: K.C. Liu
education: National Chiao Tung University (Bachelor of Engineering)
profile: Co-founded Advantech in 1983 at 29 with two HP Taiwan colleagues and built it into the world's largest industrial PC maker (about 41% share), now pushing edge-AI and IoT platforms. In 2026 he announced succession: from 2027 he will focus on governance, long-term development and new business investments.
interesting_fact: An avid reader of management books, he shares titles such as Built to Last and Blue Ocean Strategy with Advantech staff.
deep_cut_fact: Before Advantech he was an R&D engineer and then a sales engineer in HP Taiwan's Instrument Department; in 2026 he noted he had spent 42 years building the company since co-founding it at 29.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Advantech (TWSE: 2395); becomes full-time Chairman on Jan 1, 2027 when Miller Chang takes over as CEO
public_contact: press_email: corp.pr@advantech.com (Media and Public Relations) | ir_email: IR.Advantech@advantech.com | official_website: https://www.advantech.com/

name: Hans Georg Naeder
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
profile: Hans Georg Näder (b. 1961, Duderstadt) is the third-generation head of Ottobock, the prosthetics and orthotics maker founded by his grandfather Otto Bock in 1919. He took over from his father in 1990 at age 28 and built it into a world leader with over 10,000 staff and 60 country branches. Ottobock listed in Frankfurt in October 2025; his family holding keeps roughly 80% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Ottobock has given on-site technical repair service at every Paralympic Games since Seoul 1988, became the IPC's first Worldwide Partner in 2005, and is signed on through Brisbane 2032.
deep_cut_fact: He has been an honorary professor at PFH Göttingen since 2005 and pushed for its new 'Orthobionik' (orthobionics) degree course. He has also been a guest professor at Capital Medical University in Beijing since 2009.
current_role: Chairman of the Board (Verwaltungsrat) / Chairman of the Management Board, Ottobock SE & Co. KGaA; majority owner via Näder Holding
public_contact: press_email: Merle.florstedt@ottobock.de | ir_email: Julia.Hartmann@ottobock.de | official_website: https://corporate.ottobock.com
research_notes: Press contact is Merle Florstedt, Head of Corporate Communications, as named in Ottobock press releases. Avoid the pending VAT investigation over yacht purchases and the May 2026 short-seller report. He is a keen sailor (yacht Pink Gin won the 2007 Millennium Cup per Forbes), but no independent source was confirmed for that.

name: Hussain Binghatti Aljbori
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
profile: Emirati entrepreneur who founded Binghatti in Dubai in 2008, starting as a contractor before becoming a vertically integrated developer of distinctive residential towers. He owns 100% of the firm, which has launched branded towers with Mercedes-Benz, Bugatti and Jacob & Co and raised $500M in sukuk in 2024; day-to-day leadership has passed to his son Muhammad.
interesting_fact: Binghatti built the Bugatti- and Mercedes-Benz-branded residential towers in Dubai, among the first car-brand residences in the region, and became one of the UAE's biggest developers by launches.
deep_cut_fact: He named the company after his late father, Ghatti Bin Ghaeb, and holds a PhD in Industrial Technology and an MSc from the Cranfield Institute of Technology in the UK.
current_role: Founder, Binghatti (Dubai real estate developer); son Muhammad Binghatti now chairs the company
research_notes: Founder keeps a low profile; son Muhammad Binghatti is the public face and gives frequent interviews - likely the better route. Uses title 'Dr.' Name spellings vary (BinGhatti, Aljbouri).

name: Robert Friedland
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)

profile: Chicago-born, Singapore-based mining financier Robert Friedland built a fortune finding giant deposits: Voisey's Bay nickel (Canada), Oyu Tolgoi (Mongolia) and now the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC (JV with Zijin), whose on-site smelter began producing copper anodes in January 2026. He also chairs Ivanhoe Electric (US copper exploration, Typhoon geophysics tech) and backs Ivanhoe Atlantic iron ore in Guinea/Liberia.
interesting_fact: He is an outspoken voice on electrification: he argues that the world's energy transition and AI/data-center build-out require vastly more copper than is being mined.
deep_cut_fact: At Reed College (political science, class of 1974) he was student body president, and he managed his uncle's apple orchard near McMinnville, Oregon (the 'All-One Farm') where his friend Steve Jobs tended trees, an experience credited with inspiring the name Apple.
current_role: Founder and Executive Co-Chairman, Ivanhoe Mines; Executive Chairman, Ivanhoe Electric (NYSE American: IE)
public_contact: press_email: Tanyat@ivanhoemines.com (Tanya Todd, Manager, Corporate Communications) | ir_email: Tommyh@ivanhoemines.com (Tommy Horton, VP Investor Relations) | office_email: info@ivanhoemines.com
research_notes: Excellent podcast fit (copper for electrification and data centers) and a famously talkative conference speaker. Interesting_fact is a paraphrase of his frequent public theme; verify a specific quote before using. Avoid Summitville/Jobs-era counterculture anecdotes.

education: The University of Glasgow (Masters in Finance)
profile: Daughter of billionaire Murali Divi, founder of Divi's Laboratories, one of the world's largest makers of active pharmaceutical ingredients and a custom-synthesis partner to big pharma; she holds a minority stake. On the board as Director - Commercial, she oversees sourcing and procurement, capital projects, corporate finance and investor relations.
interesting_fact: Divi's Laboratories is among the world's top suppliers of active pharmaceutical ingredients and also does custom manufacturing for global pharma companies.
deep_cut_fact: She joined Divi's in July 2012 after building experience in material-requirement planning and procurement, and holds two master's degrees: international business from the Gitam Institute of Foreign Trade and international finance from the University of Glasgow.
current_role: Whole-Time Director (Commercial), Divi's Laboratories Ltd, Hyderabad
public_contact: office_email: info@divislabs.com | ir_email: cs@divislabs.com (company secretary / shareholder contact)
