name: Bret Taylor
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
education: Stanford University
profile: Stanford-trained engineer who led the team that co-created Google Maps, co-founded FriendFeed (sold to Facebook, where he became CTO), built Quip (sold to Salesforce, where he rose to co-CEO) and chaired Twitter's board through the Musk sale. Co-founded Sierra with Clay Bavor in 2023; a roughly 25% stake at a $10B valuation made him a billionaire, and he has chaired OpenAI since Nov 2023.
interesting_fact: Facebook's 'Like' button came from FriendFeed, the startup Taylor co-founded and sold to Facebook in 2009; in Dec 2025 he bought a ~1% minority stake in the San Francisco 49ers.
deep_cut_fact: Recounting Google's pre-Maps local search, Taylor noted that a search for 'coffee near Menlo Park' returned only Sun Microsystems pages, because Sun's Java-themed site was full of coffee puns. His follow-up, Google Local, was a formative near-miss that led to Google Maps.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Sierra (AI customer-service agents); Chairman of the board, OpenAI

name: Clay Bavor
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
profile: Clay Bavor cofounded Sierra with Bret Taylor in 2023 after 18 years at Google, where he rose from associate product manager to VP running Google Labs and its AR/VR work (Cardboard, Daydream, ARCore, Lens, Project Starline). Sierra builds AI agents for customer service; a $350M round led by Greenoaks valued it at $10B.
interesting_fact: He and Bret Taylor were both hired into Google's associate product manager program by Marissa Mayer and stayed friends for ~20 years (incl. a 'monthly' poker game that met about twice a year) before founding Sierra.
deep_cut_fact: Sierra was hatched over a long lunch in December 2022, a week after ChatGPT launched. Though known as Google's 'AR/VR guy', Bavor says he had become obsessed with language models in Google Labs, the group that produced NotebookLM.
current_role: Cofounder, Sierra (AI customer-service agents), San Francisco
public_contact: x: https://x.com/claybavor | official_website: https://sierra.ai (company) | x: https://x.com/sierraplatform (company account)

name: Zhang Xin
education: University of Cambridge; University of Sussex; Wolfson College
profile: Born in Beijing in 1965, she worked in Hong Kong factories as a teen, studied at Sussex and Cambridge, then worked at Barings and Goldman Sachs. In 1995 she co-founded SOHO China with husband Pan Shiyi. Now US-based, she invests in Manhattan trophy buildings and, since 2021, film via Closer Media.
interesting_fact: She won a special prize at the 2002 Venice Architecture Biennale as a patron for Commune by the Great Wall, a collection of villas by 12 Asian architects. In 2026 she was invited into the Executives Branch of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
deep_cut_fact: To pay her way in England as a student she worked in a traditional fish-and-chip shop run by a Chinese couple. Years later she made a cameo as a Chinese investor in Oliver Stone's 'Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps' (2010).
current_role: Founder, Closer Media (film production/finance); CEO, Closer Properties / Closer Group family office (New York); co-founder of SOHO China (resigned 2022)
research_notes: Shares her fortune with her husband Pan Shiyi. She is a frequent speaker (WEF, Aspen trustee, MoMA trustee) and fairly media-friendly; film, architecture and US real estate are good hooks. No published email was found. My web-search budget ran out at this point, so contacts beyond her company sites were not checked.

name: Brenninkmeyer family
profile: Dutch-German family that founded fashion retailer C&A in 1841 in Sneek, the Netherlands. Its 100% family-owned holding Cofra has become a diversified investment group with about EUR 40 billion under management across private equity (Bregal), real estate (Redevco), asset management (Anthos), retail and clean energy, now moving from the fifth to the sixth generation.
interesting_fact: Cofra is moving leadership from the fifth to the sixth generation: CFO Florian Brenninkmeyer becomes board chair in April 2027, succeeding Martijn Brenninkmeijer (CEO from 2015, chair from 2018).
deep_cut_fact: The name C&A comes from the founding brothers' initials, Clemens and August Brenninkmeijer, who started as textile traders and opened the business in Sneek, Friesland.
current_role: Owners of Cofra Holding AG (Zug), parent of C&A, Bregal Investments, Redevco and Anthos; chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, to be succeeded by Florian Brenninkmeyer in April 2027
research_notes: Famously secretive family (owner circle of several dozen members). Cofra site blocked automated access, so no verified press email captured; check cofraholding.com manually. Clean-energy activities under Cofra are a possible podcast angle.

name: Joseph Lewis
profile: Assumed to be Joe Lewis (b. 1937), the East London-born currency trader and investor behind Tavistock Group, which holds 200+ companies in 15 countries (real estate such as Lake Nona and Albany, restaurants, life sciences, golf). He controlled Tottenham Hotspur via ENIC from 2001 until handing control to a family trust in 2022; lives in the Bahamas.
interesting_fact: He made a fortune betting on sterling's exit from the ERM on Black Wednesday in 1992, and owns several versions of Arturo Di Modica's 'Charging Bull', possibly including the original installed guerrilla-style on Wall Street in 1989.
deep_cut_fact: Born above a pub on Roman Road in Bow, he left school at 15 to help run his father's West End catering firm, Tavistock Banqueting (the name lives on in Tavistock Group), and at his Hanover Grand club gave Planet Hollywood founder Robert Earl his first job.
current_role: Founder and principal investor, Tavistock Group (Bahamas-based private investment group)

name: Phillip Ruffin
profile: Wichita-raised Phil Ruffin built a fortune in Midwest convenience stores, then hotels, oil distribution and hand-truck manufacturing before moving into casinos. He bought the New Frontier (and ended a record strike), sold the site for about $1.2bn in 2007, then bought Treasure Island from MGM in 2009 (~$775m) and Circus Circus in 2019-20 ($825m). Forbes ranked him No. 972 in 2026 at about $4.3bn.
interesting_fact: In 1972 he pioneered self-serve gasoline in Kansas, building a chain of about 60 Midwest convenience stores whose cash funded his first hotel, a Wichita Marriott, in 1987.
deep_cut_fact: He was a state wrestling champion at Wichita North High School (class of 1953). One profile recalls that his father, who never went to a match, asked whether he was the one the newspaper was talking about. His family's surname was originally 'Rufan'.
current_role: Owner, Treasure Island (TI) and Circus Circus, Las Vegas; Ruffin Companies (Wichita)
public_contact: office_email: TI-General@treasureisland.com (Treasure Island general inbox) | contact_form: https://treasureisland.com/press-media | x: https://twitter.com/TIvegas (property account)
research_notes: Aged about 90-91. Long-time Trump friend. Recent profile: https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/for-phil-ruffin-timing-is-everything. Has floated selling Circus Circus at ~$5bn (Forbes, Jan 2025). No dedicated press email found.

name: Carolus Nolet, Sr.
profile: Carolus Nolet Sr. (b. 1941) joined his family's 1691-founded Schiedam distillery in 1962 and took it over in 1979. After touring US bars from 1983 he created Ketel One, a pot-distilled premium vodka, landing its first US case sale in 1989; in 2009 Diageo bought 50% of Ketel One for $900m. He later launched NOLET'S gin and remains chairman, with sons Carl Jr. and Bob running the business.
interesting_fact: Ketel One is named after Distilleerketel #1, the coal-fired copper pot still at the Nolet distillery, a method normally used for jenever and whisky rather than vodka.
deep_cut_fact: Ketel One's first-ever case sale came in 1989 from Doug Biederbeck of Bix restaurant in San Francisco; Nolet's own after-dinner drink is a Vesper made with 50% Ketel One and 50% NOLET'S Silver gin, stirred over ice.
current_role: Chairman, Nolet Distillery (Schiedam, Netherlands); 10th-generation head of the family that co-owns Ketel One with Diageo
research_notes: In his mid-80s; sons Carl Jr. and Bob Nolet are the active executives and more accessible for interviews. Last on Forbes list 2015-17. Alive status assumed from lack of any obituary; not explicitly confirmed with a dated 2026 source.

profile: Sister of longtime Brose chief Michael Stoschek and co-owner of family-held Brose, the Coburg-based mechatronics auto supplier (door and seat systems, electric motors, e-bike drives) founded by Max Brose in 1908. Brose is owned 100% by the Stoschek and Volkmann family branches; she has no management role and almost no public profile.

name: Ronald Burkle
profile: Pomona-born (1952) investor who rose from bagging groceries at Stater Bros. to founding private-equity firm Yucaipa in 1986, rolling up supermarket chains (Fred Meyer, Ralphs, Food4Less, Dominick's). Yucaipa now invests across hospitality, sports, entertainment and logistics; he is executive chairman of Soho House and a co-owner/investor in pro sports teams.

name: Oleg Misevra
profile: Former USSR/Russian Internal Troops officer who became a top manager and minority partner at MDM Group and president of SUEK (2002-04). In 2004 he bought SUEK's Sakhalin assets, building East Mining Company around the Solntsevsky open-pit coal mine and Shakhtersk port, now one of Russia's fastest-growing thermal coal exporters to Asia.
interesting_fact: He was named Russia's 'Exporter of the Year' in 2019 in the All-Russian People-2019 competition, as VGK ramped Sakhalin coal exports and expanded its Shakhtersk port.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 interview he explained that VGK was then Russia's only exporter of brown (lignite) coal, so its real competitor is Indonesia rather than Australia, and that the business is fully self-contained: 'We have everything of our own: the mine, the port, the conveyor line.'
current_role: Controlling owner and chairman, East Mining Company (VGK / Vostochnaya Gornorudnaya Kompaniya), Sakhalin, Russia
public_contact: official_website: https://www.eastmining.ru/en/ (East Mining Company; was unreachable from our network when checked)
research_notes: Very low public profile; no published personal or press contacts found. Russian coal exporter: sanctions/compliance considerations for any outreach. Interviews exist only in Russian regional/business media (EastRussia, PortNews).

name: Hitesh Doshi
education: University of Mumbai (Bachelor of Commerce)
profile: Founder of the Waaree Group, which began in 1990 making thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers and moved into solar modules in 2007 with a 30 MW plant in Surat. Waaree Energies is now India's largest solar-panel maker by capacity and listed in Mumbai in October 2024 at a 70% premium. He is expanding into cells, US manufacturing and other clean-energy businesses.
interesting_fact: On listing day in October 2024, Waaree shares jumped about 56% after a $514M IPO, roughly doubling the Doshi family's fortune to about $5.2B, according to Bloomberg as reported by Fortune.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Tunki, a village in Maharashtra, Doshi moved about 600 km to attend Shri Chinai College of Commerce and Economics in Mumbai in 1985. He borrowed Rs 5,000 (about $60) from a relative to trade hardware, electronics and instrument gauges, which paid his college fees (he told the Economic Times in 2014).
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Waaree Energies Ltd (NSE: WAAREEENER); head of the Waaree Group, Mumbai
public_contact: office_email: waaree@waaree.com | x: https://x.com/waareegroup | official_website: https://www.waaree.com/
research_notes: waaree@waaree.com is the company's general/customer-service inbox, not a personal or press address; no dedicated press or IR email was confirmed (the web-search budget ran out). The X account is the company's (@waareegroup). Strong fit for an energy podcast.

profile: Fumio Sakiya founded Rorze, a manufacturer of production equipment for semiconductor and flat-panel display makers, in 1985. Sakiya was CEO of the Hiroshima Prefecture-based company until  2015 and chairman for two years after that. He's now a board member and advisor.
interesting_fact: Rorze listed on the JASDAQ bourse for startups in 2013 and is now listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
deep_cut_fact: Santa Clara-based chip-equipment giant Applied Materials is Rorze's biggest customer,  accounting for nearly one-fourth of sales.

name: David Humphreys
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
profile: Grandson of TAMKO founder E.L. Craig, David C. Humphreys took over the roofing-shingle maker in 1994 after his father J.P. Humphreys died, expanding production; TAMKO is now the fourth-largest US shingle maker (~$1.2bn revenue in 2023). The family sold a 25% stake to Carlyle in 2019 and he and his sister's families own the rest.
interesting_fact: His grandfather E.L. Craig founded TAMKO in 1944 at age 69 in an old Joplin streetcar barn, after earlier ventures including a sausage business, a soup kitchen, a boxing gym and a frozen-custard shop; TAMKO's name comes from Texas, Arkansas, Missouri, Kansas and Oklahoma.
deep_cut_fact: TAMKO has run on W. Edwards Deming's continuous-improvement principles since his father saw a June 24, 1980 TV special introducing Deming's quality methods; and for a decade TAMKO has donated its company planes and fuel for veterans' 'Hero Flights'. Humphreys is also a rare-books and history enthusiast.
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, TAMKO Building Products (Joplin/Galena area, Missouri-Kansas)
research_notes: Prominent Missouri political donor (libertarian-leaning; Forbes notes he has criticised Donald Trump) - politically sensitive, keep outreach business-focused. His mother Ethelmae Humphreys, TAMKO chairman emerita, died at 94. Media route: TAMKO communications team.

name: Sarah Humphreys Atkins
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
profile: Heiress to the TAMKO roofing fortune and only granddaughter of founder E.L. Craig. TAMKO is the fourth-largest US shingle maker, with about $1.2bn in revenue in 2023. Carlyle bought 25% in 2019, and she and her brother David (CEO) split the rest with their families. She sits on TAMKO's board with her husband Paul Atkins, chairman of the SEC, and leads the family's J.P. Humphreys Foundation.
interesting_fact: Her grandfather E.L. Craig founded TAMKO in 1944 at the age of 69, in an old streetcar barn in Joplin, Missouri.

She has served on the boards of the Foundation for Economic Education, Free to Choose Network, Atlas Network and The Future of Freedom Foundation, and now sits on the board of the Moving Picture Institute, which backs liberty-themed films.
current_role: President, J.P. Humphreys Foundation; director, TAMKO Building Products; board member, Moving Picture Institute; trustee, Capital Research Center

The TAMKO communications office is the company's media contact, not hers personally. The nonprofit boards (Capital Research Center, Moving Picture Institute) are an alternative route.

name: Colette Kress

sec_insider_companies: NVIDIA CORP (NVDA) - EVP & Chief Financial Officer

profile: Ex-wife of Cherkizovo founder Igor Babaev. He built the Moscow Cherkizovsky meat plant into Cherkizovo Group, which listed in London and Moscow in 2006, and later passed his shares to their sons. She holds about 15% alongside sons Evgeny and Sergei Mikhailov (about 28% each). The group has over 20,000 employees and about $3.4bn in 2025 revenue.

deep_cut_fact: Babaev gave all his shares to his sons, who manage the company. They own about 28% each; Lidiya owns about 15%.
current_role: Co-owner (about 15%) of Cherkizovo Group, Russia's largest meat producer; her sons Evgeny (chairman) and Sergei (CEO) run it
research_notes: Passive shareholder with no public profile; Forbes lists her as 'former' (2024). The company site blocked automated access, so no IR contact was captured. Russian-sanctions context applies, and this is not a useful podcast guest.

name: Gerald Engström
education: Stockholm University
profile: Gerald Engström founded Swedish ventilation maker Systemair in 1974 and was CEO until 2015, then chairman until 2025. Systemair now has about 90 companies in 51 countries and roughly 6,700 employees, and listed in October 2007. He also holds a portfolio of listed stocks worth over $1bn and owns businesses such as fashion retailer Indiska and RVM Systems.
interesting_fact: Systemair is increasingly a data-centre supplier. In August 2026 it won a SEK 60m order for Geniox Tera Fanwall cooling units for a new Finnish data centre whose waste heat will feed the local district-heating network.
deep_cut_fact: Systemair's very first product was an inline duct fan with circular connections that installs directly into the duct system, greatly simplifying installation. The company is still headquartered in the small Bergslagen town of Skinnskatteberg, where it is the largest employer and exports about 70% of the factory's output.
current_role: Founder and major shareholder, Systemair (Nasdaq Stockholm: SYSR); chairman until 2025; private investor
research_notes: A strong podcast fit (data-centre cooling, heat recovery, energy efficiency). Systemair's press releases list CEO Robert Larsson and CFO Anders Ulff as contacts, but their emails are obfuscated, so none are listed here. Engström's own investment company may be a better route than Systemair.

name: Sir Dennis
profile: British-born statistician (b. 1944, London) who co-founded Quintiles in Durham, NC, growing it from UNC biostatistics consulting into the world's largest clinical-research organisation; Quintiles merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form IQVIA. Now an investor/chair at London-based GHO Capital and a dementia-research advocate.
interesting_fact: In 2014 David Cameron appointed him World Dementia Envoy; he helped found and became first chairman of the World Dementia Council, and was knighted in 2020 for services to dementia and life-sciences research.
deep_cut_fact: Quintiles traces back to a single 1974 project: Hoechst hired the UNC biostatistics professor to analyse trial data for a new diabetes drug; his analysis showed which patients to exclude, letting Hoechst bring it to market. The company was only incorporated in 1982 with fellow professor Gary Koch.
current_role: Non-Executive Chair and Founder, GHO Capital (healthcare investment firm); retired IQVIA lead director (2018)
research_notes: Lane name 'Sir Dennis' = Sir Dennis Gillings (wealth shared with wife Mireille Gillings, per Sunday Times). Son of a London fishmonger (Wikipedia). Best route likely via GHO Capital (ghocapital.com) — no published personal contact found.

profile: Montreal-born neurobiologist (PhD Radboud Nijmegen, postdocs at Bordeaux and Scripps) who founded San Diego-based HUYA Bioscience International in 2004 to in-license and develop novel drugs discovered in China. deep_cut_fact: The company name HUYA combines the Chinese abbreviations for Shanghai (Hù) and Asia (Yà); before HUYA she was also a co-founder of MIR3, and she calls herself a 'serial entrepreneur'. She speaks French natively plus Mandarin.
current_role: Founder, CEO & Executive Chair, HUYABIO International; Co-founder & Non-Executive Vice Chair, GHO Capital

profile: Born 1938, Jacques Merceron-Vicat is the patriarch of the family that controls Vicat, the listed French cement group founded in 1853 near Grenoble by Joseph Vicat, son of cement pioneer Louis Vicat. He led the group as chairman/CEO for decades before handing operations to son-in-law Guy Sidos (CEO 2008, chairman 2014); he remains honorary chairman with a board mandate running to 2030.

current_role: Honorary Chairman (Président d'honneur) and director, Vicat SA
research_notes: Aged ~88, low public profile. Company now active in cement decarbonisation and alternative fuels (energy angle). Better podcast guest may be CEO Guy Sidos; approach via Vicat press office (named press officer as published in Vicat's July 2026 release).

current_role: Chairman (Director), Yamato Kogyo Co., Ltd. (TSE: 5444)

name: Michaela Herz
profile: Granddaughter of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz and daughter of Günter Herz, who ran Tchibo for ~35 years. After Günter and his sister sold their Tchibo stake in 2003 they founded Mayfair, a Hamburg family holding investing in companies, bonds and real estate; Michaela owns about 45% and helps steer investment decisions.
interesting_fact: Mayfair's first big deal was a 17% (later 27%) stake in Puma in 2004, sold to PPR at €330/share; it then bought Germanischer Lloyd for €575m, which expanded into oil & gas and renewable-energy services before merging into DNV GL in 2013 (stake sold 2017).
deep_cut_fact: As one of Mayfair's managing directors, Michaela Herz is active in shaping investment decisions.
current_role: Managing director and ~45% owner, Mayfair Vermögensverwaltungs SE (Herz family holding, Hamburg)
research_notes: Extremely private — almost no public footprint under her own name. Energy angle for the podcast: Mayfair's Germanischer Lloyd/DNV GL investment. Aunt Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel's branch has exited Mayfair (Forbes). Mayfair website did not load; no published contact found.

name: Anton Fedun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
education: University of Surrey (Master)
profile: Anton Fedun's fortune stems from Lukoil, Russia's No. 2 oil producer, where his father Leonid Fedun was a long-time controlling shareholder and in 2018 transferred part of his stake to him. A dual Russian-UK citizen living in London, he runs his own boutique hotels: The Ampersand in South Kensington and Vintry & Mercer, a 92-room City hotel opened in 2019.
interesting_fact: He is hands-on in hospitality rather than oil: he is managing director of Vintry & Mercer, built on the City site where medieval Vintners unloaded wine and Mercers traded silks and textiles, hence the name.
deep_cut_fact: In an Oct 2020 Boutique Hotel News video interview he discussed repurposing Vintry & Mercer and The Ampersand during the pandemic, courting London's local market and designing distinctive concepts; Vintry & Mercer's design deliberately references its City neighbourhood's history.
current_role: Hotel owner / managing director, The Ampersand Hotel (South Kensington) and Vintry & Mercer (City of London); Lukoil shareholder
research_notes: Private; no personal channels found. Best route is via the hotels (Ampersand / Vintry & Mercer, an SLH member). Russian oil-wealth links (Lukoil) mean sanctions sensitivity should be checked before outreach. SLH journal Q&A (journal.slh.com, post 7096) describes him as MD of Vintry & Mercer.

name: Judith Neilson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2017-2021); Hurun Global (2018-2020)
profile: Zimbabwe-born former graphic designer and Sydney philanthropist whose fortune stems from her stake in Platinum Asset Management, the global equities manager co-founded by her ex-husband Kerr Neilson (divorced 2015). She founded and solely funds the White Rabbit Gallery of post-2000 Chinese contemporary art, backed the Phoenix arts spaces in Chippendale, and set up the A$100M Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas.
interesting_fact: White Rabbit holds one of the world's largest collections of 21st-century Chinese art; in 2024 she said it held work by around 800 artists and 'there were 4,000 pieces the last time I counted'. Her interest began on trips to Beijing in the late 1990s.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 she endowed a Chair of Architecture at UNSW to develop housing solutions for displaced people such as climate refugees and disaster or conflict victims, and in 2017 a Chair of Contemporary Art at UNSW. She was made a Member of the Order of Australia (AM) in 2016.
current_role: Founder and director, White Rabbit Gallery (Sydney); philanthropist and Platinum Asset Management shareholder
research_notes: Private, rarely interviewed. Note: neilson.org.au (contact@neilson.org.au) is the Neilson Foundation run by ex-husband Kerr Neilson, NOT her - do not use. Best route is via White Rabbit Gallery or the Judith Neilson Institute. Arts/journalism focus rather than energy.

name: Peter-Alexander Wacker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2024); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
profile: Great-grandson of founder Alexander Wacker, he owns roughly 10% of Munich-based Wacker Chemie. After ten years at BMW he joined Wacker's board in 1993, became CEO when it went public in 2005, and moved to chair the supervisory board in 2008. Wacker is a major maker of silicones and of hyperpure polysilicon for solar cells and semiconductors.
interesting_fact: Energy/chips angle: Wacker began producing polysilicon, the base material for solar cells and semiconductors, at a new plant in Bradley County (Charleston), Tennessee, in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: He collects elephant figures from around the world because elephants symbolize strength to him, which is why his holding company is named Blue Elephant. He was also named Germany's family businessman of the year in 2006.
current_role: Chair of the Supervisory Board, Wacker Chemie AG (since 2008; re-elected 2023)
public_contact: ir_email: investor.relations@wacker.com | press_email: Manuela.Dollinger@wacker.com (Wacker Media Relations, as listed in company profile)
research_notes: Holds a doctorate (listed as Dr.). Polysilicon for solar and semiconductors is a strong energy/data-center hook. Approach via Wacker corporate communications in Munich.

name: KR Sridhar
sec_insider_companies: Bloom Energy Corp (BE) - Chairman & CEO
profile: Tamil Nadu-born engineer (MS nuclear engineering, PhD mechanical engineering, UIUC) who directed the University of Arizona's Space Technologies Laboratory, building Mars oxygen-generation tech for NASA. After NASA shelved its Mars Surveyor 2001 lander he co-founded Ion America (2001), renamed Bloom Energy, whose solid-oxide fuel cells now supply on-site power to AI data centers; IPO 2018.
interesting_fact: Bloom has become an on-site 'bring your own power' supplier for AI data centers, including a 2025 collaboration with Oracle to deliver power to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure sites at the speed of AI build-outs.
deep_cut_fact: He co-authored the 1997 Solid State Ionics paper 'Oxygen production on Mars using solid oxide electrolysis' (with B.T. Vaniman): a zirconia cell splitting Martian CO2 into oxygen. Bloom's fuel cell is essentially that Mars device run in reverse. Fortune named him one of five young innovators in 2000.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE)
public_contact: press_email: press@bloomenergy.com | ir_email: investor@bloomenergy.com | official_website: https://www.bloomenergy.com/
research_notes: Highly on-topic for an energy/data-center podcast; Bloom actively promotes its data-center power story. Media contact on releases: Katja Gagen (press@bloomenergy.com). Also an independent director at C3.ai (per Wikipedia).

name: Wee Wei Ling
profile: Eldest child of the late UOB patriarch Wee Cho Yaw. At UOL's Pan Pacific Hotels Group she oversees owned hotels, the St. Gregory spa and Si Chuan Dou Hua restaurant brands and the group's sustainability and community partnerships; she also sits on the family's Kheng Leong property firm and Wee Foundation boards.
interesting_fact: A champion of inclusive hiring, she has pushed companies to treat employing people with special needs as corporate strategy rather than charity, and chaired Project We Care, the People's Association's CEO network for corporate volunteerism, from 2011.
deep_cut_fact: She personally curated Pan Pacific's corporate art collection of local artists, published as the book 'Along the Journey', and co-founded the performing-arts charity Extra.Ordinary People with her cousin Wee Boo Kuan; she kept a Delia Prvacki ceramic bought in 1997 even after selling the hotel it was in.
current_role: Executive Director (Sustainability Partnerships, Lifestyle & Asset), Pan Pacific Hotels Group; director, Kheng Leong and the Wee Foundation
research_notes: Gives lifestyle-press interviews (Peak, Prestige, Tatler, Sleeper) on sustainability and inclusive hiring; best route is Pan Pacific Hotels Group corporate communications (Singapore) via its Mynewsdesk newsroom.

name: Wee Wei Chi
profile: Younger daughter of the late Wee Cho Yaw (d. Feb 2024), longtime chairman of United Overseas Bank; her wealth stems from the family's UOB and related holdings. She sits on the board of Kheng Leong, the family's commercial property development and investment arm, and is married to David Eu of the Eu Yan Sang TCM family. Brother Wee Ee Cheong is UOB CEO.
interesting_fact: She studied fine arts, earning a bachelor's degree from Moravian University in Pennsylvania, an unusual path in a banking dynasty.
deep_cut_fact: She has a bachelor's degree in fine arts from Moravian University in Pennsylvania.
current_role: Board member, Kheng Leong Co. (Wee family property and investment company), Singapore
research_notes: Very private; no public contact or social accounts found. Forbes lists her as a former (dropped-off) billionaire. Any approach would likely need to go through the Wee family office / Kheng Leong, which publishes no contact for her.

name: Azman Hashim
education: High School (High School Graduate)
profile: Malaysian banker (born 1939) who bought the Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank in 1982 and built it into AmBank Group (AMMB Holdings), chairing it until 2019 and retiring fully in 2022. He holds stakes in RCE Capital and Amcorp Properties and still chairs bodies including the Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers and the Malaysia-Japan Economic Association.
interesting_fact: He summited Mount Kinabalu (4,095m) on 31 October 2023 at age 84, his second ascent after first climbing it at 71 in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He passed the Senior Cambridge exam with first-class marks at 15, then trained as a chartered accountant in Perth, Australia (1955-60) on a Colombo Plan scholarship; his grandmother came from Imabari in Japan's Ehime prefecture.
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, AmBank Group; Chairman, Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers
research_notes: Retired from AmBank; best route is via the Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers (aicb.org.my) or AmBank corporate communications. Received a Chartered Banker Institute (UK) lifetime achievement award in June 2025 (Bernama). No personal contact published.

name: Chandubhai Virani
profile: A farmer's son from Jamnagar district, Virani and his brothers moved to Rajkot in 1974 and worked at the Astron Cinema canteen. In 1982 they began making their own potato wafers, and Balaji grew into one of India's largest regional snack brands. The brothers became billionaires after selling a minority stake to General Atlantic in January 2026.
interesting_fact: For years he turned down stake offers from PepsiCo, General Mills and about 50 private-equity firms, saying he was there to run the company, not sell it. The 2026 General Atlantic minority deal was the family's first outside investment.
deep_cut_fact: At Astron Cinema he earned Rs 90 a month and repaired torn seats after night shows in exchange for a plate of chorafali. He started making wafers after 'changing suppliers three times'.
current_role: Cofounder and chairman/managing director, Balaji Wafers Pvt. Ltd. (Rajkot, Gujarat)
research_notes: His Vad plant (2003) ran about 5,000 kg of potatoes per hour, a record at the time. He gives interviews mostly in Gujarati/Hindi media. contact@balajiwafers.com is the company's general inbox.

name: Kanjibhai Virani
profile: Kanjibhai (Kanubhai) Virani co-founded Balaji Wafers with brothers Chandubhai and Bhikhubhai; the Rajkot firm grew from wafers sold at a cinema canteen into one of India's largest regional snack makers (chips, namkeen, noodles, confectionery). The family became billionaires after agreeing in Jan 2026 to sell a ~7% minority stake to General Atlantic; the next generation is increasingly running the business.
interesting_fact: The brothers began in 1974 selling wafers from the canteen of Astron Cinema in Rajkot, where they had done odd jobs; wafers were made at home until the first factory opened in 1989. Balaji is said to hold ~90% of Gujarat's chips market.
deep_cut_fact: Their first venture failed: their farmer father Popatbhai sold ancestral farmland to give the brothers Rs 20,000, which they put into farm equipment and lost, before turning to snacks.
current_role: Co-founder, Balaji Wafers Pvt Ltd (Rajkot, Gujarat)
research_notes: Kanjibhai is commonly listed as 'Kanubhai Virani'. Chandubhai Virani is the public face of the company; approach likely via the company. GA deal announced 22 Jan 2026 (https://www.generalatlantic.com/media-article/balaji-wafers-announces-strategic-investment-from-general-atlantic/).

name: Ellis Short
education: Missouri University of Science and Technology; William Chrisman High School
profile: American financier (b. 1960, Independence, Missouri) who became president of Dallas private equity firm Lone Star Funds and ran its Asian operations, then founded Kildare Partners in 2013 to buy distressed European property and non-performing loans. Owned Sunderland AFC 2008-2018.
interesting_fact: In 2003 he paid about GBP 23m for Skibo Castle in Scotland, the members-only club famous for hosting Madonna and Guy Ritchie's 2000 wedding.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he was an engineer: he earned a mechanical engineering degree from Missouri University of Science and Technology (then Missouri-Rolla) in 1983 and started his career at General Electric.
current_role: Founder, Kildare Partners (distressed European real estate private equity)
research_notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Only route found is Kildare Partners (offices in Dallas/Westlake TX, London, Dublin, Bermuda). Returned to the US from London in 2017.

name: Diane Briere de l'Isle
profile: Diane Briere de l'Isle Engelhardt OBE is married to Henry Engelhardt, founder and former CEO of Cardiff-based car insurer Admiral Group; their fortune comes from Admiral shares after its 2004 LSE flotation. The couple set up the Moondance Foundation in 2010, funded by regularly donating Admiral shares. She chairs it, and it has given away well over £76m, mostly to causes in Wales.
interesting_fact: The Moondance Foundation is funded by gifts of the couple's Admiral shares. When the pandemic hit, she launched a Covid-19 Relief Fund, and the foundation later committed a further £10m to Welsh organisations.
deep_cut_fact: She and Henry Engelhardt received the First Minister's Special Award at the Welsh Government's St David Awards 2026.
current_role: Chair, Moondance Foundation (Welsh grant-making charity, reg. 1139224)
public_contact: office_email: rebecca@moondancefoundation.org.uk (Moondance Foundation contact) | official_website: https://www.moondancefoundation.org.uk
research_notes: Wealth is shared with husband Henry Engelhardt; the Rich List entry is joint. I couldn't verify any formal Admiral role for her, so don't describe her as an Admiral co-founder. The foundation's published contact is the best route. Moondance Cancer Initiative is a related Welsh initiative.

name: James Cameron
education: Fullerton College (Drop Out)
profile: Canadian-born (now also New Zealand citizen, 2025) director of The Terminator, Titanic and the Avatar films, three of the four highest-grossing movies ever; his films have grossed roughly $9-10bn. Much of his wealth comes from Avatar profit participation. He developed his own 3D camera and performance-capture tech, and released Avatar: Fire and Ash in December 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2012 he became the first person to make a solo dive to the bottom of the Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) in the Deepsea Challenger, a sub he helped develop; he also sold The Terminator script for $1 on condition he could direct it.
deep_cut_fact: After dropping out of Fullerton College he worked as a truck driver and high-school janitor, teaching himself special effects in the USC library; he financed his first short film, Xenogenesis (1978), by borrowing money from a consortium of dentists. A frog species, Pristimantis jamescameroni, is named after him.
current_role: Filmmaker (Lightstorm Entertainment); director of the Avatar franchise; National Geographic explorer and ocean-exploration advocate
public_contact: official_website: https://www.avatar.com/ (Avatar franchise site, not personal)
research_notes: Lives in New Zealand. No personal social accounts or published personal contact found; approaches go via Lightstorm Entertainment or his talent agency/publicist. Strong energy/sustainability angle: plant-based food businesses, OceanX adviser, ocean exploration tech.

name: Jerry Seinfeld
education: City University of New York Queens (Bachelor of Arts/Science)
profile: Jerry Seinfeld (b. 1954, raised in Massapequa, NY) co-created and starred in NBC's 'Seinfeld' (1989-98) with Larry David; his billionaire fortune comes mainly from his share of the show's syndication and streaming revenue plus touring. He still tours stand-up and has made Netflix specials, 'Comedians in Cars Getting Coffee', 'Bee Movie' and the 2024 film 'Unfrosted'.
interesting_fact: A serious car collector with about 150 cars, mostly Porsches; the centerpiece has been Steve McQueen's Porsche 917 (chassis 022) driven in the 1971 film 'Le Mans'.
deep_cut_fact: At 16 he volunteered on Kibbutz Sa'ar in Israel; he later started at SUNY Oswego before transferring to Queens College (BA communications and theater, 1976), doing open-mic nights at Budd Friedman's Improv while still a student. He has practiced Transcendental Meditation since about 1972.
current_role: Stand-up comedian, writer and producer; co-creator of 'Seinfeld'; touring comic
public_contact: official_website: https://jerryseinfeld.com/ | x: https://twitter.com/jerryseinfeld | instagram: https://www.instagram.com/jerryseinfeld/ | http://jerryseinfeld.com/ | https://x.com/JerrySeinfeld | https://www.facebook.com/JerrySeinfeld
research_notes: Celebrity; outreach realistically via his talent representation/publicist rather than direct. Car collecting and his long-form interview podcast appearances are natural hooks; not an energy/data-center figure.

name: Weijian Shan
education: University of California, Berkeley (Doctorate); University of California, Berkeley (Master of Economics); University of San Francisco (Master of Business Administration)
profile: Beijing-born (1954) private equity investor who spent six years as a sent-down youth in the Gobi Desert before studying in the US (MBA USF, PhD UC Berkeley). After the World Bank, Wharton faculty and J.P. Morgan, he was TPG/Newbridge's top Asia dealmaker (incl. Korea First Bank), then built PAG from 2010 into a ~$50B+ AUM Asia alternatives firm. Author of three books; British Museum trustee.
interesting_fact: His 2019 memoir 'Out of the Gobi: My Story of China and America' recounts laboring in the Gobi during the Cultural Revolution; Janet Yellen was one of his Berkeley thesis advisors.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wall Street he was an assistant professor at the Wharton School for six years, where he founded the academic journal China Economic Review; he first came to Beijing's Institute of Foreign Trade in 1975 to study English.
current_role: Executive Chairman and Co-Founder, PAG (Asia-focused alternative investment firm); independent director, Alibaba Group
public_contact: office_email: info@pag.com | contact_form: https://www.pag.com/en/media-center | linkedin: https://hk.linkedin.com/in/weijian-shan
research_notes: Very public: frequent op-ed writer (FT, NYT, Foreign Affairs) and conference speaker; books (Money Games, Money Machine) give a natural hook. ir@pag.com is investor-only; info@pag.com (Hong Kong HQ) is the general route.

name: Andrew Brode
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Hurun Global (2022); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
profile: Chartered accountant who sold a family publishing business to Wolters Kluwer, bought legal journal Eclipse in 1990, and merged it with translation firm RWS in 1995, building RWS into a global AI-driven language and IP services group via acquisitions. Long-time RWS chairman and major shareholder; also a key backer/chair of Learning Technologies Group.
interesting_fact: Took over as interim chair of RWS when the chair left at end-2025, then handed over to ex-Microsoft EMEA chairman Patrick De Smedt in Oct 2026 while staying on the board.
deep_cut_fact: An Old Edwardian (left 1959), he funded half of King Edward's School Birmingham's £5m 2012 appeal and much of the school's new sports hall, named The Andrew Brode Sports Centre.
current_role: Non-Executive Director, RWS Holdings plc (interim Chair Jan–Oct 2026, succeeded by Patrick De Smedt)
public_contact: pr_agency: MHP Group (RWS financial PR) – rws@mhpgroup.com | official_website: https://www.rws.com/about/investors/directors
research_notes: Passionate mentor of young entrepreneurs (coached LTG's Jonathan Satchell, Cera's Mahiben Maruthappu) — good angle for an entrepreneurship podcast. Route via RWS company secretary or MHP.

name: Lance Gokongwei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2021-2024); Hurun Global (2020-2024)
education: The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania (Bachelor of Science); University of Pennsylvania, School of Engineering and Applied Science (Bachelor of Science)
profile: Only son of the late John Gokongwei Jr., Lance Gokongwei runs JG Summit, a Philippine conglomerate spanning Cebu Pacific airline, snack maker Universal Robina, Robinsons property and retail, banking, petrochemicals and stakes in power and telecom. A Penn graduate (finance and applied science, 1988), he is shifting the group from owner-operator to an active investor model.
interesting_fact: Cebu Pacific, the family's budget airline, has been in talks for an order of up to 150 new aircraft, among the largest in Philippine aviation history.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was management trainee at Universal Robina selling Jack 'n Jill snacks door to door to supermarkets and sari-sari stores, paid P2,000 a month and driving an old Datsun with a broken air-conditioner, as he told PLV graduates in 2019.
current_role: President & CEO, JG Summit Holdings (also chairs key affiliates such as Cebu Pacific, Robinsons Land and Universal Robina)
research_notes: Low-key, rarely gives interviews; corporate route via JG Summit IR/corporate communications. Group has power and data-related interests relevant to energy podcast.

name: Jason Gardner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Hurun Global (2022); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
sec_insider_companies: Marqeta, Inc. (MQ) - Director,TenPercentOwner; Pagaya Technologies Ltd. (PGY) - Director
profile: New Jersey-born Jason Gardner co-founded rent-payments startup PropertyBridge (sold to MoneyGram in 2007), then founded Marqeta in 2010, building a card-issuing API used by DoorDash, Square and others; it IPO'd in 2021. He handed the CEO role to Simon Khalaf in 2023 and stepped down as executive chairman in June 2024, remaining a director with roughly 40% voting power.
interesting_fact: As a teen he worked at a thrift store and sold T-shirts on trains to Grateful Dead concerts; in his 20s he worked as an assistant to Senator John McCain.
deep_cut_fact: His first company, Vertical Think, was an early Elance/Upwork-style marketplace matching web developers with small projects, which he called 'more a lifestyle business'. Marqeta's original idea was a debit card that could hold many merchant coupons such as Groupon deals.
current_role: Founder and board director, Marqeta (NASDAQ: MQ); director, Pagaya Technologies
research_notes: No longer an executive at Marqeta, so company press may route slowly; he has done many podcast interviews (a16z, Founders Network, Stifel) and is approachable on founder topics.

name: Somporn Juangroongruangkit
name_chinese: 索姆波恩·让古恩广基特
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2019); Hurun Global (2015-2021)
profile: Somporn Juangroongruangkit (สมพร จึงรุ่งเรืองกิจ) took over Thai Summit Group, founded in 1977 by her late husband Phatana, and built it into one of Thailand's and ASEAN's largest auto-parts makers: 40+ companies, 26 factories in Thailand, Indonesia, India, China, Vietnam, Japan and the US, and revenue above US$2.6bn. Her children Sakulthorn and Chanapun now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: In Feb 2026 Bloomberg reported global PE firms were circling Thai Summit at a possible $1.5–2bn valuation; the group publicly denied any sale, saying it was proud to be a Thai company with leading technology able to compete globally amid the EV transition.
deep_cut_fact: Thai Summit's flagship Thai Summit Autoparts Industry, on whose board she sits, has reported a profit every single year since 2005.
current_role: Chair/President, Thai Summit Group; director of Thai Summit Autoparts Industry Co.
public_contact: office_email: info@thaisummit.co.th (Thai Summit Group general contact) | official_website: https://www.thaisummit.co.th
research_notes: Very low profile; mother of politician Thanathorn — politics is sensitive (company states politically active family members have no role in management). EV-transition angle for podcast. Route via Thai Summit corporate office.

name: Edgar Sia II
profile: Edgar 'Injap' Sia II, an Iloilo-born architecture dropout, opened the first Mang Inasal grill restaurant in 2003 at 26 and sold it to Jollibee (Tony Tan Caktiong) in 2010-2016. With Tan Caktiong he built DoubleDragon (listed 2014), now an investment holding firm spanning CityMalls, Hotel101 (incl. Madrid, opened 2026) and MerryMart groceries; he targets P500bn revenue by 2035.
interesting_fact: DoubleDragon's Hotel101 opened a 680-room property in Madrid in March 2026, part of Sia's plan to take the Filipino condotel brand global.
deep_cut_fact: In 2002 he won a Honda Civic in a nationwide 'Text Challenge' by texting all day and paying a jobless college classmate P200/day to text overnight (with 3 a.m. wake-up calls); he sold the car and within a year opened the first Mang Inasal in an Iloilo mall carpark.
current_role: Chairman and CEO, DoubleDragon Corporation (Philippines)
research_notes: Media-friendly and frequently interviewed by Philippine business press; nicknamed the 'promdi billionaire' (provincial).

name: Masayuki Ishihara
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2023); Hurun Global (2020)
profile: Masayuki Ishihara draws his wealth from Tokyo-listed pachinko machine maker Heiwa. Ishihara is not involved in running Heiwa.
interesting_fact: He founded another pachinko firm, Olympia, which Heiwa acquired in a stock swap in 2007.
deep_cut_fact: Heiwa subsidiary PGM is one of Japan's largest golf course operators.

name: Seifeddin Rustamov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2023); Hurun Global (2024)
profile: Seifeddin (Seyfeddin) Rustamov/Roustamov has controlled Metafrax, one of Russia's largest methanol and derivatives producers (based in Gubakha, Perm Krai), via MetaHolding since 2014. He describes himself as an energy and chemicals professional, developer, investor and philanthropist. Forbes lists him as a US resident.
interesting_fact: Under his ownership Metafrax adopted a development strategy to 2030 and began a large construction programme at Gubakha, including an ammonia-urea-melamine complex, expanding from methanol into fertilisers and resins.
deep_cut_fact: In 2018 Rustamov personally decided that Metafrax would fund a full year of bone-marrow donor recruitment centres in Perm region with the Dedmorozim foundation ('Mind Donation' project). Over 150 employees registered as potential donors, and later matches went on to help patients.
current_role: Beneficial owner, Metafrax Group (via JSC MetaHolding), the Russian methanol and chemicals producer
research_notes: Name also spelled Seyfeddin Roustamov. Low profile; communications go out through Metafrax press releases. The assets are Russian, so check sanctions and compliance before outreach. Found no published personal or press email.

name: Kazuo Okada
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2000-2024); Hurun Global (2014-2024)
profile: Kazuo Okada founded Universal Entertainment, which manufactures and sells pachinko machines and casino equipment, in 1969. Formerly known as Aruze Corporation, Universal Entertainment trades on Tokyo's JASDAQ exchange.
interesting_fact: An art enthusiast, Okada possesses art from Japan, China and Korea, which are displayed at The Okada Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan.
deep_cut_fact: Okada dropped out of high school to enroll in an engineering vocational school, and later started repairing broken jukeboxes from America.

name: David Helgason
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2022); SEC insider holdings (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
sec_insider_companies: Unity Software Inc. (U) - Director
profile: Iceland-born David Helgason cofounded game engine company Unity Software in 2004 in Copenhagen, Denmark. Some of the world's most popular online and mobile games were built using Unity's engine, including Pokemon Go, Among Us and Overcooked.
interesting_fact: Helgason is one of just two billionaires from Iceland; the other is investor Thor Bjorgolfsson.
deep_cut_fact: Helgason has a wide array of interests; he studied physics, Arabic, and psychology at the University of Copenhagen from 1997 to 2001.

name: Sathien Setthasit
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2018-2022); Hurun Global (2020-2024)
profile: Sathien Setthasit runs Carabao Group, maker of Thailand's hugely popular Carabao Dang energy drink. Sathien founded the company in 2002 with his folk singer pal Aed Carabao and took it public in 2014.
interesting_fact: Carabao, which has close to a fourth of the Thai energy drink market, outsells Red Bull in Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: Carabao is the title sponsor of the English Football League.

name: Michael Schmidt-Ruthenbeck
name_chinese: 迈克尔·施密特·鲁滕贝克
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2001-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2020)
profile: Secretive brothers Michael Schmidt-Ruthenbeck and Reiner Schmidt are heirs to a piece of the Metro retail fortune. Their grandfather Karl Schmidt expanded into the wholesale trade in the 1920s, supplying food retailers around Duisburg, Germany.
interesting_fact: Germany's Mercator foundation is attributed to Michael. It has spent over $650 million on projects including climate change mitigation and cultural education.
deep_cut_fact: Two Swiss foundations, Mercator Schweiz and the Karl Schmidt Family Foundation, are also funded by the family.

name: Eduardo Belmont Anderson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2013-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2023); Wikidata (2021)
education: University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill (Bachelor of Arts/Science)

profile: Ajay 'Jay' Puri runs NVIDIA's global sales and field organisation, which sells the GPUs and systems behind the AI data-center boom. He joined NVIDIA in 2005 after 22 years at Sun Microsystems in sales, marketing and general management. His wealth comes from NVIDIA stock (about 0.02% stake), and he remains in the role as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Puri holds about 0.02% of NVIDIA, which in October 2025 became the first company ever worth $5 trillion. That was enough to make a sales executive a billionaire on Forbes' real-time list.

He holds electrical engineering degrees from the University of Minnesota (BS) and Caltech (MS) as well as a Harvard MBA, so he is an engineer by training, not a career salesman.
current_role: Executive Vice President, Worldwide Field Operations, NVIDIA (still listed with this title on an Aug 2026 SEC Form 4)
research_notes: Low public profile with no NVIDIA newsroom bio page, so requests are best routed through NVIDIA corporate communications. SEC filer CIK 0001347842 ('Puri Ajay K'). Forbes now marks him as 'former' on its real-time list.

With Alexander Machkevich and Alijan Ibragimov ('The Trio') he built ENRC in Kazakhstan, floated it in London in 2007 and took it private in 2013; it is now ERG, a mining, smelting and energy group active in 14 countries.
interesting_fact: He speaks fluent Japanese and received Japan's Order of the Rising Sun in 2020 for developing Japan-Russia economic and cultural ties.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he acquired the Kubota Collection, 104 kimono by textile artist Itchiku Kubota made with the revived 'tsujigahana' dyeing technique, and his foundation has since toured it to Kazakhstan, Russia, Europe and North America, with key pieces shown at the Tokyo National Museum in 2020.

Review before featuring. Best route is the foundation (ICF), which is PR-active; ERG (erg.kz) has its own press office.

name: Roy Vagelos
profile: Physician-scientist (b. 1929) who moved from NIH and Washington University to Merck's research labs, then ran Merck as CEO and chairman until 1994. He chaired Regeneron for nearly 29 years from 1995 and co-founded Theravance. His fortune comes largely from Regeneron stock, and he and his wife Diana are major donors to Columbia, Penn and Barnard.
interesting_fact: As Merck's CEO he had the company give its river-blindness drug ivermectin (Mectizan) free to governments and patients. Over two decades the programme reached more than 55 million people.
deep_cut_fact: The son of Greek immigrants, he grew up during the Depression working in his family's small restaurant in Rahway, New Jersey, the town where Merck's labs were based. He left on a partial scholarship to Penn, where he earned a chemistry BA (Phi Beta Kappa, 1950).
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Merck (1985–1994) and longtime Chairman of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (1995–c.2024); philanthropist
research_notes: Aged 97 and living in New Jersey. Columbia's medical school is named the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons, and the couple gave $400m to Columbia in 2024. No personal contact published; Regeneron or Columbia communications offices are the likely routes (pages blocked automated fetches).

As CEO since 1997 he runs the U.S. operations (brands such as Montblanc, Coach, Jimmy Choo licences sit across the group).
interesting_fact: Madar never wears fragrance himself, to keep his sense of smell clear.
deep_cut_fact: The company's original name, Jean Philippe Fragrances, was a contraction of the founders' first names, Jean and Philippe, and it started out selling inexpensive alternatives to pricier designer scents before moving upmarket.

profile: Dong Mingzhu (b. 1954, Nanjing) joined Gree's predecessor in 1990 at 36 as an air-conditioner saleswoman and rose to head of sales (1994), president (2001) and chairwoman (2012), making Gree one of the world's largest air-conditioner makers. Led the Business Russia lobby, served as Russia's first business ombudsman (2012-2024 per most sources), founded the Party of Growth, and ran for president in 2018 (0.76%). research_notes: Sanctioned by the UK (incl. 2025 director-disqualification sanction re Abrau-Durso; listed on OpenSanctions). Russian state official. Outreach likely inappropriate/legally sensitive for a Western podcast; no personal contacts researched.

name: Denis Shtengelov

profile: Denis Shtengelov controls KDV, a large food business in Russia that sells everything from candy and beverages to pasta. Born in the village of Gubino in the Tomsk region, Shtengelov's first business was selling sunflower seeds.
interesting_fact: Shtengelov was an investor in a shopping mall that caught fire in 2018 in a deadly incident that killed  60 people, including 37 children.
deep_cut_fact: Shtengelov, who has lived in Australia for years, invested $20 million to set up KDV Sport's golf and tennis academy on the country's Gold Coast.

name: Alexander Samwer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2024)
education: Harvard Business School (Master of Business Administration); Oxford University (Master of Arts)
profile: Alexander Samwer and his brothers Oliver and Marc founded Berlin-based tech incubator Rocket Internet in 2007 and took it public in October 2014. The youngest of the brothers, Alexander does not take part in day-to-day management of the company, leaving that to Oliver.
interesting_fact: Alexander is on the board of directors of Zalando, a German e-commerce company founded by Rocket Internet and modeled after Zappos in the U.S.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Oxford University and earned an MBA from Harvard University.

name: Alexander Vik
education: Harvard University (Bachelor of Arts/Science)
profile: Alexander Vik comes from a wealthy family of fur merchants and has dabbled in everything from closed-end country funds to insurance and tech startups. He remains locked in a contentious legal battle with Deutsche Bank, which in late 2013 obtained a $250 million judgment against his trading operation.
interesting_fact: A Norwegian who was raised in Sweden and schooled in the Canary Islands, Vik was a former golf champion at Harvard University.
deep_cut_fact: During the first Internet bubble, Vik was behind Xcelera.com, one of the biggest dot.com boom and bust stocks of the era.

name: Ramesh Kumar Dua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2024); Hurun India (2015-2019)

interesting_fact: Ramesh Kumar Dua is a London-trained rubber technologist.
deep_cut_fact: Bollywood stars Salman Khan and Akshay Kumar are Relaxo's brand ambassadors.

name: Bhawari Bai Surana
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun India (2017-2019)
profile: Bhawari Bai Surana is the matriarch of the Surana family, which controls Banaglore pharma firm Micro Labs. The generics company makes drugs for cardiac diseases, diabetes and pain management. It also makes ophthalmic products for Bausch & Lomb's Asia-Pacific market.
interesting_fact: The privately held company gets nearly 60% of its annual revenue of from the domestic market.
deep_cut_fact: The company was founded by her late husband G.C. Surana, a former pharma distributor, in 1973 in Chennai.

name: Francesco Saputo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2023-2024); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
profile: Francesco Saputo owns a stake in his family's eponymous Canadian dairy company. His father, Giuseppe, founded the business in 1954 with $500 and a bicycle for deliveries after immigrating to Canada from Sicily.
interesting_fact: His brother, Emanuele (Lino) Saputo, was chairman from 1969 until retiring in 2017. His nephew, Lino, Jr., is the current chairman.
deep_cut_fact: The publicly traded, Montreal-based company had revenues of $11.9 billion in 2022 and sells its products in more than 40 countries.

name: David Sainsbury
profile: Great-grandson of J. Sainsbury's founder; joined the family grocer in 1963 and chaired Sainsbury's 1992-97. Made a life peer in 1997, he served as UK Science Minister until 2006. A major philanthropist, he has given Gatsby over £1.7bn for plant science, neuroscience, education, Africa and the arts.
interesting_fact: In October 2026 Gatsby committed a further £77.5m to UCL's Sainsbury Wellcome Centre and Gatsby Unit for neuroscience and AI research, taking its cumulative support there above £292m.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Gatsby in 1967, just four years after graduating from King's College, Cambridge; Gatsby's £82m gift later paid for Cambridge's Sainsbury Laboratory (plant science), opened in 2011.
current_role: Founder and settlor, Gatsby Charitable Foundation; Labour peer (Lord Sainsbury of Turville); former Chancellor of the University of Cambridge (2011-2024)
research_notes: Strong science/innovation-policy angle (former science minister; funds Babbage policy network/industrial strategy work). Best route is Gatsby's contact form.

name: Kenshin Oshima
profile: Born 1948, Oshima graduated top of his class from Keio's commerce faculty and worked at Mitsui & Co. (including Jakarta) before founding Shohkoh Fund in 1978 to lend to small businesses. It listed in 1989 and on the TSE First Section in 1999, and he ranked 61st on Forbes' 1997 list. SFCG collapsed in 2009.
interesting_fact: While at Mitsui & Co. in Jakarta, a Singaporean banker entertained him and thanked him 'for borrowing'. Oshima said that moment made him decide to go into finance himself.
deep_cut_fact: His father ran the 'Dance Hall Shinseiki' in Tokyo, the ballroom used as a setting in the 1996 film 'Shall We Dance?'.
current_role: Former founder/chairman of SFCG (formerly Shohkoh Fund), a Japanese SME lender that went bankrupt in 2009; no current role found
research_notes: Not a suitable guest: SFCG went bankrupt in 2009; he was arrested that year and finally fully acquitted by the Tokyo High Court in 2016. The trustee won a ~JPY71.7bn damages ruling. He is almost certainly no longer a billionaire. Alive status not confirmed (no death reported on ja.wikipedia). No public contacts.

name: Mohammed Al Fahim
profile: Most likely Mohammed Abdul Jalil Al Fahim (b. 1948, Al Ain), who joined his family's Abu Dhabi business in 1968 after studying in England and diversified it from car imports into real estate, hotels and industry. He later chaired the Al Fahim family council and Makarem, and is best known as author of the bestselling memoir 'From Rags to Riches: A Story of Abu Dhabi' (1995).
interesting_fact: His 1995 memoir of pre-oil Abu Dhabi has been translated into about ten languages and was adapted into a short film, 'The Early Years: The Untold Story of Abu Dhabi'.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in the Ruler's palace in Al Ain going barefoot with friends, started at a Qur'an school and joined Al Falahiya School in 1959; he founded two special-needs centres in Abu Dhabi and keeps a private museum of documents on old Abu Dhabi.
current_role: Chairman, Makarem General Trading & Real Estate LLC; supervisory board member, Al Fahim Group, Abu Dhabi (as of 2019)
public_contact: office_email: info@alfahim.ae (Al Fahim Group general) | official_website: https://alfahim.com
research_notes: Input only says Forbes 1999 UAE list with no company; match to the Al Fahim Group/author is probable, not confirmed. Latest coverage found is 2019; current status unverified. A relative, Mohamed Abdullah Al Fahim, also works in the group, so check name carefully.

name: Anastasia Soare
profile: Born 1957 in Constanța, Romania, Soare emigrated to Los Angeles in 1989 speaking little English and worked as an aesthetician. She developed a brow-shaping method based on facial bone structure, opened her Bedford Drive salon by 1997 and built Anastasia Beverly Hills, sold in about 2,000 stores. TPG invested in 2018. Known as the 'Eyebrow Queen', she still runs the company.
interesting_fact: She has said her first eyebrow clients were Cindy Crawford and Naomi Campbell. She had to rent a room in a Beverly Hills salon after her manager doubted there was a market for eyebrow shaping.
deep_cut_fact: Before emigrating she studied art history and architecture in Romania. She based her brow-shaping method on proportions from that training, fitting brows to each person's bone structure.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Anastasia Beverly Hills (ABH)
public_contact: official_website: https://anastasiasoare.ro/en/ | contact_form: https://www.anastasiabeverlyhills.com/contact-us.html | instagram: https://www.instagram.com/anastasiabeverlyhills | x: https://twitter.com/ABHcosmetics | https://x.com/anastasiasoare | https://www.instagram.com/anastasiasoare/ | https://www.facebook.com/AnastasiaSoare
research_notes: The Instagram and X accounts belong to the company, not to her personally. Forbes listed her as a billionaire only in 2019; its 2023 estimate valued ABH at about $500M, so she may no longer be a billionaire. She is a frequent podcast and interview guest on immigrant-founder stories. The web-search budget ran out before this profile, so it relies on Wikipedia and company sites.

name: Evan Sharp
appears_on: Forbes annual (2016-2019); Hurun Global (2017-2019); Hurun Global U40 (2019)
education: Columbia Graduate School of Architecture, Planning and Preservation; University of Chicago; York Suburban Senior High School
profile: Co-founder and long-time chief design & creative officer of Pinterest, which he built as a side project while a designer at Facebook. He left full-time Pinterest work in 2021 (briefly joining Jony Ive's LoveFrom), and now runs West Co., a public-benefit startup co-founded with Biz Stone that raised a $29m seed led by Spark Capital and makes Tangle, an 'intentional living' social app.
interesting_fact: West Co.'s first app, Tangle (invite-only, late 2025), asks users each day 'What's your intention for today?'; the company draws on religious and communal rituals and has a 'Founding Ancient Technologist' on its team.
deep_cut_fact: He studied architecture at Columbia but never finished; he says 'Because I had never finished architecture school, I had felt like I'd never truly learned my design craft' and that at Facebook 'all I wanted to do was go work on Pinterest.'
current_role: Founding CEO, West Co. (The Workshop for Emotional and Spiritual Technology PBC), San Francisco
research_notes: Active angel investor. Best route: West Co. (hello@west.co). Funding coverage: https://www.pymnts.com/news/social-commerce/2026/twitter-and-pinterest-vets-pitch-new-social-app-tangle/

name: Kenny Park
profile: Yonsei graduate who founded Simone Accessory in 1987 and built it into one of the world's largest contract makers of designer handbags, supplying brands such as Michael Kors, Coach, Kate Spade, Marc Jacobs and DKNY from factories in Vietnam, Cambodia, Indonesia and China (about 18m bags and small leather goods a year).
interesting_fact: For decades he quietly manufactured luxury handbags for famous labels while staying almost unknown himself, until joining the Forbes Korea rich list in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: After university he first worked at his father's fishing company, then at handbag maker Chungsan, before starting Simone in 1987. His own description of the craft: 'My canvas was small, but I could paint the drawing I liked, the painting I wanted.'
current_role: Founder and CEO, Simone Accessory Collection (Seoul; KOSPI-listed)
research_notes: Low-profile; Simone's website could not be reached during research and no official contact was verified. Route via Simone Accessory Collection corporate office in Seoul / its KRX disclosures.

name: Jia Yueting
appears_on: Forbes annual (2014-2017); Hurun Global (2014-2017); Hurun China (2010-2019); Wikidata (2021)
education: Shanxi Finance & Taxation College
profile: YT Jia (b. 1973, Xiangfen, Shanxi) built LeEco (Le.com), once a high-flying Chinese video-streaming, TV and smartphone empire, and founded EV maker Faraday Future in 2014. LeEco collapsed under debt and he moved to Los Angeles in 2017; he returned as FF co-CEO in April 2025 and became sole Global CEO in May 2026 as FF pivots toward 'embodied AI' robots and AI-centric EVs.
interesting_fact: Faraday Future is repositioning itself around physical/embodied AI, with Jia announcing FF robots for sale and delivery alongside its FF 91 and FX vehicle lines.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career doing tech support at a tax office in Shanxi Province after studying finance at the Shanxi Provincial Finance and Taxation Vocational College.
current_role: Founder and Global CEO (sole CEO since May 2026), Faraday Future Intelligent Electric (Nasdaq: FFAI), Los Angeles
research_notes: Net worth figure (Wikidata 2021) is likely stale; he went through US personal bankruptcy in 2019 and is on China's debtor blacklist, and FF has had SEC scrutiny - avoid in outreach. He is very active on Weibo/WeChat and FF's own channels, which is how he communicates publicly.

name: Patricia Matte
education: Pontifical Catholic University of Chile
profile: Patricia Matte Larraín (b. 1943, Santiago) is the eldest child of industrialist Eliodoro Matte Ossa and shares in the Matte family fortune built on forestry/paper giant Empresas CMPC. A sociologist (Universidad Católica, 1969), she worked on social and anti-poverty policy and later concentrated on education through the SIP network of free schools.
interesting_fact: She focused much of her career on the Sociedad de Instrucción Primaria, a Chilean network of tuition-free schools founded in 1856 that celebrated 170 years in 2026; she now sits on its council of honorary members.
deep_cut_fact: A trained sociologist, she started her career at the UN's Economic Commission for Latin America (CEPAL) and later helped design poverty-reduction programmes at the national planning office (Odeplan); she received Chile's Premio Bicentenario in 2007.
current_role: Honorary councillor, Sociedad de Instrucción Primaria (SIP Red de Colegios); member of the Matte family (CMPC shareholders)
research_notes: Low profile, ~83 years old; wealth is shared family wealth (CMPC). Her role in the Pinochet-era government is politically sensitive; avoid in outreach. SIP communications is the only published channel found.

name: Bryan Sheffield
education: Southern Methodist University
profile: Son of Pioneer Natural Resources CEO Scott Sheffield. In 2008 he founded Parsley Energy on his grandfather's old Midland wells, listed it in 2014 and sold it to Pioneer in 2021 for about $7.6bn including debt. Since 2020 he has run Formentera Partners ($2.8bn+ commitments, about 70,000 boe/d), which is developing Australia's Beetaloo Basin with INPEX.
interesting_fact: Parsley Energy started in 2008 with 109 old wells his grandfather Joe Parsley had drilled around Midland. Bryan had no energy experience, only 'family connections' and a 'trader's taste for risk', per Forbes.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 he founded the Drop Shot Series, Austin's first professional tennis tournament series, with former world-ranked pro Christo van Rensburg. It grew into the ATX Open, a WTA 250 event and Austin's largest women's pro sporting event. He is also a co-owner of Austin FC.
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Formentera Partners (Austin, TX)
research_notes: Good podcast fit: shale plus Australian gas/LNG, with first Beetaloo gas sales in Sept 2026. He speaks at Hart Energy conferences. Firm news goes out via BusinessWire; I found no published press email. The LinkedIn link is the company page, not his own.

name: Pier Luigi Loro Piana
profile: Sixth-generation member of the Piedmont wool family who, with his late brother Sergio, ran Loro Piana for decades and turned the fabric maker into a global luxury brand built on rare fibres (vicuña, baby cashmere, lotus). The brothers sold 80% to LVMH in 2013; he remains deputy chairman and a prominent maxi-yacht racer.
interesting_fact: A lifelong sailor, he races his maxi yacht 'My Song' (latest in a series of boats with that name) at events such as the Loro Piana Giraglia, competing again in 2025 and 2026.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-1990s he had the idea of separating the ultra-fine under-fleece of Mongolian kid goats (baby cashmere) into its own fibre, launching what the company calls a 20-year development effort.
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Loro Piana (LVMH-controlled Italian luxury textiles and fashion house)
research_notes: Approach via Loro Piana/LVMH corporate communications; no personal channels found. Sailing (My Song) is a strong rapport topic.

name: Filaret Galchev
education: Moscow State Mining University
profile: Russian-Greek businessman born 1963 in Georgia's Tsalka District; a Moscow Mining Institute graduate, he co-founded coal trader Rosuglesbyt, then moved into cement and built Eurocement into the largest cement producer in the CIS. He sold Eurocement to Sberbank in 2020 and has kept a low profile since.
interesting_fact: Eurocement grew to be ranked among the world's top ten cement producers, holding a large share of the Russian cement market at its peak.
deep_cut_fact: Born into an ethnic Greek family in the village of Tarson (Tsalka District, Georgia), he holds both Greek and Russian citizenship and returned to academia as a professor at MISIS, the Moscow university that absorbed his alma mater, the Moscow Mining Institute.
current_role: Former owner and chairman of Eurocement Group (sold to Sberbank in 2020); listed as a professor at NUST MISIS, Moscow
research_notes: No longer a billionaire per recent lists (off Forbes after 2018). No published contacts found. Russia-based; sanctions/compliance checks advisable before any outreach. Low priority for the podcast.

name: Luca Barilla
profile: Born in Milan in 1960, Luca Barilla is one of three brothers (with Guido and Paolo) who with their family own about 85% of Barilla, the Parma-based pasta and bakery group whose brands include Barilla, Mulino Bianco and Wasa. He joined the family business in 1980, trained at Barilla France and in the US, and has been deputy chairman since 1988; he also invests in confectionery.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he and his wife Michela Petronio bought Pastiglie Leone, the historic Turin maker of pastilles and sweets, after earlier running confectioner GranMilano as president from 1997 until its sale in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: Before rising in the family firm he studied in the United States and did his military service with Italy's Carabinieri; he started at Barilla in 1980 and became a product manager in 1984.
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Barilla Group (since 1988)
research_notes: Low media profile compared with brother Guido (chairman). Barilla's media relations office is the realistic route. Pastiglie Leone ownership offers a personal angle.

name: Kunal Naresh Shah
profile: Kunal Shah (b. 1979, Mumbai) co-founded recharge/payments app FreeCharge in 2010, sold it to Snapdeal in 2015 for roughly US$400m, then founded members-only credit-card rewards platform CRED and became one of India's most prolific angel investors (200+ deals). In June 2026 Meta named him head of WhatsApp, succeeding Will Cathcart, while investing $900m in CRED for ~20%.
interesting_fact: Mark Zuckerberg hired him to run WhatsApp, the world's biggest messaging app, saying he 'built CRED into one of India's most important technology companies'; Meta simultaneously took a ~20% stake in CRED for $900m.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Wilson College, Mumbai, worked from his teens, and dropped out of a part-time MBA at NMIMS in 2004; FreeCharge grew out of a pivot of his earlier cashback start-up PaisaBack (2009). ET named him 'Comeback Kid of the Year' in 2016.
current_role: Head of WhatsApp, Meta (since June 2026); founder of CRED (stepped down as CEO)

The family-run chain now has 20+ showrooms across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and is known for Kanchipuram silk sarees such as its in-house 'Samudrika Pattu' line.
interesting_fact: Pothys began over 90 years ago as a humble Srivilliputhur shop making cotton sarees, dhotis and towels, and grew into one of South India's best-known silk-saree retailers.
current_role: Patriarch/principal of the family behind Pothys (South Indian textile and silk-saree retail chain); exact current title not confirmed
