name: Charles Ruggieri
profile: French property entrepreneur who spent 15+ years managing the housing stock of Lorraine's steel industry, took it independent as Batibail, merged it with Gecina in 1999 and grew Foncière des Régions (now Covivio) and the care-home group that became Korian. Batipart, founded 1988, now manages ~€4.5bn of real estate, tourism and hotel assets in Europe, Africa and North America, 100% family-controlled.
interesting_fact: Batipart was a French and European pioneer of large sale-and-leaseback deals in the 2000s and incubated what became Korian, one of Europe's largest care-home operators.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in social housing for Lorraine steelworkers: Batipart's name comes from 'Batigère-Participations', set up in 1988 to hold the group's staff profit-sharing stake. With his wife Marianne he founded the Fondation Juniclair (2007), which funds education, women's protection and environmental projects, committing to each region for at least 5 years.
current_role: Founder, Batipart (family real-estate/tourism/hotel investment group, Luxembourg); day-to-day led by his children Nicolas (CEO), Claire and Julien
public_contact: office_email: contact@batipart.com | contact_form: https://www.batipart.com/contact/ | official_website: https://www.batipart.com
research_notes: Family group values 'discretion and humility' — expect a private founder; route via Batipart (Luxembourg) or Nicolas Ruggieri. Batipart governance page lists him as founder (https://www.batipart.com/le-groupe/gouvernance/); alive status inferred from current site, no recent personal news found.

name: Bernhard Schadeberg
profile: Born 1965 in Kreuztal, he studied business administration, joined the family brewery in 1993 and took over as managing director from his father Friedrich Schadeberg in 2001. With his sister Petra Schadeberg-Herrmann he runs Krombacher, one of Germany's best-selling beer brands, whose group also includes Schweppes Germany and other drinks businesses.
interesting_fact: The brewery carries his grandfather's name: Bernhard Schadeberg senior took over management of the Krombach brewery in October 1922, and it has been family-run ever since.
deep_cut_fact: He went to school at the local Gymnasium in Kreuztal, a few kilometres from the brewery in Krombach, and in a 2008 FAZ interview reflected on how young people's drinking habits had changed ('Frueher haben junge Leute vier Tage durchgetrunken').
current_role: Co-owner and Managing Director, Krombacher Brauerei Bernhard Schadeberg GmbH & Co. KG
research_notes: Rarely gives interviews; route via Krombacher press office. Biography source: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernhard_Schadeberg

name: Chris Oglesby
appears_on: Hurun Global (2021-2022); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
profile: Manchester-raised property entrepreneur who joined Bruntwood, the commercial-property company his father Michael Oglesby founded in 1976, in 1991 and became CEO in 1999. He has grown it into a major owner of offices and science parks across Manchester, Liverpool, Leeds and Birmingham, including Bruntwood SciTech (Alderley Park, Manchester Science Park), a JV with Legal & General.
interesting_fact: Bruntwood donates 10% of its annual profits to charitable causes, and Oglesby is a trustee of The Oglesby Charitable Trust, which works with 40+ community charities a year.
deep_cut_fact: After studying at LSE and City University and a brief spell working in the City of London, he returned north in 1991 to join his father's firm; today he leads Greater Manchester Business Board's Clean Growth Mission and is interim chair of Innovation Greater Manchester.
current_role: CEO and majority shareholder, Bruntwood; CEO, Bruntwood SciTech
research_notes: Accessible, civic-minded and media-friendly (appeared on Business Leader podcast, Jan 2025: https://bruntwood.co.uk/blog/in-conversation-with-business-leader-bruntwood-and-bruntwood-scitech-ceo-chris-oglesby/). Strong on clean growth / science-park infrastructure angle.

name: Chris Thomas
profile: Chris Thomas co-founded T and R Pastoral with Bob Rowe in 1988, trading livestock before moving into feedlots and meat processing. The business bought the Murray Bridge abattoir in 1999 and became Thomas Foods International. It is now Australia's largest wholly family-owned red-meat processor, with five plants, 3,000+ staff and exports to 85+ countries. Day-to-day management has passed to the next generation.
interesting_fact: After a January 2018 fire destroyed the Murray Bridge processing line, TFI built a replacement plant on a new site about 8 km away, completed in May 2023.
deep_cut_fact: The company began in 1988 as 'T and R Pastoral', named for founders Thomas and Rowe, as a livestock-trading business before it processed any meat itself.
current_role: Co-founder and family owner, Thomas Foods International (Murray Bridge, South Australia)
research_notes: Low-profile and largely retired from management; the managing director is a family member. The company site blocked automated access, so I could not extract a contact email. He was on Hurun's list only from 2018 to 2021. I could not verify current status because the web-search budget ran out.

name: Dinesh Chandra Agarwal
profile: Computer-science graduate of HBTI Kanpur who worked at CMC, C-DOT and HCL (moving to the US in 1992), then quit after India launched public internet in Aug 1995 to start IndiaMART from a house in Patparganj, Delhi, in 1996 with ~Rs 40,000 seed money. IndiaMART pivoted from exporters to Indian MSMEs, listed in 2019, and dominates India's online B2B marketplace.
interesting_fact: He decided to quit HCL in the US the day India announced public internet access (15 Aug 1995); IndiaMART began as an online directory of Indian exporters and now claims ~60% of India's online B2B marketplace.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from a trading family in Nanpara (UP), which he credits for keeping him grounded; his two favourite books are Freakonomics and Sun Tzu's Art of War, he looks forward to TiE's annual global retreats, and he supports Olympic Gold Quest.
current_role: Founder, Managing Director and CEO, IndiaMART InterMESH Ltd
public_contact: official_website: https://dineshagarwal.com | x: https://x.com/DineshAgarwal | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/indiamart/ | instagram: https://www.instagram.com/dineshchetna/

name: Eric Wu
appears_on: Hurun Global (2021); Hurun Global U40 (2021); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
education: Harvard Law School; Harvard University; National Taiwan University
profile: Eric Wu co-founded Opendoor in 2014, popularising 'iBuying' (instant cash offers for homes); it went public in 2020 and he served as CEO before leaving at the end of 2023 to build again. In May 2026 he launched NavigateAI with a $25m seed round led by Elad Gil (with Khosla, Fifth Wall, Lennar and Tishman Speyer). It is a real-time AI coach for trades and field workers that runs on phones and Meta glasses.
interesting_fact: NavigateAI's angel list reads like a founder roll-call: Brian Armstrong (Coinbase), Tony Xu (DoorDash), Logan Green (Lyft), Apoorva Mehta (Instacart) and others. Wu calls the product a 'second set of expert eyes' for field workers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Opendoor he co-founded Movity, a Y Combinator Winter 2010 startup surfacing neighborhood geodata for people moving home. Trulia bought it in December 2010, and he went on to run Trulia's geo and social products. He also co-founded RentWiki.com.
current_role: Founder, NavigateAI (San Francisco; AI copilots for construction/field workers, launched May 2026); co-founder and former CEO of Opendoor
research_notes: Very active as a founder and good for an entrepreneurship episode; the AI-for-skilled-trades angle ties to data-center and energy construction labor shortages. The Hurun billionaire listing was 2021 only, and his net worth is likely lower now. I found no verified personal email; NavigateAI is the route.

name: Geoffrey Guy
profile: British physician-pharmacologist (b. 1954, Barts-trained) who co-founded GW Pharmaceuticals in 1998 and developed the first FDA-approved cannabis-derived medicine, Epidiolex (2018), plus Sativex for MS spasticity. Jazz Pharmaceuticals bought GW for US$7.2B in 2021, when he stepped down. He now funds and leads quantum-biology research in medicine through The Guy Foundation.
interesting_fact: GW's Epidiolex (2018) was the first cannabis-derived drug approved by the US FDA; Guy has contributed to more than 200 clinical studies and wrote 'A Worthwhile Medicine' (2021).
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career at Napp Laboratories he helped develop slow-release morphine sulphate for pain; today his foundation runs a research programme on quantum biology (including light-and-health and space-health initiatives) and he has written a book titled 'Quantum Biology'.
current_role: Founder, The Guy Foundation Family Trust (quantum biology research charity, Dorset); former founder-chairman of GW Pharmaceuticals
research_notes: Engaged public intellectual on quantum biology; foundation hosts online lectures and meetings - good conversational hook (bioenergetics, mitochondria, light). Foundation is the best route.

profile: A St. Stephen's College, Delhi alumnus, Deepak Seth founded what became Pearl Global (formerly House of Pearl Fashions) and built it into one of India's largest listed apparel exporters and supply-chain groups, with ~25 factories in India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and Guatemala supplying Gap, Ralph Lauren, PVH, Inditex and Primark. research_notes: Input name 'Sanjeev Kumar' = Sanjeev Kumar Bijli. Gives frequent trade-press interviews (Hollywood Reporter India, Bollywood Hungama); media-friendly. Energy/data-centre angle weak.

name: Vidya Rashesh Shah
profile: Co-founding figure of India's Edelweiss financial group, where she was earlier CFO, after 11 years in investment banking (ICICI, Peregrine, NM Rothschild). In 2008 she founded EdelGive Foundation, Edelweiss's philanthropy arm, which she ran as CEO until 2021 and now chairs, building collaboratives in education, women's empowerment, climate and migration.
interesting_fact: EdelGive pioneered a 'zero-cost platform' model: besides its own grants it channels funding from other institutional and corporate donors to small and mid-sized NGOs without taking a fee.
deep_cut_fact: An IIM-Ahmedabad MBA, she spent her first 11 years in investment banking at ICICI, Peregrine and NM Rothschild before moving into philanthropy; she also sits on boards including Agastya International Foundation, Janaagraha and Mann Deshi Foundation.
current_role: Executive Chairperson, EdelGive Foundation; Non-Executive Director, Edelweiss Financial Services
public_contact: official_website: https://www.edelgive.org/ | x: https://x.com/EdelGive (foundation account) | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/edelgive-foundation/ (foundation page)
research_notes: Best route is via EdelGive Foundation. A third-party directory lists edelgive@edelweissfin.com (https://philanthropywomen.org/philanthropy-women-funder-database/edelgive-foundation/) but it is not confirmed on EdelGive's own site. Since April 2021 Naghma Mulla is EdelGive CEO.

name: Bharat H Parajia
profile: Bharat Himatlal Parajia is a Singapore-based investor and part of the promoter group of India's IIFL (India Infoline) financial-services group, previously listed as a managing director of IIFL Asia. Third-party filings data show stakes of ~4.4% in IIFL Finance, ~3.6% in IIFL Securities and ~2% in 5paisa Capital (2023).
interesting_fact: Holds stakes across three listed IIFL-family companies (IIFL Finance, IIFL Securities and online broker 5paisa Capital).
current_role: Co-promoter / significant shareholder of the IIFL group (IIFL Finance, IIFL Securities, 5paisa); Singapore-based
research_notes: Low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Best route is likely via IIFL group corporate communications. Alive status not confirmed by a recent public source.

name: Rajvi H Mariwala
profile: Rajvi (Raj) Mariwala is the daughter of Marico founder-chairman Harsh Mariwala and part of the promoter family behind the Parachute/Saffola consumer-goods group. In 2015 she co-founded with her father the Mariwala Health Initiative, which funds rights-based, community-led mental-health work across India; she also advocates for animal rights.
interesting_fact: Under her leadership MHI shifted to a psychosocial, 'nothing about us, without us' funding model; per Fortune India it partnered with 33 NGOs on 37 projects in 20 states over seven years.
deep_cut_fact: She describes philanthropy as 'an exercise in redistribution of wealth' and says MHI blended her father's focus on service-delivery innovation with her own rights-and-agency approach; early partners included iCALL counselling and the Bapu Trust in Pune bastis.
current_role: Director, Mariwala Health Initiative (mental-health grant-maker); member of the Marico promoter family
public_contact: office_email: contact@mariwalahealthinitiative.org | press_email: comms@mariwalahealthinitiative.org | official_website: https://mhi.org.in/ | x: https://twitter.com/mariwalahealth | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/mariwalahealth/
research_notes: Goes by 'Raj Mariwala' professionally. Best route is via MHI comms. Her public focus is mental health/queer-affirmative and animal advocacy rather than business, so podcast fit is indirect.

name: Prava Ranjan Patnaik
profile: Prava Ranjan Patnaik is listed as managing director of Falcon Marine Exports, a Bhubaneswar, Odisha-based shrimp/seafood exporter, and of other Falcon Group companies. The group was founded in 1985 by Tara Ranjan Patnaik and grew into one of India's largest shrimp exporters, using thousands of contract farms. It later added real estate and other businesses.
interesting_fact: Falcon Marine Exports' promoters (the Patnaik family) appeared in the 2024 Hurun India Rich List at about Rs 4,900 crore. The company won MPEDA's award as India's highest-value seafood exporter over 15 years (2017).
current_role: Managing Director, Falcon Marine Exports Ltd (per company-registry aggregators, DIN 00417793); also director of Falcon Holdings, Falcon Finance and Falcon Real Estate
research_notes: Almost all press covers group founder Tara Ranjan Patnaik and his son Parthajeet; Prava's exact relationship to them (likely a family member) is not confirmed in sources found. Very low public profile. No official website or published contact found; outreach via Falcon Group HQ (Falcon House, Bhubaneswar) or the Tara/Parthajeet Patnaik side is likely the best route.

name: R Lakshmanan
profile: Founded Shanthi Feeds in 1988 as a small poultry farm in Pappampatti, near Coimbatore; it grew into an integrated broiler business (hatcheries, poultry and cattle feed mills, processing, soya/corn cultivation) with capacity of ~47 million birds a year, and also runs wind energy projects.
interesting_fact: Shanthi Feeds has set up more than 1,000 contract broiler farms over 30 years and in 2019 commissioned a Petersime single-stage hatchery able to hatch 14+ million eggs a year; the group also invests in wind energy.
deep_cut_fact: He started the business in Pappampatti, a rain-shadow area so dry that conventional farming was limited, and expanded with the explicit aim of creating paid work in the village.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Shanthi Feeds (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu)
research_notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Alive status not confirmed though a 'Lakshmanan, Shanthi Hatcheries' chaired a Poultry Farmers Regulatory Committee summit in Nov 2025 (businessminutes.in). Wind-energy angle may suit the energy podcast. Best route: company website/office in Coimbatore.

name: Nara Bhuvaneswari
profile: Runs Heritage Foods, the Hyderabad-based listed dairy company, which she joined in 1994 as a whole-time director before becoming Vice Chairperson & MD; she is its largest individual shareholder (~24%). She also leads the NTR Memorial Trust (healthcare, blood banks, education, clean water) and is the daughter of N. T. Rama Rao.
interesting_fact: In November 2025 she received the Institute of Directors (UK) Distinguished Fellowship in London for her social work through the NTR Trust, while Heritage Foods won the Golden Peacock Award for Excellence in Corporate Governance 2025.
deep_cut_fact: She took charge of NTR Trust Bhavan in June 2014; the trust she leads runs NABH-accredited blood centres in Hyderabad, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati, and its NTR Sujala scheme supplies clean drinking water to about 18 lakh people in AP and Telangana.
current_role: Vice Chairperson & Managing Director, Heritage Foods Ltd; Managing Trustee, NTR Memorial Trust
research_notes: Wife of Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu; politically high-profile family, so outreach is best via Heritage Foods corporate office or NTR Trust. Heritage's site blocks some automated fetches.

name: Nemish S Shah
profile: Mumbai investor who co-founded ENAM with Vallabh Bhanshali in 1984. ENAM began as a broking firm, then grew into a leading IPO investment bank. ENAM's banking and broking businesses were merged into Axis Bank. Shah now runs ENAM Holdings' treasury and long-term proprietary investing in Indian equities, using bottom-up fundamental research.
interesting_fact: He is widely credited with pioneering equity investment research in India. ENAM's investment banking arm went on to top India's IPO league tables.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a B.Com from Lala Lajpat Rai College (Mumbai University) in 1977. He reads Jain scriptures, follows cricket and loves music, and peers say his spirituality balances his investing.
current_role: Co-founder, ENAM Holdings (manages treasury and proprietary capital); Governing Body member, FLAME University
research_notes: Very low public profile and no personal social media found. ENAM founders also set up FLAME University in Pune, which may be a warmer route in. No published office email found.

name: B Umapathy Reddy
profile: Bathina Umapathy Reddy co-founded BGR (originally B Girijapathi Reddy & Co.) in 1988 with Girijapathy Reddy and I. Sudhakara Reddy. It is now a Hyderabad-based contract-mining and Mine Developer & Operator (MDO) group running coal and mineral projects for NTPC, CCL, Vedanta and Hindalco. He still leads the group alongside the second generation.
interesting_fact: BGR says it runs 900+ dump trucks and 8,000+ employees across 7 states. It has won a string of coal MDO contracts, including NTPC's Kerendari 'A' (2023) and Badam (2024) and Hindalco's Meenakshi (2025).
deep_cut_fact: BGR began in 1988 as a small partnership firm, B Girijapathi Reddy & Co., set up by three co-founders including Umapathy Reddy. It became a company only in 2011, and by FY2022-23 it was moving about 29 million tonnes of coal a year.
current_role: Founder director / head (listed as Managing Director in registry data), BGR Mining & Infra Ltd, Hyderabad
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.bgrmining.com/contact | official_website: https://www.bgrmining.com/ | linkedin: https://linkedin.com/company/bgrmining (company page)
research_notes: Low personal media profile. The company publishes only a careers email (careers@bgrmining.com) and a Hyderabad office line, so the contact form or the corporate office is the best route. Relevant to the energy angle as a coal mining contractor.

name: Ghisulal Rathod
profile: Ghisulal Dhanraj Rathod founded the Mumbai-based Cello plastics group, starting with plastic bangles and PVC footwear in Goregaon before building the Cello brand of housewares, writing instruments and furniture; Wim Plast (Cello moulded furniture) was a listed group company. The business is now run by his sons Pradeep and Pankaj and grandson Gaurav via Cello World Ltd (listed 2023).
interesting_fact: Cello started in 1967 with seven machines and about sixty workers making plastic bangles and PVC footwear in Goregaon, Mumbai, and grew into one of India's best-known consumerware brands.
deep_cut_fact: After seeing American households store food in round plastic containers on a US trip, he launched insulated casseroles in India in the late 1980s, a product that became a Cello staple.
current_role: Founder, Cello group; former non-executive chairman of Wim Plast Ltd (1988-2020)
public_contact: ir_email: grievance@celloworld.com | office_email: wimplast@celloworld.com | official_website: https://corporate.celloworld.com/
research_notes: Patriarch, likely elderly and not public-facing; sources differ on founding dates (1962/1967/1974). Day-to-day leadership is son Pradeep Rathod (CMD, Cello World), the more practical outreach target. Reports say Wim Plast was being merged into Cello Consumer Products (2026, unverified).

name: Mayur Mukundlal Desai
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2018 (approx. US$144m) with wealth from Infibeam Avenues, the Ahmedabad fintech/e-commerce company behind the CCAvenue payment gateway. Infibeam's March 2019 shareholding filing lists 'Mayur Mukundlal Desai' as a public shareholder holding more than 1%. Not a director or executive of the company.
interesting_fact: Appears in Infibeam Avenues' official March 2019 shareholding pattern among public shareholders owning more than 1% of the company.
current_role: Shareholder (>1%), Infibeam Avenues Ltd (now AvenuesAI)
research_notes: Passive investor in Infibeam rather than founder (founders are Vishal Mehta and Vishwas Patel). No public profile found; identity beyond the shareholding filing unverified. Company was renamed AvenuesAI in 2025-26.

name: Uday J Desai
profile: Uday Jayant Desai is listed as founder director and managing director of Frost International Ltd, a Mumbai commodity-trading company (incorporated 1995, also with a Kanpur presence) that traded a large portfolio of agri and other commodities. Hurun ranked him in 2017-18. Registry sites show the company under insolvency resolution (CIRP) as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Frost International traded a broad commodity portfolio out of Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex and Kanpur; company material credits Uday J. Desai as founder director who grew its trade volumes.
current_role: Founder director / managing director, Frost International Ltd (Mumbai commodity trader) per company registry listings
research_notes: Thin, aggregator-only sourcing; identity only partly confirmed. Company reportedly in insolvency (CIRP) per IBBI listing https://ibbi.gov.in/claims/pub-process/U05001MH1995PLC243081 - likely no longer UHNW; low-priority outreach target. No published contacts found.

name: Ajay S Shriram
profile: Indian industrialist who leads DCM Shriram, the diversified group spanning chloro-vinyl chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, Shriram Farm Solutions and Bioseed. A B.Com graduate of Sydenham College, Bombay, he also attended Harvard Business School's Program for Management Development, and he was president of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in 2014-15.
interesting_fact: He chairs the Governing Body of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), the Delhi college his family founded, and chairs the board of IIM Sirmaur.
deep_cut_fact: Before leading CII, he was President and Chairman of the Paris-based International Fertilizer Industry Association (2009-11), and earlier he chaired the Fertilizer Association of India (2000-02).
current_role: Chairman & Senior Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd (New Delhi)
research_notes: The press email is DCM Shriram's published Corporate Communication/CSR contact (Ms. Aman Pannu). The group's chlor-alkali business is power-intensive and runs captive power plants, which could make a good energy angle.

name: Ajit S Shriram
profile: Ajit S. Shriram is the youngest of three brothers (with Ajay and Vikram Shriram) running DCM Shriram, the Delhi-based conglomerate spun out of the old DCM Group in 1990, spanning chlor-alkali chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, Bioseed, Fenesta windows and PVC. He has served on the board for about two decades.
interesting_fact: He is a past President of the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) and a member of the CII National Council on Agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: After a commerce degree from Osmania University, Hyderabad, he did his MBA at IMD Lausanne; his company bio lists his passions as travel, photography and theatre.
current_role: Joint Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd.
public_contact: press_email: amanpannu@dcmshriram.com | contact_form: https://www.dcmshriram.com/contact | official_website: https://www.dcmshriram.com
research_notes: Press email is the published Corporate Communication/CSR contact (Ms. Aman Pannu). Energy angle: DCM Shriram is a large captive power and chlor-alkali (energy-intensive) operator.

name: Vikram S Shriram
profile: Member of the Shriram business family, Vikram S. Shriram co-runs DCM Shriram, a Delhi-based conglomerate in chlor-alkali/vinyl chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, agri-inputs and captive power, alongside elder brother and Chairman Ajay S. Shriram. A chartered accountant, he has been Vice Chairman & MD since 2001.
interesting_fact: He is a qualified chartered accountant (Associate Member, ICAI) with a B.Com (Hons) from Calcutta University, and the company bio notes his strong aptitude for finance.
deep_cut_fact: After training across SRF Group functions, he joined Shriram Bearings Ltd in Ranchi in 1981 as senior management (works, marketing, general management); he studied at Mayo College, Ajmer, and lists swimming and cooking as hobbies.
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd (since Sept 2001)
public_contact: office_email: response@dcmshriram.com | ir_email: shares@dcmshriram.com | official_website: https://www.dcmshriram.com
research_notes: response@dcmshriram.com is the general corporate email in 2022-24 annual reports; shares@ appears in a 2022 AGM notice (shareholder services). DCM Shriram has a large captive power business - an angle for an energy podcast. Not to be confused with DCM Shriram Industries (separate company).

name: Pravinbhai Patel
profile: Pravinbhai Vithalbhai Patel is a second-generation leader of Patel Infrastructure, the Vadodara road, highway, bridge and irrigation contractor founded by his father Vitthalbhai Gobarbhai Patel in 1972. He long served as chairman alongside his brother, MD Arvind Patel; the company has filed for an IPO (Rs 400 cr fresh issue) with SEBI.
interesting_fact: Patel Infrastructure was among the contractors for the first phase of the Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway, and its highway arm won a Silver Award at India's National Highway Awards for Excellence 2018.
current_role: Whole-time Director (long-time Chairman) of Patel Infrastructure Ltd, Vadodara
research_notes: Title conflict: older sources (Craft, MarketScreener, CEO Magazine) call him Chairman & Whole-time Director; the current patelinfra.com About page lists brother Arvindbhai as Chairman and Pravin V. Patel as Whole-time Director. A 2015 Volvo CE case study quotes the family on PIPL's 'humble beginnings as a small family business in the 1970s'. Low public profile.

name: Arvind Patel
profile: Arvindbhai Vithalbhai Patel runs Patel Infrastructure, the Vadodara road/highway EPC contractor founded in 1972 by his father Vithalbhai Patel as a builder of government buildings and hotels; his brother Pravinbhai Patel is chairman. The firm became a major NHAI contractor (Delhi–Vadodara, Ganga expressways) and has filed a draft prospectus for an IPO.
interesting_fact: In May 2025 Patel Infrastructure laid 34.24 lane-km (20,105 t) of bituminous concrete in 24 hours on UP's Ganga Expressway, a record recognised by Golden Book, India Book and Asia Book of Records; Patel called it a contribution to nation-building.
deep_cut_fact: Patel received Built India Magazine's 'Legendary award for outstanding work in road construction'; in an NBM&CW interview he argued technology 'will not replace employees, rather, it will alter the working pattern at construction sites.'
current_role: Managing Director, Patel Infrastructure Ltd (Vadodara, Gujarat) — note one registry record shows his MD term ending Oct 2024; company is pursuing an IPO (DRHP filed)
research_notes: Shares Hurun listing with brother Pravinbhai Patel. Company website (has Contact Us / Media Corner pages) blocks scripted access; check it manually for press/IR email, or the DRHP's compliance-officer contact. Confirm whether he is still MD given the Oct 2024 registry end date.

name: Ramesh Chauhan
profile: Indian beverage entrepreneur (b. 1940) of the Parle family. Parle bought the Bisleri brand from an Italian entrepreneur in 1969 and he built it into India's dominant bottled-water brand; he also created Thums Up, Limca, Gold Spot and Maaza, sold to Coca-Cola in 1993. After talks to sell Bisleri to Tata Consumer ended in 2023, daughter Jayanti (Vice Chairperson) and CEO Angelo George run it.
interesting_fact: After Coca-Cola left India in 1977 he launched Thums Up and built it into India's leading cola; Coca-Cola later bought Parle's soft-drink brands (Thums Up, Limca, Gold Spot, Maaza, Citra) in 1993.
deep_cut_fact: Known as 'RJC' to friends, he holds a double major in mechanical engineering and business management from MIT, returned home at 22, and introduced bottled mineral water to India at 27. His 2013 biography 'Thunder Unbottled, From Thums Up to Bisleri' was written by friend and ex-Newsweek UN bureau chief Patricia J Sethi.
current_role: Chairman, Bisleri International Pvt. Ltd. (Mumbai)
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.bisleri.com/contact-us | office_email: wecare@bisleri.co.in (Bisleri general customer contact, not personal) | official_website: https://www.bisleri.com/ramesh-chauhan
research_notes: Private company; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Bisleri corporate communications. Biography source: https://www.afaqs.com/39024_ramesh-j-chauhan-unveils-his-biography

name: Khushboo Rajiv Poddar
profile: Khushboo Poddar is part of the promoter family behind Balkrishna Industries (BKT), Mumbai-based maker of off-highway tyres for agriculture, construction and mining, chaired by Arvind Poddar with Rajiv Poddar as Joint MD. Her listed wealth stems from the family's BKT shareholding. MarketScreener lists her as a former management-committee member; a media report calls her joint MD, unconfirmed by filings.
interesting_fact: BKT, the source of the family wealth, is a global off-highway tyre specialist serving customers in 163 countries and runs an extensive sports-sponsorship programme.
current_role: Member of the Poddar promoter family of Balkrishna Industries (BKT); role at the company not confirmed in filings
research_notes: Very private; almost no public footprint of her own. Board filings name Arvind and Rajiv Poddar, not her. Best route is via BKT corporate channels. Role claim (joint MD) comes only from a tabloid-style DNA India piece — treat as unverified.

name: Suresh Venkatachari
profile: Chennai/US-based serial IT entrepreneur who founded 8K Miles Software in 2008 (renamed SecureKloud Technologies), a cloud, security and healthcare-IT services firm; earlier founded SRM Technologies (1999). He also served as CEO of Nasdaq-listed spinoff Healthcare Triangle (2019-2023) and returned as SecureKloud chairman & CEO in 2024.
interesting_fact: Over 35 years in IT services, he has founded several technology companies, three of which went public.
deep_cut_fact: Back in 2011, when 8K Miles was a young cloud startup, he told YourStory that 'security in cloud is one of the biggest concerns' of customers, foreshadowing the company's later rebrand to SecureKloud.
current_role: Chairman & CEO, SecureKloud Technologies Ltd (formerly 8K Miles Software Services), since Feb 2024
public_contact: office_email: info@securekloud.com | ir_email: cs@securekloud.com | official_website: https://www.securekloud.com
research_notes: Also known as Suresh V. Chari. Company has had governance/audit controversies in the past; keep outreach focused on cloud/healthcare-IT and data infrastructure.

name: Vishnukant Bhutada
profile: Vishnukant C. Bhutada is a first-generation pharma entrepreneur who founded Shilpa Medicare in his hometown of Raichur in 1987, at age 22, right after his B.Pharm. The company started with antibiotics, moved into oncology APIs and generics around 2000, and now sells globally. He remains Managing Director; Omprakash Inani is chairman.
interesting_fact: He came from a cotton-trading family but chose to build a pharma company in Raichur rather than a metro city: "I wanted to develop the region where I grew up." He started with Rs 50 lakh and 20 staff, and took the company public in 1994.
deep_cut_fact: His early export push targeted Bangladesh, which other Indian pharma firms ignored ("Nobody was focusing on Bangladesh back then"). Before a USFDA inspection of one API line, he added two more lines so inspectors would review all three at once.
current_role: Managing Director, Shilpa Medicare Ltd (Raichur, Karnataka)
public_contact: office_email: info@vbshilpa.com | ir_email: cs@vbshilpa.com | official_website: https://www.vbshilpa.com
research_notes: Low media profile. info@vbshilpa.com is the general company email. cs@vbshilpa.com is the company secretary's address (Ritu Tiwary), so the best route is a general corporate enquiry. His son Keshav Bhutada runs the subsidiary Shilpa Pharma Life Sciences.

name: Vijay S Nair
profile: Vijay S. Nair (Vijayasankaran Sivaraman Nair) founded Visen Industries in Mumbai in 1985 to make water-based polymer emulsions, starting with a 500-tonne-a-year plant at Tarapur. Visen now supplies binders to the paint, textile, adhesive and construction industries from plants in Tarapur, Silvassa, Jammu and Chennai plus a UAE unit; he remains CMD, with family members Cherry and Rohnit Nair on the board.
interesting_fact: Visen started in 1985 with capacity of just 500 tonnes a year at Tarapur near Mumbai; by the late 2000s it was producing about 60,000 tonnes a year across two plants with turnover over US$50m.
deep_cut_fact: In his 'From the Director's Desk' note he writes: 'I began this company with nothing but a handful of dreams and a drive to make it big in the industry... It still takes me by surprise to see how far Visen has come.'
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Visen Industries Ltd (Mumbai)
public_contact: official_website: https://www.visen.net/ | office_email: info@visen.net (general / company secretary contact) | ir_email: info@visen.net (Secretarial Dept., Ms. Binita Gosalia, Company Secretary) | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/visen-industries-ltd- | x: https://twitter.com/VisenIndustires
research_notes: Unlisted public company (CIN U24100MH1985PLC037350). Website footer is dated 2018, so plant list and contacts may be stale. Corporate contacts only (no personal channel found). Director Cherry V. Nair has given trade-press interviews (Indian Chemical News, 2022) and may be a route in. LinkedIn/X are the company's accounts, not his.

name: Atit Agarwal
profile: Atit Omprakash Agarwal is a member of the Agarwal family that owns and manages Responsive Industries, a BSE/NSE-listed Mumbai maker of PVC/vinyl, SPC and LVT flooring, synthetic leather and (via Axiom Cordages) ropes. He chaired the company until 2018; the family business has since been fronted by Rishabh Agarwal.
interesting_fact: Responsive Industries describes itself as India's No.1 LVP/SPC flooring maker, with plants in India, Vietnam and Thailand exporting to 70+ countries; the family moved from ropes into PVC flooring in the early 1990s.
current_role: Former Non-Executive Chairman, Responsive Industries Ltd (Mumbai) - chairmanship ended 2018; current role not confirmed
public_contact: office_email: office@responsiveindustries.com | contact_form: https://responsiveindustries.com/contact | official_website: https://responsiveindustries.com
research_notes: Low public profile; little press coverage of Atit personally. Insider profiles (MarketScreener) show chairmanship ending 2018-09-30. Company contacts are corporate, not personal. Best route probably via company office or Rishabh Agarwal.

name: Vijay Darda
profile: Vijay Jawaharlal Darda (b. 1950, Yavatmal) is the elder son of freedom fighter Jawaharlal Darda, who launched the Marathi daily Lokmat in 1971. He built Lokmat into a multi-language media group and served three Rajya Sabha terms for Maharashtra. He remains group chairman, writes columns and has published books such as 'Ringside' (2023) and 'The Churn' (2025).
interesting_fact: He won his first Rajya Sabha seat in 1998 as an independent, defeating the official Congress candidate, before Congress nominated him for the 2004 and 2010 terms.
deep_cut_fact: His long-running 'dream project' is the 284 km Wardha-Yavatmal-Nanded railway line serving his home district; by 2021 he said he had pursued it for 13 years and discussed it with eleven Railway Ministers.
current_role: Chairman, Lokmat Media Group (Lokmat newspapers, Nagpur/Mumbai); former Rajya Sabha MP (1998-2016)
public_contact: official_website: https://www.vijaydarda.in/ | x: https://twitter.com/vijayjdarda | linkedin: http://www.linkedin.com/in/dardavijay | instagram: https://www.instagram.com/vijayjdarda/
research_notes: Active on social media and writes regularly, so reachable via his site/X. Be aware he and his son were defendants in a coal-block allocation case (2023 conviction reported, later acquittal reported by Lokmat Times); avoid the topic.

name: Nitin Raojibhai Desai
profile: Pune industrialist who heads Desai Brothers, a family group founded in Gujarat in 1901 that is one of India's largest bidi makers and diversified into food (Mother's Recipe pickles, acquired 2002), finance, hospitality and renewable energy. He has been an independent director of Zydus Lifesciences since 2011 and was on the Force Motors board 2014-2022.
interesting_fact: The Desai group traces back to 1901 in Gujarat, still makes about 70 million bidis a day, and bought the 'Mother's Recipe' pickle brand in 2002 for roughly Rs 6 crore before demerging food into Desai Foods in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He is a civil engineer with a master's in environmental engineering from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, and chairs The Poona Blind Men's Association; he was also President of Poona Club.
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Desai Brothers Ltd (Pune); Independent Director, Zydus Lifesciences
research_notes: Private family group; no published personal/office email found. Group's renewable-energy arm is a possible angle for the energy podcast. Route via Desai Brothers corporate office or Zydus company secretary.

name: Arpan Paul
profile: Arpan Paul heads SAJ Food Products, the Kolkata-based maker of Bisk Farm biscuits founded in 2000 by his father Krishnadas Paul, who launched it at age 60. Arpan took over as executive chairman after his father's death in 2020; the company has been reported at roughly Rs 2,000+ crore turnover.
interesting_fact: His father Krishnadas Paul started SAJ Food at age 60 after suffering a Rs 15 crore business loss, and grew Bisk Farm into one of eastern India's leading biscuit brands.
deep_cut_fact: The company name SAJ comes from the initials of Krishnadas Paul's three children - Sharmistha, Arpan and Jayeeta - so Arpan's own initial is in the company name.
current_role: Executive Chairman, SAJ Food Products Pvt Ltd (Bisk Farm), Kolkata
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.biskfarm.com/contact-us/ | office_email: customercare@biskfarm.com (company customer care, general) | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/saj-food-products-pvt-ltd/ (company page)

name: Hemant Kamala Jalan

name: Karthik Ganapathy
profile: IIT Bombay (EE '93) and IIM Bangalore (MBA '95) graduate who left Arthur Andersen's financial-services consulting practice to co-found BillDesk in 2000 with MN Srinivasu and Ajay Kaushal. BillDesk became India's leading bill-payment gateway; a $4.7bn sale to Prosus/PayU agreed in 2021 was later terminated (2022), and he remains co-founder and VP.
interesting_fact: BillDesk processed over Rs 12 trillion in digital transactions in 2023; when the Prosus deal was announced in 2021, the three co-founders were each expected to receive about $500m for their combined ~30% stake.
deep_cut_fact: Spent ~5 years at Arthur Andersen consulting for banks and brokers before BillDesk; lists tennis and reading as hobbies and his mantra as 'Be yourself, everybody else is already taken.' Fond of his IIT Bombay hostel-council and Mood Indigo days.
current_role: Co-founder and Vice President, BillDesk (IndiaIdeas.com Ltd), Mumbai
research_notes: Low-profile founder; rarely gives interviews. The Prosus/PayU acquisition was terminated in Oct 2022, so the founders retain their stake. Approach via BillDesk corporate or IIT Bombay / IIM Bangalore alumni networks. Bloomberg 2021 piece on the founders: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-09-02/three-men-pushing-50-reap-millions-selling-india-payments-firm

name: Sameer Padmakar Mulay
profile: Second-generation head of Ajeet Seeds, one of India's largest cotton-seed companies, founded by his father Padmakar Mulay. Joining when revenue was Rs 18 crore, he grew it to roughly Rs 700 crore by 2015, driven by the Bt cotton hybrid Ajeet 155, and diversified into bajra, corn, wheat, paddy and vegetable seeds.
interesting_fact: The Ajeet 155 Bt cotton hybrid (2006), developed with Mahyco-Monsanto technology, pulled the company back into profit by 2008 and became its breakout product.
deep_cut_fact: He originally aspired to be a civil engineer and join the family construction business, but a 1996 tea-time talk with his father steered him to the College of Agriculture, Pune (graduated 2001) and into seeds.
current_role: Managing Director, Ajeet Seeds Pvt Ltd (Aurangabad / Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar)
research_notes: Private company; corporate general email is the only published route. Agri focus, little energy/data-center angle.

name: N Srinivasan
profile: Narayanaswami Srinivasan (b. 1945, Tirunelveli) ran India Cements from 1989 and built it into a major South Indian cement producer. He was also a top cricket administrator: BCCI president and the ICC's first chairman. In December 2024 he sold the family's stake to UltraTech (Aditya Birla Group) and resigned as CEO & MD. He remains the figure most associated with Chennai Super Kings.
interesting_fact: After selling India Cements to UltraTech in 2024, he told staff the sale was driven by cost pressures, price wars and the inability to sell some land. The deal ended a family link to the company: his father, T.S. Narayanaswami, was one of India Cements' first employees.
deep_cut_fact: He has an MS in chemical engineering from the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago. He served two terms as Sheriff of Madras (1989–91), was president of the All India Chess Federation, and heads the Tamil Nadu Golf Federation.
current_role: Former VC & MD of India Cements (stepped down Dec 2024 after the UltraTech takeover). Promoter figure behind IPL team Chennai Super Kings.
research_notes: Well known in India because of cricket, and his cricket-administration years drew controversy, so outreach should stay on business and the industry. He has no personal website or social accounts that I could find. Best route is probably via Chennai Super Kings Cricket Ltd's corporate office. Source on his exit: https://www.dtnext.in/news/business/india-cements-promoter-n-srinivasan-steps-down-as-ultratech-completes-acquisition-816723

name: Sat Paul Singhla
profile: Sat Paul Singla (also spelled Singhla) is a civil engineer and first-generation entrepreneur who founded S P Singla Constructions in 1996 with no capital. The privately held firm specialises in river bridges, highways and metro work across ~15 Indian states and reported revenue of Rs 1,150 crore in FY2017, while remaining fully owned by him.
interesting_fact: His company built what it calls India's longest cable-stayed bridge, between Okha and Beyt Dwarka in Gujarat, plus an extradosed bridge across the Ganges between Aunta and Simaria in Bihar.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting out on his own he spent 12 years with small construction firms in Punjab and Haryana building river bridges in J&K, Punjab and Himachal; his first project as an entrepreneur was a small bridge over the Yamuna in 1996 worth just Rs 10 lakh.
current_role: Founder & Managing Director, S P Singla Constructions / SPS Construction India Pvt Ltd
research_notes: Private company, low media profile; Forbes India 'Built To Last' profile is the main press source. Registered office New Delhi, corporate office Panchkula (Haryana). Alive status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Sheela Ashwin Chiniwalla
profile: Listed on the Hurun India Rich List (2018-2019) with about US$132m, wealth attributed to Parle Products, the Mumbai biscuit maker (Parle-G) owned by the Chauhan family. Presumably a Chauhan family member/shareholder; no public profile found and she is not among the listed directors of Parle Products.
research_notes: Private family shareholder with no public footprint found. Parle Products current directors are Vijay, Ajay, Arup and Samar Chauhan; any approach would realistically go via the company (parleproducts.com).

name: SV Balasubramaniam
profile: Dr. S.V. Balasubramaniam, a chartered accountant and company secretary from Sangampalayam village near Coimbatore, founded the Bannari Amman Group, which grew from sugar in the early 1980s into distilleries, granite, wind power and education. The board re-appointed him as chairman of listed Bannari Amman Sugars in 2025.
interesting_fact: Bannari Amman Group started Tamil Nadu's first biodiesel plant (2007) and runs wind power alongside its sugar, alcohol and granite businesses, using molasses from sugar production for its distilleries.
deep_cut_fact: He hails from Sangampalayam village near Coimbatore and trained as both a chartered accountant and a company secretary before building the group; he also founded the Bannari Amman Institute of Technology in Sathyamangalam.
current_role: Chairman, Bannari Amman Sugars Ltd and founder-chairman, Bannari Amman Group (Coimbatore)
research_notes: Elderly founder; son B. Saravanan is MD. Energy angle: wind power, cogeneration, ethanol/biodiesel. Company secretary C. Palaniswamy signs filings; secretary@bannari.com also published in BRSR report.

name: Bhupinder Singh Manhas
profile: Bhupinder Singh Minhas (also spelled Manhas) founded Harman Finochem in 1983, an Indian maker and exporter of active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates (45+ APIs, 75+ countries served). The company is now run by family directors Harpreet Singh Minhas and Dr. Gurpreet Singh Minhas; he is presented on the company site as founder.
interesting_fact: Harman Finochem, which he founded in 1983, makes 45+ APIs including 10+ WHO essential medicines and supplies 75+ nations, with approvals from regulators such as Health Canada and Mexico's COFEPRIS.
deep_cut_fact: The company website quotes him as founder: 'At Harman Finochem, our work is guided by a simple principle: to foster health, happiness, and harmony in every life we touch, while staying true to our responsibility towards humanity.'
current_role: Founder, Harman Finochem Ltd (Mumbai/Aurangabad API manufacturer); not listed among current board directors
public_contact: office_email: info@harmanfinochem.com (company general) | contact_form: https://harmanfinochem.com/contact-us/ | x: https://x.com/HarmanFinochem (company) | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/harman-finochem-ltd/ (company)
research_notes: Name spelled 'Minhas' on company site. He does not appear among current registered directors (Inderjit Kaur, Harpreet, Gurpreet, Savreen Minhas), so he may have retired or passed away - status unverified. Very low public profile; approach via company.

name: Omprakash Inani
profile: Omprakash Tulsiram Inani is chairman and a promoter-shareholder of Shilpa Medicare, a Raichur-based maker of oncology APIs, formulations, biologics and CDMO services co-founded with MD Vishnukant Bhutada. With 35+ years in business, he oversees the company's plants and also runs a cotton business, Inok Cottons, in Raichur.
interesting_fact: Shilpa Medicare grew from Raichur, a cotton town in northern Karnataka, into one of India's leading suppliers of oncology active pharmaceutical ingredients; Inani still runs a cotton ginning business alongside it.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond pharma he is a Managing Committee member of the Karnataka State Cotton Association (Hubli), a council member of Raichur's Taranath Shikshana Samsthe (which runs a medical/dental/pharmacy academy), and a trustee of the Akhil Bhartiya Maheshwari Education Trust in Pune.
current_role: Chairman, Shilpa Medicare Ltd (Raichur, Karnataka); Managing Director, Inok Cottons Pvt Ltd
research_notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts or interviews found. Company website lists no press/IR email; route via company enquiry form or company secretary listed in BSE/NSE filings.

name: Vijaykumar Taparia
profile: V.K. Taparia is a member of the Taparia family that controls The Supreme Industries, India's largest plastics processor (piping systems, moulded furniture, packaging films, industrial products). A B.Com graduate, he has been on Supreme's board since October 1984 and was re-appointed Executive Director at the 2026 AGM with his term running to Sept 2027.
interesting_fact: He has sat on Supreme Industries' board for over four decades (appointed 29 Oct 1984) and personally holds about 244,890 Supreme shares per the 2025-26 annual report.
current_role: Executive (Whole-time) Director, The Supreme Industries Ltd (Mumbai)
public_contact: ir_email: investor@supreme.co.in | office_email: info@supreme.co.in | official_website: https://www.supreme.co.in
research_notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Company is fronted by Chairman & MD M.P. Taparia, so outreach via the company (registered office Raheja Chambers, Nariman Point, Mumbai) is the realistic route.

name: Sudhir Dhingra
profile: Sudhir Dhingra founded Orient Craft, one of India's largest garment exporters, supplying global fashion brands from factories around Gurugram. A law graduate from a Punjab cotton-farming family, he started exporting shirts in the 1970s and registered Orient Craft in 1978. The company has since rebuilt, declared itself debt-free and is expanding to Jharkhand.
interesting_fact: He told Outlook Business he wanted Orient Craft to be 'a 32-legged animal' that never depends on a single client; by 2014 it had revenue over Rs 1,151 crore and 30,000+ employees.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Fazilka near the Pakistan border, he studied law like his father and grandfather; after a 1972 US trip a London trader friend asked him for 1,000 'cheese cloth' shirts, made in Delhi at Rs 15 each - the Rs 15,000 he calls his 'seed capital'.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Orient Craft Ltd (Gurugram)
research_notes: Company site orientcraft.com was unreachable when checked; recent press releases (Newsvoir, May 2024+) cover the debt-free turnaround and Jharkhand/Ranchi expansion - a positive hook. Avoid the NPA/debt history.

name: Jimmy William Almeida
profile: Jimmy William Almeida Kashyap founded G.M. Breweries in Mumbai in 1981 and took it public in 1993. It is now Maharashtra's largest country-liquor maker, best known for its orange-flavoured G.M. Santra brand. He is still chairman and MD; shareholders reappointed him as MD through March 2028, and he owns a majority stake.
interesting_fact: G.M. Breweries started out bottling 200 cases a day. Its fully automatic plant at Virar, near Mumbai, can now turn out about 50,000 cases a day, and the company says it has paid a dividend every year since its 1993 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Country liquor used to be sold only in 750 ml and 375 ml bottles. According to the company, Almeida introduced the 180 ml bottle to the industry and was also the first to use PET (plastic) bottles for it.
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, G.M. Breweries Ltd (BSE 507488 / NSE GMBREW)
research_notes: Low media profile. Filings use several name forms: Jimmy Almeida, Jimmy William Almeida Kashyap. The company secretary, Sandeep Kutchhi, is the formal contact route (https://www.gmbreweries.com/overview.html).

name: Mridu Hari Dalmia
profile: Mridu Hari Dalmia is a son of industrialist Jaidayal Dalmia. With his brothers he controlled OCL India (formerly Orissa Cement), the cement and refractories company, and served as its Joint President. In 2015 he and his family trust sold a combined ~26.6% of OCL to Dalmia Cement (Bharat), a deal worth about US$165m. Hurun lists him as UAE-based.
interesting_fact: OCL changed its name from Orissa Cement Ltd in 1996 to reflect its non-cement ventures. After Jaidayal Dalmia's death it was controlled by his sons Ajay, Mridu and Raghu Hari Dalmia. OCL later became part of Dalmia Bharat.
current_role: Former Joint President, OCL India; family-business investor (current directorships unclear; listed by MarketScreener at First Capital India Ltd)
research_notes: Very low public profile; I found no interviews, website or social accounts. 'Alive' could not be confirmed from a recent source. His directorships are listed inconsistently across data aggregators, so check MCA filings (DIN 00009529) before approaching. 2015 stake-sale source: https://globalcement.com/news/8916-ocl-india-and-dalmia-bharat-merger-moves-ahead

name: Seema Suryavanshi
profile: Seema Suryavanshi is a promoter of Dilip Buildcon, the Bhopal road and infrastructure EPC contractor founded by her husband Dilip Suryavanshi, who is chairman. She was a director of the company from 2006 to 2010 and has sat on boards of group entities such as Suryavanshi Infrastructure and DBL toll-road SPVs.
interesting_fact: Dilip Buildcon grew from a small Bhopal contractor into one of India's largest road builders; she was on its board when it incorporated as a company in 2006.
current_role: Promoter/shareholder of Dilip Buildcon Ltd (Bhopal); former executive director (2006-2010)
research_notes: Low public profile. Best route is through the company (head of IR Gautam Jain is named on earnings calls) or via Dilip/Rohan Suryavanshi. Her current board status is unclear: sources conflict.

name: Sajan Kumar Bansal
profile: Commerce graduate who in 1981 incorporated Skipper Investments Ltd, later Skipper Steels and then Skipper Ltd. Starting with steel poles for telecom, he built Skipper into a major Indian maker of power transmission & distribution towers, plus polymer pipes; he still runs it as CMD.
interesting_fact: Skipper began as a small maker of 'Hamilton' steel poles for telecom connectivity and became a leading supplier of telecom poles and masts in India in the 1980s-90s before pivoting to power transmission towers.
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Skipper Limited (Kolkata)
public_contact: ir_email: investor.relations@skipperlimited.com | office_email: mail@skipperlimited.com | official_website: https://www.skipperlimited.com
research_notes: Skipper's T&D tower business is directly relevant to grid/energy-infrastructure topics. mail@ is the company's general inbox, not personal. Also Managing Trustee of Skipper Foundation.

name: Bharat Naresh Oberoi
name_chinese: 巴拉特·纳雷什·奥贝罗伊
profile: Bharat Oberoi is a promoter and Joint MD (since 2003) of Powerica, the Mumbai power-solutions firm his father Naresh Chander Oberoi founded in 1984. Powerica builds diesel generator sets and medium-speed large generators for standby/prime power (a key data-center backup market) and since 2008 has been a wind IPP and wind EPC/O&M contractor. He joined in 1994 and leads its marketing side.
interesting_fact: Powerica began as a diesel-generator business in 1984, added medium-speed large generators in 1996, and in 2008 moved into wind energy as an independent power producer, later adding wind EPC and O&M services.
current_role: Joint Managing Director and Promoter, Powerica Ltd (Mumbai)
public_contact: office_email: atp@powericaltd.com (Powerica DG-set business / head office) | office_email: wind@powericaltd.com (Powerica wind power division) | contact_form: https://www.powericaltd.com/contact-us#form | official_website: https://www.powericaltd.com
research_notes: Low public profile; last on Hurun India in 2018. Backup-power gensets for Indian data centers plus wind IPP make a natural energy/data-center angle. Route via company. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so no sourced personal deep-cut.

name: Rajas R Doshi
profile: Rajas Ratanchand Doshi, a civil engineer from the Walchand-Hirachand business family, has run The Indian Hume Pipe Company (est. 1926), a Mumbai-listed maker of concrete/steel water pipes and builder of water-supply and irrigation projects. He has spent 49+ years at the company and also sits on the boards of family foundations and the IMC Chamber of Commerce.
interesting_fact: Indian Hume Pipe was established in 1926 to manufacture and popularise Hume pipes in India, and today executes large urban and rural water-supply pipeline projects; Doshi has been its chairman for over three decades.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the bottom: a B.E. in civil engineering, he joined Indian Hume Pipe in 1981 as a Senior Executive at its Wadala (Mumbai) factory, then rose via Chief Engineer and General Manager to Joint MD in 1988 and CMD in 1994.
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, The Indian Hume Pipe Company Ltd (since 14 April 1994)
public_contact: ir_email: investors@indianhumepipe.com | office_email: info@indianhumepipe.com | official_website: https://indianhumepipe.com
research_notes: Company emails are corporate (general info / investor relations), not personal. Low media profile; a water-infrastructure angle fits better than energy/data centres.

name: Mohan Anand Chandavarkar
profile: Second-generation leader of FDC Limited, the Mumbai drugmaker his father Anand Chandavarkar started as Fairdeal Corporation (incorporated 1940) to import and distribute medicines and infant foods. FDC makes ~147 brands across anti-infectives, gastro, ophthalmology and more, and is best known for Electral oral rehydration salts. Long-time MD, he was re-designated Chairman & MD in April 2026.
interesting_fact: FDC began as an importer/distributor (Fairdeal Corporation) of drugs, infant foods and surgical appliances before turning manufacturer; its Electral ORS is one of India's best-known rehydration brands.
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, FDC Limited (Mumbai) since 1 April 2026
research_notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal social accounts found. Route via company secretarial/investor desk (Mumbai, tel published on filings). Pharma, not energy/data-center.

name: Anupama Menda
profile: Anupama Manoj Menda is a member of the Bengaluru Menda family behind RMZ Corp, the commercial real-estate group founded in 2002 by Arjun Menda and his sons Raj and Manoj; registry data lists her as a director of RMZ Corp Holdings since Dec 2019. Hurun India listed her (2017-18) with RMZ wealth. RMZ now spans real estate, digital infrastructure and private capital.
interesting_fact: RMZ, the family's company, now runs a Digital Infrastructure business line alongside real estate and private capital, relevant to a data-center podcast.
current_role: Director, RMZ Corp Holdings Pvt Ltd (Menda family, RMZ Corp, Bengaluru) per company registry listing
public_contact: press_email: akash.philip@rmz.com (Head of PR, RMZ) | office_email: contact@rmz.com | contact_form: https://rmz.com/contact-us
research_notes: Very low public profile. Likely the same person as 'Anu Menda', described as founder/managing trustee of RMZ Foundation (public art, Sustainable Health Initiative) in a Yale profile and wiki drafts, but that link is NOT confirmed; RMZ's 2021 CSR policy lists only Arjun, Raj and Manoj Menda as trustees. Verify before referencing foundation work. Registry source: qorpiq.com (RMZ Corp Holdings).

name: Neetu Menda
profile: Neetu (Raj) Menda is a member of the Menda family behind RMZ Corp, the Bengaluru commercial real-estate and infrastructure group founded in 2002 by Arjun Menda and sons Raj and Manoj Menda. Corporate registry data lists her as a director of RMZ group holding entities; she has no public executive role.
interesting_fact: RMZ's governing Supervisory Board is made up entirely of Menda family members (Raj, Manoj, Sidharth, Mihir and Kunal Menda).
current_role: Director, RMZ Corp Holdings Pvt Ltd and RMZ Realtors Pvt Ltd (Bengaluru)
research_notes: Very private; virtually no public profile. Registry names her 'Neetu Raj Menda' (likely Raj Menda's family) - relationship not confirmed. Best route is via RMZ corporate (contact@rmz.com).

name: Ajitbhai Champaklal Mehta
name_chinese: 阿吉特比·香巴拉尔·梅塔
profile: Gujarat businessman (Ajit Mehta) who served as non-executive chairman of Infibeam Avenues, the e-commerce and payments group (CCAvenue) founded in 2007 by his son Vishal Mehta. He is now chairman emeritus as the renamed AvenuesAI moves into enterprise AI infrastructure alongside payments.
interesting_fact: Infibeam Avenues renamed itself AvenuesAI. It is based in GIFT City, Gujarat, and says it is building 'enterprise-grade AI infrastructure' alongside its CCAvenue payments business.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, he spent about 20 years in textiles, chemicals, building materials and construction, then more than 16 years in the automobile industry.
current_role: Chairman Emeritus & Non-Executive Director, AvenuesAI Limited (formerly Infibeam Avenues Ltd), Gandhinagar, India
public_contact: press_email: corpcom@avenuesai.com | ir_email: ir@avenuesai.com | official_website: https://www.avenuesai.com
research_notes: Low public profile. Most interviews go to his son Vishal Mehta (Chairman & MD). Best route is the company's corporate communications. The Hurun 2018 wealth figure probably reflects family holdings.

name: Sudhir Mohanlal Jatia
name_chinese: 苏迪尔·莫汉拉尔·贾蒂亚
profile: Mumbai-based luggage industry veteran who previously ran VIP Industries as MD, then acquired control of Safari Industries in 2011 (MD since April 2012). He turned Safari into a fast-growing challenger brand by shifting to soft and polycarbonate luggage, backpacks (Genius, Genie) and online channels; his wealth is his Safari stake.
interesting_fact: After leaving VIP Industries, India's largest luggage maker, he built rival Safari from about Rs 67 crore revenue in FY12 to roughly INR 5.7bn by 2018, nearly a tenfold increase.
deep_cut_fact: Rather than build a new Rs 40-50 crore plant, he converted Safari's existing Halol factory to polycarbonate luggage, lifting capacity from 27,000 to 80,000 pieces a month for about Rs 22 crore; he also turned down a PE offer that would have made him a minority holder and relisted Safari on the NYSE.
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Safari Industries (India) Ltd
public_contact: ir_email: investor@safari.in | office_email: corporate@safari.in | official_website: https://www.safaribags.com/about-us
research_notes: Studied commerce at Mumbai University and attended Harvard Business School's Owner/President Management program (per Safari site). Also a director of the Association for Development of Luggage and Accessories. Manufacturing-localisation angle (China sourcing to India) could suit the podcast.

name: Vasant Laxminarayan Rathi
name_chinese: 瓦桑特·拉斯米纳雷恩·拉蒂
profile: V. L. Rathi, a pharmacist turned enzyme entrepreneur, co-founded Rathi Papains (1978), set up Cal-India Foods in the US (1985) and has been with Advanced Enzyme Technologies since 1993. The Thane-based enzyme and probiotics maker listed in India in 2016; from the US he runs its American subsidiaries.
interesting_fact: Advanced Enzymes grew from a family papain business into one of India's largest enzyme makers, with US and European arms. It owns Germany's evoxx technologies in Monheim am Rhein.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture, Rathi Papains (1978), made enzymes from papain, the protein-digesting enzyme taken from papaya latex. He trained as a pharmacist (B.Pharm, Nagpur University) and earned an MS at the University of Hawaii.
current_role: Promoter and Non-Executive Director, Advanced Enzyme Technologies Ltd (NSE: ADVENZYMES); heads its US subsidiaries
research_notes: Categorized as Chemicals/Petrochemicals 'energy', but the business is industrial and nutritional enzymes, so the fit for an energy podcast is weak (enzymes are used in biofuel/biogas, which could be an angle). Low media profile; route via the US subsidiaries (Cal-India Foods / AST Enzymes in California) or the company's general email.

name: Satish Parakh
profile: Civil engineer who joined the Ashoka Group in 1982 and rose to Managing Director of Ashoka Buildcon, one of India's largest highway developers (EPC plus 35+ PPP/BOT road projects). He led its diversification into power transmission/distribution EPC, railways and city gas distribution; his wealth stems from his shareholding in the listed company.
interesting_fact: Ashoka Buildcon was an early mover in India's build-operate-transfer (BOT) road model from the 1990s and has even built a road network for the Housing Development Corporation in the Maldives.
deep_cut_fact: His association with Ashoka began in 1982 and he has received the 'Industry Doyen' award from the Construction Industry Development Council; in interviews he credits the company's in-house highway research facility and its policy of avoiding 'ambitious bidding'.
current_role: Managing Director, Ashoka Buildcon Ltd (Nashik, India)
public_contact: ir_email: investors@ashokabuildcon.com | pr_agency: Stellar IR Advisors (investor relations advisor) - vgaurang@stellar-ir.com | official_website: https://www.ashokabuildcon.com
research_notes: Power T&D EPC business is the energy angle. Low public profile beyond trade-press interviews (NBM&CW, Construction World).

name: Manoj Kumar
profile: Manoj (Kumar) Gyanchandani is the elder son of RSPL founder-chairman Murli Dhar Gyanchandani and a promoter/whole-time director of RSPL Ltd (since 2008), maker of Ghadi detergent. The Kanpur-based group has diversified into dairy (Namaste India), footwear (Red Chief), real estate and 50+ MW of wind/solar power; Manoj runs the dairy arm.
interesting_fact: RSPL operates wind and solar plants across India generating over 50.1 MW of renewable energy, alongside its FMCG business that employs 25,000+ people.
deep_cut_fact: Ghadi broke into a Nirma/Surf-dominated market by making its detergent white (rivals were yellow or blue), with the tagline 'Pehle istemaal karein phir vishwas karein' (First use it, then trust it).
current_role: Whole-time Director, RSPL Ltd (RSPL Group, Kanpur); oversees the group's dairy business
research_notes: Hurun lists him as 'Manoj Kumar'; company registry (DIN 00049387) shows him as Manoj (Kumar) Gyanchandani, whole-time director of RSPL Ltd. Family is notably low-profile; only the general corporate inbox is published. RSPL renewable-energy arm is a possible energy-podcast angle.

name: Rahul Gyanchandani
profile: Second-generation leader of Kanpur-based RSPL Group, founded in 1988 by Murli Dhar and Bimal Kumar Gyanchandani with Ghadi detergent, now one of India's largest detergent brands. As Joint MD he fronts Ghadi's marketing (e.g. the Madhuri Dixit 'Vishwas Ki Pariksha' campaign) and launches such as Ghadi Rapid Wash liquid detergent.
interesting_fact: Beyond detergent, RSPL has diversified into dairy (Namaste India), footwear, real estate and renewable energy, operating wind and solar plants across India generating over 50 MW.
deep_cut_fact: RSPL began as Rohit Surfactants Pvt. Ltd. in 1988; in 2006 four family detergent companies, including one named Rahul Detergents Pvt. Ltd., were merged into RSPL, and Ghadi Industries was folded in in 2008.
current_role: Joint Managing Director, RSPL Group (Ghadi detergent), Kanpur
public_contact: office_email: info@rsplgroup.com (company general contact) | official_website: https://www.rsplgroup.com
research_notes: Family is known as low-profile ('silent billionaire' coverage of Murli Dhar Gyanchandani). Forbes wealth likely listed for the family; Rahul appears as company spokesperson in campaign press releases. Only general company email published.

name: Rohit Gyanchandani
profile: Second-generation director of Kanpur-based RSPL Group, the family FMCG conglomerate behind Ghadi, one of India's best-selling detergent brands, founded in 1988 by his father's generation (Murli Dhar and Bimal Kumar Gyanchandani). Alongside brother Rahul he helps run the group, reportedly focusing on international markets and hygiene/personal-care brands.
interesting_fact: Energy angle: RSPL has 15 solar plants totalling about 50.1 MW and built a ₹40bn+ soda-ash plant in Devbhumi Dwarka, Gujarat (commissioned FY2019-20) to backward-integrate its detergent supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: The group was originally incorporated in Kanpur in 1988 as 'Rohit Surfactants Pvt. Ltd.' (later renamed RSPL Ltd.); a predecessor company merged in 2006 was named 'Rohit Soaps & Detergents Pvt. Ltd.'
current_role: Director, RSPL Group (maker of Ghadi detergent), Kanpur, India
research_notes: Family is famously low-profile ('silent billionaires'). He was quoted as Director in RSPL's 50-year anniversary release (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/spotlight/news-wire/from-kanpur-to-global-rspl-group-celebrates-50-years-contributing-to-india-s-growth-story). The division-of-responsibility detail comes from a Wikipedia mirror, so treat it as indicative. The deep-cut fact doesn't say the company was named after him, so don't present it that way.

name: Rishabh H Mariwala
profile: Son of Marico founder Harsh Mariwala. Worked at Marico's Kaya skin clinics (2007-10), then left to build his own soap brand before founding Sharrp Ventures (c.2014-15), the family's consumer-focused investment office.
