Also linked to the Estalea venture vehicle with co-founder Per Pettersen.

name: Todd Crawford
profile: Affiliate-marketing pioneer who was on the founding team of Commission Junction (CJ) in 1998, later guided strategy for Digital River's OneNetworkDirect, and in 2008 co-founded Impact Radius (now impact.com), the Santa Barbara partnership-automation platform. He remains VP of Strategic Initiatives and co-hosts the company's Partnership Economy podcast.
interesting_fact: Industry peers call him the 'Godfather of Affiliate'; he was named to PartnerCentric/Hello Partner's Hero100 2025 as 'The OG Hero'.
deep_cut_fact: He was an original board member of the Performance Marketing Association, the US affiliate-industry trade group, and has offered paid one-on-one advice calls on Clarity.fm.
current_role: Co-Founder and VP Strategic Initiatives, impact.com
public_contact: press_email: public.relations@impact.com | contact_form: https://clarity.fm/toddcrawford | podcast: The Partnership Economy (impact.com podcast, co-host)
research_notes: Very approachable, conference-circuit regular; his Clarity.fm paid-call profile is a direct route. Some sources describe him as CJ's first employee rather than co-founder.

name: Wade Crang
profile: Cal Poly graduate and ad-tech data specialist who co-founded Impact Radius (now impact.com) in Santa Barbara in 2008 with Todd Crawford, Per Pettersen, Roger Kjensrud and Lisa Riolo. The partnership-automation platform reached a ~$1.5-2B valuation; Crang remains with the company in a strategic/technology role.
interesting_fact: impact.com was founded by a group of former Commission Junction (CJ) affiliate-marketing veterans; Crang had been CJ's VP of Business Intelligence & Product.
deep_cut_fact: Before impact.com he was on the founding team at LeadPoint, where he built the business-intelligence architecture credited with lifting revenue per lead.
current_role: Co-founder, impact.com (listed as Co-Founder & Growth Technologist / VP Strategic Operations)
research_notes: Very low public profile; no personal accounts verified. Best route is via impact.com communications (contact block on latest press release; EMEA releases have listed impact@mww.com agency address).

name: Eric Larchevêque
education: ESIEE Paris
profile: French serial entrepreneur since 1996 (Montorgueil, Prixing). Founded La Maison du Bitcoin in Paris, which merged with BTChip and Chronocoin in 2014 to form Ledger, the hardware crypto-wallet maker he led as CEO until 2019. Now an angel investor, TV investor on M6, and head of TBSO, which in 2026 dropped a bitcoin-treasury plan to build an AI/fintech group.
interesting_fact: Ledger was born in Vierzon (Cher), and in 2019 he co-founded ALGOSUP, a five-year software-development school, in the same town with Franck Jeanin.
deep_cut_fact: As an investor on M6's 'Qui veut être mon associé ?' he committed €590,000 in season 1, the third-largest total of the panel; he trained as an engineer at ESIEE Paris (MSc in information-processing architecture).
current_role: Manager (gérant) and largest shareholder of TBSO (listed AI/fintech group); co-founder and former CEO/chairman of Ledger
research_notes: Very public in French media and podcasts; best route is likely via TBSO investor relations or the M6 show/press. No published personal contact found in this pass. Recent interview: https://www.toutsurmesfinances.com/actualites/?p=799

name: Joel Pobeda
profile: French entrepreneur and one of four co-founders of Ledger, the Paris-based crypto hardware-wallet maker, alongside Eric Larchevêque, Thomas France and Nicolas Bacca. He served as COO in Ledger's early years, helping build its operations. His current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Ledger was formed in 2014 by merging his startup Chronocoin with BTChip and Eric Larchevêque's La Maison du Bitcoin.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ledger he founded Chronocoin, which let people buy Bitcoin with 3D-Secure credit/debit cards; its purchasing service was later rebranded Coinhouse, now one of France's main crypto brokerages.
current_role: Co-founder of Ledger (former COO); no current public title confirmed
research_notes: Very low public profile; sources are mostly profile aggregators. Alive status assumed (no death reports found). Best route likely via Ledger press/comms or LinkedIn.

name: Nicolas Bacca
profile: French hardware-security engineer who co-founded Ledger (2014), the Paris crypto hardware-wallet unicorn, serving as CTO and from 2019 chief innovation officer until leaving in 2023. After briefly launching smart-wallet project Smoo.th, he co-founded ZKNox in 2025 with cryptographers from Ledger and Thales, and angel-invests in French crypto startups (Bitstack, Spiko, Bubblemaps, Hyli).
interesting_fact: He read the Bitcoin whitepaper in 2012 while holding a smart-card design that could store secrets but had no business model: 'Bitcoin gave me that. So I'm very grateful for Satoshi.'
deep_cut_fact: As a child he printed his own fake banknotes and 'paid' his parents with them ('I was kind of my own central bank'); today he's invested in a champagne house that pays dividends in bottles, and says he's famous for bringing champagne to every party.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, ZKNox (hardware security & zero-knowledge cryptography); angel investor
research_notes: Long known in crypto by the handle 'btchip' (on Devcon profile) - personal X not independently verified here. Speaks regularly at Paris Blockchain Week, EthCC, Devcon; conference circuit is a natural route. Ledger's Recover controversy preceded his exit - avoid.

name: Thomas France
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Ledger, the Paris-based maker of crypto hardware wallets, in 2014 (Ledger later raised $380M in 2021 at unicorn valuation). Earlier he co-founded the shopping app Prixing. After stepping back from operations around 2019 he co-founded Cygni Capital, investing in blockchain, privacy and AI, and is an active angel investor.
interesting_fact: Ledger, which he co-founded in 2014, became one of France's best-known crypto unicorns, building secure hardware wallets for digital assets and raising $380M in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2014, with Eric Larcheveque, he opened La Maison du Bitcoin on rue du Caire in Paris, a physical venue for training in and buying cryptocurrencies, often described as Europe's first bitcoin space and a precursor to Ledger.
current_role: Co-founder of Ledger (board advisor per profile aggregators); founder/managing partner of Cygni Capital (crypto/trust-tech VC)
research_notes: Ledger press email is for the company, where he is no longer an operator. Cygni Capital has no confirmed official website; dates from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener, Dealroom) are inconsistent. Low media profile; appeared on the 'Can't Be Done' podcast (ep. 58).

name: Assaf Eisenstein
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Lusha, a B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform, with developer Yoni Tserruya in 2016. Lusha bootstrapped to profitability before raising a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation; Eisenstein oversees business operations (legal, finance, investment strategy) as president.
interesting_fact: Lusha began as a side project aimed at recruiters, but salespeople quickly became its main users; it grew from a Chrome extension into a data platform with 515M+ data entries and now an MCP/API layer for AI agents.
deep_cut_fact: Before Lusha he was an HR-tech founder (Lusha's own site calls him 'an HR tech creator'), having built employee-referral software in Tel Aviv - which is why Lusha was first pitched as a recruiting tool.
current_role: Co-Founder & President, Lusha
research_notes: Low public profile compared to CEO Yoni Tserruya. No published press email found; LinkedIn (linked from Lusha's About page) is best route. Lusha's name comes from a family nickname (avoid in outreach per rules).

name: Yoni Tserruya
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded Lusha with Assaf Eisenstein in 2016; the B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform grew largely bootstrapped before a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation. He still leads it as CEO, now pitching Lusha as a GTM data layer for AI agents via API and MCP.
interesting_fact: Lusha reached unicorn status in 2021 with a $205M Series B led by PSG at a $1.5B valuation after years of near-bootstrapped growth.
deep_cut_fact: Lusha began as a side project he built while working his first job as an iOS developer at AT&T, after studying computer science; he calls himself 'a builder at heart' who was 'more into tinkering than following plans'.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Lusha (Tel Aviv / New York)
research_notes: Recent interview talks about AI agents and data infrastructure (MCP), a natural data/AI podcast angle.

name: Ed Thompson
profile: British software engineer who co-founded Manchester-born data-integration company Matillion with CEO Matthew Scullion in 2011. He led the team that launched Matillion ETL in 2014; the cloud data pipeline company (now pushing its 'Maia' agentic data team) raised $150M Series E at a $1.5B valuation in 2021 and reached ~$2B in later rankings.
interesting_fact: Matillion is one of the few UK tech unicorns founded in Manchester; it later built a major second hub in Denver.
deep_cut_fact: Before Matillion he spent 11 years as an IBM software consultant to UK blue-chip companies; Matillion ran for three years before he and his team shipped the flagship ETL product in 2014.
current_role: CTO and co-founder, Matillion
research_notes: Common name; identity tied to Matillion CTO. Writes bylines for DBTA, DevOps.com, Solutions Review; appeared on 'Data Sharks' podcast. Route via Matillion press.

name: Matthew Scullion
profile: Altrincham-born entrepreneur who co-founded Matillion in Manchester in 2011 after 15 years in UK/European IT systems integration (incl. software division director at Imtech ICT). He built Matillion into a cloud data-integration unicorn and led its pivot to 'Maia' AI data automation; in Aug 2026 Girish Pancha became CEO and Scullion stayed on the board.
interesting_fact: Named EY UK Entrepreneur of the Year 2021; Matillion is one of the few Manchester-born software unicorns, with a second HQ in Denver.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded his first startup at age 18, then spent fifteen years in commercial IT and software development before starting Matillion.
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Matillion (stepped down as CEO Aug 2026); lay member of the University of Manchester Board of Governors
research_notes: CEO transition announced 4 Aug 2026 (PR Newswire): 'Building Maia has been the work of the last several years...' Now has more time; good podcast timing. info@ is a general company inbox, not personal.

name: Adrien Nussenbaum
education: HEC Paris
profile: HEC Paris graduate and serial founder who co-founded Mirakl with Philippe Corrot in 2012; Mirakl's marketplace and dropship SaaS is used by retailers such as Best Buy, Carrefour and Galeries Lafayette and was valued around $3.5-4B. After leaving executive duties in 2026 he became Mirakl's chairman (announced 10 Nov 2026), focusing more on philanthropy and film production.
interesting_fact: Mirakl's Nov 2026 governance change named him Chairman and said he will devote more time to philanthropy and film production, while ex-Sitecore CEO Steve Tzikakis took over his co-CEO remit.
deep_cut_fact: Before Mirakl he founded All Instant, a New York instant-messaging platform sold in 2003, then with Corrot built SplitGames, a video-game marketplace sold to Fnac in 2008, after which the pair designed Fnac.com's marketplace - the blueprint for Mirakl.
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Mirakl (stepped back from co-CEO role in 2026)
research_notes: Now non-executive; film production and philanthropy are new interests - a possible angle. No published press email found on Mirakl newsroom; approach via Mirakl comms/newsroom or LinkedIn.

name: Philippe Corrot
profile: Paris-born serial e-commerce founder (b. 1976). With Adrien Nussenbaum he built SplitGames, sold it to Fnac in 2008, ran Fnac's marketplace, then founded Mirakl in 2012 -- the marketplace software used by Macy's, Kroger, Carrefour, H&M and others. Mirakl became a unicorn in 2020, turned profitable in 2025 and is pushing 'agentic commerce' (Mirakl Nexus).
interesting_fact: He co-wrote 'The Online Marketplace Advantage' (Wiley, 2023) with Adrien Nussenbaum, which became a Wall Street Journal bestseller; he calls AI a 'change of civilisation' for business.
deep_cut_fact: Before Mirakl, he and Nussenbaum ran SplitGames (founded 2006), an online marketplace for trading used video games; Fnac bought it in 2008 and the pair spent three years building Fnac's own marketplace -- the experience that became Mirakl's playbook. He reportedly taught himself to code at age 4.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mirakl (Paris/Boston); co-CEO Steve Tzikakis reports to him since Nov 2026
research_notes: Nov 10 2026 governance change: ex-Sitecore CEO Steve Tzikakis joined as co-CEO reporting to Corrot; co-founder Adrien Nussenbaum became chairman. Corrot keeps strategy, product, tech; good podcast angle on AI agents in commerce.

name: David Sehyuk Park
profile: Korean-born engineer who co-founded machine-learning ad-tech company Moloco in 2013 with CEO Ikkjin Ahn after ~6 years at Oracle on cloud/virtualization (Nimbula) teams. As CIO he leads Moloco's largest global team of ML engineers, data scientists and data engineers behind its ML ad platform. BS in CS from Seoul National University; graduate studies at Stanford.
interesting_fact: Before Oracle he did graduate work at Stanford in CS/machine learning; Moloco grew into a ~$2B-valued ML performance-advertising company serving mobile apps, retail media and streaming.
deep_cut_fact: Per co-founder Ikkjin Ahn (2021 ZDNet Korea interview), Park did his master's under Andrew Ng at Stanford, was Ahn's junior by three years in SNU computer science, swept International Olympiad in Informatics medals as a youth, and had tried founding startups several times before Moloco.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Information Officer, Moloco (Redwood City, CA)
research_notes: Low public profile; Ahn is the main spokesperson. Moloco HQ moved to Redwood City. Route via Moloco PR (pr@moloco.com).

name: Ikkjin Ahn
profile: Korean-born ML engineer (BS Seoul National University; MSE UPenn) who worked at Google/YouTube before co-founding Moloco in 2013. Moloco builds machine-learning performance advertising for mobile apps and commerce media and has been reported to be weighing an IPO.
interesting_fact: At Google he developed YouTube's video profitability prediction system; that work on early YouTube monetization revealed the ML-for-mobile-ads opportunity that led to Moloco.
deep_cut_fact: He was the founding Tech Lead Manager of Google's Android Data team before leaving to start Moloco with a small team of ML engineers.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Moloco
research_notes: Moloco's PR team publishes a dedicated how-to-contact page; press route is the best bet.

name: Elad Raz
profile: Israeli chip entrepreneur who founded NextSilicon in 2017 to build adaptive 'Maverick' processors for HPC and AI as an alternative to GPUs. Earlier he founded Integrity Project, a low-level software/security firm acquired by Mellanox in 2014, and then served as a software director at Mellanox. NextSilicon has raised ~$300M and has 400+ staff.
interesting_fact: His first company, Integrity Project (founded 2006, Ramat Gan), was formed out of an elite military technology unit and was bought by Mellanox in July 2014 for its software expertise.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong retro-computing fan: he got hooked tinkering with Commodore 64s and Ataris as a kid and says he still collects them to this day.
current_role: Founder & CEO, NextSilicon (Israel)
research_notes: Highly relevant to data-center/AI-compute theme. info@ is the company's general inbox. Writes a blog on nextsilicon.com/insights.

name: Karim Pichara Baksai
profile: Chilean computer scientist who co-founded NotCo (2015, Santiago) with Matías Muchnick and Pablo Zamora and built 'Giuseppe', the AI that reverse-engineers animal products from plant ingredients. NotCo became a ~$1.5B+ unicorn, struck a JV with Kraft Heinz, and is pushing its AI platform to B2B clients (incl. fragrance/flavour formulation).
interesting_fact: Before food, he applied machine learning to astronomy: TechCrunch described him as an astrophysicist using data science to explore the inner workings of stars, and he did a 2011-12 Harvard postdoc in ML for astronomy.
deep_cut_fact: He co-authored 'Meta-Classification for Variable Stars' (Astrophysical Journal, 2016) with Harvard's Pavlos Protopapas, and still publishes on automatic variable-star classification (e.g. streaming classifiers, MNRAS 2020).
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, NotCo; associate professor of computer science, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile
public_contact: pr_agency: Rachel Kay Public Relations - notco@rkpr.net (US media contact on NotCo releases, 2022-23)
research_notes: Academic as well as founder; likely receptive to AI/data angles. PR agency contact is from 2023 releases and may be outdated.

name: Matias Muchnick
profile: Chilean entrepreneur who co-founded NotCo in 2015 with Karim Pichara and Pablo Zamora, using its AI 'Giuseppe' to formulate plant-based foods (NotMilk, NotMayo); backed by Jeff Bezos' fund and valued at ~$1.5B+. In 2025-26 NotCo pivoted toward selling its AI formulation platform to food majors (Kraft Heinz JV, Ferrero, Coca-Cola), exiting several consumer markets.
interesting_fact: Named to TIME's Next Generation Leaders; NotCo attracted investors including Bezos Expeditions and Roger Federer.
deep_cut_fact: Before NotCo he left finance to launch Eggless, a vegan mayonnaise brand in Chile; earlier still his first startup, a gamified-wellness app called Chooz, was in his words 'a total failure'.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, NotCo (The Not Company)
research_notes: Active on LinkedIn and frequent podcast guest. No published press email found in quick search; go via NotCo comms (notco.com).

name: Pablo Zamora
profile: Chilean biochemist with a PhD in biotechnology from Universidad de Santiago. In 2015 he co-founded NotCo, the AI-driven plant-based food company later valued as a unicorn, with Matías Muchnick and Karim Pichara. He was CSO from 2018 to March 2020, then left to work as an investor and consultant. He chairs Fundación Chile, whose board is split between the Chilean state and BHP, and was named to BancoEstado's board.
interesting_fact: Fundación Chile's board, which he chairs, is half appointed by the Chilean state and half by the mining company BHP. That gives him a seat where mining, energy and innovation policy meet.
deep_cut_fact: Before NotCo he did postdoctoral research on the genetics of Mexican maize at UC Davis from 2009. He also worked on plant and microbe genomics as a senior scientist with the Mars Advanced Research Institute (2013-2015).
current_role: President of the board, Fundación Chile (since 2022, proposed by President Boric). Co-founder and former CSO of NotCo. Investor and board member.
research_notes: Spanish-language media covers him often (DF, El Mercurio). A 2026 DF piece hinted his Fundación Chile tenure may end with the change of government; I could not confirm his current status. He has spoken publicly about lithium (the SQM-Codelco deal), which fits an energy podcast. No personal email found.

name: Charles Yeh
profile: Charles Yeh co-founded San Francisco identity-verification company Persona with CEO Rick Song in 2018 and serves as CTO. Persona raised a $200M Series D in April 2025 (led by Founders Fund and Ribbit) at a $2B valuation, positioning itself as a 'verified identity layer' for an agentic-AI world.
interesting_fact: Yeh tracks how fraudsters use generative AI: he notes deepfakes once carried detectable traces of their root models, but mixing models has made those traces harder to find. He is most interested in where identity and payments meet, especially privacy-conscious biometrics.
deep_cut_fact: Yeh was Rick Song's roommate for three to four years before Persona. He was the one who had long wanted to start a company and pushed Song to co-found one. Early on, he personally built a custom solution for a large Japanese identity-verification customer.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Persona (identity verification)
research_notes: Low profile compared with CEO Rick Song. No published press email found. Asked to describe founder life in one word, he chose 'Fulfilling' (Visa interview).

name: Rick Song
profile: Rick Song spent about five years at Square as an engineer and early Square Capital team member. In 2018 he co-founded Persona with CTO Charles Yeh to build configurable identity-verification building blocks. In April 2025 Persona raised a $200M Series D led by Founders Fund and Ribbit at a $2B valuation, pitching a 'verified identity layer' for an AI-agent internet.
interesting_fact: Persona's $200M Series D (April 2025) valued it at $2B, up from $1.5B in its 2021 Series C. The pitch is building the verified identity layer for an increasingly AI-driven internet.
deep_cut_fact: At Square he worked on lending fraud at Square Capital and on trust and safety for the Caviar food-delivery business, which exposed him to many identity-verification use cases. He calls himself 'slightly obsessed' with pre-mortems and jokes that Persona is 'an entire company of people who have never done startups'.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Persona (identity verification platform, San Francisco)
research_notes: The press email came from the withpersona.com/about page text as returned by search; a direct fetch of the page was blocked (403). He has done podcasts (First Round 'In Depth' ep. 22, Product Market Fit Show), so he is receptive to founder-story interviews.

name: Jerome Ternynck
profile: French entrepreneur who spent a decade in recruiting software, founding Lumesse (formerly in the UK) in 1999 and serving as CEO until 2010. He moved from Paris to San Francisco in 2010 and founded SmartRecruiters, a talent-acquisition SaaS used by 4,000+ organisations, which SAP agreed to acquire in August 2025.
interesting_fact: SAP announced the acquisition of SmartRecruiters on Aug 1, 2025 and completed it on Sept 11, 2025, planning to integrate it with SuccessFactors while keeping it available standalone.
deep_cut_fact: After moving from Paris to San Francisco in 2010 he raised $1M in seed money; SmartRecruiters launched in summer 2011 as a free job-posting app and didn't launch its first paid product until May 2014. His stated goal: 'I wanted to make hiring a quality business, and I wanted to give people a job they loved.'
current_role: Founder of SmartRecruiters (acquired by SAP, closed Sept 2025); MarketScreener lists him as Chairman since April 2023; Rebecca Carr is now SmartRecruiters CEO
public_contact: podcast: Interview: 'Itw Jérôme Ternynck, CEO & Founder SmartRecruiters' (French Tech San Francisco podcast)
research_notes: Post-acquisition role unclear; best route likely via SmartRecruiters/SAP press or LinkedIn. The podcast entry is a past interview, not his own channel.

name: Aaron King
profile: Aaron King founded Snapdocs in 2013. It started as a mobile-notary scheduling tool and grew into a digital mortgage-closing platform valued at about $2B. He led it as CEO for a decade, then handed the CEO role to Michael Sachdev in Sept 2023 and stayed on full-time as executive chairman, focused on product direction and customers.
interesting_fact: He was a mortgage-industry veteran of roughly 20 years who worked as a notary signing agent himself. That front-line experience led to a nationwide notary signing service and eventually Snapdocs.
deep_cut_fact: Asked for the best advice he ever received, he said: 'There's tremendous power in being a great listener... hyper-effective leaders continuously hone this skill.'
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Snapdocs (CEO until Sept 2023)
public_contact: press_email: press@snapdocs.com | pr_agency: Sam Garcia, Strategic Vantage Marketing & PR - samgarcia@strategicvantage.com | official_website: https://www.snapdocs.com
research_notes: Aggregator sites say his earlier notary company was NotaryLink, founded at age 21; I could not confirm this from a primary source. Contacts come from a Sept 2023 release.

name: Mark Gainey
education: Harvard University
profile: Reno-raised Harvard grad (AB Fine Arts, 1990) who co-founded enterprise email software firm Kana Communications with Michael Horvath in 1996 and took it public in 1999. In 2009 the pair co-founded Strava; Gainey was its first CEO and CEO again 2013-2017, and remains executive chairman of the ~$2.2B fitness social network.
interesting_fact: Gainey and Horvath met on Harvard's rowing crew in the 1980s; Strava's name comes from the Swedish word 'sträva', meaning 'strive'.
deep_cut_fact: He only took up rowing at Harvard after a running injury in his freshman year, joining the varsity lightweight crew; before startups he spent 1991-1995 at private equity firm TA Associates.
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Strava
research_notes: Press email on PR Newswire is Cloudflare-obfuscated (decodes to press@strava.com). Has done podcasts (Rich Roll, Antler Early Days, Terra) - receptive to long-form interviews.

name: Mark Shaw
profile: Mark Shaw was part of Strava's 2009 founding team alongside Mark Gainey, Michael Horvath, Davis Kitchel, Chris Donahue and Pelle Sommansson. Per his professional profile he was Strava's CTO 2009-2017 and head of growth 2017-2019, after earlier co-founding Guidewire Software; since 2020 he has been co-founder and CTO of Inclined.
interesting_fact: Michael Horvath's 2023 open letter announcing his CEO succession named Shaw among the six-person founding team that started Strava in 2009.
deep_cut_fact: Before Strava he started as a software engineer at Kana Software (1997-2001) and co-founded insurance-software firm Guidewire in 2001; he holds BS (1996) and MS (1998) degrees in computer science from Stanford.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Inclined (per The Org profile; Strava co-founder)
research_notes: Low public profile; career details come from The Org aggregator profile (not self-published), treat dates as approximate. Strava press form is only an indirect route since he appears to have left Strava ~2019. Alive status not explicitly confirmed (no reports of death).

name: Michael Horvath
education: Harvard University; Northwestern University
profile: Harvard economist-turned-founder who co-founded Kana Communications (1996) and then Strava (2009) with Harvard crew teammate Mark Gainey. He was Strava CEO 2009-2013 and again 2019-2023. Since 2024 he runs Nyfik, a small 'stay small but profitable' software company building tools for niche communities.
interesting_fact: Before Strava he was an academic: assistant professor of economics at Stanford (1994-2000) and at Dartmouth's Tuck School (2000-2004), with a PhD from Northwestern; he also captained Harvard's lightweight rowing crew.
deep_cut_fact: His new company's name, Nyfik, is Swedish for 'curious', and its first product is a fog-focused app to help San Francisco locals understand the city's elusive weather.
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Nyfik (software company); co-founder and former CEO of Strava
research_notes: Industry tag 'Life Sciences' in input is inaccurate; Strava is a fitness/social app. Nyfik's general inbox is the most direct published route.

name: Grant LaFontaine
profile: Maine-raised consumer-tech product executive who co-founded Whatnot with Logan Head in 2019. It went through Y Combinator's Winter 2020 batch, starting with Funko Pops before expanding into trading cards, fashion and more. Whatnot is now a leading US live-stream shopping platform, reported by Fortune at a $20B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: While raising money, the founders pitched hundreds of investors and logged each rejection in a spreadsheet, but stopped updating it at 100 rows because they were too 'demoralized'. Whatnot's first livestream, which LaFontaine hosted, sold out in about 2.5 hours.
deep_cut_fact: He opened an eBay store in fourth grade, selling Pokemon cards with friends in Maine. His first online sale was a holographic Chansey card, the sale that hooked him as both a collector and a seller.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Whatnot (live-shopping marketplace)
research_notes: Could not verify a current Whatnot press email in this session. 2022 Business Wire releases reportedly listed Moxie PR (whatnot@moxiegrouppr.com) as the agency, but I could not open those pages to confirm, so it is not listed as a contact. Has appeared on the a16z and Masters of Scale podcasts.

name: Logan Head
profile: Engineer who co-founded Whatnot with CEO Grant LaFontaine in Los Angeles in December 2019, inspired by their shared collectibles habits; the app went through Y Combinator and grew into the leading US live-shopping marketplace, reportedly valued around $20B by 2026. Head leads engineering and product.
interesting_fact: Whatnot's first livestream test split the founders' own Funko Pop collection between static listings and live auctions; the livestreamed half sold out in about 2.5 hours, earning roughly $5,000 in one evening.
deep_cut_fact: He built Whatnot's first livestream product by shutting himself in his room for roughly four to five weeks; LaFontaine said he was 'coding 16 hours a day, six days a week,' and Head was nervous the livestream format wouldn't work.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Whatnot (livestream shopping marketplace)
research_notes: Low public profile; LaFontaine is the public face. No official Whatnot press email found (only in-app support). Pre-Whatnot roles (GOAT, Flight Club) appear only in third-party profiles and were not confirmed from primary sources.

name: Anand Arvind
profile: Enterprise-software veteran who co-founded Zenoti (Seattle/Hyderabad cloud software for salons, spas and fitness businesses, founded 2010) with Sudheer and Dheeraj Koneru. As Chief Product Officer he leads Zenoti's technology and product vision; previously VP of Products at SumTotal Systems.
interesting_fact: At SumTotal Systems he led development of a learning platform used by over 20 million users.
deep_cut_fact: Earlier in his career at Microsoft he contributed to Windows System Restore. He holds degrees from BITS Pilani and Ohio State University and an MBA from the Indian School of Business.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Zenoti
research_notes: Low public profile; Sudheer Koneru (CEO) is the company's public face. Zenoti press page: https://www.zenoti.com/press (no press email found).

name: Dheeraj Koneru
profile: Dheeraj Koneru co-founded Zenoti in 2010 with his brother Sudheer, who is CEO. Zenoti makes cloud management software for salons, spas, med spas and fitness businesses and is valued at about $2B. Dheeraj leads global product sales and drove the company's international expansion, including into fitness and gym management.
interesting_fact: Zenoti began as software he built in-house for the brothers' own Hyderabad chain, Latitudes Health Club and Tangerine Spas, after finding no suitable product on the market.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in particle physics from Cornell. He also co-founded Intelliprep Technologies, which later merged with Click2Learn, and held roles at Microsoft and SumTotal Systems.
current_role: Co-Founder & SVP, Global Product Sales, Zenoti (Bellevue, WA / Hyderabad)

name: Saritha Katikaneni

name: Sudheer Koneru
profile: IIT Madras and UT Austin computer-science grad who spent ~8 years at Microsoft, then ran e-learning firm Intelliprep (merged into Click2learn/SumTotal Systems). After co-founding a spa/fitness chain in Hyderabad, he founded Zenoti (originally ManageMySpa) in 2010; it became the beauty-and-wellness software industry's first unicorn and powers 30,000+ businesses.
interesting_fact: Zenoti grew out of his own pain running Latitudes Health Club and Tangerine Spas, a fitness/spa/salon chain he co-founded with his brother Dheeraj in Hyderabad in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: He practices yoga, tracks workouts with the Nike+ app, names Ubud in Bali as a favorite place, and says his life mantra is 'Live and be present to the moment'; he credits his father's habit of focusing on the points he missed on tests for how he coaches employees.
current_role: Founder & CEO, Zenoti (Bellevue, WA)
research_notes: No published press email found on Zenoti's press/contact pages; use the press page or contact form.

name: Brian Barnes
profile: Chicago-born, Stanford economics graduate who did hedge-fund equity research and management consulting before founding M1 Finance in 2015 at about 25. M1 is a 'finance super app' that combines automated investing in user-built 'pies' with borrowing and banking; it has raised more than $300M and reached a unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Frustrated by $10 trade commissions and poor tools in his first job after college, he built M1 to automatically route recurring deposits into a user's chosen allocation so no cash sits idle.
deep_cut_fact: He bought his first stock at age 10. After a fifth-grade virtual portfolio contest, his parents opened a real brokerage account in his name on one condition: he had to bring them 'thoughtful research on what to buy and why.'
current_role: Founder & CEO, M1 Finance (Chicago)
public_contact: press_email: pr@m1.com | contact_form: https://www.m1.com/contact-us | official_website: https://www.m1.com
research_notes: He has appeared on many podcasts, including Millennial Investing (The Investor's Podcast) and ChooseFI. The press page also lists pr@m1finance.com.

name: Ramki Gaddipati
profile: Co-founded Bengaluru/US banking-tech company Zeta in 2015 with Bhavin Turakhia, building its cloud-native card-processing and core-banking stack. Before Zeta he spent over a decade at the Directi Group and earlier worked at Morgan Stanley in India building data services and middleware. He now runs Zeta's Asia-Pacific business as well as global technology.
interesting_fact: Holds two master's degrees from BITS Pilani (management and software systems) and earlier co-founded Bridle Information and Technology Solutions.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, Bridle, was billed as 'BITS Pilani's First Incubated Company' in the 2004 alumni magazine Sandpaper, supported by the BITS Technology Business Incubator (he appears as 'Rama Krishna (Ramki)').
current_role: Co-founder, APAC CEO and Global CTO, Zeta

name: Allon Bloch
profile: Israeli-American serial entrepreneur who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Ran Shaul. It uses AI models trained on large clinical datasets to power virtual primary care and has partnerships with health systems such as Northwell, Cedars-Sinai and Penn Medicine. Earlier he was co-CEO and president of Wix.com (2008-2010) and CEO of online car retailer Vroom (2014-2016).
interesting_fact: He has built companies in three very different sectors (website building at Wix, used cars at Vroom, AI medicine at K Health), and before that was a venture partner at Greylock and a general partner at JVP.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he trained in science: per his bios he holds a B.Sc. in biology from Tel Aviv University, then took an MBA at Columbia Business School (class of '97) and started at McKinsey; he now sits on the Columbia Business School board.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, K Health (AI-powered primary care); independent director, Wix.com
public_contact: pr_agency: khealth@moxiegrouppr.com (Moxie Group PR) | press_email: press@khealth.com | official_website: https://khealth.com/press
research_notes: The PR emails come from K Health press releases (2022 and 2025), seen via search; khealth.com/press hides its address behind Cloudflare. The biology B.Sc. comes from secondary profiles. Media-accessible; frequent health-tech conference speaker.

name: Israel Roth
profile: Israeli software entrepreneur and ex-Scitex manager who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Allon Bloch, Ran Shaul and Taboola CEO Adam Singolda and served as its CTO. K Health builds AI-driven primary care (symptom checking and virtual clinicians) and was valued as a unicorn. Earlier he co-founded print-personalisation software firm XMPie and Labgoo.
interesting_fact: According to a 2023 report on K Health's funding, Roth left the CTO post a few months earlier to become a chef.
deep_cut_fact: He was chief software architect and a co-founder of XMPie, a Scitex spin-off (with Jacob Aizikowitz and Reuven Sherwin) that pioneered variable-data/personalised printing and was bought by Xerox for $54M in 2006.
current_role: Co-founder (former CTO) of K Health; reported in 2023 to have stepped back from the CTO role to work as a chef
research_notes: Low public profile; no published personal or office contact found. Company route would be K Health press (khealth.com), but he may no longer be operational there. Name is common: confirm the right Israel Roth before outreach.

name: Ran Shaul
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur (Tel Aviv University) who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Allon Bloch, Israel Roth and Adam Singolda. K Health uses AI trained on millions of anonymised medical records to power a symptom checker and virtual primary care, partnering with health systems such as Cedars-Sinai; it reached unicorn status. Shaul leads product.
interesting_fact: K Health's pitch is 'a doctor in your pocket': its AI compares a user's symptoms against millions of patient records to show how doctors diagnosed similar people, before routing them to a clinician - Shaul has explained the approach on podcasts such as The MAML Podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 he co-founded Pursway, an audience-targeting startup that mapped real-life relationships among 150m+ North American consumers using machine-learning and techniques borrowed from anti-terrorism link analysis; it was acquired by Interpublic (IPG) in 2015.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, K Health (New York / Tel Aviv)
research_notes: Has done podcast interviews before (MAML podcast) - receptive to podcast format. Route via K Health press team.

name: Augusto Marietti
profile: Rome-born entrepreneur who started Mashape with schoolmate Marco Palladino in a rented Milan garage in 2009, moved to San Francisco after failing to raise money in Italy, and pivoted to an API marketplace. Mashape became Kong, whose open-source API gateway grew into an enterprise API/AI-gateway platform; Kong reached unicorn status (~$2B valuation).
interesting_fact: He and his co-founders lived on about $1,000 a month in Silicon Valley, gave themselves '90 days to make it or break it', and got their first break after cold-emailing hundreds of contacts from a Stanford entrepreneurship event list.
deep_cut_fact: Travis Kalanick let him stay at his San Francisco 'JamPad' for a few weeks on one condition: Marietti had to cook carbonara for Kalanick's partner once a week. He told the story on the a16z podcast with Martin Casado.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kong Inc. (API and AI connectivity platform, San Francisco)
research_notes: Goes by 'Aghi'. Open, story-friendly founder who appears on podcasts (a16z) and in Business Insider. Kong now positions itself around AI-agent/API connectivity, which fits AI infrastructure. Best route: press@konghq.com.

name: Marco Palladino
profile: Italian-born, self-taught engineer who co-founded API marketplace Mashape in Milan (2009-10) with Augusto Marietti, moved to San Francisco in 2011, and pivoted it into Kong, the open-source API gateway (2015) that became a cloud-native API and AI-connectivity platform. Kong passed $100m ARR and raised at a ~$2bn valuation in 2024; as CTO he now focuses on APIs for AI agents.
interesting_fact: Kong began in a garage in Milan: Marietti and Palladino struggled to raise money because few Italian investors understood APIs, so in 2011 they moved to San Francisco and slept on friends' couches while building Mashape.
deep_cut_fact: He has been a self-taught programmer since about age 13 and still recalls coding on Windows 3.1 on a 486 PC 'with a Turbo button' - an early fascination with networking software that led him to RPC/HTTP APIs in the SOA/Web Services era.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Kong Inc. (San Francisco)
research_notes: Active technical voice: frequent conference speaker and podcast guest (e.g. Software Engineering Daily, The Business of Open Source). Natural fit for an AI-infrastructure episode (API gateways for LLM/agent traffic). Personal social handles not verified from an official source.

name: Michele Zonca
education: University of Milan-Bicocca
profile: Italian software engineer (MSc computer science) who co-founded Mashape with Augusto Marietti and Marco Palladino in July 2009; Mashape pivoted into Kong, the API-gateway/cloud-connectivity company valued at $1bn+. He served as Chief Architect until ~2012-2013, then returned to Italy, later working in startups including sports-fan app Tok.tv.
interesting_fact: Mashape's first $51,000 came from three former YouTube employees; the company's API-marketplace idea later evolved into Kong's open-source API gateway used widely in cloud infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: After raising a $1.5M seed round, the Mashape founders lived and worked in a green house-office at 433 Bryant Street in San Francisco, trading lower salaries for room and board — and threw away and rewrote at least 100,000 lines of code within months.
current_role: Unclear — former co-founder/Chief Architect of Mashape (now Kong); listed as partner at Italian startup studio The Liquid Factory (Crunchbase) and CTO of Tok.tv since 2019 (MarketScreener)
research_notes: Left Kong operations around 2012; current role unconfirmed and he has a low public profile. Wealth tied to his Kong founder equity. Best fit is an origin-story conversation about Kong.

name: Brad Goldoor
profile: Pittsburgh-educated (BA, University of Pittsburgh) sales and recruiting-tech veteran who co-founded Phenom around 2010-11 with Mahe Bayireddi and Hari Bayireddy. Phenom became an applied-AI talent-experience platform (recruiting automation, AI agents for HR, internal mobility) valued at over $1bn. He led business development, then people/HR, then employee experience.
interesting_fact: Phenom's stated mission is 'helping a billion people find the right work'; Goldoor, its people chief for years, has written publicly about running a 'not normal' candidate and employee experience, including an ERE piece 'Put Employees First, Work Second During a Crisis' (May 2020).
deep_cut_fact: Before Phenom he spent his early career selling for CareerBuilder and Gannett - i.e. he came to HR-tech from the job-board/newspaper-classifieds world that AI recruiting platforms like Phenom later disrupted.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Employee Experience Officer, Phenom (Ambler, PA) - most recent reported title (formerly Chief People Officer)
public_contact: press_email: jennifer.lyons@phenompeople.com (Phenom Director of PR, media inquiries) | official_website: https://www.phenom.com
research_notes: Not a data-center/energy figure - Phenom is HR/AI software; fit for the podcast is weak. Exact current title not confirmed by a dated official source. Also reportedly an angel investor and earlier VP BD at coupon app SnipSnap (directory sources only).

name: Hari Bayireddy
profile: Hari Bayireddy co-founded Phenom in 2010 (originally iMomentus) with Mahe Bayireddi (CEO) and Brad Goldoor. Phenom sells an AI-driven 'talent experience' platform for recruiting, onboarding and retention to large enterprises. It became a unicorn with a $100M Series D in 2021, and he runs operations as co-founder, president and COO.
interesting_fact: Phenom's stated mission is to help one billion people find the right work; Forbes reported a valuation of about $1.4bn after its $100M Series D in 2021.
current_role: Co-founder, President and COO, Phenom (Phenom People), Ambler, Pennsylvania (title per third-party profiles)
public_contact: press_email: jennifer.lyons@phenompeople.com (Phenom media team, listed for press inquiries) | official_website: https://www.phenom.com
research_notes: Low public profile; CEO Mahe Bayireddi is the public face of Phenom. Earlier ventures (SnipSnap CTO, Bija Health COO) appear only on aggregator profiles, so they are not used as facts. Weak fit with the energy/data-center theme (HR-tech AI).

name: Mahe Bayireddi
profile: Co-founded Phenom around 2010-11 with Hari Bayireddy and Brad Goldoor to build an AI-powered talent-experience platform for hiring, employee development and retention. A $100m Series D in 2021 valued Phenom at about $1.4bn; the company runs the IAMPHENOM conference and has been acquiring AI firms (e.g. Included AI, Be Applied in 2026) while selling AI hiring agents to large enterprises.
interesting_fact: He argues generative AI could deliver 30-40% productivity gains for knowledge workers, and says a founder starting today should ask: 'What is the new data set I will create, which doesn't exist, that will give me leverage that most of the industry does not have?'
deep_cut_fact: Phenom wasn't his first startup: his earlier company, iMomentous, failed, and he has said the lessons from it - especially seeing talent from the candidate, HR and manager perspectives at once - shaped how he built Phenom.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Phenom (Phenom People), Ambler/Philadelphia
research_notes: Media-friendly; frequent podcast guest on AI and HR tech. Press contact is Phenom's Director of PR, Jennifer Lyons (published on the newsroom). Topic fit is AI rather than energy/data centers.
