deep_cut_fact: He and Nosralla met at McKinsey (Renato spent 5+ years there serving retail/consumer clients); the Merama idea came after they read about a funding round for US brand aggregator Perch and found nothing similar in Latin America.
current_role: Co-founder, Merama; reportedly CEO of Omniteca since 2025 (directory listing only, unverified)
research_notes: Current role uncertain: theofficialboard.com lists him as CEO of Omniteca (joined 2025) - verify via LinkedIn before outreach. Common name in Brazil; match via Merama/McKinsey/INSEAD. No published direct contact found.

name: Sujay Tyle
profile: US-born serial founder who entered Harvard at 15, left as a 2011 Thiel Fellow, and worked at Scopely before moving to Berlin to co-found Frontier Car Group (emerging-market used-car marketplaces), acquired by OLX/Naspers in 2019. He then co-founded Merama, which acquires and scales consumer brands selling on Mercado Libre and Amazon across Latin America, reaching unicorn status.
interesting_fact: He was a freshman at Harvard by age 15 and left in his junior year to become one of Peter Thiel's original '20 Under 20' fellows.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008, as a teenager, he co-founded ReSight with his older brother Sheel, a venture aimed at democratizing eye-care services.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Merama (Latin American e-commerce brand builder/aggregator)
research_notes: No published personal/press contact found; Merama's website has no press email. Route via Merama or Frontier Car Group investors.

name: Deepak Diwakar
profile: IIT Bombay computer-science grad (2008) who started as a machine-learning/platform engineer at ad-tech startup PubMatic, then co-founded Mindtickle in Pune in 2011-12 with Krishna Depura, Nishant Mungali and Mohit Garg. Mindtickle became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1.2B) selling sales-readiness and revenue-enablement software; he runs technology and operations as COO.
interesting_fact: Mindtickle helped define the 'sales readiness' software category and was named a Leader in the Forrester Wave for Revenue Enablement Platforms (Q3 2024).
deep_cut_fact: At IIT Bombay he wrote three of the four Performing Arts Festival (PAF) productions during his time there; he is a keen cyclist and nature lover whose mantra is 'Truth, honesty, and transparency build trust, and trust builds transformation.'
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, Mindtickle (revenue-enablement software; HQ San Francisco, engineering in Pune)
research_notes: Some sources list him as CTO; Mindtickle's own leadership page says COO. Older press releases cite a pr@ Mindtickle mailbox but I could not verify it on a live page, so it is omitted. Recognised by IIT Bombay alumni awards page.

name: Krishna Depura
profile: Indian-born engineer and ISB MBA (Class of 2006) who co-founded Mindtickle in 2011 with former PubMatic colleagues Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali. Mindtickle grew from a gamified employee-learning tool into a revenue-enablement and sales-readiness platform, valued at over $1B; he leads it as CEO, now pushing AI coaching and role-play products.
interesting_fact: Before Mindtickle he spent about five years at startups building photonic and semiconductor chips, then worked at Infinera, Microsoft (program manager) and ad-tech firm PubMatic (Director of Products until 2010).
deep_cut_fact: In a 2012 ISB alumni profile he said Mindtickle came 'after ten years of trying, failing and learning,' wished he'd started his entrepreneurial journey during his ISB days, and named his fondest ISB memory as alumni worldwide making the 'world's first wiki movie' Sapney.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mindtickle (San Francisco / Pune)
public_contact: press_email: helen.waite@mindtickle.com (Mindtickle media contact, Helen Waite) | official_website: https://www.mindtickle.com/leadership/krishna-depura/
research_notes: Also writes occasional TechCrunch contributor pieces (techcrunch.com/author/krishna-depura). Personal interests per ISB profile: travel and water sports.

name: Mohit Garg
profile: One of four co-founders (with Krishna Depura, Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali) of Pune-born Mindtickle, which pivoted from gamification to onboarding to sales enablement and became a unicorn in Aug 2021. In 2018 he co-founded OLOID, a passwordless/physical-identity platform for frontline workers, which has raised ~$23M Series A/A1 from Dell Technologies Capital, Honeywell, Okta Ventures and Yaletown.
interesting_fact: Mindtickle was the product of three pivots: it began in 2011 as a gamification platform, moved to employee onboarding, then to sales-rep productivity before reaching a $1B+ valuation.
deep_cut_fact: The Mindtickle idea began with online 'treasure hunts' the founders ran for fun - they later converted those treasure hunts into a way to engage and onboard new employees.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, OLOID (passwordless workforce identity, Sunnyvale CA); co-founder of Mindtickle
research_notes: Now focused on OLOID rather than Mindtickle (listed as Mindtickle co-founder/advisor). Appeared on Founder Thesis podcast ('Once Tickled, Twice OLOID'). No dedicated press email found; OLOID site has Contact Us form/newsroom.

name: Nishant Mungali
profile: Indian product designer-turned-founder who co-founded Mindtickle (Pune/San Francisco) in 2011 with Krishna Depura, Mohit Garg and Deepak Diwakar. The company grew from gamified onboarding into a sales-readiness and revenue-enablement platform, reaching unicorn status in 2021 (~$1.2B); he leads product.
interesting_fact: He recalls that at launch Mindtickle 'had difficulty landing one client, let alone five' and leaned on its network and a pilot program for its first referenceable customers.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Almora in the Kumaon hills of Uttarakhand, he studied at IIT Guwahati and took his first job at investment firm D. E. Shaw in Hyderabad (as a UX designer) before the four co-founders started dabbling with the Mindtickle idea in 2010.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Mindtickle
research_notes: Mindtickle 2025 releases name individual media contacts without emails; older releases show a generic pr(at)mindtickle address that I could not confirm on a live page, so not listed. Route via Mindtickle newsroom (https://www.mindtickle.com/blog/news_tax/news).

name: Darpan Sanghvi
profile: Mumbai-based entrepreneur who founded MyGlamm in 2015 and built it into the Good Glamm Group, a content-to-commerce beauty conglomerate valued at $1.2B in 2021 (backers incl. Warburg Pincus, L'Occitane, Amazon). After the group was broken up by lenders in 2025, he launched CoFounder Circle, an AI-native accelerator for startups and MSMEs, and judges on JioHotstar's 'Pitch To Get Rich'.
interesting_fact: He is credited with pioneering the 'content-to-commerce' model in India's beauty industry, buying media/influencer platforms POPxo, Plixxo and ScoopWhoop to sell MyGlamm products; the group later launched Wyn Beauty with Serena Williams.
deep_cut_fact: While studying engineering at MIT Pune he worked at Baazee.com, the Indian auction site later bought by eBay; he later did a dual MBA at ESADE (Barcelona) and UT Austin.
current_role: Founder, CoFounder Circle (AI-native startup acceleration/venture studio platform, India)
research_notes: Sensitive: Good Glamm Group collapsed in July 2025; he pledged part of future earnings/CoFounder Circle equity to make stakeholders whole. Avoid as an opener. Likely official site cofoundercircle.com (unconfirmed link to him); LinkedIn is his main public channel.

name: Priyanka Gill
profile: A former London-based journalist, Gill turned her blog eStylista into POPxo, a digital community for Indian women, after moving back to India in 2014. POPxo/Plixxo merged with MyGlamm in 2020 and became part of the Good Glamm Group in 2021, where she ran the media and content arm. She was later a venture partner at Kalaari Capital, then left in early 2025 to found COLUXE.
interesting_fact: COLUXE pitches AI-powered personalisation, virtual try-ons and modular jewellery, and has backers including Ajai Chowdhry (HCL co-founder) and Startup Sherpas.
deep_cut_fact: Born in a village in Punjab and an English Literature graduate of Lady Shri Ram College, she wrote for The Guardian, The Independent and Vogue India in London. She co-chaired the Pratham Gala (2009-10), which raised over GBP 3M. Her early collection of modern Indian art later sold at Christie's first auction in India.
current_role: Founder & CEO, COLUXE (lab-grown diamond jewellery brand, launched 2025); co-founder, Good Glamm Group (MyGlamm)
public_contact: official_website: https://www.priyankagill.com/ | x: https://twitter.com/priyankagill | instagram: https://www.instagram.com/priyankagill_official/ | linkedin: https://in.linkedin.com/in/priyankagill
research_notes: Media-friendly and active on social media. Her current focus is COLUXE (consumer/luxury), not the Good Glamm Group, so lead with COLUXE or her founder journey rather than Good Glamm's recent difficulties.

name: Michael Dombowsky
profile: Saskatchewan-born builder and inventor who co-founded Vancouver green-construction company Nexii (2017/18) with Ben Dombowsky and Stephen Sidwell. He invented its 'Nexiite' panelised low-carbon building system, which carried a unicorn valuation in 2021. Profiles credit him with 40+ years of designing and building residential, commercial and institutional projects.
interesting_fact: He is described as the inventor behind Nexii's whole-building system: prefabricated panels made of 'Nexiite', a concrete alternative pitched as cutting building emissions and construction time.
current_role: Co-founder, co-inventor and (per TheOrg) SVP Building Technology, Nexii Building Solutions; current status after Nexii's 2024 restructuring unclear
research_notes: Sensitive: Nexii entered CCAA creditor protection in Jan 2024 and was sold and relaunched under interim CEO Bill Tucker (SBIZ, Aug 2024); his role since then is unconfirmed. The 'unicorn' valuation is historical. A profile claim that he designed the Tunnels of Moose Jaw could not be verified, so I left it out. Very low public profile.

name: Ed Felten
profile: Princeton computer scientist and security researcher who was the FTC's first Chief Technologist (2011) and Deputy US CTO in the Obama White House (2015-17). In 2018 he co-founded Offchain Labs with former Princeton students Steven Goldfeder and Harry Kalodner; its Arbitrum rollup became the largest Ethereum layer-2. He served on the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board until January 2025 and still keynotes events like EthCC 2026.
interesting_fact: As the US government's witness in United States v. Microsoft, he demonstrated in court a tool built with two students that removed Internet Explorer access from Windows 98, rebutting Microsoft's claim that it couldn't be done.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a physicist: after a Caltech BS in physics (1985) he spent three years as a staff programmer on a Caltech parallel-supercomputer project before his CS PhD at the University of Washington, where his thesis was on communication protocols between parallel processors.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Offchain Labs (developer of Arbitrum); Robert E. Kahn Professor of CS and Public Affairs emeritus, Princeton
public_contact: personal_email: felten@cs.princeton.edu | official_website: https://www.offchainlabs.com/founders/ed-felten | x: https://x.com/Offchain (company account) | substack: Freedom to Tinker (blog he founded/writes for): https://freedom-to-tinker.com
research_notes: Princeton email is from his (older) self-published faculty homepage, written as 'felten at cs dot princeton dot edu'; may be less monitored now. Frequent podcast guest and conference speaker, so a podcast invitation fits him well. Also a NAE member and former EFF board member.

name: Harry Kalodner
profile: Princeton computer-science PhD researcher who co-founded Offchain Labs in 2018 with Ed Felten and Steven Goldfeder to commercialise their Arbitrum research. Arbitrum became the most widely used Ethereum layer-2 rollup; Kalodner leads Offchain's engineering and technical vision.
interesting_fact: Arbitrum began as an academic project: the three founders developed the technology at Princeton and published it as a 2018 paper before forming the company.
deep_cut_fact: As a Princeton PhD student he was lead author of BlockSci, an open-source blockchain analysis platform (2017 paper 'BlockSci: Design and applications of a blockchain analysis platform').
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, Offchain Labs (Arbitrum)
research_notes: Technical founder; appears on crypto podcasts (e.g. Masters of Web3).

name: Steven Goldfeder
profile: Computer scientist who earned a Princeton PhD in cryptocurrency security and, after a Cornell Tech/IC3 postdoc, co-founded Offchain Labs in 2018 with Ed Felten and Harry Kalodner to commercialise the Arbitrum research project. Arbitrum became the largest Ethereum layer-2 rollup; he continues to lead the company as CEO.
interesting_fact: Arbitrum began as an academic research project at Princeton before being spun out as Offchain Labs, which raised at a $1.2B valuation in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: As a Princeton PhD student advised by Arvind Narayanan, he co-authored the widely used textbook 'Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies' (Princeton University Press) alongside Narayanan, Bonneau, Felten and Miller.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Offchain Labs (now branded Offchain), developer of Arbitrum
public_contact: press_email: pr@offchain.io | x: https://x.com/sgoldfed | official_website: https://www.offchain.io/
research_notes: Frequent podcast guest (Bankless, Castle Island, Fintech Blueprint) - receptive to long-form interviews.

name: Avi Shua
profile: Israeli cybersecurity veteran (Unit 8200/IDF, then a decade-plus at Check Point, rising to Chief Technologist for threat prevention). Co-founded Orca Security in 2019 and was CEO until March 2023, building its agentless 'SideScanning' cloud security platform to a ~$1.8B valuation; he now leads innovation (SideScanning, Unified Data Model) as CIO.
interesting_fact: Orca's core idea, 'SideScanning', reads cloud workloads' block storage via the cloud provider's APIs instead of installing agents, giving full-stack visibility without touching running workloads.
deep_cut_fact: On CyberWire's 'Career Notes' he said he has been excited about cybersecurity since age 13, when he started probing his high school's network, and advised 'try to do things by yourself'.
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Innovation Officer and board member, Orca Security
research_notes: info@orca.security is Orca's general company email, not personal. Frequent conference speaker/podcast guest on cloud security, so a podcast invite fits his pattern.

name: Ety Spiegel Hubara
profile: Israeli engineer and one of eight co-founders of Orca Security, the agentless cloud-security platform founded in 2019 (largely by ex-Check Point colleagues) and valued at about $1.8B in 2021. She has kept a low public profile, working on the site-reliability/engineering side rather than as a company spokesperson.
interesting_fact: Orca Security was founded by eight co-founders and reached unicorn status within about two years, joining the Israeli unicorn club in late 2020/2021.
current_role: Co-founder, Orca Security (listed on org charts as Head of SRE)
research_notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Orca's About page publishes a general info@orca.security address; better route may be via CEO Gil Geron or Orca PR.

name: Gil Geron
profile: Israeli cybersecurity executive who co-founded Orca Security in 2019 with Avi Shua, serving as chief product officer before becoming CEO in 2023. Orca pioneered agentless cloud security (its patented SideScanning approach). Before Orca he spent nearly 11 years at Check Point.
interesting_fact: Orca was co-founded by a group of senior Check Point veterans; Geron was promoted from CPO to CEO in 2023 to drive 'efficient growth'.
deep_cut_fact: His last role at Check Point (2017-2019) was overseeing its cybersecurity gateway and cloud products, capping nearly 11 years at the company before he left to start Orca.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Orca Security
research_notes: Frequent conference and podcast guest on cloud/AI security; reachable via Orca comms.

name: Hadas Amitay
profile: Hadas Amitay appears (sometimes as 'Amitay Hadas') in founder lists of Orca Security, the Tel Aviv-founded agentless cloud-security (CNAPP) company started in 2019 by eight colleagues largely from Check Point, which reached a $1.8B valuation in 2021. No public biography, title or current role was found.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by eight co-founders - unusually large for a startup - most of them former Check Point colleagues, and pioneered 'SideScanning', agentless cloud-workload scanning.
current_role: Listed co-founder of Orca Security (current role not publicly documented)
public_contact: press_email: press@orca.security (Orca Security) | pr_agency: Inkhouse - orcasecurity@inkhouse.com
research_notes: Very low public footprint; only insider-data aggregators (MarketScreener) list the name. Name order/spelling inconsistent. Public faces of Orca are CEO Avi Shua and Gil Geron - route via them/company press.

name: Liran Antebi
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded cloud-security company Orca Security in 2019 with Avi Shua, Gil Geron and Matan Ben Gur, all Check Point Software veterans. Orca's agentless 'SideScanning' cloud-security platform raised large rounds and reached a ~$1.8B valuation. Antebi keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by a team of former Check Point executives and architects; Antebi and Matan Ben Gur were the founding 'chief architects' when the company emerged from stealth with a $6.5M seed round in 2019.
current_role: Co-founder and (founding) Chief Architect, Orca Security; current title not confirmed
public_contact: press_email: press@orca.security | pr_agency: Inkhouse on behalf of Orca Security: orcasecurity@inkhouse.com (per a 2026 Orca press release; verify)
research_notes: Not listed on Orca's current leadership page (orca.security/about), so he may have stepped back from an executive role. No interviews found. Aggregators claim ~16 years at Check Point before Orca, unverified by a primary source. Route via Orca press.

name: Matan Ben-Gur
profile: Israeli engineer and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (Tel Aviv, founded 2019), the agentless cloud-security company built on 'SideScanning', which raised ~$630M and was valued at $1.8B. A Tel Aviv University alumnus and Check Point Software veteran like most of the founding team, he served as Orca's Chief Architect and is also an angel investor.
interesting_fact: Orca's founders largely came out of Check Point Software; the company reached unicorn status within about two years of launching its product in 2019.
current_role: Co-founder of Orca Security (previously Chief Architect; current operational role unconfirmed); angel investor
research_notes: Very low public profile; not listed on Orca's current leadership page and some insider databases list his Orca role as former. No published personal contact found; route via Orca Security's PR team or LinkedIn. Database bios conflict on whether he or Liran Antebi held the Chief Architect title.

name: Shay Filosof
profile: Israeli engineer and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (founded 2019), the agentless cloud-security company valued at $1.8B in 2021. Like several Orca founders he came from Check Point, where he was a software architect and R&D group manager; he remains at Orca in a hands-on engineering role building cloud-security products.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by a group of eight ex-Check Point engineers and executives, an unusually large founding team, and pioneered 'SideScanning' agentless cloud security.
deep_cut_fact: At Check Point he worked on firewall gateway performance as a software architect and R&D group manager; he holds a BSc in CS from the Academic College of Tel Aviv-Yaffo and an MSc in CS from the Open University of Israel.
current_role: Co-founder and Senior Software Engineer, Orca Security (Tel Aviv)
research_notes: Very low public profile; details come mainly from directory profiles (TheOrg, Crunchbase). CEO Avi Shua / Gil Geron are Orca's public faces; approach via Orca's comms.

name: Wagde Zabit
profile: Israeli software engineer from Kafr Manda in the Galilee and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (2019), the agentless cloud-security (CNAPP) company valued at $1.8B in 2021. A Technion computer-science graduate, he left a long engineering career at Check Point to co-found Orca, where he remains a hands-on senior engineer.
interesting_fact: He is one of the very few Arab-Israeli co-founders of an Israeli cybersecurity unicorn; Calcalist profiled him as 'the entrepreneur from Kafr Manda who built a cybersecurity unicorn'.
deep_cut_fact: At age five his father, a math teacher turned computer instructor, gave him a Commodore 64 - the first computer in Kafr Manda - and he was programming in BASIC and Logo by first and second grade.
current_role: Co-founder (senior engineer), Orca Security
research_notes: Low public profile; an engineer rather than spokesperson (CEO Gil Geron and CTO Avi Shua front the company). Recent releases also route media via Inkhouse agency. Best route: Orca press.

name: Jessica McKellar
profile: MIT-trained software engineer and three-time co-founder (with Waseem Daher and Jeff Arnold): early engineer at Ksplice (sold to Oracle 2011), co-founder of Zulip (sold to Dropbox 2014), then Pilot (2017), a startup bookkeeping, tax and CFO service that reached a $1.2B valuation in 2021. Long-time Python community leader (PSF director 2012-14).
interesting_fact: She was a senior technical advisor for 16 episodes of HBO's 'Silicon Valley', and won the 2013 O'Reilly Open Source Award for her contributions to Python.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT undergrad studying chemistry, she co-authored a 2006 Science paper, 'Triple-Bond Reactivity of Diphosphorus Molecules' (Cummins group). She also co-wrote O'Reilly's 'Twisted Network Programming Essentials' (2nd ed., 2013).
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Pilot.com (moved from CTO to CEO around July 2024, per recent profiles)
public_contact: official_website: https://web.mit.edu/jesstess/www/ | x: https://x.com/jessicamckellar | office_email: info@pilot.com
research_notes: Some directories still list Daher as CEO and McKellar as CTO; a June 2026 podcast and other profiles call her CEO - verify before outreach. info@pilot.com is a general company inbox. Open-source/Python community angle works well.

name: Waseem Daher
profile: MIT computer-science graduate and three-time founder. He co-founded Ksplice (rebootless Linux updates, sold to Oracle in 2011) and Zulip (team chat, sold to Dropbox in 2014), then in 2017 co-founded Pilot with fellow MIT alumni. Pilot provides bookkeeping, tax and CFO services for startups and was valued at about $1.2B.
interesting_fact: He and his MIT co-founders Jessica McKellar and Jeff Arnold have now started three companies together: Ksplice, Zulip and Pilot.
deep_cut_fact: Ksplice, which grew out of Jeff Arnold's MIT master's thesis, won the top prize in the 20th annual MIT $100K Entrepreneurship Competition in May 2009; Daher (MIT '07, MEng '08) was one of its four co-founders.
current_role: Co-founder, Pilot.com (CEO per most bios; some 2026 directories list him as Executive Chair)
research_notes: Talks openly about frameworks for validating startup ideas (First Round Review podcast ep. 27). Current title unclear (CEO vs Executive Chair) - check before outreach.

name: Harsimarbir Singh
profile: Harsimarbir 'Harsh' Singh co-founded Pristyn Care in 2018 with Dr. Garima Sawhney and Dr. Vaibhav Kapoor. The Gurugram-based company runs an end-to-end care-delivery model for elective surgeries across Indian cities, partnering with hospitals and its own surgeons; it became a unicorn in Dec 2021 with backing from Tiger Global, Sequoia and Hummingbird.
interesting_fact: Pristyn Care was his fourth startup: he says he failed three times over about ten years before it worked, and after the third shutdown 'wanted to do anything but start up again'.
deep_cut_fact: His earlier ventures included an electricity-theft detection business (~2010), a Groupon-style restaurant app and a hyperlocal quick-commerce delivery service (~2015); between failures he worked at Urban Company in its pre-revenue days. His line: 'There's always noise in failure; it's the success that gives you clarity.'
current_role: Co-founder, Pristyn Care (leads business, technology and growth)
research_notes: Low public profile; best covered via Entrepreneur India and Hummingbird features. No published press email found on Pristyn Care site.

name: Jett McCandless
profile: Logistics-tech veteran with 25+ years in freight; built GlobalTranz and Inc. 500-ranked Metafora before founding supply-chain visibility platform project44 in Chicago in 2014. project44 (valued ~$3B) is used by 500+ Global 200 brands; he also leads spin-off LSP44 for logistics providers and is a frequent Bloomberg TV voice on supply chains.
interesting_fact: project44's company bio says he has advised the White House Council of Economic Advisers and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Blue Water Companies, a diversified portfolio company through which he pursues philanthropy and sustainability, including directing a significant portion of his personal net worth to organizations supporting women in crisis.
current_role: Founder and CEO, project44 (Chicago); also Founder and CEO of LSP44
public_contact: pr_agency: project44-pr@walkersands.com (Walker Sands, for project44) | official_website: https://www.project44.com/team/jett-mccandless
research_notes: Media-friendly (Bloomberg TV regular). press@project44.com appears in a 2025 republished release per search but not directly verified; LSP44 uses press@lsp44.ai.

name: Wally Ibrahim
profile: Chicago technologist who co-founded supply-chain visibility platform project44 with Jett McCandless in 2014 and served as its CTO (until about 2018). He has since been CTO and co-founder of Aloi, a platform for building and sharing business integrations. project44 has been valued at about $2.7B.
interesting_fact: Co-founded project44 in Chicago in 2014 with CEO Jett McCandless; project44 grew into one of the leading real-time freight/supply-chain visibility platforms.
current_role: Technical co-founder and CTO, Aloi (integrations platform); co-founder and former CTO of project44
research_notes: Low public profile; sources are mostly third-party profiles (Crunchbase, MarketScreener). No published contact found; LinkedIn likely the only route. Not currently at project44 (CEO is Jett McCandless).

name: Jannick Malling
profile: Danish fintech entrepreneur who co-founded the multi-asset investing platform Public with Leif Abraham and runs it as co-CEO. Earlier he worked at Saxo Bank, was Head of Product at CFH Group and co-founded trading-API startup Tradable. Public has recently pushed into direct indexing, bonds and AI-driven 'agentic brokerage' features.
interesting_fact: Public's userbase roughly doubled within days during the January 2021 GameStop frenzy, after having grown 13x the year before, per Malling.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Copenhagen he built websites to organise video-game meetups, and he joined Saxo Bank at 17; he credits that early stint with teaching him speed and user-centric design, and later collaborated with ex-Saxo colleagues on new ventures.
current_role: Co-founder & Co-CEO, Public (Public.com investing platform, New York)
research_notes: Shares CEO role with Leif Abraham; has spoken publicly (Stanford eCorner) about the co-CEO model. Frequent podcast guest on fintech topics.

name: Matt Kennedy
profile: Listed as a co-founder of Public.com, the New York investing app co-founded with Jannick Malling, Leif Abraham and Sean Hendelman, where he led brokerage operations and served as COO. Public is valued at over $1B. Details come mainly from directory profiles; current title unverified.
interesting_fact: Before Public he reportedly worked as a trading associate at broker-dealer Dominick & Dominick (per a company-profile listing).
current_role: Co-founder (brokerage), Public.com; former COO
research_notes: Very common name and low profile; only aggregator sources confirm role. Public's media contact is Rachel Livingston (press@public.com).

name: Peter Quinn
profile: Named in several broker reviews as one of Public.com's founders (with Jannick Malling, Matt Kennedy and Sean Hendelman); Public is a US commission-free investing app now run by co-CEOs Leif Abraham and Malling. No reliable biography or current role found.
interesting_fact: Public.com, which he is credited with co-founding, launched in 2019 as a 'social investing' app and in 2025 launched an AI-powered brokerage.
current_role: Listed as a co-founder of Public.com (Public Holdings); current role unconfirmed
research_notes: Common name; could not confirm identity or current involvement from primary sources. Treat with caution; route via Public press.

name: Sean Hendelman
profile: New York trading entrepreneur who founded T3 (T3 Live, T3 Trading Group), a trading, training and technology provider for professional traders, and co-founded social investing app Public.com, where he sits on the board. In 2024 prime broker Clear Street hired him to run its active trading division.
interesting_fact: Spent most of a 25+ year career running T3, building a global platform spanning equities, options, futures and algorithmic trading, before co-founding retail investing app Public.com.
current_role: CEO, Active Trading division, Clear Street (since May 2024); co-founder and board member, Public.com
research_notes: Clear Street bio: https://www.clearstreet.io/about/team/sean-hendelman (page errored on fetch). No published personal contact found; route via Clear Street media relations.

name: Aaron Passey
profile: Caltech-trained systems engineer and Isilon Systems veteran who co-founded Qumulo in 2012 with Peter Godman and Neal Fachan and served as its first CTO. He stepped away in 2016, then returned in December 2022 as a senior principal engineer. Qumulo now lists him as Co-founder & Chief Architect; the company sells file storage for AI/GPU, energy and HPC workloads.
interesting_fact: Qumulo's three founders met at Isilon Systems. Passey left Qumulo in 2016 and rejoined in 2022, calling his return 'a true homecoming'.
deep_cut_fact: When he rejoined, Qumulo's CTO Kiran Bhageshpur noted that Passey had worked on four distinct distributed storage products and called him 'a fearless and imaginative technical leader'.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Architect, Qumulo (Seattle scale-out file-data platform)

name: Neal Fachan
profile: Systems engineer Neal Fachan co-founded Seattle scale-out file-storage company Qumulo in 2012 with fellow Isilon veterans Peter Godman and Aaron Passey, and later served as its Chief Scientist. name: Peter Godman
profile: Peter Godman is a Seattle systems engineer. At Isilon he led several major releases of the OneFS distributed file system, then was VP engineering and CEO at Corensic. name: Avi Baum
profile: Israeli chip architect who co-founded Hailo in 2017 after serving as CTO for Wireless Connectivity at Texas Instruments and in senior architecture roles in the Israel Defense Forces. Hailo designs low-power AI accelerators and vision processors (Hailo-8, Hailo-10H with on-device generative AI, Hailo-15) used in cameras, cars, PCs and the Raspberry Pi AI HAT; it reached a ~$1B unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Hailo's chips power the official Raspberry Pi AI Kit/AI HAT add-ons, putting dedicated neural-network accelerators in the hands of hobbyists, and its Hailo-10H brings LLMs/VLMs onto edge devices.
deep_cut_fact: He argues TOPS is no longer the right yardstick for edge AI: for generative models, memory bandwidth matters more, and each product needs its own 'power-cost-latency working point' (Unite.AI interview, Aug 2025). He also writes on the DRAM shortage's effect on edge AI.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Hailo (Tel Aviv-based edge-AI processor company)
research_notes: Accessible technical leader who regularly blogs and gives interviews (hailo.ai/blog). LinkedIn is linked from Hailo's own leadership page. Edge-AI counterpoint to data-center AI; good on power-efficiency and memory-bandwidth topics.

profile: Hurun (2021-2024) lists Hadar Zeitlin as a founder of Hailo, the Israeli maker of edge AI processors (Hailo-8, Hailo-10 and vision processors), founded in 2017 and valued at about $1B. Hailo's current leadership team (CEO Orr Danon, CTO Avi Baum) does not include him; his current role could not be verified.

current_role: Listed as a co-founder of Hailo (Tel Aviv edge-AI chipmaker); not on Hailo's current leadership team page

name: Orr Danon
profile: Orr Danon co-founded Hailo in Tel Aviv in February 2017 with Avi Baum, Hadar Zeitlin and Rami Feig, and became CEO after Feig's passing. Hailo designs low-power AI processors for edge devices - the Hailo-8 accelerator, Hailo-15 vision processors and Hailo-10H generative-AI module - and became a unicorn with its $136M Series C in 2021. Microchip Technology agreed to buy Hailo in July 2026 and closed the deal on 21 Sept 2026.
interesting_fact: Hailo went from a $3.5M seed round in 2017 to a $1B valuation in 2021, and its Hailo-10H powers what ASUS billed as the world's first USB edge-AI accelerator.
deep_cut_fact: At Calcalist's AI Conference in Sept 2025 he argued AI's next frontier is embodied systems: 'What's really big in AI today is undoubtedly the cloud, but the issue of AI entering the physical world is a revolution no less significant,' adding that China's robot competitions 'feel like the moments before ChatGPT.'
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Hailo Technologies (Tel Aviv edge-AI chipmaker; acquired by Microchip Technology, completed Sept 2026)
research_notes: Hailo's site still lists him as CEO, but his role post-Microchip acquisition (Sept 2026) should be checked. Strong fit for an edge-vs-datacenter AI compute conversation; regular conference speaker (CES, Calcalist). info@ is a general company inbox.

name: Jeffrey Spector
profile: Co-founded Karat in 2014 with Mo Bhende (now CEO) to re-engineer the technical interview for software engineers, outsourcing structured interviews to professional 'Interview Engineers'. Karat, valued around $1B, now pitches AI-native simulations and workforce intelligence for engineering leaders in the 'human + AI era'; Spector serves as President.
interesting_fact: Karat says it works with 7 of the 25 largest public companies in the world, 4 of the 7 largest payment companies and all 4 of the largest UK banks, having run hundreds of thousands of technical interviews.
deep_cut_fact: Spector and Bhende were friends who founded Karat around a shared belief that access to career growth is too often limited by where a person went to school, who their friends and family are, or past work experience - so they set out to make the technical interview itself more objective.
current_role: Co-founder and President, Karat (technical-interviewing and workforce-intelligence company, Seattle)
research_notes: Fit for data-center/AI podcast is indirect (hiring/talent in the AI era). Route via press@karat.com.

name: Mohit Bhende
profile: Mohit 'Mo' Bhende co-founded Karat in 2014 with Jeffrey Spector to re-engineer how software engineers are interviewed; Karat runs technical interviews for large enterprises and reached unicorn valuation in 2021. Before Karat he was a senior director at Microsoft working on Xbox product strategy (including in China), and a strategy consultant at Oliver Wyman.

current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Karat (Seattle technical-interviewing / Human+AI hiring platform)
research_notes: Press contact in Karat releases: Gordie Hanrahan, Sr. Director Communications (press@karat.com). He also co-founded Seattle-based Topic Magazine (per secondary profiles, not verified). Gates Cambridge annual report 2024 lists him as a 2001 first-cohort scholar. name: David Cummings
profile: Atlanta serial entrepreneur David Cummings co-founded marketing-automation firm Pardot, which was sold to ExactTarget (later Salesforce) for $95M in 2012. He then co-founded SalesLoft with Kyle Porter. Salesloft reached a $1B+ valuation before Vista Equity bought it. He now runs the Atlanta Tech Village startup hub and the Atlanta Ventures fund.
interesting_fact: Atlanta Tech Village, which he founded, is billed as the Southeast's largest tech entrepreneur center. Its alumni include SalesLoft, Calendly and Terminus. He was an early investor in Calendly.
deep_cut_fact: A Tallahassee, Florida native with an economics degree from Duke, he has founded 10+ companies. Besides software, they include Intown Golf Club, an Atlanta indoor golf venture.
current_role: Founder, Atlanta Tech Village; founder/CEO, Atlanta Ventures
research_notes: Very accessible. He has blogged on davidcummings.org for years and is active on X. Atlanta Tech Village and Atlanta Ventures are natural routes in.

name: Kyle Porter
profile: Atlanta entrepreneur who co-founded sales-engagement platform Salesloft in 2011 out of Georgia Tech's ATDC and led it as CEO through Vista Equity's ~$2.3bn acquisition (2021). He stepped down as CEO in 2023 (David Obrand succeeded him) and stayed on the board; Salesloft agreed to merge with Clari in 2025.

deep_cut_fact: Salesloft killed its original, most profitable product, the lead-scraping tool Prospector, because customers were using it for spam, betting the company on Cadence, then a tiny ~$75k business, which became the flagship.
current_role: Founder and board member/former chairman, Salesloft (now merged with Clari); LP at Stage 2 Capital
research_notes: Active in Atlanta startup ecosystem (Endeavor Atlanta board per directories) and appears on podcasts; LinkedIn is the most direct published route.

Thiel Fellow, Forbes 30 Under 30 (2019) and named by Forbes in 2021 the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company.

name: Arad Levertov

research_notes: Has done many podcasts (Mixergy, DealMakers, Fintech Business Weekly) - receptive to founder-story interviews. Reported military background varies between sources; not used.

research_notes: Also known as Ornit Maizel. Degrees: BSc Information Systems Engineering (Ben-Gurion Univ.), MBA in Finance (Tel Aviv Univ.). Mentors startups.

He leads Sunbit's revenue/sales effort. Before Sunbit he co-founded video-ad company Eyeview (2008) and worked at HP and Google.

current_role: Working on AI at Chainalysis (after Chainalysis acquired his startups Nash and Once Upon in 2025)
public_contact: official_website: https://jordanmessina.com | press_email: press@density.io (Density media/speaking inquiries)
research_notes: Hurun lists him as Density founder; Density is now led by co-founder/CEO Andrew Farah. His personal site is the best direct route; Density press email only reaches the company he co-founded.

name: Robert Grazioli
profile: Listed by Hurun's Unicorn Index (2021-2024) as a founder of Density, a U.S. maker of privacy-preserving people-counting/occupancy sensors and workplace analytics (valued around $1B). Density's current leadership page lists Andrew Farah as CEO/founder and does not list Grazioli, so his present role could not be confirmed.
research_notes: Shared web-search budget was exhausted before his role could be verified; he does not appear on Density's current leadership page, so he may have left. Needs a follow-up check (e.g. Density press materials) before outreach.

name: Steven VonDeak
profile: Listed by Hurun's unicorn-founder ranking (2021-2024) as a founder of Density, the Syracuse-born (founded 2014) maker of privacy-preserving people-counting sensors and workplace-occupancy analytics, valued around $1B. His current role could not be confirmed: Density's current leadership page lists Andrew Farah as CEO/founder and does not mention VonDeak.
interesting_fact: Density designs and assembles its sensors in the US and measures how people use space without cameras capturing identities; its products are available in 30+ countries.
research_notes: Could not independently verify his founder role or current status (web search budget exhausted; not on Density's current leadership page). Likely no longer at the company. press@density.io is the company press contact, not his.

name: Suhail Doshi
profile: Self-taught programmer who left Arizona State to co-found product-analytics company Mixpanel with Tim Trefren (YC Summer 2009), serving as CEO until 2018. He then built Mighty (a browser streamed from a data center) before pivoting to Playground, an AI-first graphics editor that trains its own image models.
interesting_fact: Mixpanel's idea came from his 2008 internship at Max Levchin's Slide, where he saw the company spending over $1M to build its own internal analytics, as Zynga and others were doing too.
deep_cut_fact: He landed the Slide internship via an offer over IRC while a computer systems engineering student at ASU; Levchin tried to hire him full-time after three months, but he went back to school and then left to start Mixpanel.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Playground (AI graphic design/image model company)
research_notes: Very active on X (@Suhail) and a frequent podcast guest (Latent Space, YC Lightcone) - X is the most natural public route. Data-center angle: Mighty streamed Chrome from cloud servers; Playground trains large diffusion models.

name: Tim Trefren
profile: Co-founded product-analytics company Mixpanel with Suhail Doshi in Y Combinator's Summer 2009 batch and worked there 2009-2019 (latterly VP of Customer Success); Mixpanel hit a $1.05B valuation in 2021. He now works on climate through Recheck, a Hanover, NH-based identity, compliance and reputation layer for the residential solar industry.
interesting_fact: Recheck says it has 50,000+ verified solar sales reps and that partners account for 90%+ of US residential solar financing - a natural fit for an energy-focused podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Recheck's founding team is drawn from Mixpanel, HipChat, Notarize and Ohm Analytics, and the company is based in Hanover, New Hampshire rather than Silicon Valley.
current_role: Working on climate at Recheck (identity/compliance platform for US residential solar; reported as co-founder & CEO)
research_notes: YC's Mixpanel page says he is 'now working on climate change at Recheck'; his exact title (CEO) comes from aggregator sites, so confirm. Strong energy-podcast angle (residential solar trust/compliance).

name: Brandon Y Jeon
profile: Korean co-founder of Sendbird, the in-app chat, voice and AI-agent API company founded in 2013 with John S. Kim, Harry Kim and Forest Lee; it became a Korean-founded unicorn in 2021 (~$1B+ valuation). Profiles list him in developer-experience/quality-engineering and trust-and-safety roles at the company.
interesting_fact: Sendbird was named among Korea's new unicorns after its 2021 raise, with Jeon listed as one of its four co-founders.
current_role: Co-founder, Sendbird (San Mateo, CA / Seoul)
research_notes: Very low public profile; titles differ across aggregators. Sendbird reportedly grew out of an earlier Korean community app (SmileMom) but only aggregator sources say so. Best route is via Sendbird or CEO John Kim.

name: Forest Lee
profile: Forest Lee is one of the four co-founders of Sendbird (2013, Korea; now San Mateo), the chat/messaging API company valued at $1.05B in 2021 that has pivoted to AI customer-service agents (Delight.ai). He led Sendbird's product design for over a decade; CEO John S. Kim is the company's public face.
interesting_fact: Sendbird began in Seoul in 2013 as a community app for mothers; the team pulled out its messaging engine and turned it into a B2B chat API, becoming only the second Korean company backed by Y Combinator (W16).
current_role: Co-founder, Sendbird (formerly Head of Design; aggregator profiles list an 'AI Agent Workforce Manager' role since 2025)
research_notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Current role per aggregator profiles (Crunchbase/Humantic) only - verify on LinkedIn. Founder rosters vary by source; MarketScreener lists him as co-founder. Origin story detail also at https://koreatechdesk.com/?p=1370. Route via CEO John Kim/company.

name: Harry Kim
profile: Korean-born engineer who co-founded Sendbird with CEO John S. Kim, Brandon Jeon and Forest Lee; it went through Y Combinator (W16), moved HQ to San Mateo and became a chat/messaging API unicorn (~$1B+ valuation in 2021). Sendbird is now pivoting to AI customer-service agents (Delight.ai). Per profiles he was earlier technical director at Paprika Lab (acquired by GREE).
interesting_fact: Sendbird began as a pivot: the team was building 'Smile Mom', an app to connect nearby mothers, couldn't find a good off-the-shelf chat tool, built their own, and friends kept asking to use it - so they turned the chat engine into the company.
current_role: Co-founder, Sendbird (listed as Founder/CTO on Y Combinator; some profiles say Chief Architect)
research_notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Not to be confused with John S. Kim (CEO). Earlier career details (Paprika Lab, GREE Korea, Wisenut, Monash University) come only from aggregator profiles. No verified Sendbird press email found; a past release listed Moore Communications as PR contact.

name: Peter Meusel
profile: German robotics engineer from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) who co-founded Agile Robots in 2018 with Dr. Zhaopeng Chen and eight other DLR experts. The Munich-based DLR spin-off builds force-sensitive robot arms, hands and AI-driven automation systems and has become one of Europe's most valuable robotics companies, backed by Sequoia China, Hillhouse and others.
interesting_fact: Agile Robots' first robot, the seven-axis lightweight arm 'Diana 7', debuted in 2019, only a year after founding; the company has since moved into humanoids and 'physical AI'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Agile Robots, Meusel and Chen co-founded an earlier DLR spin-off, Wessling Robotics, built on the humanoid robot hand Chen developed at DLR; Meusel is also credited as a key member of the team behind the DLR/KUKA Light-Weight Robot (LWR).
current_role: Co-Founder, Agile Robots SE (Munich); role beyond co-founder not confirmed (TheOrg lists Co-CEO/Managing Director)
research_notes: Low public profile; CEO Zhaopeng Chen is the company's public face. LWR credit comes from his Crunchbase profile (https://www.crunchbase.com/person/peter-meusel). No published press email found on the JS-rendered site.

name: Zhaopeng Chen
profile: Chinese-born roboticist who completed his doctorate at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and was deputy director of its Modular Dexterous Robotics Lab before co-founding Agile Robots with DLR scientist Peter Meusel in 2018. The Munich company makes force-sensitive AI-driven robot arms and systems and now the Agile ONE humanoid; it became a unicorn in 2021.
interesting_fact: At DLR he worked on the team that developed a widely acclaimed humanoid robotic hand, which became the basis of his first spin-off with Peter Meusel, Wessling Robotics, before Agile Robots.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong science-fiction fan, he says getting into his Chinese university's robotics institute 'was not easy'; from his third year he built robot hands and arms end-to-end, and at DLR spent years on robotic systems for outer space.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Agile Robots SE (Munich)
research_notes: No published press email found (site is JS-heavy); use the company website or DLR spin-off page (https://www.dlr.de/en/rm/transfer/spin-offs/agile-robots) for context. Space-robotics and humanoid angle fits a deep-tech podcast.

name: Jonathan Anguelov
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded cloud-telephony company Aircall in 2014 with Olivier Pailhès, Pierre-Baptiste Béchu and Xavier Durand; he built its sales organisation and US expansion from New York as Aircall became a $1B+ unicorn. Since leaving operations in 2023 he invests in real estate via Aguesseau Capital, angel-invests and appears as a TV investor.
interesting_fact: Raised in foster care in Sucy-en-Brie, he told his rags-to-unicorn story in the autobiography 'Rien à perdre' (Éditions Alisio / Albin Michel, March 2025).
deep_cut_fact: He sold pizzas at 17 and began investing in real estate at 18 with savings from student jobs; those rental investments were his main income during Aircall's early, unpaid years.
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder of Aircall (left operations Sept 2023); co-founder of real-estate investor Aguesseau Capital; investor-juror on M6's 'Qui veut être mon associé ?'
research_notes: Very public in France (TV, book, podcasts). Aircall went through 500 Startups in San Francisco and raised $2.75M seed. contact@aircall.io is a general company inbox; he is no longer operational there, so outreach via his book publisher or Aguesseau Capital may be better.

name: Olivier Pailhès
profile: HEC Paris MBA and ex-BCG/ArcelorMittal staffer who co-founded Paris-based cloud phone company Aircall in 2014 with three partners and ran it until 2023, then stayed on the board. He returned as CEO in October 2026 to push Aircall, now at $250M ARR and 24,000+ customers, into AI voice agents.
interesting_fact: On returning as CEO he framed the bet as: 'AI has handed us a rare opportunity; to bring voice back to the center of customer conversations.' Aircall was valued at about $1B+ in its 2021 round.
deep_cut_fact: He is an accomplished pianist - Aircall's own announcement says the Paris team knows that an unscheduled jazz performance usually means the founder is in the building.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Aircall (returned as CEO on 29 Oct 2026, succeeding Scott Chancellor)
research_notes: Very timely: just returned as CEO (Oct 2026) with an AI-voice-agent agenda. Press contact is Aircall's published media contact on that release.

name: Pierre-Baptiste Béchu
profile: French engineer and one of Aircall's four co-founders (with Olivier Pailhès, Xavier Durand and Jonathan Anguelov). Joining in 2014, he built the first version of Aircall's backend and infrastructure; the cloud phone system for sales and support teams reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. He now runs the engineering team behind Aircall's global voice platform and has served as interim CTPO.
interesting_fact: Unusual dual training: a Master of Engineering from École Centrale de Lyon plus a master's in industrial and organizational psychology from Université Lumière Lyon 2.
deep_cut_fact: He personally wrote the first version of Aircall's backend and infrastructure in 2014, and today leads 20+ engineers keeping its worldwide voice services reliable -- voice quality and security are his core focus.
current_role: Co-founder, Aircall; leads the communications-platform (VoIP/WebRTC) engineering team
research_notes: Technical, low-profile co-founder (no CEO role); Aircall's press room lists no email. Also an angel investor (50 Partners, per aggregator profiles -- unverified). A data/infra-focused podcast angle fits him.

name: Thibaud Elziere
education: École Centrale de Lyon
profile: French serial entrepreneur (b. 1979, Aix-en-Provence) who co-founded stock-photo site Fotolia in 2004 (sold to Adobe in 2014 for ~EUR800M), then in 2011 co-founded startup studio eFounders (Hexa since 2022), which launched ~40 startups including unicorns Spendesk, Front and Aircall. He has run Folk since 2019 and has angel-invested in ~100 startups (Algolia, Notion, Hugging Face).
interesting_fact: Hexa's studio model hands founders a ready idea, seed funding and support; its startups (Spendesk, Front, Aircall) reached a combined ~$5B valuation and ~2,800 jobs.
deep_cut_fact: He started Fotolia while still a student at Ecole Centrale de Lyon, and his side ventures include Gama Space, a solar-sail space project, and Kate, a microcar maker.
current_role: Co-founder of Hexa (formerly eFounders) startup studio; CEO of Folk (CRM built within Hexa)
research_notes: Spendesk's operating co-founder/CEO is Rodolphe Ardant; Elziere is co-founder via the eFounders studio. Based in Brussels. Gama Space solar sail could be a good energy/space hook.

name: Xavier Durand
profile: French engineer with front-end development expertise who co-founded cloud phone-system company Aircall in 2014 at the eFounders startup studio in Paris, alongside Olivier Pailhes, Jonathan Anguelov and Pierre-Baptiste Bechu. Aircall became eFounders' first unicorn in 2020; Durand left in late 2020.
interesting_fact: Aircall's founders went through the 500 Startups 2015 batch in San Francisco, then raised $2.75M; within five months the team grew from 5 to 15 and turnover tripled.
deep_cut_fact: When Aircall struggled with hiring and fundraising, Durand moved to New York with CEO Olivier Pailhes while the technical team stayed in Paris -- a split that became a blueprint for French founders building in the US.
current_role: Co-founder of Aircall (left the company in late 2020); current role not found
research_notes: Very low public profile and no longer at Aircall; contact@aircall.io is a company address, not his. LinkedIn is likely the only route.

name: Anderson Sumarli
profile: Indonesian fintech founder who started Ajaib with Stanford GSB classmate Yada Piyajomkwan; it went through Y Combinator (S18) and became Southeast Asia's first investment-fintech unicorn, offering stocks, mutual funds and crypto. Ajaib also controls Bank Bumi Artha (BNBA). In Aug 2026 it raised a US$270M Series C led by SBI Group at a valuation above its prior ~US$1B mark.
interesting_fact: Ajaib's US$270M Series C (Aug 2026), led by Japan's SBI Group, was reported as Indonesia's biggest tech funding round since 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Ajaib he studied Applied Economics & Management at Cornell (summa cum laude), worked in IBM's Chief Analytics Office (2014-16) and was a BCG consultant (2016-18), then did his MBA at Stanford GSB.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Ajaib Group (Indonesian investment app; also President Commissioner of Ajaib Sekuritas)
research_notes: No published press email found on Ajaib's site. Stanford GSB has a case study on Ajaib (useful conversation hook). EY Indonesia 2022 Young Entrepreneur Award; Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2020.

name: Yada Piyajomkwan
profile: Thai-born co-founder of Jakarta online brokerage Ajaib, started in 2019 with Stanford GSB classmate Anderson Sumarli; it became a unicorn in 2021 and passed one million investors. Ex-McKinsey and Unilever, Stanford MBA '19; Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2020.
interesting_fact: Ajaib went through Y Combinator and hit a $1B valuation in 2021 only about two years after founding; Stanford GSB later wrote a teaching case on it.
deep_cut_fact: She mentors women through UNHCR's Leading Women Fund and She Loves Tech, and was profiled by UNHCR Thailand for that work.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Ajaib (Indonesia)
research_notes: Some older sources list her as COO; recent ones say CPO.

name: Derek Slager
profile: Seattle engineer who co-founded customer data platform Amperity (2016) with Kabir Shahani after both were on the founding team of Appature (acquired by IMS Health). He built Amperity's patented ML-based identity resolution; the company hit a $1B valuation in 2020. Now co-CEO leading its AI-first transformation.
interesting_fact: Amperity uses machine learning rather than hand-written rules to resolve customer identity, stitching together billions of records across a brand's systems; the patented identity resolution was built under Slager.
deep_cut_fact: Before Amperity and Appature he was a software developer at Seattle-era companies Activate, Loudeye (an early digital-music/streaming firm) and Blue Dot, then ran engineering at IMS Health after Appature's acquisition.
current_role: Co-founder & co-CEO (also CTO), Amperity (Seattle)
research_notes: Frequent podcast guest (NVIDIA AI Podcast 2025, Databricks Data+AI Summit speaker). Amperity site titles vary (CTO vs co-CEO).

name: Kabir Shahani
profile: Seattle entrepreneur (b. 1982, Kansas City) who co-founded health-marketing software firm Appature (sold to IMS Health in 2013) and then customer-data platform Amperity (2016) with Derek Slager, leading it to unicorn status before stepping down as CEO in 2022. He now incubates and backs software startups through Amp It Up Ventures and teaches at UW.
interesting_fact: Holds more than 10 US patents spanning databases, entity resolution and machine learning; Amperity worked with UW's Dan Suciu on a probabilistic customer database.
deep_cut_fact: He founded his first company at 24 and was named the U.S. Small Business Administration's Young Entrepreneur of the Year in 2012; he earned a BS in Informatics from UW in 2004.
current_role: Founder, Amp It Up Ventures; co-founder and former CEO of Amperity; Affiliate Assistant Professor, UW Information School
research_notes: Email is his UW iSchool affiliate-faculty address published by the university. 2024 GeekWire piece on his new venture: https://www.geekwire.com/2024/ex-amperity-ceo-kabir-shahani-is-amped-about-building-startups-with-his-latest-venture/

name: Amir Jerbi
profile: Israeli security engineer who served about four years in an IDF IT unit and later became a chief architect at a large security software company (CA Technologies). In 2015 he co-founded Aqua Security with Dror Davidoff; the cloud-native and container security company reached a $1B valuation in 2021. In November 2025 both founders stepped back to advisory roles, Mike Dube became CEO and Nir Makowski became chief product and technology officer.
interesting_fact: Aqua grew out of a weekly meetup. Jerbi saw an early Docker demo, went home, 'fell in love' with containers within days, and then quit his chief-architect job to work on container security full time.
deep_cut_fact: He has said he decided that 'leveraging containers for better security was my destiny'. He first worked on it as a 'new hobby' before founding Aqua with friends a year later; the original idea was to make containerised apps 'secured anywhere' as well as 'run anywhere'.
current_role: Co-founder of Aqua Security; strategic advisor since stepping down as CTO in November 2025
research_notes: The leadership change is dated 5 Nov 2025 (Calcalist). As of 2025, Aqua's press releases appear to route media through an agency (Look Left Marketing), but I could not open the release to verify the address, so it is not recorded. Note that Aqua cut staff after the 2025 reorganisation. He is a technical voice on cloud and container security and appeared on 'The IaC Podcast'.

name: Dror Davidoff
profile: Dror Davidoff co-founded cloud-native security company Aqua Security in Ramat Gan in 2015 with CTO Amir Jerbi and was its CEO for a decade, growing it to about 450 staff, roughly $235M raised and a peak valuation of about $1B. In November 2025 he stepped back to strategic advisor, and President/CRO Mike Dube became CEO.
interesting_fact: Aqua was founded as 'Scalock' and rebranded in 2016. Jerbi said the original name 'ended up not fitting what we aim to do.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Aqua, Davidoff was EVP Sales & Business Development at database-security startup Sentrigo (joined 2008), which McAfee acquired in 2011. He then headed global sales of database security products at McAfee (Intel Security).
current_role: Co-founder and strategic advisor, Aqua Security (stepped down as CEO in Nov 2025)
public_contact: pr_agency: Look Left Marketing (Aqua's media contact on 2025 releases, e.g. Geena Pickering / Jennifer Tanner) | official_website: https://www.aquasec.com
research_notes: Now an advisor, no longer running Aqua day to day, so he may have more time for a podcast. He has author pages on Dark Reading and Cloud Native Now. The PR agency was seen via a search snippet (page blocked direct fetch).

name: Adam Crawshaw
profile: Adam Crawshaw is listed as a co-founder of Assembly, an e-commerce software roll-up formed around 2018. Assembly bought Refersion and Amazon-seller tool Helium 10 in 2020, then the ad platform Pacvue in 2021, and later unified its products under the Pacvue brand. In July 2020 he was quoted as President of Assembly. His current role could not be verified from official sources.
interesting_fact: Assembly assembled Helium 10, the Amazon-seller toolkit, and Pacvue, the commerce-advertising platform, into one software group serving brands that sell on online marketplaces.
current_role: Unverified; co-founder and former President of Assembly (e-commerce software group behind Helium 10, Refersion and Pacvue)
research_notes: Identity marked uncertain: the only official mention found is a 2020 Assembly press release naming him 'President of Assembly'. Co-founder status and later roles (Refersion GM, Helium 10 GM) come only from aggregator profiles. Don't confuse this Assembly with the ad agency Assembly Global. No published contact found.

name: Sandeep Kella
profile: Co-founder and former CEO of Assembly, an e-commerce software roll-up that bought Amazon-seller tool Helium 10 (2020) and enterprise retail-media platform Pacvue (2021), then took the Pacvue name. In September 2024 he handed the CEO role to Rahul Choraria and became executive chairman, overseeing strategy.
interesting_fact: He bought Pacvue just one month after an Advent International-led round pushed Assembly's valuation above $1B; Pacvue says revenue quadrupled in four years and it has been 'highly profitable since inception'.
deep_cut_fact: When he stepped up to executive chairman in 2024 he brought onto Pacvue's board Harry Shum, the computer scientist who led Microsoft's AI and Research group.
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman of the Board, Pacvue (since Sept 2024; previously CEO)
research_notes: Acquirer/operator rather than original Pacvue founder (Pacvue was founded by Melissa Burdick and others; Kella co-founded Assembly). Low media profile.

name: Criag Iley
profile: UK banker (name is Craig Iley; input has a typo) who joined Atom Bank from Santander as commercial/business banking director and is described as a co-founder of Atom Bank and of Bank North. He later founded Business Finance Market, a platform matching lenders with SMEs. Atom's commonly cited founders are Anthony Thomson and Mark Mullen, so 'founder' attribution is loose.
interesting_fact: He argues the UK has room for about ten more SME lenders in a ~£200bn market, and that a new bank needs 6-10 years to build a £5bn lending book; he points to Germany's tiered banking system as a model.
current_role: Founder of Business Finance Market (UK SME lending platform), per 2022 interview; current role not verified
research_notes: Hurun listing 'Atom Bank founder' is a stretch; he was an early senior exec (Finextra: 'Atom names Santander's Craig Iley as commercial director', https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/55176/atom-names-santanders-craig-iley-as-commercial-director). Low profile; likely not UHNW. Alive status not specifically confirmed.

name: Gal Shaul
profile: Gal Shaul co-founded Augury in 2011 (with CEO Saar Yoskovitz). Augury uses AI on vibration, temperature and magnetic sensor data to predict machine failures in factories. It launched its Machine Health product in 2017, became one of the first industrial-AI unicorns in 2021 and closed a Series F in 2025. It now pitches an 'Industrial AI Workforce' of monitoring and AI agents for manufacturers in 10+ industries.
interesting_fact: Augury's own timeline marks 2019 as the year its system first helped a manufacturer avoid a production loss, two years after Machine Health launched; in 2021 it became one of the first industrial-AI unicorns.
current_role: Co-founder, Augury Inc. (industrial AI / machine health, New York & Israel); current title not verified
public_contact: pr_agency: augury@panblastpr.com (Panblast PR) | office_email: info@augury.com | official_website: https://www.augury.com
research_notes: Augury's leadership page is JS-rendered and the web-search budget was exhausted, so his current title (formerly CTO, per general knowledge, unverified here) and personal background were not confirmed. Co-founder Saar Yoskovitz is the public face. Good fit for an energy-efficiency and industrial-AI angle. Best route: Panblast PR.

name: Saar Yoskovitz
profile: Saar Yoskovitz, a Technion graduate in electrical engineering and physics, co-founded Augury in 2012 with CTO Gal Shaul. Augury combines IoT sensors and AI to monitor industrial machines and predict failures before they happen, for customers such as PepsiCo, Nestlé and Colgate-Palmolive. It became a unicorn with a $180M round in October 2021 and raised $75M at a >$1B valuation in February 2025.
interesting_fact: Augury's sensors 'listen' to machines, continuously capturing sound, temperature and electromagnetic signals so AI can detect faults early. Its customers include utilities such as Israel Electric Corporation and the national water company Mekorot.
deep_cut_fact: Augury started small: its first seed round, in October 2014, raised just $2M, well before the later $55M and $180M rounds. In 2019 it acquired the US startup Alluvium. In 2021 it won Israel's Atlas Award.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Augury (machine-health AI; Haifa/Tel Aviv and New York)
research_notes: He is a strong fit for an industrial-AI/energy-efficiency episode and is a frequent speaker. augury.com blocked automated access (403), so I could not retrieve a press email or contact form. The web-search budget was exhausted before I could verify his social accounts. Try Augury's newsroom page manually.

name: Hari Ravichandran
education: Mississippi State University; Stanford University; The Wharton School
profile: Indian-born American serial founder. He started BizLand, which grew into Endurance International Group (Bluehost, HostGator), and ran it until 2017. He has been CEO of Aura, a consumer identity-theft and online-safety company, since 2019. In 2026 Aura completed its acquisition of Australia's Qoria, creating a group with more than $300M ARR that trades on the ASX as AXQ.
interesting_fact: He started BizLand with most of his $8,000 savings. After the dot-com crash he cut staff to 14 and made customers pay subscriptions; only about 2% converted, yet the company broke even the next year on $2M revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Instead of spending on marketing, Endurance grew by buying small hosting firms with 2,000-5,000 customers each, often with seller financing. His lesson from the crash: 'If you don't focus on profitability, things can go bad.'
current_role: Founder & CEO, Aura (digital safety; ASX: AXQ after the 2026 Qoria merger)
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.aura.com/press/contact (Aura press contact page) | official_website: https://www.aura.com/leadership | https://hariravichandran.com/
research_notes: Aura's bio says he has an MBA from Wharton, a computer engineering degree from Mississippi State and studied electrical engineering at Stanford. He founded the Ravichandran Foundation (Boston area and India; source: latinpost). Aura is now ASX-listed, so ASX investor-relations channels apply.

name: Kam Ghaffarian
profile: Iranian-born American engineer-entrepreneur who moved to the US at 17. Co-founded NASA contractor Stinger Ghaffarian Technologies (sold to KBR for $355M in 2018), then built a space-and-energy portfolio: X-energy (high-temperature gas-cooled nuclear reactors, 2009), Intuitive Machines (Moon lander, public via SPAC 2023), Axiom Space (private space station, 2016) and Quantum Space (2020).
interesting_fact: Watching the 1969 Apollo 11 landing on TV in Iran sparked his interest in space; decades later his Intuitive Machines lander touched down on the Moon on Feb 22, 2024. His X-energy nuclear reactor company makes him directly relevant to energy/data-center power.
deep_cut_fact: As keynote speaker at Capitol Technology University's May 2, 2026 commencement (his alma mater: BS 1983, PhD 2022), he surprised every graduate crossing the stage with $1,500 in a gold envelope.
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Axiom Space; founder of X-energy; co-founder of Intuitive Machines and Quantum Space
research_notes: Also founded nonprofit Limitless Space Institute (2019). X-energy (nuclear SMRs) is the strongest angle for an energy/data-center podcast; X-energy's press office is an alternative route.

name: Michael Suffredini
education: University of Texas at Austin
profile: Mike Suffredini spent decades at NASA, including as International Space Station program manager (2005-2015), overseeing completion of ISS assembly. In 2016 he co-founded Houston-based Axiom Space with Kam Ghaffarian to build the first commercial space station, and led it as president/CEO; he stepped down as CEO in August 2024 and remains a board member and advisor.
interesting_fact: His honors include the NASA Distinguished Service Medal, Presidential Meritorious and Distinguished Executive ranks, the National Air and Space Museum Trophy and the Yuri Gagarin Medal.
deep_cut_fact: After watching Neil Armstrong land on the Moon as a child he wanted to be a 'space guy'; at UT Austin (aerospace engineering, 1983) he originally aimed at high-performance aircraft until studying orbital dynamics under Victor Szebehely pulled him toward space. He also created NASA's ISS Research Office.
current_role: Co-founder, board member and advisor, Axiom Space (CEO until Aug 2024)
research_notes: Stepped back from CEO 'for personal reasons' (Axiom release Aug 2024) - avoid probing. Axiom now markets orbital data centers, a strong hook for an energy/data-center podcast. Current Axiom CEO is Tejpaul Bhatia (since Apr 2025).

name: Jaswinder Chadha
profile: Jaswinder 'Jassi' Chadha co-founded Axtria in 2010, building it into a cloud software and analytics provider for pharma commercial operations (sales, marketing, data management) valued around $1B. An IIT Delhi mechanical engineer with operations-research graduate training (UTEP, Texas A&M), he has worked with 100+ global companies.

name: Peter Chaljawski
profile: Berlin entrepreneur who founded Chal-Tec in 2005 at 19, selling affordable DJ and event gear on eBay, then expanded into audio and household appliances (Klarstein, auna, blumfeldt). Renamed Berlin Brands Group in 2019, it became a D2C/Amazon-marketplace unicorn backed by Ardian. He handed the CEO role to ex-eBay manager Eben Sermon in Jan 2024 after 18 years.
interesting_fact: He skipped university: he postponed his studies, never started them, and used his savings to found Chal-Tec, saying 'we basically democratized DJ equipment' by offering affordable alternatives to premium brands.
deep_cut_fact: The company began because at 18 he wanted DJ equipment and found only expensive premium gear or cheap junk; he asked why there was no 'Zara' of DJ gear. Its first eBay sale came in 2007, and he personally oversaw construction of the company's central warehouse.
current_role: Founder of Berlin Brands Group (formerly Chal-Tec); stepped down as CEO in January 2024
research_notes: Left CEO role Jan 2024 (Börsen-Zeitung, https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/personen/berlin-brands-group-holt-ebay-veteranen-an-die-spitze). A deutsche-startups.de headline links him to 'D11Z.Ventures' investments (not verified). Named to Capital's Top 40 under 40 (2021). BBG website was unreachable this session; no contact verified.

name: Chanakya Hridaya
profile: Chanakya Hridaya co-founded BlackBuck in Bengaluru in 2015 with Rajesh Yabaji and B. Ramasubramaniam. BlackBuck is a digital platform for India's truck operators, covering payments, telematics, freight marketplace and vehicle finance. It listed in India in 2024 and has since renamed itself from Zinka Logistics Solutions to BlackBuck Limited. Hridaya is an executive director and promoter.
interesting_fact: BlackBuck, which he co-founded, listed on Indian exchanges in 2024. Its investor-relations page publishes his employment agreement among the IPO material documents, and he is named as a promoter and executive director.

name: Rajesh Yabaji
profile: IIT Kharagpur alumnus and former ITC supply-chain manager who co-founded BlackBuck in 2015 with ITC colleague Chanakya Hridaya and Ramasubramaniam B. The company began as a B2B full-truckload freight marketplace and grew into India's largest digital platform for truck operators, covering FASTag/fuel payments, telematics, loads and vehicle financing. It is now a listed company with Yabaji as chairman, MD and CEO.
interesting_fact: BlackBuck's growth exploded after India mandated FASTags for toll payments in 2019. Yabaji told Fortune India that '99% of the growth in business happened after 2019.'
deep_cut_fact: The idea came from his ITC project to modernise a 100-year-old supply chain. He could improve planning and warehousing, but transportation stayed out of reach because it was in the hands of fragmented truck owners.
current_role: Chairman, Managing Director & CEO, BlackBuck Ltd (formerly Zinka Logistics Solutions; listed on NSE/BSE)

profile: Georgia Tech-trained engineer who co-founded New York retail-marketing software company Bluecore (originally TriggerMail, founded 2013) with Mahmoud Arram and Max Bennett and led it as CEO to unicorn status, serving 400+ brands such as Sephora, J.Crew and Ralph Lauren. name: Max Bennett
profile: Former Goldman Sachs trader who in 2013 co-founded Bluecore (AI marketing personalisation for retailers, valued at $1B+) and served as its Chief Product Officer, then co-founded AI shopping-assistant company Alby; both were acquired. He wrote 'A Brief History of Intelligence' (Mariner, 2023) and now does neuroscience/AI research at Columbia and the Astera Institute.

deep_cut_fact: Despite no academic post at the time, he published peer-reviewed neuroscience papers, e.g. 'An Attempt at a Unified Theory of the Neocortical Microcircuit in Sensory Cortex' (Frontiers in Neural Circuits, 2020); he sits on the board of the Thousand Brains Project and is writing a sci-fi novel about the origins of life.
current_role: Researcher (neural memory, cortical microcircuits) at Columbia University and the Astera Institute; author

name: Blake Scholl
profile: Cincinnati-born Carnegie Mellon computer scientist who worked at early Amazon, then co-founded mobile startup Kima Labs (acquired by Groupon in 2012). He founded Boom in 2014 to build the Overture supersonic airliner; its XB-1 demonstrator went supersonic in 2025. In Dec 2025 Boom launched 'Superpower', a 42 MW natural-gas turbine for AI data centers, with a 1.21 GW launch order from Crusoe plus a $300M raise.
interesting_fact: Boom's Superpower turbine shares the core of its Symphony jet engine, needs no water, and Crusoe ordered 29 units (1.21 GW, >$1.25B backlog); Scholl says turbine revenue will help fund Overture. Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He left high school early on a scholarship for early entry to Carnegie Mellon, earned his private pilot license in 2007, and before founding Boom took aircraft-design classes and built his own aerodynamics model in early 2014; he put half his Kima sale proceeds into Boom.

He brought decades of certification experience from Hawker Beechcraft, Adam Aircraft, Eclipse Aviation and ICON Aircraft, and has led several passenger aircraft from clean-sheet design through FAA certification.
interesting_fact: He is one of only three Boom co-founders. He has led development of several passenger aircraft from clean-sheet design through FAA certification, the experience Boom needed to certify a new supersonic airliner.
deep_cut_fact: Before Boom, he was Chief Engineer of the Adam A700, a twin-engine very light jet from Adam Aircraft Industries. He was also an early employee at three aerospace startups and worked on experimental and military aircraft projects.

name: Kohsuke Kawaguchi
profile: Tokyo-born programmer (b. 1977) who created Hudson at Sun Microsystems in 2004, which became Jenkins, the dominant open-source CI/CD automation server, after a 2011 fork from Oracle. His start-up InfraDNA merged into CloudBees (2010), where he became CTO (2014); in 2020 he left to co-found Launchable (ML-driven test selection), which CloudBees acquired in 2024.
interesting_fact: Jenkins exists because of a trademark fight: when Oracle claimed the 'Hudson' name after buying Sun, the community voted in January 2011 to rename the project Jenkins, and both sides still call the other the fork. He won the 2011 Google-O'Reilly Open Source Award.
deep_cut_fact: A keen long-distance cyclist who blogs his rides: in 2026 he and an old friend pedalled ~519 km over five days along the Shinano, Japan's longest river, to the Sea of Japan and up the coast, after riding Japan's historic eastern highway together the year before.
current_role: Creator of Jenkins; co-founder of Launchable (acquired by CloudBees, Aug 2024); former CTO of CloudBees
research_notes: Hurun's $1B figure is CloudBees' valuation, not his wealth. Approachable, frequent conference speaker, active blogger in English and Japanese (cycling, cooking, coffee, AI). His site's About page still says CloudBees CTO (outdated). Best route: LinkedIn or X.

At Block he led engineering at its TBD unit. He now works on goose, Block's open-source on-machine AI agent, which is now under the Agentic AI Foundation.
interesting_fact: At AI Engineer Melbourne 2026 he spoke on 'What If You Never Needed an API Key Again? Building a Mesh LLM From Spare Compute', which pools idle machines into a shared LLM inference mesh.
deep_cut_fact: Long before CloudBees he built the early versions of the Drools rules/inference engine (later JBoss Rules) while an open-source architect at Red Hat. The AI-agent work he does today is a return to his roots in reasoning engines.
current_role: Principal Engineer, Block (works on goose, Block's open-source AI agent); co-founder of CloudBees

name: Sacha Labourey
profile: Swiss software entrepreneur (b. Neuchâtel 1975, EPFL) who was CTO of open-source middleware firm JBoss through its 2006 sale to Red Hat, then GM of Red Hat middleware. In 2010 he founded CloudBees (enterprise Jenkins CI/CD, DevOps), serving as CEO then CSO; since 2025 he is a board member and advisor.
interesting_fact: CloudBees became the main commercial company behind Jenkins, the open-source CI/CD automation server, and appointed Jenkins creator Kohsuke Kawaguchi as its Chief Technology Officer.
deep_cut_fact: Before JBoss he founded Cogito Informatique, a Swiss consultancy specialising in application servers and middleware; at JBoss he wrote the first implementation of load-balancing/fail-over (clustering) for the JBoss application server and ran JBoss Europe before becoming CTO.
current_role: Co-founder and board member, CloudBees (stepped back from day-to-day role as Chief Strategy Officer in Feb 2025).
research_notes: Based in Neuchâtel, Switzerland; frequent conference speaker and blogger. Now off day-to-day CloudBees duties (new CEO Moritz Plassnig, June 2026), so reach him personally via LinkedIn rather than company PR. Cloud/DevOps rather than energy.
