name: Hillel Kobrinsky
profile: Former IDF brigadier general who founded Interwise (sold to AT&T in 2007), then co-founded DriveNets with Ido Susan in 2015 to replace proprietary routers with disaggregated white-box networking. DriveNets now sells Ethernet AI fabric for GPU clusters and raised a $410m Series D in June 2026.
interesting_fact: DriveNets, built to displace Cisco in telcos like AT&T, has pivoted into AI data-center networking as an Ethernet alternative to Nvidia's fabrics - it reports $1bn+ in secured business and has been cash-flow positive since 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he was a brigadier general in the IDF Armored Corps; after selling Interwise he built and ran AT&T's Israeli R&D center, and from 2013-2015 was a senior adviser to Israel's Minister of Finance.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Strategy Officer, DriveNets (Ra'anana, Israel)
research_notes: Globes notes both founders 'recoil from media interviews' - expect a hard get. Also a co-founder and early secretary-general of Yair Lapid's Yesh Atid party (Globes). Press releases list agency contacts (Crystal Monahan, Martin Perlin) but emails are obfuscated. Strong AI data-center networking angle.

name: Ido Susan
profile: Serial Israeli founder Ido Susan co-founded Intucell, which invented self-optimising network (SON) software, and sold it to Cisco in 2013 for $475m after raising only $6m. He then spent about two years at Cisco. In 2015 he co-founded DriveNets with Hillel Kobrinsky to replace carrier routers with disaggregated, cloud-native software. DriveNets now also sells Ethernet fabrics for AI clusters and raised a $410m Series D in 2026.
interesting_fact: DriveNets, started to take on Cisco and Juniper at telecom operators, now competes with Nvidia in AI-factory networking. Globes reported a roughly $1bn five-year order book in 2025, and in 2026 it announced the first commercial long-distance 'scale-across' AI supercluster deployment.
deep_cut_fact: He never earned a university degree. He founded Intucell at about 24 and sold it to Cisco at 26, then founded a company to compete with his acquirer.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, DriveNets (Ra'anana, Israel)
public_contact: press_email: press@drivenets.com | pr_agency: drivenets@guyergroup.com (The Guyer Group; Crystal Monahan +1-617-290-2882) | official_website: https://drivenets.com/company
research_notes: Globes says both founders 'recoil from media interviews', so pitch through the PR agency with a data-centre and AI-networking angle. He has spoken at Calcalist's Tech TLV and on the DealMakers podcast (Alejandro Cremades).

name: Eli Harris
profile: Eli Harris, a former DJI strategic-partnerships lead, co-founded portable power-station maker EcoFlow with DJI battery engineer Lei 'Bruce' Wang (co-founder/CEO c.2016-2020). He then co-founded R-Zero (disinfection/building air quality) and Honor Pet, and now runs venture studio One Dream Ventures.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for EcoFlow at DJI, where disaster-relief and emergency projects showed him how critical portable batteries were; EcoFlow's pitch was to 'replace fuel generators and provide clean personal energy storage.'
deep_cut_fact: EcoFlow's first product, the 412-watt River 'personal grid', launched on Indiegogo and raised over $157,000 from 267 backers within days (523% of its $30k goal); early on EcoFlow also worked with an anti-poaching group in Kenya.
current_role: Co-founder & Partner, One Dream Ventures (venture studio for SaaS/AI tools for real estate & construction); co-founder of EcoFlow and R-Zero
public_contact: office_email: contact@onedreamventures.com | official_website: https://www.onedreamventures.com/ | podcast: Guest appearance: Tangent podcast (Nov 2024) on One Dream Ventures
research_notes: Forbes 30 Under 30 alum; podcast-friendly (has done several). Fits energy/climate-tech angle (portable storage, building energy). Some role dates come from profile aggregators. Note: the 'podcast' entry is a guest appearance, not his own show.

name: Hannah Sieber
profile: Mandarin-speaking, Stanford-educated co-founder of Shenzhen-based EcoFlow, the portable-power and home-battery unicorn, and a Forbes 30 Under 30 Energy honoree (2018). She now runs Artyc, which makes reusable, battery-powered, sensor-tracked coolers (Medstow) for shipping medical samples. It had raised about $14M by mid-2024.
interesting_fact: Artyc grew out of her Stanford research on California's wildfire power shutoffs. Seeing small businesses lose refrigerated stock in a 56-hour outage led her to ask 'Could we electrify the cold chain?'
deep_cut_fact: Artyc's first product, the hand-sized Medstow Micro, uses a USB-C-charged lithium battery and a solid-state heat pump to hold up to four vials at 3°C for at least 56 hours, matching the length of the shutoff that inspired it. She has lived in Shenzhen, Shanghai, Hangzhou and Beijing.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Artyc PBC (battery-powered cold-chain shipping for healthcare); co-founder of EcoFlow
public_contact: press_email: press@shipartyc.com (Artyc media contact) | official_website: https://www.shipartyc.com
research_notes: No longer at EcoFlow. A great podcast guest with a hardware/battery founder story from Shenzhen to San Francisco. She has appeared on My Climate Journey and speaks at conferences. Artyc's domain is shipartyc.com (artyc.com is parked). Nationality not confirmed.

name: Lei Wang
profile: HK PolyU mechanical engineering graduate (BEng 2010) with a PhD in battery technology who set up DJI's battery R&D department, then founded EcoFlow in Shenzhen (2016-17). Its RIVER and DELTA portable power stations, launched via crowdfunding, made EcoFlow a ~$2B unicorn in portable and home battery storage and solar generators.
interesting_fact: EcoFlow's DELTA power station sold US$2.8M on Kickstarter in 48 days; its first product, the RIVER, raised ~US$1M on Indiegogo and within six months topped Tmall's outdoor-power category.
deep_cut_fact: Before EcoFlow he established DJI's battery R&D department, and in about three years his team doubled the battery life of DJI's drones. He later completed CKGSB's Master of Entrepreneurship and Technology Innovation (METI) programme.
current_role: Founder and CEO, EcoFlow (Shenzhen portable power stations and home energy storage)
public_contact: press_email: media.na@ecoflow.com (North America PR; regional media.eu@ / media.apac@ also listed) | official_website: https://www.ecoflow.com
research_notes: Goes by 'Bruce Wang' in English and is profiled by PolyU as an alumnus (polyu.edu.hk/alumni ... bruce-wang-lei). Good energy-storage and home-backup-power angle. CKGSB dates EcoFlow's founding to 2016; most other sources say 2017.

name: Mikki Nasch
profile: Mikki Nasch co-founded Evidation Health (2012) with Christine Lemke, Luca Foschini and Alessio Signorini. Evidation runs a consumer app through which millions share wearable and app data for research, and sells real-world evidence to pharma; it was valued at about $1B. Earlier she held senior roles at Fair Isaac, BackWeb and Sense Networks.
interesting_fact: She argues 'between-care' data from wearables and apps should shape drug development from early trials through payer access, so the patient's voice reaches the people deciding reimbursement.
deep_cut_fact: Before Evidation she was EVP of business development at Sense Networks, a New York location-analytics startup co-founded with MIT's Alex 'Sandy' Pentland. Newsweek put it on its cover as 'The Next Google', and its Citysense app mapped nightlife hotspots from phone and taxi GPS data. Christine Lemke, her later Evidation co-founder, was its COO.
current_role: Co-founder of Evidation Health (former SVP Commercial/business development); current role unverified
research_notes: Low public profile; Crunchbase lists her Evidation role in the past tense and her location as Canada. Christine Lemke (CEO) is Evidation's public face. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Dave Merkel
profile: Cybersecurity veteran who co-founded Herndon, VA managed detection-and-response firm Expel in 2016 with Yanek Korff and Justin Bajko and led it as CEO for a decade to a $1B+ valuation. Previously CTO of Mandiant and then FireEye after their 2014 merger. In November 2026 he handed the CEO role to Steve Kelley and stayed on the board.
interesting_fact: Expel's founders said they started it because they couldn't buy the security service they wanted: 'a few practitioners left to build the service they wished they could buy.'
deep_cut_fact: He started his ~30-year security career as a federal agent investigating cybercriminals (other bios specify the US Air Force Office of Special Investigations); his own author bio jokes that he is often mistaken for Willy Wonka.
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Expel (stepped down as CEO Nov 2026; succeeded by Steve Kelley)
research_notes: Just transitioned out of the CEO seat (GovInfoSecurity, 10 Nov 2026) -> may have more time for a podcast. Frequent RSA Conference speaker; blogs on expel.com.

name: Justin Bajko
profile: Security-operations veteran who co-founded managed detection and response (MDR) firm Expel in 2016 with fellow Mandiant alumni Dave Merkel and Yanek Korff; Expel reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. Long its VP of Strategy and Business Development, he became Chief Strategy Officer in Nov 2025, overseeing corporate and product strategy including AI in the SOC.
interesting_fact: Before Expel he ran Mandiant's Managed Defense, one of the industry's first MDR services, and then built FireEye's global SOCs as senior director of global service delivery; earlier he worked at Symantec.
deep_cut_fact: Expel's own profile calls him a University of Tennessee football fan and 'video game connoisseur'; he has compared bloated security platforms to cable TV, where 'you have to buy 100 channels just to access the specific one you want.'
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer, Expel (since Nov 2025)
research_notes: Publicly invites outreach in his CSO announcement ('Reach out. I'd love to chat.'). Route via Expel comms.

name: Yanek Korff
profile: Security veteran Yanek Korff co-founded Expel, a managed detection and response firm in Herndon, Virginia, with fellow Mandiant alumni Dave Merkel and Justin Bajko around 2016. Expel became a $1B+ unicorn in 2021. Before that, Korff ran Mandiant's managed services business, was CTO of FireEye as a Service, and was responsible for most of AOL's security infrastructure.
interesting_fact: He co-authored the O'Reilly book 'Mastering FreeBSD and OpenBSD Security'.
deep_cut_fact: His IT career began as a student help-desk technician in a 'musty basement' at the College of William and Mary. Expel's bio also says that whenever anything looks about to catch fire, he walks towards it.
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Expel (some Expel pages list him as Chief of Staff)
research_notes: He writes on Expel's blog and speaks at SecureWorld events. Sources disagree on his title (COO vs Chief of Staff).

name: Elram Goren
profile: Israeli entrepreneur and former IDF intelligence-technology officer who co-founded CommonSense Robotics in 2015 with Ori Avraham and Shay Cohen; it rebranded as Fabric in 2019, moved HQ to New York, and raised hundreds of millions for robotic micro-fulfillment centers for grocers and retailers (partners incl. Instacart, Super-Pharm, Walmart).
interesting_fact: Fabric's pitch was a 'third option' for retailers: robotic micro-fulfillment hubs close to customers so on-demand delivery doesn't require loss-making unit economics.
deep_cut_fact: Fabric started life as CommonSense Robotics; asked in a 2021 Calcalist '20-Minute Leaders' interview for three words to describe himself, Goren answered: 'Yes, we can.'
current_role: Co-founder, Fabric (Get Fabric); former CEO (stepped down 2022) - current role not publicly confirmed
research_notes: Replaced as CEO by COO Jack Jacoby in July 2022 restructuring (said to remain with the company); no public info on his current activity. No published direct contact found.

name: Eyal Goren
profile: Israeli engineer who in 2015 co-founded CommonSense Robotics (later Fabric) with his brother Elram Goren (CEO), Ori Avraham and Shay Cohen, building robotic micro-fulfillment centers for grocery and retail e-commerce. Fabric raised $200M in 2021 at a $1B+ valuation. Eyal held software, business development and strategic partnerships roles and is a named co-inventor on Fabric patents.
interesting_fact: Fabric's 2021 $200M Series C made it what the company billed a 'robocorn' - a robotics unicorn built on small urban micro-fulfillment sites.
deep_cut_fact: Fabric (then CommonSense Robotics) was founded in 2015 by two brothers, Elram and Eyal Goren, together with Ori Avraham and Shay Cohen.
current_role: Co-founder of Fabric (formerly CommonSense Robotics); reportedly no longer at the company, founder of AutoBirds (AI/MVP studio, Israel) per aggregator profile
research_notes: Low public profile; the CEO and public face of Fabric is his brother Elram Goren. Current role (AutoBirds) only from an aggregator; verify on LinkedIn. No published contact found.

name: Ori Avraham
profile: Israeli Air Force major and Talpiot graduate (physics/maths, Hebrew University; MBA, Tel Aviv University) who co-founded CommonSense Robotics in 2015 with Elram Goren and Shay Cohen. Renamed Fabric in 2019, the company builds robotic micro-fulfillment centers for grocers and retailers and was valued at ~$1B; he now leads product and strategy and holds several patents.
interesting_fact: Fabric's founders came from outside logistics entirely (IDF technology/intelligence backgrounds) and set out to put compact robotic fulfillment centers inside cities so retailers could deliver online orders within an hour.
deep_cut_fact: In the Israeli Air Force he specialised in operations research and received the Air Force Commander Distinction Award; he is a graduate of the elite Talpiot program.
current_role: Co-founder and VP Product & Strategy, Fabric (formerly CommonSense Robotics; earlier titled CTO)
research_notes: Title varies by source (CTO on Crunchbase; VP Product & Strategy on Fabric's own About page - use the latter). No press email published. Low public profile; Israel-based.

name: Shay Cohen
profile: Israeli engineer and former IDF lieutenant colonel who co-founded Fabric (founded 2015 as CommonSense Robotics) with Elram Goren and Ori Avraham. Fabric builds compact robotic micro-fulfillment centers that let retailers run fast, profitable on-demand and grocery delivery inside cities; it reached a ~$1B valuation. Cohen leads hardware, manufacturing and deployment.
interesting_fact: CommonSense built the world's first underground automated warehouse, in the -1 parking level of Tel Aviv's Shalom Meir Tower (the city's oldest skyscraper), to serve one-hour grocery deliveries from under-used urban real estate (2019).
deep_cut_fact: Before Fabric he served as a Lieutenant Colonel in the IDF Intelligence Technology Unit, received the Israel Defense Prize for leading complex multidisciplinary systems, and holds a BSc in mechanical engineering from Ben-Gurion University and an MSc in biomechanics from the University of Delaware.
current_role: Co-founder and VP Engineering, Fabric (formerly CommonSense Robotics), Tel Aviv
public_contact: pr_agency: joseph@headline.media (Joseph Moses, Headline Media, listed as Fabric/CommonSense media contact, 2019) | official_website: https://www.getfabric.com
research_notes: Engineering/operations co-founder, low media profile; CEO Elram Goren is the usual spokesperson. PR agency contact is from a 2019 release and may be stale. Patents list him as inventor on robotics patents assigned to Get Fabric/CommonSense Robotics.

name: Tom Bassett
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of 'Get Fabric' (logistics, valued ~$1B), i.e. Fabric (getfabric.com, formerly CommonSense Robotics), the Tel Aviv micro-fulfillment robotics company. However, Fabric's own leadership page lists co-founders Ori Avraham and Shay Cohen and CEO Avi (Jack) Jacoby, and does not mention a Tom Bassett; he is also not on fabric.inc's pages. Could not confirm who he is.

name: Nuno Sebastiao
profile: Portuguese engineer who co-founded AI fraud-prevention company Feedzai (Coimbra/San Mateo) in 2011, growing it into Portugal's fourth unicorn, used by major banks and payment firms. In October 2025 Feedzai was selected by the ECB to provide fraud detection for the forthcoming digital euro and raised $75M at a $2B valuation.
interesting_fact: Feedzai was chosen by the European Central Bank as the fraud-detection and prevention provider for the future digital euro (Oct 2025).
deep_cut_fact: Before Feedzai he spent 2006-2010 as a product manager at the European Space Agency in Germany, leading development of its Satellite Simulation Infrastructure; earlier he founded a startup doing software validation for aerospace. He holds MBAs from both London Business School and UCLA, and a CS degree from Coimbra.
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Feedzai
research_notes: Active speaker/podcast guest on fraud and AI. PR email appears in syndicated Oct 2025 release (page blocked to direct fetch; per search snippet).

name: Paulo Marques
profile: Portuguese computer scientist (PhD, University of Coimbra) who co-founded Feedzai with Nuno Sebastião and Pedro Bizarro; Feedzai builds real-time machine-learning fraud and financial-crime detection used by major banks and payment firms. He served as CTO for about 13 years and is now Technical Fellow; Feedzai was valued at $2B+ in an October 2025 round.
interesting_fact: Feedzai, which he co-founded in Coimbra, was selected by the European Central Bank to provide fraud & risk management for the forthcoming digital euro.
deep_cut_fact: Before Feedzai he spent six years as an expert technical consultant at the European Space Agency's operations centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, while also teaching as an assistant professor at Coimbra and directing CMU Portugal's professional master in software.
current_role: Co-founder & Technical Fellow, Feedzai (former CTO)
research_notes: Full name Paulo Jorge Pimenta Marques. Academic and technical profile; author of 40+ peer-reviewed papers; Forbes Technology Council member.

name: Pedro Bizarro
profile: Portuguese computer scientist who co-founded Feedzai in Coimbra in 2011 with Nuno Sebastiao and Paulo Marques. Feedzai builds real-time machine-learning tools to detect payment fraud and financial crime for banks, retailers and e-commerce. It became a unicorn in 2021 and was valued above $2B in an October 2025 round. As Chief Science Officer he runs Feedzai Research (AI, data visualisation, systems).
interesting_fact: Feedzai was selected by the European Central Bank, together with Capgemini Germany, to provide the fraud and risk-management solution for the Digital Euro.
deep_cut_fact: Outside the lab he is an avid runner and an Ironman triathlete, per his Feedzai author bio.
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Science Officer, Feedzai (heads Feedzai Research)
research_notes: Technical founder who blogs on Feedzai's site and is a good fit for AI/data-infrastructure topics. No published press email found on feedzai.com; use the contact page or newsroom. Web-search quota ran out mid-lane, so research was limited to direct page fetches.

name: Daniel Litvak
profile: Hurun lists him as a founder of Fetch, the receipt-scanning rewards app and outcomes-based ad platform. Fetch started in Madison, Wisconsin, is led by CEO Wes Schroll and was valued at about $2.5B. I couldn't confirm his role or background from accessible primary sources.
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Fetch (Fetch Rewards); current role not confirmed (not on Fetch's leadership page)
research_notes: Couldn't verify: my web-search quota ran out and Wikipedia was rate-limited. Fetch's 2026 leadership page doesn't list him, so he is probably no longer an executive. Check his link to Fetch before outreach. Contact via Fetch press only.

name: Tyler Kennedy
profile: UW-Madison business graduate (BBA '13) who co-founded Fetch Rewards with Wes Schroll; the receipt-scanning rewards app grew from a 2012 class business-plan assignment into a Madison-based company valued above $2B. He has led operations at Fetch and received UW-Madison's 2023 Chancellor's Entrepreneurial Achievement Award.
interesting_fact: Fetch began as a business-plan assignment in a Wisconsin School of Business entrepreneurship class in 2012; Kennedy met Schroll via the campus Collegiate Entrepreneurs Organization.
deep_cut_fact: Before Fetch he mowed neighborhood lawns as a kid and later ran a boat-cleaning business in Milwaukee: 'I saw early on that the people who had the most time freedom were business owners.'
current_role: Co-founder and SVP Operations, Fetch (Madison, WI) - per UW-Madison 2023 materials
research_notes: Low-profile operator; CEO Wes Schroll is Fetch's public face. Current title not confirmed beyond 2023 UW sources. Name is common (not to be confused with others named Tyler Kennedy).

name: Wes Schroll
profile: Massachusetts native who came to UW-Madison for its entrepreneurship programs and left to build Fetch Rewards with Tyler Kennedy, launching in 2013. The receipt-scanning rewards app grew to tens of millions of users and a ~$2.5B valuation; he still runs the Madison-based company.
interesting_fact: He came to UW-Madison in 2011 'mostly because I was attracted to the entrepreneurship programs' and left to build Fetch; UW later gave him its 2023 Chancellor's Entrepreneurial Achievement Award.
deep_cut_fact: Fetch's first version (2014) was an in-store scan-as-you-shop app that auto-applied coupons, test-run at Fresh Madison Market in Madison before pivoting to receipt scanning.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Fetch (formerly Fetch Rewards)
research_notes: Received UW-Madison 2023 Chancellor's Entrepreneurial Achievement Award. He has told CNBC the business spent six weeks on the edge of collapse early on.

name: Di Weijie
profile: Chinese technologist who spent over eight years at Alibaba before co-founding Bangkok courier Flash Express with Komsan Saelee in 2017-18. Flash grew to more than 1 million parcels a day across all 77 Thai provinces and became Thailand's first logistics unicorn; Di leads technology and operations.
interesting_fact: Within about two years of launch Flash Express was delivering over 1 million parcels a day from 5,000+ branches, becoming Thailand's second-largest private express carrier.
deep_cut_fact: At Techsauce Global Summit 2025 he said Flash has run its workforce through its own software since day one and that he believes 'the future belongs to small teams or even single individuals' adept at AI.
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Flash Express / Flash Group (Thailand)
research_notes: Komsan Saelee (CEO) is the public face; Di appears at Thai tech conferences such as Techsauce. Only customer-service emails are published.

name: Komsan Lee
profile: Thai entrepreneur (also spelled Komsan Saelee) who launched parcel-delivery firm Flash Express in 2017-18 with a 25-baht starting fee that undercut rivals charging 60 baht. Flash Group, now spanning logistics, fulfillment, payments and tech, became Thailand's first unicorn in 2021 after a $150M Series D+/E led by SCB 10X and Buer Capital; he still leads it with co-founder/COO Weijie Di.
interesting_fact: On becoming Thailand's first unicorn founder at 29, he said: 'Regardless of how poor you are, which surname you have or where you graduated from, you can become a unicorn startup if you select the right industry... and have a good team.'
deep_cut_fact: Born to a poor family of Chinese descent in Doi Wawee, Chiang Rai, he ran his first business, a local grocery shop, in his first year of university, then worked as a property sales agent and freight forwarder and ran a logistics firm shipping to the US, Japan and China before Flash.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Flash Group (Flash Express), Thailand
research_notes: Bangkok Post named him 2021 Start-up Founder of the Year. Interviews are mostly with Thai media (Bangkok Post, The Story Thailand). Flash has pushed EV delivery motorbikes with battery swapping at PTT stations, a possible energy angle.

name: Olugbenga Agboola
education: MIT Sloan School of Management
profile: Nigerian fintech founder ('GB') who co-founded Flutterwave with Iyinoluwa Aboyeji in 2016 and became CEO in 2018. Flutterwave builds pan-African payments infrastructure, raised a $250M Series D at a $3B+ valuation in 2022, holds licences in 34+ African countries, acquired open-banking firm Mono in 2026 and in April 2026 won a Nigerian microlender licence.
interesting_fact: Before Flutterwave he worked at PayPal, Google (on the Wallet payments product), Royal Bank of Scotland, Standard Bank Nigeria and Sterling Bank; he holds an MIT Sloan MBA.
deep_cut_fact: Besides an MIT MBA he holds a master's in behavioural engineering and IT security plus EC-Council IT-security certifications; in 2024 he was named vice chair of the US Chamber of Commerce's US-Africa Business Center board.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Flutterwave
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker (Milken, Money20/20, US Chamber events) - speaker bureaus/event organisers are a viable route. No published press email confirmed in this pass. Vice-chair info from Wikipedia Flutterwave article.

name: Brett Seyler
profile: Games-industry technologist and investor who co-founded Forte (c. 2018-19), a platform helping game developers add blockchain economies, with former Kabam CEO Kevin Chou. He was earlier VP of Strategy and then GM of the Union division at Unity, after running the Torque engine business at GarageGames. Recent ventures include First Foundry and a stealth startup.
interesting_fact: Unity hired him from GarageGames in January 2010 as VP of Strategy, and he later led Unity's Union division bringing games to new platforms.
deep_cut_fact: He has a B.S. in Math from the University of Oregon and did graduate work in math, political science and economics; he joined GarageGames when it had about two dozen staff, before IAC bought a majority stake.
current_role: Co-founder, Forte; chairman of First Foundry (per Crunchbase)
research_notes: Titles and dates vary across profiles; confirm current role (Forte vs First Foundry) on LinkedIn.

name: Josh Williams
profile: Serial games/tech entrepreneur who co-founded Forte (~2018) with Kabam founder Kevin Chou to give game developers compliant blockchain infrastructure (ownership of in-game goods, token/economy design). Forte raised $725M in 2021 at a ~$1B valuation, backed by a $100M developer fund. He previously led indie game-engine company GarageGames as CEO/CTO.
interesting_fact: Forte's $100M developer fund gave grants to game studios to integrate blockchain without asking for equity or revenue share; early partners included Kongregate, Netmarble and Hi-Rez Studios.
deep_cut_fact: Before Forte, Williams spent ~20 years in machine learning, real-time tech and big data, and was CEO/CTO of GarageGames, the indie engine company (Torque) that was an early pioneer of digitally distributed games.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Forte (blockchain gaming infrastructure) - current status as of 2026 not re-verified
research_notes: Common name - make sure outreach targets Forte's Josh Williams (San Francisco), not Gowalla's or Very Great's. Forte site (forte.io) blocked automated fetch; no published press email found. Long-form interview: Naavik podcast https://naavik.co/podcast/forte/. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane; 2026 status unverified.

name: Kent Wakeford
profile: Serial tech entrepreneur who co-founded de-extinction company Colossal Biosciences (with Ben Lamm and George Church) and served as its COO, then became co-founder and co-CEO of Form Bio, the computational-biology software company Colossal spun out in 2022. Earlier he co-founded Integral Ad Science (NASDAQ: IAS) and was COO of game maker Kabam.
interesting_fact: Colossal, which he co-founded, aims to 'de-extinct' the woolly mammoth, thylacine and dodo; it hit unicorn status with a $150M Series B in 2023, and Form Bio commercialises the software built for that work.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was a media/gaming tech builder: he is a co-inventor on more than 85 patents covering virtual reality and streaming technology, and co-founded four software companies including Integral Ad Science.
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Form Bio (computational biology spinout of Colossal); co-founder and former COO of Colossal Biosciences
research_notes: Dallas-based. For outreach, Form Bio is his current company; Colossal press is agency-run (R&CPMK, Zeno, The 10 Group). Some aggregators list him as special advisor to Colossal's CEO. A Dec 2025 Colossal Foundation release reportedly lists Emily@colossal.com as media contact, but this could not be verified directly.

name: Kevin Chou
profile: UC Berkeley alum (BS 2002) and ex-Deutsche Bank banker / Canaan Partners VC who co-founded Kabam, the mobile game maker (Kingdoms of Camelot, Marvel Contest of Champions) whose assets were sold in 2016-17 for roughly $800M-$900M. He then led Gen.G Esports, founded blockchain-gaming platform Forte (valued ~$1B in 2021) and co-founded Rally and the SuperLayer venture studio.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Kabam signed an $18M deal with UC Berkeley that included naming rights to Kabam Field at California Memorial Stadium.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife pledged up to $25M to Berkeley Haas - the largest gift ever from a Haas alum under 40 - and the resulting Connie & Kevin Chou Hall became the first US academic building certified TRUE Zero Waste at the platinum level (2019).
current_role: Founding CEO/Chairman of Forte; Managing Partner, SuperLayer (crypto venture studio, Palo Alto); co-founder of Rally
public_contact: official_website: https://medium.com/forte-labs-inc/why-i-started-forte-633ff5325ad4 (his own essay 'Why I Started Forte')
research_notes: Forte CEO title passed to co-founder Josh Williams; Chou's current focus appears to be SuperLayer/Rally. Kabam's first product was Watercooler, a fantasy-sports social network (2006) that pivoted to Facebook games. No verified personal/press email found.

name: Mahesh Vellanki
profile: Former Redpoint Ventures investor (Principal, 2012-18; earlier Citi investment banking) who co-founded blockchain-gaming platform Forte with Kevin Chou and others, which reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. With Chou he also co-founded the Rally/RLY social-token network and in 2021 the crypto venture studio SuperLayer.
interesting_fact: SuperLayer launched in Oct 2021 with backing from Marc Andreessen, Chris Dixon and Michael Ovitz, and in 2022 Polygon led a $25M fund for the studio.
deep_cut_fact: He moved from VC to founder: after six years as a Principal at Redpoint Ventures, he partnered with Kabam founder Kevin Chou; he studied finance at the University of Maryland's Robert H. Smith School of Business.
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, SuperLayer (Web3 venture studio); co-founder of Forte and Rally (RLY) (current status unverified)
research_notes: No published contact found; low public profile since 2022. Rally/RLY wound down; confirm current focus before outreach. Education detail from directory profiles (MarketScreener/TheOrg).

name: Adrian Aoun
profile: Serial founder: started NLP company Wavii in 2008 (acquired by Google), then worked on Google's AI efforts and as Larry Page's head of special projects, helping found Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs. In 2016 he launched Forward, a tech-driven primary-care company that raised ~$400M (later building AI 'CarePods') before closing in Nov 2024; he has since been backing a new venture.
interesting_fact: Before Forward he was head of special projects for Larry Page at Google/Alphabet, where he founded Sidewalk Labs.
deep_cut_fact: He told Fortune his 'happy place' is the bike ride up Mount Tamalpais ('Hard to imagine a better way to start the day') and that he's never been a big coffee drinker.
current_role: Former founder & CEO of Forward (shut down Nov 2024); reported co-founder, board member and advisor of a new, as-yet-unnamed startup with ex-Forward leaders
research_notes: Forward closed abruptly in Nov 2024 - avoid dwelling on it. He discussed the wind-down candidly on the 'More or Less' podcast ep. 74. No current company site/press contact found; LinkedIn is likely best route. He has written guest posts for TechCrunch (techcrunch.com/author/adrian-aoun).

name: Levi Cooperman
profile: Levi Cooperman co-founded Toronto cloud-accounting company FreshBooks in 2003-04 with Mike McDerment and Joe Sawada, early on quitting his job to work on it full time and later serving as VP Operations and in government relations. FreshBooks, used by millions of small businesses, reached a ~$1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: FreshBooks was founded in Toronto by McDerment, Cooperman and Sawada and grew from a small-business invoicing tool into a unicorn cloud accounting platform.
deep_cut_fact: Before FreshBooks he was a professional engineer (BEng, University of Victoria) who managed systems-integration projects at Apex Systems Integrators for clients including Canadian Tire, Nestle and Parmalat.
current_role: Co-founder of FreshBooks (later Government Relations); Crunchbase lists him as a partner at RevvWorks (not confirmed on RevvWorks' own site)
research_notes: Low public profile. The FreshBooks author bio used for the deep-cut fact now returns 404 (archived Nov 2024 on web.archive.org). No published personal/office contact found; RevvWorks lists only a generic info@revv.works and does not name him.

name: Michael McDerment
profile: Mike McDerment co-founded FreshBooks in Toronto with Levi Cooperman and Joe Sawada, growing it from a web-design shop's invoicing tool into cloud accounting software for small businesses worldwide. He bootstrapped for about a decade before raising $30M (2014) and later reaching a $1B+ valuation; he handed the CEO role to Don Epperson in 2021 and remains board chair.
interesting_fact: FreshBooks began in 2003 when he accidentally saved over an old invoice while billing clients of his small web-design agency; frustrated, he built his own billing tool and ran the business from his parents' basement for about 3.5 years.
deep_cut_fact: His first businesses straight out of college were an Ultimate Frisbee tournament and a league; a caterer for the event needed a website, which is how he drifted into web design -- the agency that later spawned FreshBooks.
current_role: Co-founder and Chair of the Board, FreshBooks (Toronto); CEO 2003-2021
research_notes: Press contact is Chloe Matcham, Senior Manager, Communications (named on FreshBooks press releases). FreshBooks recently launched an Anthropic MCP connector -- AI/small-business angle. CEO seat has turned over several times since 2021; McDerment's own status beyond 'chair' not confirmed for 2026.

name: Henrik Müller-Hansen
profile: Norwegian-based entrepreneur, former CEO of Tele2 Norway, who launched Optimalprint around 2007 and then Gelato in 2012. Gelato's software and network route print-on-demand orders to local production hubs in 30+ countries, cutting transport distance and waste; it also sells GelatoConnect, a production OS for print factories. Gelato reached a US$1B+ valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Gelato's model is a 'local on-demand production' network: orders are produced in partner factories near the end customer across 30+ countries rather than shipped from a central plant.
deep_cut_fact: Before studying at the Stockholm School of Economics he served as a team leader in a military Underwater Demolition Team; as CEO of Tele2 Norway (2003-06) he roughly doubled revenue from NOK 1.5bn to 3.2bn.
current_role: Founder & CEO, Gelato (on-demand print/production software, Oslo/Fornebu); board member, Patricia Industries (since Jan 2025)
research_notes: Gelato press releases name a VP PR & Communications (Julie Ryland, 2025) but email addresses are obfuscated on the pages; route via gelato.com news/press section. Tele2 revenue figure is from Gelato's leadership page (https://www.gelato.com/leadership).

name: Joel Hyatt
profile: Serial entrepreneur. He co-founded Hyatt Legal Services (1977), which brought affordable legal services to middle-income families, and Hyatt Legal Plans (later sold to MetLife). With Al Gore he co-founded Current TV (2004; sold to Al Jazeera in 2013). In 2015 he co-founded Globality, an AI platform for enterprise procurement and sourcing backed by SoftBank, and led it as CEO until 2026.
interesting_fact: He was the face of his own firm's nationwide TV ads, which always ended with the line: 'I'm Joel Hyatt and you have my word on it.'
deep_cut_fact: He co-authored the 2000 book 'The Long Boom' with futurists Peter Schwartz and Peter Leyden. He taught entrepreneurship at Stanford GSB from 1998 to 2003 and was founding chairman of VideoSurf, a computer-vision video search engine that Microsoft acquired in 2011.
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Globality (stepped down as CEO in late 2026, per Procurement Magazine)
research_notes: An experienced public figure: 1994 Democratic Senate nominee in Ohio, 2000 DNC national finance chair, former HP director, RAND trustee. He does podcasts readily. His personal site links to his X and LinkedIn, and he is reachable through Globality. The CEO handover is reported only by procurementmag.com, so confirm his current title.

name: Lior Delgo
profile: Israeli-American serial entrepreneur. Co-founded travel meta-search engine FareChase (acquired by Yahoo, 2004) and computer-vision video search company VideoSurf (acquired by Microsoft in 2011, reportedly ~$70M, for Xbox LIVE), then worked on Xbox at Microsoft. In 2015 he co-founded Globality with Joel Hyatt; the AI-driven sourcing platform for services spend reached unicorn status (~$1B).
interesting_fact: His VideoSurf technology used computer vision to 'see' frames inside videos, identifying people and moments rather than relying on text tags; Microsoft bought it in 2011 to power video search and Kinect voice search on Xbox LIVE.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded VideoSurf with applied mathematician Prof. Achi Brandt (a pioneer of multigrid methods), Dr. Eitan Sharon and Shai Deljo; its computer-vision engine analyzed video about 10x faster than playback speed.
current_role: Co-founder, Globality (AI platform for enterprise services procurement, Menlo Park/Palo Alto); listed as co-founder & president
public_contact: pr_agency: slafferty@roundearthconsulting.com (Sarah Lafferty, Round Earth Consulting; Globality media contact) | official_website: https://www.globality.com/
research_notes: Jared Hyatt succeeded Joel Hyatt as Globality CEO; Delgo remains co-founder. PR contact is from a Mar 2026 Business Wire release seen via search (page not directly fetchable; verify). FareChase/Yahoo link per Globality's own bio. Low personal media profile.

name: Ran Harpaz
profile: Israeli-born tech executive who was founding CTO of procurement-AI unicorn Globality (2015-2019), then CTO/COO of Hippo Insurance and COO of Noname Security, after strategy roles at PayPal. In 2023 he founded Lettuce Financial, an AI platform handling accounting, tax, payroll and benefits for solopreneurs; it has raised $28M+ and bought Besolo and Carry's retirement platform.
interesting_fact: He has helped scale three unicorns (Globality, Hippo, Noname Security) and now says Lettuce aims to put at least $50 billion back into solopreneurs' businesses through smarter tax and accounting.
deep_cut_fact: Before Silicon Valley he was CIO of Israeli ISP Netvision/Cellcom and worked at security firms Skybox Security and Sanctum; he holds an MBA, a BA in economics and an LLB in law, all from Tel Aviv University.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Lettuce Financial (AI operating system for solopreneurs)
public_contact: linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ranharpaz | official_website: https://lettuce.co/ | x: https://twitter.com/joinlettuce
research_notes: Active founder who gives press interviews; LinkedIn is linked from his official Lettuce author page. The X account is the company's (@joinlettuce), not his personal account. Unit 8200 veteran per aggregator profiles (unverified).

name: Andrew Barnes
profile: Brisbane entrepreneur who co-founded workplace-learning platform Go1 with high-school friends Vu Tran, Chris Eigeland and Chris Hood; it went through Y Combinator and reached a ~$3B valuation. He led it as CEO for about a decade before handing the top job to Eigeland in 2024.
interesting_fact: Go1 started in a Brisbane suburban garage as a web-development shop he ran with Vu Tran; it now serves 10,000+ organisations and 50M+ users.
deep_cut_fact: A 2013 Rhodes Scholar, he did an Oxford MSc in Education (Learning and Technology) and a UQ PhD in business management, after UQ degrees in economics (2009) and business management honours (2011).
current_role: Co-founder & director, Go1 (stepped down as co-CEO Aug 2024)
research_notes: Common name - distinguish from the NZ 4-day-week Andrew Barnes. Holds a doctorate (Dr Andrew Barnes).

name: Chris Eigeland
profile: Australian co-founder of Go1, the Brisbane-born (2015, Y Combinator S15) corporate learning-content aggregator, started by four school friends. Former CRO and co-CEO, he became sole CEO in August 2024. Go1 was valued at $2B+ in 2022.
interesting_fact: Go1 went through Y Combinator's Summer 2015 batch and became one of Australia's first edtech unicorns, aggregating training content into whatever LMS a company already uses.
deep_cut_fact: A Griffith law graduate and trained international lawyer, he was Australia's Youth Representative to the United Nations in 2016 and gave a TEDx talk in 2015.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Go1 (Brisbane)

name: Chris Hood
profile: Australian software engineer and one of Go1's four co-founders (with Andrew Barnes, Vu Tran and Chris Eigeland). Go1 grew from a Logan/Brisbane garage web-dev business into a corporate e-learning content aggregator valued at about $2B, Brisbane's first unicorn. Hood is the technical co-founder who built the platform's software.
interesting_fact: Go1 began as a web development business started in a garage by school friends; it became Brisbane's first tech unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Andrew Barnes met Hood at a tech conference; in Go1's early days, when salespeople promised features that didn't exist yet, Hood had to build them fast - 'It's how we learnt what people wanted.'
current_role: Co-founder, Go1 (Brisbane-born workplace learning platform)
research_notes: Very low public profile; current title not confirmed. Griffith University alumnus and ex-Intellidesign software engineer per Crunchbase (unverified). Route via Go1 (go1.com/about-us).

name: Vu Tran
profile: Dr Vu Tran is a Brisbane GP who grew up in Logan as a migrant. He co-founded workplace e-learning marketplace Go1 with school friends Andrew Barnes, Chris Eigeland and Chris Hood; Go1 raised $272M in 2021 and was valued at about $3B when it bought Blinkist in 2023. He has since stepped back from Go1's day-to-day running and co-founded Black Sky Industries, which makes solid rocket propellant and rocket motors for Australian defence.
interesting_fact: Black Sky Industries describes itself as Australia's only sovereign supplier of solid rocket propellant and motors, and it produces ammonium perchlorate locally. Tran argues Australia has only one local firm in the top 100 defence suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: In high school, instead of stacking shelves at Coles, he and Andrew Barnes started a software business that 'made a dollar an hour'. Around 2006 it was building websites for ANZ and News Corp, which did not realise they were dealing with students. He did not pay off his last credit-card debts until early 2020.
current_role: Co-founder, Black Sky Industries (Logan, Qld solid-rocket-motor and defence manufacturer); co-founder and former Chief Growth Officer of Go1
public_contact: official_website: https://www.blackskyindustries.com.au/ | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/bsaero (Black Sky company page) | podcast: Long-form interview: 'Meet the Founder - Vu Tran (Go1)', The Exchange by EW Private Wealth, Sept 2024
research_notes: Practising GP (MBBS Bond, per profiles). Speaks readily on podcasts about sovereign manufacturing and defence, which suits an energy and industry angle. Also a non-executive director of ASX-listed PeopleIN (per marketindex; not re-verified). Black Sky's site has only a contact section, no published email.

name: Jörg Kattner
profile: Jörg Kattner co-founded Berlin quick-commerce grocery startup Gorillas with CEO Kağan Sümer in 2020, joining early that year to help it scale. He left in early 2021 holding about 10%. Gorillas later reached a ~$3B valuation and was acquired by Getir in December 2022.
interesting_fact: Announcing his exit after about a year, he wrote that he was leaving 'this rocket in good hands' and looked forward to new adventures, building another company from scratch.
deep_cut_fact: He started in marketing at Rocket Internet in 2014, then ran HelloFresh's Swiss market from 2017. In 2018 he helped build HelloFreshGO, HelloFresh's in-office lunch-fridge business, and was its COO for a year.
current_role: Former co-founder of Gorillas (left Feb 2021). Current role not verified; an aggregator lists him as CEO of Berlin-based JoeKa UG.
research_notes: Very low profile since 2021, with no verified current venture or public channels. WikiFX article reproduces a Gründerszene report (Feb 2021). JoeKa UG and angel-investor mentions come from aggregators (siliconvalleyinvestclub, pipeseed) and are unverified.

name: Kağan Sümer
profile: Istanbul-born Kağan Sümer worked at Rocket Internet's B2B food group in Berlin, then in May 2020 founded Gorillas, a 10-minute grocery delivery service using bike couriers. It became a unicorn in about nine months, reportedly Germany's fastest. Rival Getir bought Gorillas in December 2022 for about $1.2B, and Sümer left. German press reported in 2023 that he was starting a health-tech company.
interesting_fact: Gorillas went from founding in May 2020 to a $1B+ valuation in about nine months, which Wikipedia describes as the fastest any German company had done so.
deep_cut_fact: Rocket Internet ignored six of his job applications in one month before later hiring him. He once cycled from Istanbul to China, captained Turkey's youth water polo team, and spent 88 of his 100 euros on a bike when he arrived in Berlin. Gorillas began as 'Get Goodies' in his living room.
current_role: Former founder and CEO of Gorillas (Berlin). Reported since 2023 to be building a new health-tech startup, Mirror, with Gorillas co-founder Uğur Samut (current status unverified).
research_notes: Gorillas no longer exists (Getir wound it down in 2024), so there is no company press channel. Mirror was reported by deutsche-startups.de (May 2023): https://www.deutsche-startups.de/2023/05/02/gorillas-gruender-klonen-aware/. Aggregator listings of newer ventures (Sugar, Nutz) are unverified. A strong fit for the entrepreneurship angle (bikes, logistics, blitzscaling).

name: James Carter
profile: British entrepreneur who co-founded Gousto, the London meal-kit/recipe-box business, with Timo Boldt in 2012. Gousto reached unicorn status in 2021. Carter keeps a low public profile and Boldt has been the public face as CEO.
interesting_fact: Carter and Boldt pitched Gousto on BBC's Dragons' Den in 2013 and left without a deal, yet Gousto went on to become a unicorn in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Within weeks of walking away empty-handed from Dragons' Den, he and Boldt closed a £500,000 investment from food-industry players, plus $300,000 from ex-BSkyB MD Ian West and Rothschild vice-chairman Andrea Raffel; both founders were 29 and made the Startups 'Young Guns' class of 2014.
current_role: Co-founder, Gousto (UK recipe-box company); current role at the company not verified
research_notes: Common name - use 'Gousto co-founder' to disambiguate. No public contact found for him; route via Gousto press office. Note Startups.co.uk misnames Boldt as 'Timo Schmidt'. Whether Carter is still at Gousto is unverified.

name: Timo Boldt
profile: German-born former banker and Cambridge Judge EMBA (2014) alumnus who founded UK meal-kit company Gousto in 2012, initially packing and delivering kits himself. Gousto became a unicorn in 2022, delivers 80M+ meals a year and posted 2025 revenue of £342m with record £45m adjusted EBITDA. He also founded Bento (2021) to license Gousto's tech.
interesting_fact: Named EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year Class of 2023 (UK); about 95% of Gousto staff are shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Long banking hours and takeaway dinners inspired Gousto; at 26 he quit, moved into university housing to fund it, packed every meal by hand, delivered them himself and took no salary for three years. His advice: 'You will be rejected a thousand times...'
current_role: Founder and CEO of Gousto (announced Sept 2026 he will step down to become a board director once a successor is appointed, expected H1 2027)
public_contact: office_email: info@gousto.co.uk (listed on Gousto press page)
research_notes: Leadership transition news: https://www.grocerygazette.co.uk/2026/09/17/gousto-founder-step-down/ . Frequent conference speaker (London Tech Week, Sifted Summit).

name: Jonathan Ross
profile: Chip architect who started Google's TPU as a '20% project', left in 2016 with much of the TPU team and founded Groq (LPU inference chips, GroqCloud; $6.9bn valuation in 2025). In Dec 2025 Nvidia licensed Groq's tech (~$20bn) and Ross and president Sunny Madra joined Nvidia; Groq continues under CEO Simon Edwards.
interesting_fact: Groq's tech is credited as one of the few credible challengers to Nvidia in inference - so much so that Nvidia ultimately paid ~$20bn to license it and bring Ross and his team in-house.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of high school because he 'was bored', taught himself programming, did a stint at Hunter College, then got into NYU where he took PhD classes (incl. under Yann LeCun) as an undergrad before dropping out again: 'I didn't want to cap my earning opportunity by graduating from something.'
current_role: Founder of Groq; since Dec 2025 at NVIDIA (reported as Chief Software Architect) under Nvidia's ~$20bn non-exclusive Groq inference-technology licensing deal
public_contact: press_email: press@nvidia.com (NVIDIA corporate communications) | official_website: https://groq.com | https://x.com/JonathanRoss321 | https://www.linkedin.com/in/ross-jonathan/
research_notes: Very podcast-friendly historically (Chamath, 20VC etc.), but now an Nvidia employee, so requests likely route through Nvidia PR. 'Chief Software Architect' title comes from reports quoting his LinkedIn; not confirmed on nvidia.com. LeCun detail per Groq's former leadership bio (via search). Hurun $7bn valuation figure is outdated.

name: Adam R. Gerchen
profile: Chicago-based investor and litigation-finance pioneer (Brown, Harvard Law; ex-Goldman Sachs and Alyeska). Co-founded Gerchen Keller Capital in 2013, which raised $2B+ before its 2016 sale to Burford Capital, where he became President; co-founded law firm Keller Postman. In 2020 he co-founded Heyday, an Amazon-brand aggregator that raised $175M Series A and a $555M Series C.
interesting_fact: Gerchen Keller Capital became the largest private investment firm focused exclusively on legal and regulatory risk within about three years of launch, raising over $2B in institutional capital before Burford acquired it.
deep_cut_fact: At Harvard Law School he was President of the Harvard Association of Law and Business; he graduated Brown Phi Beta Kappa, magna cum laude.
current_role: CEO, Gerchen Capital Partners (Chicago); co-founder of Heyday and Keller Postman
research_notes: Heyday co-founded Aug 2020 with CEO Sebastian Rymarz (https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/heyday-emerges-from-stealth-with-175m-series-a-funding-to-accelerate-marketplace-native-brands-301175394.html); aggregators list Gerchen as executive chairman 2020-2024. Not to be confused with Heyday skincare. Firm website is JS-only; no published email found.

name: Sebastian Rymarz
profile: Sebastian Rymarz co-founded San Francisco-based Heyday with Adam Gerchen in August 2020 to acquire and scale marketplace-native (mainly Amazon) consumer brands; it raised about $800M including a $555M Series C in 2021, reportedly at a $1B+ valuation. In September 2024 Branded acquired Heyday to form Essor, a ~$400M-revenue consumer products group where Rymarz became president.
interesting_fact: Heyday emerged from stealth with a $175M Series A just three months after founding; Rymarz called it 'the early days of a tectonic shift toward marketplace commerce.' Unlike rivals, he said Heyday would buy only one or two brands a month to focus on growing each.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 Heyday bought ZitSticka, the direct-to-consumer acne-patch brand, as part of its push into personal care.
current_role: President, Essor (formed 2024 when Branded acquired Heyday); co-founder & CEO of Heyday
research_notes: Merger quote: 'Joining forces with Branded strengthens our platform, and, importantly, our balance sheet' (happi.com). Aggregator profiles mention prior roles at Fundbox and TPG Sixth Street, unverified. No published press email found; Essor corporate channels are best route.

name: Dror Shimoni
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded HoneyBook in 2013 with Oz and Naama Alon. HoneyBook is a San Francisco-based clientflow/business-management platform (CRM, contracts, invoicing, payments) for freelancers and small service businesses, valued at $2.2B in 2021. Shimoni leads engineering from the Tel Aviv R&D office.
interesting_fact: HoneyBook's concept came from Naama Alon planning her wedding in Tel Aviv and finding no tools to organize event vendors; the platform has since processed over $13B in transactions for small businesses.
deep_cut_fact: He was a programmer at SAP Software Solutions; when Naama Alon proposed the three founders quit their day jobs, he handed in his resignation the next day. When the others moved to the US for a Palo Alto accelerator, he stayed in Israel and built the R&D center.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, HoneyBook (runs its Israel R&D center) - per Calcalist profile; current title not re-confirmed on HoneyBook's site
research_notes: Low public profile; the Alons are HoneyBook's public faces. Best route is the HoneyBook press team.

name: Naama Alon
profile: Israeli designer who co-founded HoneyBook with Oz Alon (CEO) and Dror Shimoni; it makes client-management and payments software for US freelancers and small creative businesses, and was valued at about $2.4B in 2021. Alon leads product and creative and is based between the Bay Area and Tel Aviv.
interesting_fact: HoneyBook was her idea: it grew out of a college project she started while studying at Shenkar College, and the founders quit their jobs the day after she said they had to commit to it full time.
deep_cut_fact: Before HoneyBook she was a graphic designer and party-thrower on the Tel Aviv party scene; her only job as an employee was at the design studio Red Interactive. She has said: 'I don't want to be the CEO, I'm looking to influence and lead.'
current_role: Co-founder and Chief of Product, HoneyBook (per 2021 Calcalist profile; title varies across sources)
research_notes: Very private by her own account ('prefers to stay behind the scenes'); her husband and co-founder Oz Alon is the public face, so outreach via HoneyBook/Oz is likely more effective. No published press email found on honeybook.com.

name: Oz Alon
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded HoneyBook in 2013 with Naama Alon and Dror Shimoni after a Tel Aviv accelerator, then moved the team to Silicon Valley via a Palo Alto accelerator. HoneyBook is a clientflow, payments and AI-powered business-management platform for independent business owners; as CEO he led its 2026 expansion to the UK and Australia.
interesting_fact: HoneyBook was named to CNBC's 2026 list of the world's top fintech companies; the company has offices in San Francisco and Tel Aviv and launched in the UK and Australia in May 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech, he ran a bar called Backy on Ibn Gvirol Street in Tel Aviv and threw large all-inclusive parties with thousands of guests; he was a law-firm intern when he quit to go all in on HoneyBook, drawing on that event-organizer experience.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, HoneyBook (San Francisco / Tel Aviv)
public_contact: pr_agency: Dan Edelstein, InboundJunction - pr@inboundjunction.com (HoneyBook release contact) | official_website: https://www.honeybook.com
research_notes: Active public speaker/podcast guest (e.g. 'From bar to unicorn' podcast). HoneyBook releases have used varying media contacts (in-house comms and agencies like BAM by BIG for UK/AU launch).

name: Shadiah Sigala
profile: Shadiah Sigala moved from Mexico to southern California at age 7 and later studied at Pomona College and the Harvard Kennedy School. In 2013 she co-founded HoneyBook, the small-business client and finance management platform valued at more than $2B in 2021, with three Israeli entrepreneurs. In 2018 she co-founded Kinside, an employer child-care benefit marketplace, which acquired LegUp in 2022.
interesting_fact: She came to the US from Mexico at 7, the first in her family to go to college. She went from a $80K project-management job at Aetna to co-founding a $2B+ startup.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech, in 2010, she ran a personal-chef business, finding clients through her Pomona College alumni network. It supported her for about a year until she concluded 'My time doesn't scale.'
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kinside (child-care benefits marketplace); co-founder, HoneyBook
research_notes: Kinside's child-care focus also connects to her 2022 Kinside/LegUp press release (Business Wire). No current (2025-26) confirmation of her Kinside role was found. No published personal or press contacts were found; Kinside's website or PR is the likely route. She is open about her immigrant story and talks about it publicly (CNBC Make It, Pomona 'Sagecast').

name: Paul Sawaya
profile: San Francisco engineer who co-founded Human Interest in 2015 with Roger Lee. The YC S15 digital 401(k) provider automated retirement plans for small businesses, and Sawaya was its founding CTO for about five years and sat on its board. He is now an angel investor and founder/CEO of Elsewhere, an a16z Speedrun gaming/AI-agents startup.
interesting_fact: After Human Interest, he switched to games: his new company Elsewhere pitches itself as 'the multiplayer roguelike of your dreams' and is backed through a16z's Speedrun program.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Human Interest he built a Facebook app, worked at Bloomberg, and interviewed with Emmett Shear at Justin.tv. He spent about two years 'wandering in the wilderness' exploring ideas before settling on small-business 401(k)s.
current_role: Founder & CEO, Elsewhere (multiplayer roguelike game startup, SF); co-founder and former CTO of Human Interest
public_contact: x: https://twitter.com/automin | linkedin: https://linkedin.com/in/paulsawaya | github: https://github.com/psawaya
research_notes: No longer operational at Human Interest. Best route is X (@automin) or LinkedIn. Interested in WebAssembly and AI-driven interfaces.

name: Izabel Jelenic
profile: Croatian engineer who co-founded Infobip with CEO Silvio Kutić in 2006 in Vodnjan, a town of about 6,000 on the Istrian peninsula, starting with a €25,000 loan. Infobip grew into a global cloud communications (CPaaS) platform and Croatia's first unicorn. As CTO he leads 800+ engineers across continents.
interesting_fact: Infobip's seed idea was a Christmas SMS sent from Vodnjan's town hall to the town's diaspora community.
deep_cut_fact: In Infobip's early days he was the entire technical side: 'When we founded Infobip, there were just two of us, and I was doing almost everything on the technical side,' from development and deployment to customer support and hiring. Now leading 800+ engineers, he says he still misses the hands-on work.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Infobip
public_contact: contact_form: Infobip media kit / media team contacts
research_notes: Izabel is a male Croatian name; sources refer to Jelenić as 'he'. He is lower profile than CEO Silvio Kutić. Infobip's media kit lists named PR staff rather than a generic press inbox. Infobip is pushing into European AI/cloud infrastructure, which could be a podcast angle.

name: Roberto Kutic
profile: Croatian mechanical engineer (University of Zagreb) who co-founded Infobip with brother Silvio Kutic and Izabel Jelenic and served as COO, helping grow it from zero to $1B revenue in 14 years without outside capital; it became Croatia's first unicorn in 2020. He left Infobip in mid-2025 (remaining a co-owner) and launched Festina.ai, building domain-specific AI agents.
interesting_fact: Infobip reached $1B in revenue within 14 years without any outside investment before taking $200M from One Equity Partners in 2020, becoming Croatia's first unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career at Uljanik in Pula, one of Croatia's largest shipyards, after studying mechanical engineering and naval architecture at the University of Zagreb.
current_role: CEO, Festina.ai (AI venture studio); co-founder and co-owner of Infobip
research_notes: Left Infobip COO role in June 2025; best route is via Festina.ai ('Contact us' on site) or his LinkedIn, where he announced the venture.

name: Silvio Kutic
profile: Silvio Kutić co-founded Infobip in 2006 in Vodnjan, Croatia, with Izabel Jelenić (CTO) and his brother Roberto (COO), and is its CEO. Infobip is a global cloud communications (CPaaS) platform that handles SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice messaging for businesses. Its $200M raise from One Equity Partners in 2020 made it Croatia's first unicorn.
interesting_fact: Infobip built a 17,000 m² campus, 'Pangea', in his small Istrian hometown of Vodnjan in 2017, followed by the 20,000 m² Alpha Centauri campus in Zagreb in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He lasted four hours in his first real job at the state power company in Zagreb, left for lunch, never returned, and took the bus home to Vodnjan. In 2003 his idea sent about 14,000 Christmas text greetings from Vodnjan's town hall to its emigrant community.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Infobip (Vodnjan/Zagreb, Croatia)
public_contact: press_email: marlies.roest@infobip.com (Global External Communications Director) | press_email: marcelo.nahime@infobip.com (Global Public Relations Manager) | official_website: https://www.infobip.com/silvio-kutic-infobip-ceo

Infobip stayed bootstrapped for almost a decade. He fits a data-center/infrastructure angle via telecom APIs. Route through the Infobip global PR team (contacts from the Infobip media kit).

research_notes: Frequent speaker in national-security and supply-chain circles and media-friendly (Bloomberg, FT, CNBC). She fits an energy/data-center podcast angle on critical-infrastructure supply chains.

name: Alex Dulin
profile: Alex Dulin co-founded Morning Consult in 2014 with Michael Ramlet and Kyle Dropp and has been CTO since. The firm grew from online political polling into a $1bn+ 'decision intelligence' company. Dulin leads engineering and product technology, from daily survey data collection to the AI systems built on top of it.
interesting_fact: Morning Consult started in political polling, where forecasts are tested against election results. Its tracking data is now used by Federal Reserve researchers, and the company says it ranked first for accuracy among alternative datasets in forecasting public-company earnings.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a CTO, Dulin's degree is not in computer science: he holds a bachelor's in political science from the University of Rochester. He built the tech stack of a billion-dollar data company from a polling and politics background.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Morning Consult (Washington, DC)
research_notes: Behind-the-scenes technical co-founder; CEO Michael Ramlet is the usual spokesperson. Go through press@morningconsult.com. The AI-native data pipeline is a good podcast angle.

name: Kyle Dropp
profile: Milwaukee-born political scientist (UW-Madison; Stanford PhD 2013) who worked in the Washington Post's polling unit, then cofounded Morning Consult in 2014 with Michael Ramlet and Alex Dulin. The firm became a $1B+ global data-intelligence company tracking public and consumer opinion in real time and increasingly AI-driven. He also taught at Dartmouth (2016-18).
interesting_fact: While building Morning Consult he was also an assistant professor in Dartmouth's Department of Government, leading its Washington program (2016-18) and teaching persuasion and applied data science; he was on Ad Age's 40 Under 40 (2020).
deep_cut_fact: He co-wrote the viral April 2014 Monkey Cage study (with Joshua Kertzer and Thomas Zeitzoff) that asked Americans to find Ukraine on a map: only about 1 in 6 could, and the farther off their guess, the more they backed US military intervention.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Research Officer (formerly President), Morning Consult, Washington DC
research_notes: Title has varied across sources (President vs Chief Research Officer); the IDFA bio says Chief Research Officer. Active in DC civic/business networks (Economic Club of Washington, Aspen Vanguard, Public Affairs Council board). No published press email found on the Morning Consult site.

name: Michael Ramlet
profile: Michael Ramlet (University of Minnesota Carlson School, BSB 2009) co-founded Morning Consult around 2013-14 with Kyle Dropp and Alex Dulin. It grew from a healthcare-policy newsletter into a global survey-based business-intelligence firm polling tens of thousands of people daily, valued at ~$1bn, and is now repositioning as an 'AI-native' intelligence company.
interesting_fact: Morning Consult's daily consumer-confidence tracking became a real-time economic indicator during the 2020 pandemic, with data shared with the Federal Reserve and Germany's central bank; he co-founded the firm before he was old enough to rent a car.
deep_cut_fact: Morning Consult started as a daily healthcare newsletter he launched while still a Carlson student; its very first poll asked whether young, uninsured people would sign up for insurance on the new ACA marketplaces. He was named UMN Entrepreneur of the Year in 2024.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Morning Consult (Washington, DC)
research_notes: Grew up outside Madison, Wisconsin; worked at Purple Strategies before Morning Consult. Frequent conference speaker (Adweek, Cannes). AI angle: company pitching 'AI-native' market intelligence.

name: Matthew Strongin
profile: Matthew Strongin is one of six founders of Nature's Fynd (The Fynder Group, formerly Sustainable Bioproducts, 2012) and its long-time CFO; he came from venture capital and banking. The Chicago company makes 'Fy' protein by fermenting a fungus from Yellowstone's hot springs and raised money from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, SoftBank, ADM and Danone at a valuation above $1B.
interesting_fact: The company's 'Fy' protein comes from a fungus (Fusarium strain flavolapis) found in Yellowstone's geothermal springs during a NASA-funded study of life in extreme environments; NASA later funded work on growing it for astronauts.
deep_cut_fact: Nature's Fynd started life in 2012 as Sustainable Bioproducts, trying to turn the Yellowstone microbe into biodiesel before pivoting to food, and it pays Yellowstone a share of profits for the right to harvest from the park.
current_role: Co-founder, CFO and director of The Fynder Group (Nature's Fynd), Chicago
research_notes: Behind-the-scenes finance co-founder; no interviews found. CEO Thomas Jonas is the public face. The deep-cut fact is about the company, not him personally. Also listed as founder of Lotic Labs (per aggregators, unverified).

name: Thomas Jonas
profile: French-born HEC graduate and former packaging-industry executive (MeadWestvaco beauty & personal care, Alcan Beauty Solutions) who co-founded Nature's Fynd around 2014. The Chicago company grows 'Fy', a protein from a fungus first studied in NASA-funded Yellowstone extremophile research, via fermentation; it raised ~$500M from backers including Bill Gates' Breakthrough Energy and was valued at ~$1B.
interesting_fact: The company's microbe comes from Yellowstone's volcanic hot springs, discovered by co-founder Mark Kozubal during NASA-funded research into how life might survive on other planets.
deep_cut_fact: After HEC (class of 1993) he served as a French Air Force officer and then ran a European-food distribution business in Hong Kong; his pivot to sustainability came in 2012 when a family holiday on Kaua'i stretched to a year and he saw plastic bottles piling up on the beaches. HEC named him 'HEC of the Year' 2022.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nature's Fynd (now The Fynder Group), Chicago
research_notes: Company rebranded from Nature's Fynd to The Fynder Group (food, pharma, materials). Has done climate podcasts before (My Climate Journey ep.169) - receptive to podcast format. Quote: 'It is not by lecturing and making people feel guilty that we will have an impact on the world.'

name: Jeff Zheng
profile: Search and recommendation engineer who led Yahoo Labs in Beijing, then left in 2011 to launch Chinese news app Yidian Zixun before founding NewsBreak in Silicon Valley in 2015. NewsBreak became one of the most-downloaded local-news apps in the US, raising $115M in 2021 at a $1B+ valuation; he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Former Microsoft AI and Bing chief Harry Shum became NewsBreak's board chairman in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: At Yahoo he headed Yahoo Labs Beijing, overseeing algorithm work across search, media, advertising and mobile, before leaving to build Yidian Zixun, the main rival to ByteDance's Toutiao.
current_role: Founder and CEO, NewsBreak (Particle Media), Mountain View, CA

name: Xuyang Ren
profile: Ren Xuyang (任旭阳) was an early Baidu executive and its VP of marketing and business development. He co-founded Chinese news aggregator Yidian Zixun and, with Jeff Zheng, the US local-news app NewsBreak (Particle Media), which reached a $1B+ valuation. Zheng runs NewsBreak as CEO, while Ren is mainly a serial founder and angel investor.
interesting_fact: NewsBreak became one of the most-downloaded news apps in the US. It started out applying the 'interest engine' recommendation approach behind Yidian Zixun's success in China to the American market.
deep_cut_fact: Ren was part of Baidu's early founding-era team. Chinese media also credit him with leading the creation of iQiyi, now one of China's biggest video-streaming platforms, as well as Yidian Zixun.
current_role: Co-founder, NewsBreak (Particle Media) and Yidian Zixun; angel investor (founded Tianshan Capital in 2015)
research_notes: China-based and low profile in English-language media. Jeff Zheng is NewsBreak's public face. Ren briefly served as Yidian Zixun CEO in early 2019. No personal contact was found.

name: Dan Cogan-Drew
profile: Former teacher and charter-school digital-learning director who co-founded Newsela with Matthew Gross in 2013. Newsela began by rewriting news articles at multiple reading levels for classrooms and grew into a K-12 content platform (later adding Formative) used by millions of educators; he leads its academic work on student outcomes.
interesting_fact: Newsela 'started with news content, differentiated for students' - the same article published at several reading levels so a whole class could read it together.
deep_cut_fact: He began his education career in Teach For America and went on to teach in public and private schools - and in the U.S. Navy; he holds degrees from Wesleyan, Brown and Tufts.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Academic Officer, Newsela
research_notes: Educator-first founder; frequent speaker (ASU+GSV, ASCD). Newsela press office is the published route.

name: Matthew Gross
profile: Former Teach for America music teacher and New York education-policy leader who founded Newsela in 2013, an edtech platform that adapts news and instructional texts to each student's reading level. Newsela raised $100M in 2021 at a $1B valuation and later combined with Formative; Gross moved from CEO to executive chair.
interesting_fact: He started Newsela after a meeting with his struggling-reader son's assistant principal left him feeling the school had given up on his son.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a Teach for America corps member teaching music at C.S. 50 in the South Bronx, and before Newsela ran the Regents Research Fund, which helped implement New York's Race to the Top reforms. His favorite school subject: U.S. History.
current_role: Founder & Executive Chair, Newsela (title per recent profiles; verify)
research_notes: Exact current title unclear (sources differ between executive chair and co-founder after CEO change). Also on New Classrooms board.

name: Michael Bermingham
profile: Compliance and FX-industry veteran (Monmouth University BSBA) who spent years at forex broker GAIN Capital, latterly as director of its Australian business, before co-founding remittance startup InstaReM with Prajit Nanu in Singapore in 2014. InstaReM became Nium in 2019, a B2B cross-border payments and card-issuing platform valued at $2B+ in 2021; he drives strategy, partnerships and operations.
interesting_fact: Nium builds all its payments technology in-house and grew from a licensed money-transfer service into a full-stack payments infrastructure provider; in 2020 he said volumes were doubling year on year to about $6B.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he spent about a decade at GAIN Capital, leading its operations and compliance teams in both the UK and US before running its Australian arm; that regulatory background was the compliance backbone InstaReM was built on.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Business Officer, Nium (Singapore cross-border payments; also listed as Global Relationship Officer on some 2025 event pages)
public_contact: press_email: press@nium.com | ir_email: ir@nium.com | official_website: https://www.nium.com

name: Prajit Nanu
profile: Co-founded Instarem in 2014 with Michael Bermingham as a Singapore remittance app; rebranded Nium in 2019 and became a B2B cross-border payments infrastructure unicorn (~$2B valuation in 2022). Nium says it holds licenses in 40+ markets and processes $60B+ a year; Nanu is pushing stablecoin settlement and a planned US IPO.
interesting_fact: He started the company after personally experiencing the friction of sending money across borders; Nium now connects 190+ countries and issues 41M+ card tokens a year, and recently added USDC stablecoin funding and settlement via a Circle partnership.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2026 Nanu was named to Skift's 2026 Power Rankings of travel-industry leaders (travel is one of Nium's biggest verticals), and he has been an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year finalist.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nium (leads the company from its San Francisco office)
research_notes: Media-friendly CEO who speaks regularly on payments, stablecoins and AI; press@nium.com is the published PR route. Relocated leadership to San Francisco ahead of US IPO plans (IPO target slipped to end-2026 per 2024 reports).

It expanded into resale, home services, the NoBrokerHood society-management app and the CallZen.AI conversational-intelligence tool, raised ~$361M (Tiger Global, General Atlantic, Google) and became a unicorn in Nov 2021.
interesting_fact: NoBroker runs a consumer-to-consumer real-estate model; by 2022 it handled 500,000+ transactions a year with over 7.5 million properties registered, and its NoBrokerHood app became part of India's ONDC network.
current_role: Co-founder, NoBroker Technologies (Bengaluru proptech) - widely described as its CTO; not independently confirmed here

name: Saurabh Garg
profile: IIT and IIM Ahmedabad (PGP 2004) alumnus who co-founded Bengaluru-based NoBroker in 2014 with Amit Kumar Agarwal and Akhil Gupta to let Indians rent and buy property without paying broker commissions. NoBroker became India's first proptech unicorn (~$1B, 2021) and has expanded into home services and society-management (NoBrokerHood); Garg is also an angel investor in 30+ startups.
interesting_fact: He has said he first felt the problem in 2007, when he struggled to find accommodation in Mumbai without paying a large broker fee.
deep_cut_fact: He attempted startups while at IIT during the dot-com boom, then turned down master's-in-finance offers from LSE and Columbia to attend IIM Ahmedabad to learn 'how companies are built'; IIMA later gave him its Young Alumni Achievers' Award (YAAA 2022).
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Business Officer, NoBroker.com
research_notes: Regular speaker at IITs/IIMs/incubators - open to talks. No verified press email found (only a redacted address on YourStory). Sources differ on whether his IIT was Bombay or Delhi; omitted.

name: Benjamin Eldridge
profile: Engineer-inventor who co-founded Nutcracker Therapeutics in 2018 with former FormFactor CEO Igor Khandros, applying semiconductor-style biochip manufacturing to RNA therapeutics. Previously a longtime FormFactor executive (incl. CTO) after starting at IBM's T.J. Watson Research Center. Nutcracker has repositioned as an RNA contract research/development/manufacturing (CRDMO) business.
interesting_fact: Nutcracker's ACORN/NMU systems make nanoparticle-encapsulated RNA therapeutics on single-use biochips, essentially an RNA factory 'in a box' borrowed from chip-industry thinking.
deep_cut_fact: He is a named inventor on more than 200 US patents, and began his career doing engineering at IBM's T.J. Watson Research Center; he holds an M.S. in Physics from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Nutcracker Therapeutics (Emeryville, CA)
research_notes: Company status unclear: CEO Khandros retired March 2025 (Cynthia Collins interim CEO); PitchBook lists company out of business as of Nov 2025, while GEN covered it in Dec 2025. Verify his current role before outreach. No published press contact found.

OpenWeb passed a $1B valuation in its 2021 Series E and was valued at $1.5B+ in its 2022 Series F. Green keeps a low profile; his LinkedIn now describes him as an entrepreneur, investor and systems architect.
interesting_fact: OpenWeb's 2021 $150M round included The New York Times Company and NYU professor Scott Galloway among its investors, an unusual cap table for an ad-tech company.
current_role: Co-founder, OpenWeb (formerly Spot.IM); current operating role unclear (LinkedIn shows MGK Labs, Tel Aviv)
