name: Nadav Shoval
profile: Israeli-American entrepreneur (b. 1990) who co-founded Spot.IM in 2015, later renamed OpenWeb, the publisher comments/engagement platform valued above $1.5B in 2022. He was CEO until he left in 2024. In 2025 he co-founded Project Omega with CEO Staff Sheehan. It recycles used nuclear fuel into long-duration power sources and reactor fuel and emerged from stealth in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: Project Omega calls used nuclear fuel 'the crude oil of the future'. It uses pyroprocessing to refine it into long-life power isotopes, next-gen reactor fuel and medical/scientific isotopes, and announced an $80M raise in Nov 2026.
deep_cut_fact: At 24 he wrote in VentureBeat that he had been building startups since age 11, that Spot.IM was his fifth venture, and that 'I have had the tremendous opportunity to accrue a great many failures.'
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Project Omega (spent-nuclear-fuel recycling); CEO of FlowMode; senior advisor to OpenWeb
public_contact: office_email: info@projectomega.com (Project Omega general inbox) | official_website: https://projectomega.com | podcast: Guest appearance (episode #78)

Sensitive: he was ousted as OpenWeb CEO in Sept 2024 after a board dispute (an Israeli court rejected his petition), and per Wikipedia OpenWeb sought insolvency protection in Sept 2026. Avoid both topics. Project Omega's team page lists Staff Sheehan as CEO, and Johanna Spangenberg Jones as Head of Communications.

name: Roee Goldberg
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who joined Spot.IM (now OpenWeb) as co-founder and COO in 2014, helping build the publisher comment/conversation platform into a unicorn before leaving the COO role around January 2022. In 2025 he founded London-based Atmospheric AI, which builds digital twins of raw-material supply chains (cost, resilience, emissions) and raised a $10M seed led by DBL Partners in November 2026.
interesting_fact: Atmospheric AI models tens of thousands of industrial plants 'between the well and your factory gate' so manufacturers can see the true cost and carbon of what they buy; the seed will extend models from plastics into chemicals, paper and metals.
deep_cut_fact: Before OpenWeb he was co-founder and CEO of a startup called Servito.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Atmospheric AI (London; raw-material supply-chain modeling)
research_notes: Strong fit for an energy/climate podcast: just raised a seed for a climate/industrial supply-chain AI company (Axios exclusive, Nov 2026). Some sources say he advises Tech Nation's Climate Growth Programme (unverified). Wikipedia credits OpenWeb's founding to Nadav Shoval and Ishay Green only.

name: Ivan Dimov
profile: Engineer-turned-biotech founder (PhD applied biophysics, Dublin City University; postdocs at UC Berkeley and in Irv Weissman's Stanford lab) who co-founded Orca Bio in 2016 with Nate Fernhoff and Jeroen Bekaert. Orca develops high-precision allogeneic cell therapies (lead product Orca-T for blood cancers); Fernhoff succeeded him as CEO in May 2025 ahead of the BLA filing.
interesting_fact: He also co-founded Lucira Health, spun out of his Berkeley microfluidics work, which won FDA authorization for the first at-home COVID-19 self-test and was later acquired by Pfizer.
deep_cut_fact: His background is in electronics and bio-MEMS; he has said working with Stanford physicians changed his approach from 'building technology first' to starting from a clearly defined medical problem.
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO (2016-May 2025), Orca Bio
research_notes: CEO transition reported May 2025 (https://trial.medpath.com/news/902ccabbc6efd8da/orca-bio-appoints-co-founder-nate-fernhoff-as-ceo-ahead-of-2025-bla-submission-for-orca-t); his current exact title not confirmed. Also earlier co-founded Blobcode Technologies.

name: Jeroen Bekaert
profile: Belgian-born engineer (Ghent PhD in computer science engineering, Stanford GSB master's) who co-founded cell-therapy company Orca Bio in 2016 with Ivan Dimov and Nate Fernhoff. Orca's high-precision cell therapy Orca-T won FDA approval as Tregzi in June 2026 for blood-cancer patients undergoing stem-cell transplants; Bekaert oversees company operations as President.
interesting_fact: Orca-T (Tregzi), approved by the FDA on 30 June 2026, is described as the first regulatory T-cell therapy approved for blood-cancer patients undergoing allogeneic stem-cell transplant.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a researcher at Los Alamos National Laboratory, later ran J&J supply-chain engineering for EMEA and Merck KGaA's Silicon Valley innovation center, and was a Gustave Boel-Sofina Fellow.
current_role: Co-founder and President, Orca Bio (since May 2025; previously COO)
research_notes: Operations-focused executive with a low media profile; Nate Fernhoff is CEO since 2025. Corporate comms contact listed on press releases.

name: Nathaniel Fernhoff
profile: Scientist-founder (Stanford BS in biology and math, UC Berkeley PhD) who co-founded Menlo Park cell-therapy company Orca Bio in 2016 with Ivan Dimov and Jeroen Bekaert, serving as CSO before becoming CEO in 2025. Orca builds high-precision donor-cell therapies for blood cancers; its lead product Orca-T won FDA approval as Tregzi on June 30, 2026.
interesting_fact: Tregzi (Orca-T), approved by the FDA in June 2026, is described as the first approved therapy built on highly purified regulatory T cells, aimed at improving chronic-GVHD-free survival after matched-donor stem cell transplants.
deep_cut_fact: Before Orca he was an NIH Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA postdoctoral scholar in Irving Weissman's stem-cell lab at Stanford, and he holds two Stanford bachelor's degrees, in biological sciences and in mathematics.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO (since May 2025), Orca Bio
public_contact: press_email: media@orcabio.com | ir_email: ir@orcabio.com | official_website: https://orcabio.com
research_notes: Goes by Nate Fernhoff. Biotech rather than energy/data-center fit; timely hook is the 2026 Tregzi approval and commercial launch. Route via Orca Bio corporate communications.

name: Ronald Martell
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Orca Bio (Menlo Park/Sacramento cell-therapy company founded 2016, developer of Orca-T for blood cancers; valued ~$2B). Orca Bio's current leadership page names co-founders Nate Fernhoff (CEO) and Jeroen Bekaert (President) and does not mention a Ronald Martell, so his link to the company could not be confirmed.
research_notes: Identity unverified; not on Orca Bio's leadership page (https://orcabio.com/our-company/). Possibly an early executive/board member or a Hurun data error - verify before outreach. Search budget ran out before further checks.

name: Court Cunningham
profile: Serial operator who ran local-marketing firm Yodle as CEO from 2007, growing it to $200M+ revenue before its 2016 sale to Web.com for $342M. In 2017 he co-founded Orchard, which lets homeowners buy a new home before selling the old one, and has expanded it across multiple US states. Former DoubleClick VP and Harvard MBA.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Yodle went from about $1M to over $200M in revenue and sold to Web.com for $342M.
deep_cut_fact: In high school he spent about three years building an 18th-century-style mahogany desk; when his woodworking teacher said the dividers were too loose, he made him start over ('You're better than good enough'). His mom's mantra was 'Action TNT' (today, not tomorrow).
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Orchard (real estate tech, New York)
research_notes: Regular Inman speaker; approachable via Orchard press.

name: Phil DeGisi
profile: Phil DeGisi co-founded Orchard, the 'buy before you sell' real-estate tech company that lets homeowners purchase a new home before selling their old one, which reached a $1B+ valuation within about four years. He leads Orchard's product and marketing teams, growing marketing from one person to a 30-person department.
interesting_fact: Named a HousingWire 2022 Marketing Leader; in Orchard's early days he personally met with hundreds of homeowners to understand the pain of buying and selling a home.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product & Marketing Officer, Orchard (as of 2022; current title not re-verified)
research_notes: Low public profile. Web-search budget exhausted mid-lane, so background/deep-cut research was limited to direct page fetches.

name: Gilles Wainrib
profile: French applied mathematician and machine-learning researcher who co-founded Owkin in Paris in 2016 with haematologist Thomas Clozel. Owkin uses AI and privacy-preserving (federated) learning on hospital data for drug discovery and diagnostics, became a unicorn in 2021 after a Sanofi investment, and now builds agentic AI for biology (K Navigator, K Pro). He came from academia (Stanford postdoc, assistant professor).
interesting_fact: Owkin's founding idea was to unlock insights from vast amounts of patient data held in hospitals and research centers 'in a privacy-preserving and secure way' - Owkin describes Wainrib as a pioneer of machine learning in biology.
deep_cut_fact: Before Owkin he was a mathematical neuroscientist: with Jonathan Touboul (Collège de France team) he co-authored work on bifurcations of stochastic differential equations and macroscopic limits of large stochastic neural networks.
current_role: Co-founder of Owkin (Chief Scientific Officer since 2016 per profiles; current title unconfirmed)
public_contact: press_email: alistair.jennings@owkin.com (international media; page's mailto link points to michelle.shearly@owkin.com) | press_email: malika.labou-ext@owkin.com (French media)
research_notes: Low-profile scientist co-founder; Thomas Clozel is Owkin's public face. Press contacts on Owkin's press kit change often - check the latest release. Education (Ecole Polytechnique) per TheOrg, not independently verified.

name: Thomas Clozel
profile: French oncologist-hematologist (MD) and former clinical assistant professor at Hopital Henri-Mondor who co-founded Owkin in 2016 with ML professor Gilles Wainrib. Owkin applies AI and federated learning to drug discovery and diagnostics, became a unicorn in 2021 after a $180M Sanofi investment, and now pitches 'biological artificial superintelligence' via its K Pro AI-scientist agent.
interesting_fact: Owkin has raised 300M+ dollars and signed AI deals with Sanofi, BMS, Servier, MSD and AstraZeneca; it released K Pro, an agentic 'AI scientist' for biology, in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before medicine he flirted with moving to LA 'to crack Hollywood'. He landed his Weill Cornell lab spot by meeting Ari Melnick in a Deauville hotel lobby: his phone had died, so he scanned the room until he spotted a man sipping a Diet Coke while reading a cell-biology paper.
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Owkin (Paris / New York)
public_contact: press_email: alistair.jennings@owkin.com (international media) | press_email: malika.labou-ext@owkin.com (French media) | x: https://x.com/OWKINscience (company) | official_website: https://www.owkin.com/team
research_notes: Son of Actelion founders Jean-Paul and Martine Clozel. Frequent conference speaker on AI in biology; Owkin press team is the clear route.

name: Austin Allison
profile: Cincinnati-raised entrepreneur who founded real-estate transaction software dotloop in 2009, sold it to Zillow in 2015 (reported ~$108-120M) and ran it inside Zillow until 2018. He then co-founded Pacaso (2020), which sells co-owned second homes via property-specific LLCs; it hit a $1B valuation within five months, then a record for a US startup.
interesting_fact: Pacaso reached unicorn status in about five months after launch in 2020, among the fastest ever for a US startup.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in a small town north of Cincinnati, the son of a carpenter, and says he was 'swinging a hammer starting at age three or four'; watching his father show up every day to provide shaped his work ethic.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Pacaso
research_notes: Frequent podcast guest and speaker; receptive to founder-story interviews.

name: Spencer Rascoff
profile: Serial founder (b. 1975) who co-founded Hotwire at 24 (sold to IAC for $685M), then co-founded Zillow and ran it as CEO 2010-2019 through its IPO and 15 acquisitions. Afterwards he co-founded dot.LA, co-ownership home platform Pacaso (unicorn) and AI firm Replify via family office 75 & Sunny, before being named Match Group CEO in 2025 to turn around Tinder/Hinge.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Hotwire.com in 1999 at age 24 after stints at Goldman Sachs and TPG; it sold to IAC a few years later for $685M.
deep_cut_fact: As a Visiting Executive Professor at Harvard Business School (2020) he co-created and co-taught the 'Managing Tech Ventures' course; he also co-wrote the NYT bestseller 'Zillow Talk' (2015).
current_role: CEO, Match Group (since Feb 2025; also directly ran Tinder from July 2025); co-founder of Pacaso
research_notes: Highly visible public-company CEO; previously hosted the 'Office Hours' podcast and writes open letters on LinkedIn. Pacaso is the Hurun-listed source but Match Group is his day job; route via Match Group PR or 75 & Sunny.

name: Mikita Mikado
education: Belarusian State University of Informatics and Radioelectronics
profile: Minsk-born entrepreneur (BSUIR graduate) who, with co-founder Sergey Barysiuk, built Quote Roller in 2011 to automate sales proposals; it became PandaDoc in 2013, raised funding from Kima Ventures, Microsoft Ventures, HubSpot and others, and hit a $1B valuation in 2021. He has run the company from San Francisco since 2013.
interesting_fact: He was featured in Yury Dud's 2020 documentary on Russian-speaking founders in Silicon Valley, which made him a role model for young people pursuing IT careers.
deep_cut_fact: At 19 he first went to the U.S. on a Work and Travel student program, working part-time jobs while teaching himself web design and software development - years before returning to Minsk to build Quote Roller, PandaDoc's predecessor.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, PandaDoc (San Francisco / Minsk-origin document automation and e-signature company)
public_contact: press_email: press@pandadoc.com | contact_form: https://www.pandadoc.com/contact/ | https://x.com/mikitamikado | https://www.linkedin.com/in/mikitamikado/ | https://www.instagram.com/mikitamikado/
research_notes: PandaDoc about page lists him as CEO; Keith Rabkin also appears (some third-party sites call Rabkin CEO) - confirm current title. Avoid politics: he was outspoken during Belarus 2020 protests (Protect Belarus initiative). Has told a 'berry seller' origin story in podcasts (Mixergy, SaaS Club).

name: Sergey Barysiuk
profile: Belarusian-born engineer (also spelled Siarhei Barysiuk / Sergey Borisyuk) who, with Mikita Mikado, turned their Minsk software-outsourcing shop's sales-quote tool Quote Roller (c.2011) into PandaDoc, a document automation and e-signature platform. PandaDoc reached a $1B valuation in 2021 and is now headquartered in San Francisco with large teams in Europe.
interesting_fact: PandaDoc began life as Quote Roller, a set of proposal templates sent as a link, before broadening into all business documents and e-signatures and becoming one of the first Belarus-founded unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: He says the idea came on 'a warm June evening' at their outsourcing firm, when he was about to go home and got buried in contracts and proposals to write - as 'a true developer' who disliked paperwork, he decided the process had to be automated.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, PandaDoc
research_notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; Mikado is the public face. Company relocated staff out of Belarus after 2020 (sensitive political context - avoid in outreach). PandaDoc site blocked automated fetch; no press email confirmed.

name: Eynat Guez
profile: French-born Israeli entrepreneur (raised in Netanya) who co-founded Papaya Global in 2016 with Ofer Herman and Ruben Drong. The payroll and workforce-payments platform hit a $3.7B valuation in 2021, making it Israel's first woman-led unicorn; it now processes tens of billions in annual payments and is pushing agentic-AI compliance products (Papaya One, Papaya Talent in 2026).
interesting_fact: Papaya is her third company: she earlier founded Relocation Source (2009, corporate relocation) and Expert Source (helping firms expand into East Asia), after seven years as COO of LR Group, a holding company running infrastructure projects in Africa.
deep_cut_fact: Before business she worked as a youth journalist (Channel 2, Israeli Educational TV, Ma'ariv La'noar), served in the IDF as an F-16 squadron adjutant, and was a competitive swimmer; she sits on the board of Hagal Shely, an NGO that uses the sea (surfing) as therapy.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Papaya Global
public_contact: press_email: Marketing@papayaglobal.com | press_email: community@papayaglobal.com (Naomi Fletcher) | official_website: https://www.papayaglobal.com
research_notes: Media-friendly CEO; frequent podcast guest (e.g. Fintech Leaders). Press contact on 2026 releases is Naomi Fletcher. Reports (Finance Magnates) say Papaya has explored a sale at up to $4.5B.

name: Ofer Herman
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded global payroll and workforce-payments platform Papaya Global in 2016 with Eynat Guez and Ruben Drong, serving as CTO as it grew to a $3.7B valuation in its 2021 Series D. He announced in June 2023 that he was leaving Papaya after seven-plus years. Earlier he co-founded AASL and co-founded/led MRD-IT Solutions and SafelyGuard.
interesting_fact: Papaya Global went from a $1.5M seed in 2016 to a $3.7B valuation in Sept 2021 (Series D led by Insight Partners and Tiger Global), and later bought UK payments firm Azimo.
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of Papaya Global (2016-2023); current role not publicly confirmed
research_notes: Very low public profile; no current venture found after leaving Papaya in June 2023 (per aggregator citing his LinkedIn post). Earlier ventures (AASL, MRD-IT Solutions, SafelyGuard) from Welcome to the Jungle profile only. Best route likely LinkedIn.

name: Ruben Drong
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur and software engineer who co-founded global payroll and workforce-payments platform Papaya Global in 2016 with Eynat Guez and Ofer Herman. He was Papaya's first Chief Product Officer, charting its technology vision, before moving in 2022 to Chief Innovation Officer focused on long-term strategy.
interesting_fact: As Papaya Global's first Chief Product Officer he set the technology vision for a platform that now runs payroll and payments in 160+ countries; in 2022 he shifted to Chief Innovation Officer.
current_role: Co-founder, Papaya Global (named Chief Innovation Officer in 2022)
research_notes: Low public profile; CEO Eynat Guez is the company's public face. Earlier ventures (AASL, SafelyGuard, MRD-IT) appear only on aggregator profiles, so not used. Best route LinkedIn or Papaya PR.

name: Artavazd Mehrabyan
profile: Armenian software engineer who co-founded Picsart with Hovhannes Avoyan and Mikayel Vardanyan (c.2011), serving first as COO and later as CTO. Picsart grew to ~150M monthly active users and 1B+ downloads and became Armenia's first unicorn (2021). He now leads Picsart's push into generative AI, including a commercially safe image model built with Getty Images.
interesting_fact: Picsart reached about 150 million monthly active users and over one billion downloads, and partnered with Getty Images in 2024 on a commercially safe text-to-image model.
deep_cut_fact: Before Picsart he was a chief software architect (incl. at Lycos Europe, Sourcio and Virtual Solutions); he holds two master's degrees: Industrial Engineering from the Armenian National Agrarian University and Computer Science from the American University of Armenia.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Picsart (creative/AI photo-video editing platform, Armenia/US)
research_notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Hovhannes Avoyan is the public face. Good angle: Picsart's AI/GPU infrastructure and Armenia's tech ecosystem. Prior-employer list from a job-board company profile; degrees from conference speaker bio.

name: Hovhannes Avoyan
education: American University of Armenia; Harvard Business School; National Polytechnic University of Armenia
profile: Armenian-American serial entrepreneur (b. 1965, Yerevan) who co-founded photo/video editor Picsart in 2011 and built it into a 150M+ MAU creative platform. Earlier companies (CEDIT, Sourcio, Monitis and others) were sold to buyers including Lycos, GFI/TeamViewer and HelpSystems.
interesting_fact: Five of his startups before Picsart were acquired by global companies, and he was founding president of Armenia's Union of IT Enterprises (2000-2015).
deep_cut_fact: Besides a 1987 computer science degree, he holds a master's in political science and international affairs from the American University of Armenia (1995), which gave him its Distinguished Alumni Award in 2016; he also sits on AUA's board of trustees.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Picsart
research_notes: Active speaker/writer on AI; has a TechCrunch contributor page.

name: Ben Kinney
profile: Washington-state real estate agent turned proptech entrepreneur. Founded BKCO (Brivity, ActiveRain, Kwkly, Blueroof360) and in 2019 co-founded PLACE with Chris Suarez, a platform/services company for top real-estate teams that raised $100M led by Goldman Sachs at a $1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: He was the top-ranked agent in Washington state by transaction volume from 2012 to 2021 and appeared on the WSJ/REAL Trends top-1,000 agents lists 2011-2022.
deep_cut_fact: While studying at Western Washington University he worked as a cable-TV installer, then sold cable, phone and internet door-to-door before starting in real estate in 2004.
current_role: Co-founder, PLACE Inc.; founder, Ben Kinney Companies (BKCO)
research_notes: Active speaker and author (Inman, RISMedia). PLACE reportedly eyeing an IPO.

name: Chris Suarez
profile: Portland-area real estate entrepreneur who founded Xperience, a top Keller Williams expansion organisation, then in 2020 co-founded PLACE with Ben Kinney, a platform providing tech, back-office and services to top agent teams across 100+ US/Canada markets; PLACE reached unicorn valuation. He also owns brokerage offices and runs coaching/mastermind programmes.
interesting_fact: PLACE launched in early 2020 already carrying $1.5B in sales and $40M revenue from its founders' existing businesses, just as COVID-19 hit.
deep_cut_fact: He and Ben Kinney shared the 2023 EY Entrepreneur Of The Year Mountain West Award; he hosts the podcast 'Xperience Growth with Chris Suarez'.
current_role: Co-founder, PLACE, Inc. (real estate team platform); leads Xperience Brokerage Network and Xperience Growth Coaching
public_contact: official_website: https://xperiencechrissuarez.squarespace.com/about-chris | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/chrissuarezpdx | x: https://twitter.com/Xperience_Chris | podcast: Xperience Growth with Chris Suarez (Apple Podcasts)
research_notes: Active speaker/coach with his own site and podcast - accessible. Team page: https://place.com/team/

name: Michael Carter
profile: Michael Maxwell Carter co-founded instant-games company Playco in 2020 with Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and game producers Takeshi Otsuka and Teddy Cross. It launched with a $100M Series A (led by Josh Buckley and Sequoia) at a valuation just over $1B. Earlier he founded Game Closure, a StartX-backed HTML5 instant-games startup that raised $12M in 2012.
interesting_fact: Playco makes games that launch instantly from a link, with no download, across Facebook Instant Games, Snapchat Minis, iOS App Clips and similar platforms. Carter predicted that for mobile gaming, 'At some point, people will hit a switch.'
deep_cut_fact: Carter helped create WebSocket: in June 2008 he led the discussions that produced the first version of the protocol, and he and Ian Hickson coined the name 'WebSocket'.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Playco (Tokyo-based instant-games company)
research_notes: He met Waldron when Waldron was advising Game Closure. He works remotely (Playco execs are spread across Tokyo, Seoul, SF and LA). No published press email or verified personal accounts found. Hurun lists Playco at a $1B valuation.

name: Takeshi Otsuka
profile: Takeshi Otsuka is a Japanese game producer who led DeNA's Mobage mobile social gaming platform (2005-2015), which Playco says generated over $1B in revenue. He moved to the US in 2011 for roles at DeNA West and N3TWORK. In 2020 he co-founded Playco with Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron, WebSocket co-inventor Michael Carter and Teddy Cross. Playco builds games playable instantly inside social and messaging apps and was valued at $1B in its Series A.
interesting_fact: Playco's co-founders include Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and Michael Carter, co-inventor of HTML5 WebSockets. The company is headquartered in Tokyo but distributed-first, with founders split across Seoul, Tokyo, San Francisco and LA.
deep_cut_fact: He produced 'Kaito Royale' (2009), a mobile social game whose success helped spark Japan's mobile social gaming boom (over a thousand such games were released in 2010) and which also became a TV show. N3TWORK CEO Neil Young called him a '10x-er'.
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Producer & SVP, Playco (instant-play gaming, HQ Tokyo)
research_notes: Second source for the Kaito Royale TV show and the '10x-er' quote: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/n3twork-hires-takeshi-otsuka/. No published press email was found on play.co. Low English-language media profile.

name: Teddy Cross
profile: American game producer and engineer and early HTML5 gaming pioneer who worked with Michael Carter at Game Closure from 2011 and led software development at tech companies in Korea. In 2020 he co-founded Playco with Carter, Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and ex-DeNA executive Takeshi Otsuka; it debuted as a unicorn with a $100M Series A.
interesting_fact: Playco launched in Sept 2020 already a unicorn: a $100M Series A at just over $1B valuation, co-led by Josh Buckley and Sequoia Capital Global Equities, with backers including Keisuke Honda's KSK Angel Fund.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 2011 at age 15 as a software intern in gaming, building HTML5 puzzle games that quickly gained thousands of users, and later became a well-known figure in the Korean tech scene.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Playco (Tokyo-based instant-play games company)
research_notes: website@play.co is Playco's published general-inquiry address (not personal). Very young founder (born c.1996 per Playco bio age).

name: Philipp Nieland
profile: German co-founder of PPRO, which provides local/alternative payment-method acquiring and processing to PSPs such as PayPal and Stripe. Crunchbase says he studied economics and computer science and founded PPRO in 2006; MarketScreener credits Nieland and Tobias Schreyer as founders. PPRO's backers include PayPal, Citi Ventures and HPE Growth.
interesting_fact: PPRO raised a $50M round led by PayPal, with Citi Ventures participating and HPE Growth reinvesting.
current_role: Co-founder of PPRO (cross-border payments infrastructure, London/Munich); current role not verified
research_notes: Very low public profile; founder attribution rests on Crunchbase (https://crunchbase.com/person/philipp-nieland) and MarketScreener. Not to be confused with co-founder Philipp Bock. No published press email found on ppro.com.

name: Tobias Schreyer
profile: German payments entrepreneur who co-founded PPRO, the London-based local-payments infrastructure provider, with Philipp Nieland in 2006. PPRO was later valued at about $1B. As CCO he helped secure PPRO's UK FCA e-money licence in 2012 and launch its VIABUY prepaid card. As an undergraduate he started a Munich internet service provider.
interesting_fact: His interest in payments started in childhood: he collected prepaid calling cards and traded them at exchanges.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 PYMNTS interview he said he commuted 50 miles to work by bike, using the ride to plan his day. He also said: 'you need to have failed at some point in your career; otherwise you don't know the essentials.'
current_role: Co-founder of PPRO (former Chief Commercial Officer); not on PPRO's current leadership page
research_notes: He is not listed on PPRO's current leadership page (CEO is Motie Bring), so his current role is unverified. Low public profile; LinkedIn is likely the best route.

name: Davis Siksnans
profile: Latvian entrepreneur who co-founded print-on-demand company Printful with Lauris Liberts in 2013 out of Latvia's Draugiem Group, and was CEO from 2015 to June 2022. Printful became Latvia's first unicorn in 2021 after a $130M investment from Bregal Sagemount, and in late 2024 agreed to merge with rival Printify (combined group named Fyul).
interesting_fact: Printful was spun out of Startup Vitamins, the team's online store selling motivational-quote posters for startups; frustration with third-party printers led them to build their own printing operation.
deep_cut_fact: Printful launched on July 16, 2013 with a three-person team printing t-shirts in co-founder Lauris Liberts's garage; Siksnans's motto: 'A good time to start is anytime, because a better one will never come.'
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Printful; Senior Advisor at Draugiem Group (since June 2022) and angel investor
research_notes: Stepped down as CEO June 29, 2022 (https://www.printful.com/news/printful-management-team-change). Frequent podcast guest (Mixergy, Hack the Entrepreneur, Wix 'Now What'). No published direct email found; LinkedIn is likely best route.

name: Lauris Liberts
education: University of Latvia
profile: Latvian tech entrepreneur Lauris Liberts founded the social network draugiem.lv and created Draugiem Group in 2004. In 2013 the group incubated Printful, a print-on-demand and drop-shipping fulfilment service he co-founded with Davis Siksnans; it became Latvia's first unicorn after a $130M investment from Bregal Sagemount in 2021.
interesting_fact: Printful grew out of the team's own side businesses Startup Vitamins and Behappy.me, which sold motivational quote posters and prints; needing a reliable print-and-ship partner, they built their own and launched Printful on July 16, 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics at the University of Latvia and earned a master's in e-business and innovation from Lancaster University in the UK.
current_role: Founder and co-owner, Draugiem Group; co-founder and board chair of Printful
research_notes: Chair/board role at Printful per MarketScreener aggregator. Draugiem Group (draugiemgroup.com) and Printful press page (printful.com/press) are JS-rendered; no published email extracted. Route via Draugiem Group or Printful press team.

name: Joel Gottsegen
profile: Joel Gottsegen co-founded Qualia in 2015 with Nate Baker and Lucas Hansen; the company runs a cloud platform connecting homebuyers, sellers, lenders, title/escrow and real-estate agents to digitise the US home-closing process, and was valued around $2B. The co-founders were Forbes 30 Under 30 honorees.
interesting_fact: Qualia was the first technology company to join the Coalition to Stop Real Estate Wire Fraud, and all three co-founders were Forbes 30 Under 30 award recipients.
current_role: Co-founder, Qualia (current operating role not confirmed; Nate Baker is CEO)
research_notes: Very low public profile; aggregator sites suggest a Stanford CS degree and a later venture ('Petty Karma'), but these were not verified from primary sources. Best route is via Qualia press or CEO Nate Baker.

name: Lucas Hansen
profile: Co-founded Qualia in 2015 with Nate Baker and Joel Gottsegen; Qualia is a real-estate closing/title software platform (unicorn). In 2023 he co-founded CivAI, a Berkeley nonprofit that uses live software demos (deepfakes, phishing, AI biosecurity risks) to educate lawmakers and the public about AI capabilities and dangers.
interesting_fact: CivAI, which he co-founded in response to ChatGPT's launch, gives private AI-risk demos to lawmakers and national-security officials, and is a member of the NIST AI Safety Institute Consortium; its tools were used at the 2025 AI Action Summit.
deep_cut_fact: In October 2025 he wrote a Wall Street Journal op-ed, 'I Need a Chatbot That Won't Drive Me Crazy,' arguing AI firms should be liable for harms like chatbot-induced psychosis if they don't take adequate precautions. He met his CivAI co-founder Siddharth Hiregowdara while working together at Qualia.
current_role: Co-founder, CivAI (Civic AI Security Program); co-founder and board member, Qualia
research_notes: Now focused on AI safety (very relevant for an AI/data-center podcast angle); frequently quoted in media (NYT, S&P Global). CivAI site blocked automated fetches this session, so no CivAI contact verified; it has a press section (civai.org/press). LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/llucash (per search result, not independently verified).

name: Nate Baker
profile: Nate Baker is co-founder and CEO of Qualia, a San Francisco software platform that title, escrow and real-estate companies use to run home closings (valued at about $2B per Hurun). He had started a small company in college and then worked at the venture fund 8VC before Qualia. Qualia has since grown past $100M ARR.
interesting_fact: Qualia was chosen by spreadsheet. Baker drew up 10 'selection heuristics' for an enduring B2B software market (platform not feature, network effects, multiple paths to revenue). The finalists were life-insurance broker software, P&C claims-adjusting software and title software.
deep_cut_fact: Qualia's first customer, Massachusetts state senator and real-estate lawyer Barry Feingold, was met at a conference thanks to a Stanford sweatshirt. Baker and Qualia's first 25 employees took turns living in Feingold's Andover basement to learn the title business, and new hires also tutored his kids in math.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Qualia (real-estate closing / title software)
public_contact: official_website: https://www.qualia.com | podcast: Guest on The SaaS Podcast (SaaS Club) episode 467
research_notes: He speaks at industry events (ALTA) and on podcasts, so he is fairly accessible. No published press email was verified. Education (UPenn mechanical engineering) appears only on aggregator sites and is not verified here.

name: Mario Ciabarra
profile: Penn State-educated serial founder and son of an immigrant family, the youngest of six, from Montgomery County, PA. He sold his app-performance-monitoring startup DevStream to Compuware, built iPhone app businesses Intelliborn and Rock Your Phone, and in 2015 co-founded Quantum Metric with hacker David Wang. Quantum Metric became Colorado's first tech unicorn after a $200M Insight-led round in 2021.
interesting_fact: Quantum Metric passed $100M in annual recurring revenue in December 2022 and says it captures insights from about 45% of the world's internet users. Penn State's podcast called him the first unicorn founder to start a business in Colorado.
deep_cut_fact: At Penn State he started YourNotes.com, which paid students to take class notes and published them free for other students, funded by sponsors, as a challenge to paid service Nittany Notes. He says he still hates taking notes.

name: Andrew Reiter
profile: Andrew Reiter (Northwestern '10, Harvard MS robotics '12) is a perception and sensor-fusion engineer. He co-founded San Diego defense-autonomy company Shield AI in 2015 with Ryan and Brandon Tseng and was its first CTO; Shield AI makes the Hivemind AI pilot and the V-BAT drone. deep_cut_fact: He started at Northwestern as a chemical engineering major, but robotics hooked him when he won the 2009 McCormick Autonomous Robot Design Competition with classmates Andrew Dai and Eric West. At Draper he led teams building a handheld 3D-scanning system and a fully autonomous exploration quadrotor.
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of Shield AI (left 2022; remains an adviser). Contrary Research reports he moved to ThorCon US (molten-salt nuclear) in 2023; I could not confirm his title there.

He has no published email or verified social handle; try LinkedIn or Northwestern Engineering alumni channels. Shield AI's press office is not a good route since he left.

name: Brandon Tseng
profile: Former Navy SEAL officer and surface warfare officer (7 years; deployed to Afghanistan and the Pacific) who co-founded Shield AI in 2015 with his brother Ryan Tseng and Andrew Reiter. Shield AI builds the Hivemind AI-pilot software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft and (via Aechelon) simulation tech; it was valued at ~$12.7B in 2026 and is a leading US defense-autonomy startup.
interesting_fact: His thesis is that the AI pilot matters more than the airframe; in 2026 he said he now expects autonomous defense systems to be ubiquitous by 2040-45, not his original 2035 forecast, because procurement moved slower than he expected.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2015 he and his co-founders pitched 30 Silicon Valley investors and all said no; the next year they met 25 more and two said yes. a16z's Peter Levine, a board member, likened defense tech then to Uber or Airbnb: 'ideas that look dumb until they don't.'
current_role: Co-founder and President, Shield AI
research_notes: Frequent podcast/op-ed guest (Masters of Scale, War on the Rocks), so receptive to media. AI/autonomy plus defense angle; adjacent rather than core to energy/data centers. Shield AI's own site blocked automated fetch; personal social handles not verified.

name: Ryan Tseng

Shield AI raised a $1.5bn Series G at a $12.7bn valuation in March 2026.
interesting_fact: Shield AI's founding idea came from Brandon Tseng's SEAL deployments: small autonomous drones that could clear buildings ahead of troops; it grew into Hivemind, an AI pilot for aircraft from quadcopters to F-16s.
deep_cut_fact: Before defense tech he was a wireless-power entrepreneur: as founder/CEO/CTO of WiPower he developed wireless charging technology and sold the company to Qualcomm in 2010. He studied electrical engineering at the University of Florida and earned an MBA at MIT.
current_role: Co-founder & President (strategic growth), Shield AI; CEO 2015-May 2025

research_notes: Experienced public speaker (congressional testimony, MIT fireside chats, FAA Drone Advisory Committee). Energy angle: drones for grid and utility infrastructure inspection. Best route is press@skydio.com.

name: Christian Jorge
profile: One of six co-founders of Vestiaire Collective, the Paris resale marketplace for pre-owned luxury fashion. It launched in 2009 as 'Vestiaire de Copines' and later became a unicorn backed by Kering, Conde Nast and SoftBank. He describes himself as a repeat founder and operator, mostly in CEO/COO roles. He later held an executive role at sustainable-food brand Omie and now works with circular-economy repair startup Murfy.
interesting_fact: Vestiaire Collective launched in 2009 with just 3,000 pre-owned fashion items sourced from the founders' friends and family, and now operates in 70+ countries.
deep_cut_fact: At Vestiaire he launched the company's Tourcoing operations site in northern France. He is now climate-focused: an investor in Team for the Planet, a partner at 50 Partners Impact, and in 2025 he completed the Convention des Entreprises pour le Climat's Climate & Business programme (agri/agro track).
current_role: Serial founder/operator in Paris; LinkedIn lists Murfy (appliance-repair startup) as current company; co-founder, Vestiaire Collective
research_notes: Paris-based and trilingual (French/Portuguese/English); also a member of The Galion Project, the French founders' network. His sustainability/circular-economy angle could fit the podcast. Role details come from a partly hidden LinkedIn profile.

name: Fanny Moizant
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Paris-based Vestiaire Collective in 2009 with five others. It became a global marketplace for authenticated pre-owned luxury fashion, a French Tech unicorn backed by Kering and Tiger Global. She spent about 16 years there as the brand's public face and a pre-loved/circular-fashion advocate, leaving in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: Vestiaire was named a French unicorn in 2020 (11th on the French Tech Next 40/120 list) and raised €178M from Kering and Tiger Global in 2021, a luxury group backing the secondhand market.
deep_cut_fact: The company began in 2009 as 'Vestiaire de Copines' ('girlfriends' wardrobe'), launching with about 3,000 pre-owned pieces from the founders' friends and family; it was renamed Vestiaire Collective in 2012.
current_role: Co-founder, Vestiaire Collective (left the company in January 2026; next move not announced)
research_notes: Left Vestiaire in Jan 2026 after an organisational change she said she didn't choose (Maddyness). Treat it neutrally and don't present her as a current exec. She announced her exit on LinkedIn, which is likely her most active channel. Vestiaire's site publishes no press email. A circular-economy/sustainability angle could fit.

name: Henrique Fernandes
profile: One of six co-founders of Paris-based luxury resale marketplace Vestiaire Collective (founded 2009 as 'Vestiaire de Copines' with Fanny Moizant, Sophie Hersan, Sebastien Fabre, Alexandre Cognard and Christian Jorge), where he headed logistics. Very little public information exists on his later activities.
interesting_fact: Vestiaire Collective began life as 'Vestiaire de Copines' (a 'girlfriends' wardrobe'), later growing into a global pre-owned luxury platform backed by Kering.
current_role: Historic co-founder (logistics) of Vestiaire Collective; current role unknown
research_notes: Extremely private; no personal web presence found. FrenchWeb lists him as 'cofondateur historique, logistique' (https://www.frenchweb.fr/henrique-fernandes). Name is common, so identity beyond the co-founder listing is uncertain. Route via Vestiaire Collective press office or LinkedIn.

name: Sebastien Fabre
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Vestiaire Collective (2009), the Paris-based marketplace for authenticated pre-owned luxury fashion, and was its CEO/chairman for nearly a decade until Max Bittner took over in January 2019. Vestiaire later reached a $1.7B+ valuation; Fabre, a former ReSee board member, became ReSee's CEO in late 2023 to drive international expansion.
interesting_fact: He has stayed in second-hand luxury for 15 years: after building Vestiaire Collective he took over ReSee, a curated vintage luxury marketplace, in its 10th-anniversary year.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming ReSee's CEO he sat on its board, and he joined to work alongside its founders Sofia Bernardin and Sabrina Marshall.
current_role: CEO, ReSee (Paris luxury resale marketplace), since Dec 2023
research_notes: Appeared on French podcast 'En Orbite' (#21) about building Vestiaire: https://podcast.ausha.co/ovny-media/en-orbite-21-sebastien-fabre-vestiaire-collective-batir-une-licorne-qui-change-nos-usages

name: Sophie Hersan
profile: French co-founder of Vestiaire Collective, the Paris-born luxury resale marketplace launched in 2009 by six partners including Fanny Moizant. As fashion director she shapes curation and authentication standards; the company reached unicorn status in 2021. After Moizant's January 2026 exit she is reported as the remaining original co-founder still at the company.
interesting_fact: Vestiaire Collective was conceived in a small Parisian apartment by Hersan and five partners in 2009 as a reaction to fashion consumers 'buying more and wearing less'.
deep_cut_fact: Born and raised in France's Champagne region, she earned a degree in economic science before switching to fashion, and grew up idolizing Azzedine Alaia, Claude Montana, Thierry Mugler and Karl Lagerfeld.
current_role: Co-founder and Fashion Director, Vestiaire Collective
research_notes: Media-friendly on sustainability/circular fashion topics (frequent interviews). No dedicated press email found on Vestiaire's site.

name: Runik Mehrotra
profile: Detroit-area math prodigy who co-founded Vise, an AI-driven portfolio management platform for financial advisors, with Samir Vasavada; the pair raised from Sequoia, Founders Fund and Ribbit while still teenagers and reached a ~$1B valuation. He oversees the AI models behind portfolio construction; Vise passed $15B in platform assets in 2025.
interesting_fact: He and Vasavada met at 13 at a Northwestern University summer research program; before Vise they ran an AI consultancy that was paid $700 an hour to teach finance 'experts' about AI.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining his edge, he told TechCrunch: 'what underlies AI is math'. He also called asset management 'an unsexy industry that makes all of the money in finance.'
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Vise (per April 2025 release; also described as co-head/CIO)
research_notes: Co-founder Samir Vasavada is the more public face of Vise. No published press email found. Mehrotra's title has varied (CTO in 2019, later CIO, Co-CEO in 2025).

name: Samir Vasavada
profile: Co-founded Vise in 2016 with Runik Mehrotra while both were teenagers; Vise is an SEC-registered AI investment platform that builds, manages and explains personalised portfolios (direct indexing, models, tax-loss harvesting) for financial advisers. It reached a $1B valuation in 2021; Vasavada now co-heads the company from NYC.
interesting_fact: Flatiron Health founders Nat Turner and Zach Weinberg wrote Vise's first $100K check, and Founders Fund co-led its $2M seed.
deep_cut_fact: Vise's origin story: when Runik went to UPenn, Samir moved onto his dorm floor and refused to leave until Runik dropped out; Runik's parents agreed only if they first raised $1M - which they did.
current_role: Co-founder and Co-Head of Vise (New York)
research_notes: Team page lists him as 'Co-Head of Vise' alongside co-founder Runik Mehrotra. No published press email found; vise.com/press page is the media entry point.

name: Ryan Wong
profile: Vancouver-based business-intelligence veteran who co-founded Visier (2010), the people-analytics / 'Workforce AI' software company valued at $1B+. Before Visier he spent 20+ years in BI at Crystal Decisions, Business Objects and SAP, ending as VP Engineering for SAP BusinessObjects. Visier now pitches AI talent agents built on enterprise workforce data.
interesting_fact: Visier's leadership grew out of the Crystal Reports lineage: Wong rode Crystal Decisions through its acquisition by Business Objects and then SAP, before co-founding Visier to apply analytics to HR/workforce data.
deep_cut_fact: Wong was the original author and Chief Software Architect of the Crystal Enterprise platform, the server product behind Crystal Reports' enterprise reporting business.
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, Visier (Vancouver)
public_contact: pr_agency: Walker Sands - visierpr@walkersands.com | contact_form: https://www.visier.com/contact-us/
research_notes: Technical founder; data/AI angle fits the podcast. Common name - target Visier's Ryan Wong (Vancouver).

name: Alexander Zosel
profile: German serial entrepreneur (civil-engineering studies) who co-founded e-volo/Volocopter in Karlsruhe in 2011 with Stephan Wolf, pioneering electric multicopter air taxis and serving in roles including managing director and technical/marketing lead. Volocopter raised hundreds of millions, then filed for insolvency in Dec 2024; its assets were bought by Wanfeng's Diamond Aircraft in March 2025.
interesting_fact: On 30 March 2016 Zosel personally piloted the first manned flight of the 18-rotor Volocopter VC200, saying: 'It is definitely a sublime feeling to lift off, fly the first few meters.'
deep_cut_fact: In 1981, aged 15, he and friends built one of Germany's first skateboard halfpipes; he developed his first patent while still a civil-engineering student.
current_role: Co-founder of Volocopter (eVTOL air-taxi pioneer, Bruchsal); current role unconfirmed after Volocopter's 2025 acquisition by Diamond Aircraft
research_notes: Current activities after the Volocopter insolvency/Diamond takeover are undocumented; avoid dwelling on the insolvency. Has given interviews (tech.eu, dronebelow, re:publica 2018 speaker). No published personal or office contact found.

name: Stephan Wolf
profile: German industrial-automation software specialist who co-founded Volocopter (originally e-volo) in Karlsruhe in 2011 with Alexander Zosel and Thomas Senkel. Volocopter pioneered electric multicopter air taxis and reached a ~$2B valuation, but filed for insolvency in December 2024 and was acquired in 2025 by Diamond Aircraft (owned by China's Wanfeng).
interesting_fact: Volocopter's first prototype, the VC1, was essentially a seat on a yoga ball with 16 electric rotors; its 90-second flight on 21 Oct 2011 is credited as the world's first crewed all-electric multicopter flight.
deep_cut_fact: The Volocopter idea was Wolf's: in 2010, after being struck by how stable a small consumer quadcopter was, he did his own calculations on scaling it up to carry people and then pitched the project to his childhood friend Alex Zosel, a hobby pilot and paragliding instructor.
current_role: Co-founder of Volocopter (Bruchsal, Germany); current role not publicly documented
research_notes: Very low public profile; no current role, personal site or social accounts found. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source (no reports of death). Volocopter no longer independent, so the company press office is not a reliable route to him.

name: Chris Van Pelt
profile: Chris Van Pelt co-founded CrowdFlower (later Figure Eight, sold to Appen for $300m in 2019) with Lukas Biewald, then Weights & Biases in 2017 with Biewald and Shawn Lewis. W&B's experiment-tracking platform is used by OpenAI, NVIDIA and others; CoreWeave acquired it for about $1.7B in 2025, and he remains as co-founder.
interesting_fact: Weights & Biases became the standard experiment-tracking tool at frontier AI labs, and its 2025 sale to GPU cloud provider CoreWeave tied ML developer tooling directly to data-centre compute.
deep_cut_fact: He built OpenUI as a side project: an open-source tool that lets you describe a UI in plain English and watch it render live, then convert it to React, Svelte or Web Components. Its README jokingly calls it 'like v0 but open source and not as polished', and it passed about 20k GitHub stars.
current_role: Co-founder (and CIO / CISO-type roles), Weights & Biases, now part of CoreWeave
public_contact: x: https://x.com/vanpelt | press_email: press@coreweave.com | podcast: Guest appearances: Learning from Machine Learning #9 (2024), ThursdAI (May 2024), Software Engineering Daily (2023)
research_notes: Approachable, engineer-minded founder who does podcasts often; X @vanpelt is the most direct public channel. He says: 'My title is co-founder really at the end of the day.' Since the acquisition, press for W&B goes through CoreWeave (press@coreweave.com). Strong data-centre/AI angle.

name: Lukas Biewald
education: Cambridge Rindge and Latin School; Stanford University
profile: Two-time AI founder. After Stanford and Yahoo search, he co-founded data-labeling firm CrowdFlower in 2007 (later Figure Eight, sold to Appen in 2019). In 2017 he co-founded ML experiment-tracking platform Weights & Biases. CoreWeave acquired W&B in 2025, and he now leads AI initiatives at the GPU cloud.
interesting_fact: His companies tackled two successive bottlenecks of practical ML: getting labelled training data (CrowdFlower/Figure Eight) and making model development reproducible (W&B). W&B now sits inside one of the largest AI data-center operators, CoreWeave.
deep_cut_fact: W&B's first product began as an experiment-tracking tool built to help train models at OpenAI. Biewald had gone back to hands-on deep learning and spent time at OpenAI before starting the company.
current_role: SVP of AI Initiatives at CoreWeave and General Manager/co-founder of Weights & Biases (acquired by CoreWeave, May 2025); Xometry board member
public_contact: podcast: Gradient Dissent (hosted by Lukas Biewald) https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id1504567418 | x: https://x.com/weights_biases (company) | official_website: https://wandb.ai | https://x.com/l2k
research_notes: Very accessible: he hosts his own AI interview podcast, Gradient Dissent, so a podcast-swap or guest invite is a natural angle. Now at CoreWeave, which is directly relevant to a data-center podcast. No personal email published; reach him via W&B/CoreWeave or the podcast.

name: Shawn Lewis
profile: Shawn Lewis, a former Google engineer, co-founded Weights & Biases in 2017 with Lukas Biewald and Chris Van Pelt to build developer tools for machine learning, starting with experiment tracking used at OpenAI. W&B grew into a leading MLOps platform and was acquired by AI cloud provider CoreWeave (deal closed May 2025, reportedly ~$1.7B); he remains with the company.
interesting_fact: W&B's first product was an experiment-tracking tool developed to help build models at OpenAI; it grew into an end-to-end platform used by millions of ML practitioners and now sits inside CoreWeave's AI cloud.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 2006 on Google's platforms team, which built Google's data-center infrastructure and the software that ran it, and he built internal tools to let colleagues analyze that data (Gradient Dissent podcast).
current_role: Co-founder (CTO / distinguished engineer), Weights & Biases, now part of CoreWeave
research_notes: Great data-center angle (Google platforms team -> CoreWeave AI cloud). Lower public profile than CEO Lukas Biewald; exact current title varies by source (CTO vs distinguished engineer). Best route likely via CoreWeave/W&B press; no personal channels verified.

name: Ali Javid
profile: Co-founder and CEO of Wrapbook (founded March 2018), a payroll, accounting and AP platform for film, TV and commercial productions that hit a ~$1B valuation after a $100M Series B in Nov 2021. He is now repositioning it as an AI platform that reads invoices, updates the general ledger and answers finance questions in plain English. Previously VP of Business Development at Body Labs (acquired by Amazon in 2017).
interesting_fact: The company is named after the physical binder of onboarding, payroll documents and receipts that gets assembled at the end of every production - the 'wrap book' - which Wrapbook set out to replace.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he was VP of Business Development at Body Labs, a 3D body-modelling AI startup bought by Amazon in 2017; he holds a BBA from the University of Washington and an MBA from NYU Stern.
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Wrapbook
research_notes: Speaker at 2026 AICP Week (commercial production industry). Co-founders: Naysawn Naji, Hesham El-Nahhas, Cameron Woodward. No published press email found.

name: Cameron Woodward
profile: Former owner of the boutique commercial production house Sprinkle Lab who experienced production-payroll pain first-hand, then co-founded Wrapbook in 2018 with CEO Ali Javid, Hesham El-Nahhas and Naysawn Naji. Wrapbook, backed by investors including Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, handles payroll, insurance and accounting for productions and reached a $1B valuation.
interesting_fact: He described Wrapbook as 'built as a tech company that offers a payroll service rather than a payroll service' with software bolted on, with 100+ features for crews and productions.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he ran the boutique commercial production house Sprinkle Lab, where he learned the 'prickly problems' of paying crews that inspired the company.
current_role: Co-founder (and CMO per 2022 trade press) of Wrapbook, the production payroll/finance platform for film and TV; current title not confirmed
research_notes: Ali Javid is Wrapbook's CEO; Woodward is lower-profile. A third-party profile (standout.work) says he directed the KONY2012 marketing campaign - unverified, use cautiously. No published press email; LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Hesham El Nahhas
profile: Hesham El-Nahhas is one of four co-founders (with Ali Javid, Cameron Woodward and Naysawn Naji) of Wrapbook, founded in 2018 to digitise payroll, onboarding and insurance for film, TV and commercial productions. Wrapbook raised a $27M Series A led by a16z and a $100M Series B led by Tiger Global in Nov 2021 at a $1B valuation.
interesting_fact: Wrapbook's backers include Hollywood figures Jeffrey Katzenberg (WndrCo) and CAA co-founder Michael Ovitz; a16z said at its Series A the company was growing revenue about 7x year-over-year.
current_role: Co-founder, Wrapbook (listed as Co-Founder & Chief People Officer as of the 2021 Series B; current title unconfirmed)
research_notes: Spelled El-Nahhas in company materials. Very low individual public profile; CEO Ali Javid is the company's public face. Wrapbook press center (https://www.wrapbook.com/press) lists no press email.

name: Naysawn Naji
profile: Product-focused fintech founder who co-founded Wrapbook in 2018 with Hesham El-Nahhas, Ali Javid (CEO) and Cameron Woodward. Wrapbook, a payroll and onboarding platform for film/TV/commercial productions, raised a $100M Series B at a $1B valuation in 2021 (Tiger Global, a16z). Naji left in 2022 and moved on to construction software (Buildpal).
interesting_fact: The Wrapbook idea started at a New York tech open-mic, where an actor demoed an app she had built to help actors book gigs; he was unimpressed until he learned it had 4,000 paying users, convincing him media production was ripe for better software.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he was co-founder and CPO of Arcus, a Latin America-focused bill-payment API, where he and future co-founder Hesham El-Nahhas had lunch together 'every day for four years'; one early Wrapbook check came blind from a friend of his at Google.
current_role: Co-founder and former CPO of Wrapbook (left 2022); reportedly founded Buildpal, a scheduling tool for general contractors
research_notes: Low public profile; no published contact found. Buildpal role comes from Contrary Research (2024) and could not be independently confirmed. Wrapbook's later 2024 round was at $750M.

name: Bo Chen
profile: UC Berkeley EECS graduate (2014) who briefly worked at Brandcast and Ripple before co-founding Xendit in 2015 with fellow Berkeley alum Moses Lo (plus Tessa Wijaya and Juan Gonzalez). Xendit builds payment rails across Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, and was valued at ~$3B after its 2022 Series D.
interesting_fact: Xendit was the first Indonesian tech startup accepted into Y Combinator (S15 batch) and the first B2B payments company in Indonesia to reach unicorn status; Chen founded it at 23.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated early from Berkeley to get into startups faster, and his official festival bio notes he likes creating original rap performances for Xendit company offsites; he spoke at Singapore FinTech Festival 2023 on 'Become a Cockroach: Survive to Thrive.'
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Xendit (Southeast Asian payments infrastructure)
research_notes: CEO Moses Lo is the main public face. Xendit press releases list PR staff contacts (e.g., Ami Windarti, PR & Communications; a 2022 Series D release listed ami@xendit.co) - not independently re-verified, check newest release on xendit.co newsroom.

name: Juan Gonzalez
profile: Software engineer who co-founded Jakarta-based payments infrastructure company Xendit in 2015 with Moses Lo, Tessa Wijaya and Bo Chen; the company went through Y Combinator (Summer 2015). Xendit started as a consumer fintech app before pivoting to payment APIs for businesses across Southeast Asia, reaching unicorn status in 2021.
interesting_fact: Xendit was part of Y Combinator's Summer 2015 batch and became a unicorn in 2021 after a $150M round led by Tiger Global.
deep_cut_fact: Xendit was originally launched in 2015 as a consumer-focused fintech before the founders pivoted to B2B payment infrastructure.
current_role: Co-founder, Xendit (listed by Y Combinator as Founder/Principal Software Engineer)
research_notes: Very low public profile and common name - verify any LinkedIn match against Xendit. CEO Moses Lo is the public face.

name: Moses Lo
profile: Australian-born founder (UNSW, UC Berkeley MBA; ex-BCG and Amazon) who co-founded Xendit in 2015; it went through Y Combinator S15 and became the first YC unicorn from Indonesia. Xendit provides payment APIs across Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, and in Nov 2025 launched a Global Account product at the Singapore FinTech Festival.
interesting_fact: Xendit was among the first five Southeast Asian companies accepted into Y Combinator, and became Indonesia's first YC unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: At Radford College in Canberra (Class of 2005) he won debating tournaments and represented Australia at Model United Nations; his advice to students is that 'marks are less important than soft skills.'
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Xendit Group (Southeast Asian payments infrastructure, Jakarta)
research_notes: Accessible, frequent podcast/conference speaker (Money20/20 Asia). Press email is the named PR & Communications contact on Xendit's Nov 2025 release; based in Jakarta.

name: Tessa Wijaya
profile: Indonesian co-founder and COO of Xendit, the Jakarta-based payments infrastructure company (Y Combinator alum, valued ~$3B). A former private-equity analyst, she oversees operations, partnerships, compliance and government relations, and is often cited as Indonesia's first female unicorn founder.
interesting_fact: She joined Xendit in 2016 after being introduced via Y Combinator to the UC Berkeley founders working on payments, having spotted the missing payment rails while working with early-stage startups in private equity.
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in a small Indonesian town raised by her grandmother, who ran a small food business, and landed her first PE analyst job in Jakarta with no finance background, teaching herself finance on her own time.
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Xendit (also reported as CEO of Xendit Thailand)
research_notes: Frequent podcast/conference speaker. Xendit press releases have named Ami Windarti (PR & Comms) as media contact; I could not verify the address directly.

name: Alexis Angot
profile: French finance executive (ESSEC) who co-founded Ÿnsect in Paris in 2011 with Antoine Hubert, Jean-Gabriel Levon and Fabrice Berro. Ÿnsect farmed mealworms for animal-feed protein and fertilizer, raised about €600M and reached unicorn status; Angot served as CFO before stepping down. The company was placed in judicial liquidation in December 2025.
interesting_fact: Ÿnsect was founded by four scientists and environmental activists, became the second company in the world authorised (by ANSES, 2020) to market a natural insect-based fertilizer, and earned B Corp certification in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In episode #8 of the 'Tomorrow Now' podcast (Oct 2023), billed as 'when the financier becomes an industry builder', he discussed taking Ÿnsect from idea to industrial company, why he chose to leave the CFO role, and how a board should work best.
current_role: Co-founder and former CFO of Ÿnsect; current role not found in public sources
research_notes: Sensitive: Ÿnsect went into safeguard (2024) and liquidation (Dec 2025) amid political criticism of public funding - avoid in outreach. No published contact found; LinkedIn would be the likely route but was not verified.

name: Antoine Hubert
education: AgroParisTech, Paris-Saclay University; National Institute of Higher Education For Agriculture, Food And The Environment
profile: French agricultural engineer (AgroParisTech) who co-founded Ynsect in 2011 with three partners to farm mealworms for animal feed, fertiliser and food protein; it raised over $425M and joined France's Next40. He handed the CEO role to Shankar Krishnamoorthy in 2023 and stayed as an executive VP; Wikipedia lists Ynsect as defunct since Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: MIT Technology Review named him a 2015 Innovator Under 35 for developing 'the first insect biorefinery in the world'; Ynsect chose the mealworm beetle (Tenebrio molitor) as 'nocturnal, flightless' and very high in protein and chitin.
deep_cut_fact: Hubert has compared the insect industry to Norway's aquaculture boom 40 years earlier: 'We are now the same point in the insect industry.' Ynsect's four products from mealworms were protein flour, oil, chitin/chitosan and frass fertiliser.
current_role: Co-founder of Ynsect (insect-protein company, now defunct); current role not verified
research_notes: Ynsect ceased operations (Wikipedia: defunct 1 Dec 2025) - avoid framing outreach around company performance. Current activities unknown; no published contact found. Ynsect page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%9Cnsect

name: Fabrice Berro
profile: Ensimag-trained engineer who co-founded Ynsect in 2011 with Antoine Hubert, Jean-Gabriel Levon and Alexis Angot. The French company farmed mealworm beetles for insect protein and fertilizer, raised about EUR 600M and became a unicorn, but entered judicial reorganization in March 2025 and was liquidated by the Evry commercial court on 1 Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Ynsect launched Ynfabre, described as the first industrial genomic-selection program applied to large-scale insect farming (beetle genetics), and broke ground on a giant vertical insect farm near Amiens.
deep_cut_fact: Ynsect's four founders were described as scientists and environmental activists; Berro was the Ensimag engineering graduate among them, and held the company's data role.
current_role: Co-founder of Ynsect (former Director-Data); no current position found
research_notes: Very low public profile; no interviews, social accounts or contacts found. Ynsect was liquidated Dec 2025, so company channels no longer exist; MarketScreener/Zonebourse show no current position. Sensitive topic: avoid leading with Ynsect's collapse.

name: Jean-Gabriel Levon
profile: Jean-Gabriel Levon (HEC Paris, École Polytechnique) co-founded Ÿnsect in Paris in 2011 with Antoine Hubert, Fabrice Berro and Alexis Angot. Ÿnsect farmed mealworms for animal-feed protein and fertilizer, raised about €600M and reached unicorn valuation. After safeguard and reorganisation proceedings, the Évry commercial court ordered its liquidation on 1 December 2025.
interesting_fact: In June 2020 Ÿnsect's insect-based fertilizer 'Ynfrass' received ANSES market approval, which Wikipedia describes as the first market approval in the world for a natural insect-based fertilizer.
deep_cut_fact: Ÿnsect was started in 2011 by four young scientists and environmental activists. Levon was the HEC/Polytechnique graduate among them, and an early 2013 Le Parisien headline described the startup as wanting to 'feed the planet with flies'.
current_role: Co-founder of Ÿnsect (insect protein; company in judicial liquidation since 1 Dec 2025). Previously listed as Chief Impact Officer and director. Current role unknown.
research_notes: Sensitive: Ÿnsect was liquidated in December 2025 amid political criticism over about €148M of public funding, so avoid it as a hook. His current activity was not found (alive marked unknown, with no reports otherwise). Very low public profile; the 'Chief Impact Officer' title comes only from an aggregator.

name: Dave Nicholson
profile: David Nicholson co-founded Zopa, the UK's first peer-to-peer lender and now a digital bank, in 2004-05 with fellow ex-Egg colleagues James Alexander and Richard Duvall, plus Giles Andrews and Tim Parlett. He left Zopa in 2007. In 2013 he co-founded the mobile payments and loyalty fintech Yoyo Wallet in London with Michael Rolph and Alain Falys.
interesting_fact: Zopa co-founder Giles Andrews has credited Nicholson with coming up with the idea that became Zopa. Nicholson came from a group of former consultants who had left Egg, the UK's first online bank.
deep_cut_fact: Zopa was pitched internally as an 'eBay for money' by its three ex-Egg co-founders, Nicholson, James Alexander and Richard Duvall, before they brought in Giles Andrews to raise money.
current_role: Serial fintech founder and venture builder (London); listed as Chief Product Officer at Agricarbon (unverified profile)
research_notes: He left Zopa in 2007 (https://alternativecreditinvestor.com/2020/04/28/where-are-they-now-the-p2p-lending-giants-still-run-by-their-founding-members/), so contact via Zopa is not appropriate. His current role at Agricarbon comes from an unverified theorg.com profile. No published contact found; LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Giles Andrews
profile: British fintech pioneer who in 2004 co-founded Zopa, the world's first online peer-to-peer lending platform (now a UK digital bank), serving as CEO 2007-2015 and chairman 2015-2019. He now sits on bank boards (C. Hoare & Co., Bank of Ireland), chairs car marketplace carwow and previously chaired MarketFinance. OBE for services to financial services.
interesting_fact: Before fintech he spent a decade in the motor industry, co-founding Caverdale in 1992 and growing it into a GBP250m-turnover motor retailer sold in 1997 - a car link that resurfaces in his chairmanship of carwow.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Psychology at Christ Church, Oxford, before an INSEAD MBA; after INSEAD his consultancy clients included Tesco and Tesco Personal Finance. He likes to 'search for the sun in the microclimate of the Isle of Wight'.
current_role: Senior Independent Director, C. Hoare & Co.; NED Bank of Ireland Group; chair, carwow
public_contact: pr_agency: Champions Speakers / CSA speaker booking (speakers.co.uk enquiry form)
research_notes: No longer on Zopa's board page (2026). Named FinTech Leader of the Year at the 2016 FinTech Innovation Awards. Best route likely via speaker bureau or LinkedIn.

name: James Alexander
profile: Former LEK consultant (worked on Co-operative Bank's online bank Smile) and Egg strategy director who co-founded Zopa in 2005, the world's first peer-to-peer lender, later serving as its CEO and a board director before leaving. He now advises boards on foresight, strategy and innovation via Future Agenda, chairs Environmental Finance and advises fintechs such as Seedrs and LandBay.
