The company built RummyCircle and fantasy-sports app My11Circle, applying data science to gaming, and reached a $2.5B valuation backed by Tiger Global; it also runs a venture arm and a foundation.
interesting_fact: Pandya describes Games24x7 as 'a technology platform, gaming is just incidental' - the company brands itself around 'The Science of Gaming' and serves 120M+ players.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Trivikraman Thampy met while studying economics at New York University and bonded over a shared passion for online games; Pandya returned to India in 2006 to start the company. He also holds an electrical and computer engineering degree from Purdue.
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Games24x7 (Mumbai)
research_notes: India's 2025 online-gaming law banned real-money games, forcing a major business pivot for Games24x7 - context worth knowing but handle tactfully. Purdue degree comes from a secondary profile (theofficialboard).

name: Trivikraman Thampy
profile: IIT Bombay engineer with an NYU economics PhD who co-founded Games24x7 in 2006 with fellow NYU alumnus Bhavin Pandya. The company built RummyCircle and fantasy-sports app My11Circle into one of India's largest online skill-gaming businesses, backed by Tiger Global and Malabar; it also runs an investment arm, Games24x7 Ventures.
interesting_fact: He says Games24x7 turned profitable within 18 months of starting operations, and that RummyCircle was profitable by 2012 even though it took years to convince investors that skill gaming differed from gambling.
deep_cut_fact: Goes by 'Vikram'. He founded Games24x7 on a 'science of gaming' ethos, applying the behavioral economics from his NYU economics PhD (completed 2008) to model player behavior and personalize gameplay.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Games24x7 (Mumbai)
research_notes: Formerly styled Co-CEO alongside Bhavin Pandya; recent releases call him co-founder & CEO. Real-money gaming in India faced heavy regulatory change in 2025, so check the business's current state before outreach. No published press email found.

name: James Ferguson
profile: Australian co-founder, with Robbie Ferguson and Alex Connolly, of Fuel Games (2018), renamed Immutable in 2019. Immutable built Gods Unchained, the Immutable X Ethereum Layer-2 (with StarkWare) and now offers a game-growth suite (Passport, attribution, wishlist and player-engagement tools) used by 800+ games; it was valued at $3.5B after a $200M Temasek-led round in 2022.
interesting_fact: The company's first product, released in February 2018, was Etherbots, a robot-battling blockchain game on Ethereum, followed by the Gods Unchained trading-card game pre-sale in July 2018.
current_role: Co-founder, Immutable (Sydney-based gaming/blockchain company); exact current title not confirmed
research_notes: Lower public profile than brother/co-founder Robbie Ferguson (Immutable's public face); 'James Ferguson' is a common name, so check context. Search budget ran out before finding a sourced deep-cut fact or personal channel.

name: Robbie Ferguson
profile: Australian entrepreneur who co-founded Immutable (originally Fuel Games, 2018) with brother James and Alex Connolly; it became a leading web3 gaming platform (Immutable X/zkEVM) valued at ~$2B+ (Hurun). Became the youngest person on the AFR Rich List at 25. Previously worked at KPMG Australia.
interesting_fact: In 2017-18 the brothers built Etherbots, billed as the world's first multiplayer competitive blockchain game, which brought in $1M in its first week.
deep_cut_fact: He finished top of his school, then started a computer science/law double degree at the University of Sydney (unfinished), where he met Immutable CTO Alex Connolly; he and James spent 'countless hours' on RuneScape and League of Legends as kids.
current_role: Co-founder & President, Immutable (Sydney)
research_notes: Very active public speaker and on X/podcasts on web3 gaming; verify his X handle from Immutable's site before use.

name: Anthony Welters
profile: Harlem-raised lawyer turned healthcare entrepreneur (b. 1955) who founded Medicaid managed-care firm AmeriChoice in 1989, sold it to UnitedHealth Group and rose to EVP/Office of the CEO there. He co-founded and chairs Somatus, a value-based kidney-care company valued at $2.5B, and since 2014 chairs BlackIvy, which builds food, housing, healthcare and logistics businesses in Sub-Saharan Africa.
interesting_fact: Before AmeriChoice he started several businesses, from manufacturing to restaurant franchises, which all failed: 'You have to be prepared to accept failure to have success.' His break came in 1988 when he won Philadelphia's Medicaid-management contract, then Pennsylvania's largest ever.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he shined shoes under the elevated subway and swept a barbershop floor for tips; he skipped fourth grade, got into Stuyvesant, finished Manhattanville College in under three years, and earned his NYU law degree at 22. He and his wife Bea founded Camp Dogwood Summer Academy for low-income kids in Virginia's Blue Ridge.
current_role: Executive Chairman, BlackIvy Group; Co-Founder & Chairman, Somatus
public_contact: office_email: info@blackivygroup.com (BlackIvy Group, general) | official_website: https://blackivygroup.com
research_notes: Horatio Alger Award 1998; NYU Law lobby named for him; vice chair NYU trustees; AnBryce Scholarship founder. Avoid the Clarence Thomas RV-loan story (on Wikipedia). Somatus site blocks automated access; no press email captured.

name: Ikenna Okezie
profile: Nigerian-born physician-executive (Yale economics BA; Harvard MD/MBA) who led DaVita Kidney Care's Mid-Atlantic market (2010-15) before co-founding Somatus in 2016 with investor Anthony Welters. Somatus manages kidney (and now heart) care for 500,000+ patients across all 50 states and was valued at about $2.5B after a $325M Series E in 2022.
interesting_fact: He started Somatus because he 'wanted to start a business that focused on delaying kidney disease progression and keeping people as healthy as possible', rather than only treating patients once they reach dialysis.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Nigeria and raised in Detroit and Chicago, he studied economics at Yale before earning a dual MD/MBA at Harvard with concentrations in finance and entrepreneurship; his father and elder brother are also physicians.
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and director, Somatus (value-based kidney care, Tysons/McLean, Virginia)
public_contact: press_email: media@somatus.com (listed on syndicated Somatus press releases; not confirmed on somatus.com)
research_notes: Fairly media-friendly (CNBC Disruptor 50 profile, Nigerian press). Sits on boards of the National Kidney Foundation/ASN per profiles. Physician-father detail is from Nairametrics profile (https://nairametrics.com/2024/05/07/meet-ikenna-okezie-brain-behind-2-5-billion-kidney-care-company-in-united-states/).

name: Ravi Saraogi
profile: Indian entrepreneur who co-founded Uniphore with college batchmate Umesh Sachdev in 2008 at IIT Madras's Rural Technology & Business Incubator. Uniphore grew from Indian-language speech recognition for rural users into an enterprise conversational/business-AI platform, raising $400M in 2022 at a $2.5B valuation; Saraogi leads APAC sales and delivery from Singapore.
interesting_fact: Uniphore's first customer was Thomson Reuters' Reuters Market Light farmer-information service: pilots showed low rural literacy made SMS ineffective, so the team built voice-based systems in Indian languages instead.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006, as batchmates at Jaypee Institute of Information Technology in Noida, he and Sachdev first experimented with a mobile anti-theft security product and founded Singularis Technologies, turning down software-services job offers to pursue it.
current_role: Co-Founder & President APAC, Uniphore (Singapore-based)
research_notes: Education is reported inconsistently (Uniphore bio: MSc Mathematics, Delhi University; other profiles: B.Tech IT, Jaypee). CEO Umesh Sachdev is the company's main public face. No published press email found on Uniphore's site.

name: Umesh Sachdev
profile: Indian-born tech entrepreneur who co-founded Uniphore with college friend Ravi Saraogi in 2008 in IIT Madras's rural-tech incubator, initially building multilingual speech recognition for rural Indian phone users. Uniphore became an enterprise conversational-AI and now 'business AI' platform valued at $2.5B in 2022, with backers incl. NVIDIA, AMD and Snowflake in a 2025 round.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he was the only Indian on TIME's list of 10 'Next Generation Leaders', for 'building a phone that can understand almost any language'.
deep_cut_fact: As Jaypee Institute (Noida) IT students in 2006, he and Saraogi first built a mobile-theft security product (Singularis Technologies, to track lost phones); it led IIT Madras professor Ashok Jhunjhunwala to invite them into IIT-M's Rural Technology and Business Incubator.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Uniphore (Palo Alto / Chennai)
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.uniphore.com/contact-us/ | official_website: https://www.uniphore.com/author/usachdev/ (his author page on Uniphore blog)
research_notes: Also named MIT Tech Review Innovator Under 35 (India). AI/enterprise-data angle fits podcast; Uniphore's 2025 round included NVIDIA and AMD (verify specifics).

name: Harry O'Hanley
profile: MIT-trained engineer and ex-SpaceX Falcon 9 engineer who co-founded small-satellite launcher ABL Space Systems with Dan Piemont in 2017; ABL hit a $1.3B valuation after a $170M round in 2021, backed by T. Rowe Price, Fidelity, Venrock and Lockheed Martin. In late 2024 the company pivoted to missile-defense test vehicles and was renamed Long Wall (2025); he handed the CEO role to Piemont and stayed on as an executive.
interesting_fact: The renamed company takes its name from the Long Walls of ancient Athens; it now builds RSX, a launch vehicle for missile-defense flight testing and threat replication, plus Ironwood, a rapidly deployable ground system.
deep_cut_fact: Besides his MIT mechanical engineering degree he holds an MIT master's in Nuclear Science and Engineering; at SpaceX his roles included on-console launch operations. He is a 2003 alumnus of Shore Country Day School in Beverly, Massachusetts.
current_role: Co-founder and executive (without portfolio), Long Wall (formerly ABL Space Systems); was CEO until Nov 2024
research_notes: Hurun lists ABL; the company is now Long Wall (missile defense / hypersonic test vehicles, Long Beach CA), CEO Dan Piemont. No published press email. Mentor at Creative Destruction Lab space stream. Shore alumni source: https://www.shoreschool.org/news-detail?pk=1412905

name: Luke Li
profile: Tsinghua economics/applied-maths grad with a Columbia master's in financial engineering, Luke Li was a credit strategist on Morgan Stanley's Hong Kong fixed-income desk (2015-18) before co-founding crypto trading and liquidity firm Amber Group, which hit unicorn status in 2021. He runs Amber's trading business and joined the board of its listed arm Amber International in 2025.
interesting_fact: Five of Amber's six founders, including Li, worked together on Morgan Stanley's Hong Kong fixed-income floor; in 2015, all in their 20s, they started a side project running algorithmic trading on Chinese stocks and index futures before going full-time into crypto arbitrage.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a bachelor's in economics, finance and applied mathematics from Tsinghua (2013) and a master's in financial engineering from Columbia (2014), and is described as a trusted advisor to multiple leading crypto projects.
current_role: Co-founder of Amber Group (in charge of trading); Director of Nasdaq-listed Amber International Holding (AMBR) since Aug 2025
public_contact: press_email: pr@ambr.io | ir_email: ir@ambr.io | pr_agency: Paradigm Consulting (Asia): ambr@paradigmconsulting.com.hk; International Elite Capital (US): amber@iecapitalusa.com
research_notes: Common name - identity anchored by Amber International's Aug 2025 PR Newswire release. Low public profile; route via Amber International PR/IR.

name: Thomas Zhu
profile: Software engineer and the sixth co-founder of Amber Group, the Hong Kong/Singapore crypto trading and wealth-management firm started by ex-Morgan Stanley traders. While a Bloomberg developer exploring machine learning for trading, he joined their 2015 side project; Amber went full-time into crypto in 2017 and reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021 and ~$3B in 2022.
interesting_fact: Unlike his five co-founders, who sat together on Morgan Stanley's Hong Kong fixed-income trading floor, Zhu was the outsider: a Bloomberg developer working on machine learning for trading.
deep_cut_fact: Amber began in 2015 -- with the founders all in their 20s -- as a side project running algorithmic trading on Chinese stocks and index futures, before pivoting full-time to crypto arbitrage.
current_role: Co-founder (and formerly CTO), Amber Group; current role at listed successor Amber International (Nasdaq: AMBR) not confirmed
research_notes: Very low public profile. Not named in 2025-26 Amber International (AMBR) filings/releases; Michael Wu is chairman/CEO. Contacts are company-level only.

name: Tony He
profile: Hong Kong-based former Morgan Stanley fixed-income trader who co-founded crypto financial-services firm Amber Group (c. 2017) with Michael Wu, Wayne Huo, Tiantian Kullander and Luke Li. Amber reached a $3B valuation in 2022; its Amber Premium business later listed on Nasdaq as Amber International. Crunchbase lists him as a former co-founder and partner.
interesting_fact: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 (2019) alongside Amber co-founders Tiantian Kullander and Wayne Huo.
deep_cut_fact: All of Amber's co-founders, including He, started out on Morgan Stanley's fixed-income trading floor before leaving to build the company.
current_role: Co-founder (and former partner) of Amber Group; current role not confirmed
research_notes: Very low public profile (also known as Tony YuHao He; studied at Johns Hopkins per Crunchbase). Common name - verify carefully. Avoid referencing co-founder Kullander's death.

name: Wayne Huo
profile: Former Morgan Stanley FX options trader who co-founded Hong Kong crypto trading and wealth platform Amber Group in 2017 with fellow Morgan Stanley alumni; Amber became a unicorn in 2021. He served as CEO of listed affiliate Amber International (Nasdaq: AMBR) until 21 Aug 2025, when Chairman Michael Wu took over the CEO role.
interesting_fact: Amber began as a side project among Morgan Stanley Hong Kong fixed-income traders and reached a US$1B valuation in 2021, with five of its founders having worked together on the same trading floor.
deep_cut_fact: He had been in the workforce only about 18 months, as an FX options trader at Morgan Stanley, when he quit to build Amber; the firm later lured his former boss, Morgan Stanley's Asia FX derivatives head, to join.
current_role: Co-founder, Amber Group (crypto finance, Hong Kong/Singapore); former CEO of Nasdaq-listed Amber International (AMBR) until Aug 2025
research_notes: Status after Aug 2025 leadership change is unclear: one release says he also resigned as director, while a later 6-K still lists him as a non-independent director (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/amber-international-announces-leadership-changes-to-drive-growth). Crypto angle may be off-topic for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Gustavo Chamati
profile: Brazilian entrepreneur who co-founded Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest crypto exchange, with his brother Mauricio in 2013. It became the base of holding group 2TM, Brazil's first crypto unicorn after SoftBank invested $200M in 2021. Formerly CEO, he now sits on the board.
interesting_fact: 2TM grew beyond the exchange into a group including digital bank MeuBank, custody firm Bitrust, Blockchain Academy and others, though Mercado Bitcoin still drove 90%+ of revenue.
current_role: Co-founder & board member, 2TM / Mercado Bitcoin (Brazil)
research_notes: Sources disagree on whether he is still CEO or only board member. Best route likely Mercado Bitcoin press office.

name: Mauricio Chamati
profile: Brazilian technologist who co-founded Mercado Bitcoin (2013, with brother Gustavo) and its holding company 2TM, which became Brazil's first crypto unicorn (~$2.1B, 2021 SoftBank-led round). He served as Mercado Bitcoin's CTO, moved to the 2TM board in 2019, and in Oct 2025 launched Jumpad, which helps companies manage corporate AI use.
interesting_fact: Mercado Bitcoin started in 2013 when bitcoin was barely known in Brazil and grew into Latin America's largest crypto exchange.
deep_cut_fact: His new startup Jumpad launched with offices in São Paulo and Belo Horizonte, 10 beta clients and a pre-seed round (Oct 2025).
current_role: Founder & CEO, Jumpad (AI governance startup); co-founder and board member of 2TM (Mercado Bitcoin holding)
research_notes: Also linked to Gear Ventures (fintech VC). Speaker at South Summit. Avoid founder-credit dispute raised by an ex-executive.

name: Raj De Datta
profile: Princeton engineer and Harvard MBA who co-founded Bloomreach with Ashutosh Garg in 2009; the AI-driven digital commerce platform (search, personalisation, marketing automation) says it powers brands representing ~25% of US and UK retail e-commerce. Earlier he was an EIR at Mohr Davidow, a Cisco product-marketing director and a Lazard tech banker; he is also a Founder Partner at Founder Collective.
interesting_fact: He is author of the bestselling book 'The Digital Seeker', a playbook for digital teams, and has backed 20+ startups as an individual investor.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the US Tennis Association's Council for Player Development and on the board of RepresentUs, a bipartisan democracy-reform group; early in his career he was a founding team member of telecom startup FirstMark Communications.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Bloomreach (Mountain View, CA)
research_notes: Writes bylined columns (CMSWire, Total Retail) and does podcasts - receptive to thought-leadership outreach. Route via Bloomreach comms.

name: Tjeerd Brenninkmeijer
profile: Dutch entrepreneur with a Master's in Business Economics from the University of Amsterdam. He co-founded Amsterdam-based Hippo CMS and ran its marketing for 17 years, growing it from three people to a global business of more than 100. After Bloomreach (now a $2B+ commerce/marketing software company) bought Hippo in 2016, he became its CMO and later EVP for EMEA.
interesting_fact: Under his marketing leadership Hippo grew from a three-person start-up to over 100 staff, with subscription revenue up more than 50% a year. Gartner named it a 'visionary' in the Web Content Management Magic Quadrant before the Bloomreach sale.
deep_cut_fact: He has volunteered as a mentor at Startupbootcamp, the European startup accelerator.
current_role: Former EVP EMEA / CMO EMEA at Bloomreach (titles from 2019-era author bios); co-founder of Hippo CMS, which Bloomreach acquired in 2016. Current role not confirmed.
research_notes: Identity is marked uncertain on purpose. He co-founded Hippo, not Bloomreach itself (Raj De Datta and Ashutosh Garg founded Bloomreach), so Hurun's 'BloomReach founder' label is loose. He gets equity through the Hippo acquisition. He is not on Bloomreach's current leadership page, and I found no 2024-26 coverage of him. Dutch business press (MT/Sprout) has interviewed him.

name: Chris Pihl
profile: Chris Pihl is co-founder and CTO of Helion Energy, founded in 2013 with David Kirtley, George Votroubek and John Slough. Helion develops pulsed, non-ignition magneto-inertial fusion generators backed by Sam Altman, Dustin Moskovitz and Reid Hoffman. It is building the Orion fusion plant in Malaga, Washington to supply Microsoft data centers, and makes its own high-voltage pulsed-power capacitors in-house.
interesting_fact: Helion signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement, with Microsoft in 2023, a direct link between fusion and data-center power demand.
deep_cut_fact: Helion's founders met at MSNW, a small Redmond, Washington fusion-research firm with University of Washington ties, before spinning out. Pihl, a UW graduate, is one of three original founders still at the company.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
public_contact: press_email: press@helionenergy.com | official_website: https://www.helionenergy.com/about | contact_form: https://www.helionenergy.com/contact
research_notes: Low personal media profile; CEO David Kirtley is the main spokesperson. A strong fit for the energy and data-center theme. Requests should go through Helion press.

name: David Kirtley
profile: Michigan-trained nuclear, plasma and aerospace engineer who co-founded fusion company Helion in 2013. Helion holds the first fusion power-purchase agreement (with Microsoft) and began building its 50 MW Orion plant in Malaga, WA in July 2025, targeting 2028. In February 2026 its Polaris prototype showed the first private D-T fusion.
interesting_fact: Helion's Orion plant is meant to sell fusion electricity to Microsoft, a direct link between fusion and AI data-center power demand. On Lex Fridman's podcast, Kirtley described wanting a 'gigafactory' that turns out 50 MW fusion generators.
deep_cut_fact: He started in space propulsion, not power plants. Early in his career he studied beamed-microwave rocket concepts, in which a spacecraft needs no onboard fuel. Before spinning out Helion, his team worked on fusion rockets and advanced materials. He says they reused circuit topologies from space hardware for fusion.
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.helionenergy.com/contact/ (choose inquiry topic 'Press') | official_website: https://www.helionenergy.com/
research_notes: Very podcast-friendly. He has appeared on Lex Fridman #485, GeekWire's Positive Charge and Slush 2026, and is an ideal guest for the energy/data-center theme. Use Helion's press form. Company X account: @helion_energy. I found no verified personal handle.

name: George Votroubek
profile: Plasma physicist (MS, PhD University of Washington) who co-founded fusion company Helion Energy in 2013 with David Kirtley, Chris Pihl and John Slough, colleagues from MSNW in Redmond. Helion pursues pulsed field-reversed-configuration fusion, is building its Polaris prototype and Orion plant, and has raised ~$1.5B.
interesting_fact: Helion signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement with Microsoft (plus a deal with steelmaker Nucor) - a direct link between fusion and powering data centers.
deep_cut_fact: He was Principal Investigator for the program that demonstrated Helion's 'Fusion Engine' technology at one-third scale, work that grew out of the Inductive Plasmoid Accelerator experiments the founders ran before Helion existed.
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Scientist, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
research_notes: Low-profile scientist; CEO David Kirtley is Helion's public voice. Helion's contact form has a 'Press' inquiry option. Excellent fit for energy + data-center theme. Deep-cut sourced to Crunchbase bio (not a primary document).

name: John Slough
profile: Plasma physicist who cofounded Helion Energy in 2013 with David Kirtley, Chris Pihl and George Votroubek; Helion's pulsed fusion approach builds on his FRC plasmoid merging-and-compression research. He left Helion in 2018 to refocus on his research firm MSNW. His wealth reflects his Helion stake (company valued ~$5B).
interesting_fact: He is an inventor on Helion's foundational patents, including a 2011 patent on generating, heating and compressing plasmoids and recovering energy from them, and the 'Advanced D–3He fuel cycle for a pulsed fusion reactor'.
deep_cut_fact: NASA's Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) program funded his 'Fusion Driven Rocket' (2012 Phase II): magnetically driven metal liners crush a plasmoid to fusion and become the propellant, a concept meant to make crewed interplanetary travel 'common place'.
current_role: Cofounder (former) of Helion Energy; plasma physicist, MSNW LLC (Redmond, WA)
research_notes: No longer with Helion (left 2018), so Helion PR is not a route to him; reports cite disagreement over fuel choice, so avoid that topic. Very low public profile; MSNW's website was unreachable. Best approached as a fusion-science expert via academic or plasma-physics channels.

name: Gordon Wintrob
education: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
profile: MIT EECS grad Gordon Wintrob co-founded tech-driven commercial insurance brokerage Newfront in 2017 with CEO Spike Lipkin and served as CTO. WTW completed its acquisition of Newfront in January 2026 for up to $1.3B. In May 2026 WTW named Lipkin Chief AI Officer and Wintrob Head of AI Acceleration, helping colleagues embed AI tools into daily work.
interesting_fact: A year after graduating from MIT he founded StackLead (2013), which aggregated sales-lead data from across the web and was quickly acquired by LinkedIn. He then worked at LinkedIn for about three years. He met Lipkin through a friend who said: 'You're the only two people I know interested in insurance.'
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Los Angeles he was 'basically an IT support guy' for his neighbors, setting up Wi-Fi and installing software. As an MIT undergrad he worked on a money-transfer system for developing countries, and his team was the only undergraduate team to reach the final round of the MIT $100K Entrepreneurship Competition.
current_role: Head of AI Acceleration, WTW (Willis Towers Watson), since May 2026; Newfront co-founder and former CTO
research_notes: Appears on podcasts (Software Engineering Daily; 'The Blind Ambition' with Jack Kelly), so he is receptive to podcast formats. Now inside WTW, so outreach may go through WTW media relations (wtwco.com). Role source: riskandinsurance.com, May 1, 2026.

name: Spike Lipkin
profile: Spike Lipkin was a Blackstone investor on the startup team behind Invitation Homes, then one of Opendoor's first employees. In 2017 he co-founded Newfront, a San Francisco insurance brokerage built on its own technology covering business insurance and employee benefits. WTW agreed to buy Newfront in December 2025 and completed the roughly $1.3bn acquisition in January 2026; Lipkin joined WTW.
interesting_fact: WTW's acquisition of Newfront was reported at about $1.3bn including contingent consideration. Lipkin built the tech-enabled broker from a 2017 start into one of the largest venture-backed deals in insurance brokerage.
deep_cut_fact: Before insurance he was on Blackstone's startup team that built Invitation Homes into the largest US owner of single-family rental homes. He then joined Opendoor when it had five people. Both jobs exposed him firsthand to how painful buying insurance was.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Newfront, now part of WTW after WTW completed the acquisition in January 2026. At WTW he focuses on integration, client development, talent acquisition and technology.
research_notes: Now inside WTW, a public company, so media requests likely route through WTW media relations (contact not verified this session). He has appeared on podcasts (Category Visionaries, June 2023). Insurance Business named him a 2019 Young Gun at age 31.

name: Dileep Thazhmon
profile: Serial entrepreneur and Stanford GSB graduate who co-founded and ran ad-tech firm PowerInbox (later Jeeng) as COO before founding Jeeves (Y Combinator S20). Jeeves offers multi-currency corporate cards, payments and credit to companies across Latin America, Europe and North America; it raised $180M led by Tencent at a $2.1B valuation in March 2022.
interesting_fact: Jeeves hit a $2.1B valuation only about seven months after its $57M Series B, in a Tencent-led $180M Series C that included Stanford University and GIC as investors.
deep_cut_fact: At PowerInbox, an email ad server used by 600+ brands including CNN and Disney, he grew the team from 3 to 50+ while keeping it profitable at $35M+ ARR; it ranked #3 on Deloitte's Fast50. He also worked in venture capital earlier.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Jeeves (global corporate card, spend management and cross-border business finance platform)
research_notes: Featured on HubSpot for Startups 'Spiraling Up: The Journey to Become a Unicorn' (S1 ep3), where he calls Jeeves his 'legacy project' - good podcast hook. No published press email found for Jeeves.

name: Sherwin Gandhi
profile: Co-founder of Jeeves, a fintech offering multi-currency corporate cards, payments and expense management to startups in Latin America, Canada and Europe, led by CEO Dileep Thazhmon. Aggregator profiles list Gandhi as founder, executive officer and director, with an RPI undergraduate degree and around eight angel investments.
current_role: Co-founder and director of Jeeves (cross-border corporate cards and spend management for Latin America and beyond); also an angel investor
research_notes: Very thin public footprint; role sourced only from aggregators (https://www.pipeseed.com/investor/sherwin-gandhi-936507, https://seedtable.com/person/Sherwin_Gandhi-39W6XNJ, https://ch.marketscreener.com/insider/SHERWIN-GANDHI-A39CHL/erfahrung). Public face of Jeeves is CEO Dileep Thazhmon. No published press email found on tryjeeves.com.

name: Firmin Zocchetto
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded PayFit in 2015 with Ghislain de Fontenay and Florian Fournier while studying at ESCP, then dropped out to run it. PayFit automates payroll and HR for SMEs in Europe and became a unicorn in 2022. In 2024 he said PayFit would be profitable in 2026, and for its tenth anniversary he said an IPO was not planned for the next three years.
interesting_fact: He caught the 'startup bug' in high school in Laval. His first venture, built with classmate and future PayFit co-founder Ghislain de Fontenay, was a social network for learning languages.
deep_cut_fact: His family has Italian roots and worked as builders and construction entrepreneurs. On leaving ESCP he said: 'For me, it was an obvious choice; for my family, a little less so.' He was mentored early by Capgemini chair Paul Hermelin.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, PayFit (Paris-based payroll & HR software)
research_notes: Gives interviews often in French media (JDN, Maddyness). Good podcast candidate on the European SaaS scale-up story.

name: Florian Fournier
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Paris payroll/HR SaaS PayFit in 2015 with Firmin Zocchetto and Ghislain de Fontenay and spent nine years building it into a ~$2B company. He left his operational role in January 2024 and in 2025 launched Orasio, which raised a EUR16M seed led by Frst to build sovereign European AI that analyses video feeds for police, cities, critical sites and the military.
interesting_fact: Orasio's name comes from the Greek 'orasi' ('vision'); its AI detects fires, falls, crowd movements and weapons in real time, and France's defence ministry AI agency (Amiad) has taken up its image-analysis tools.
deep_cut_fact: A Polytechnique alumnus who also attended a military school, he met both Orasio co-founders (Arnaud Delaunay and Fabio Gennari) back in preparatory school; he says 'J'ai toujours eu une sensibilité forte pour les enjeux de défense.'
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Orasio (European AI video-analysis/defence-tech startup); co-founder and board member, PayFit
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.orasio.com/contact | official_website: https://www.orasio.com | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/orasio/
research_notes: Media-friendly: Orasio's press page lists his interviews with BFM Business, Europe 1, BFMTV etc. French-language outreach likely best. LinkedIn link is the company page, not personal.

name: Ghislain de Fontenay
profile: Ghislain de Fontenay co-founded Paris-based PayFit in 2015 with Firmin Zocchetto and Florian Fournier to automate payroll and HR for European SMEs, serving as its first CTO. PayFit became a unicorn after raising EUR 254M in late 2021. He now leads PayFit's innovation lab.
interesting_fact: To tame French payroll rules, PayFit's founders created their own programming language, JetLang, to encode labour regulations and collective agreements, later extended to other countries.
deep_cut_fact: He and Firmin Zocchetto built their first company together as high-school students: a social network for learning foreign languages, which they dropped because it became too time-consuming.
current_role: Co-founder and Director of the Innovation Lab ('Delta Team'), PayFit (former CTO)
research_notes: Current Innovation Lab title comes from an aggregator profile (me.sh); low public profile, technical founder. PayFit press contact published as mailto on its press page.

name: Gaston Taratuta
profile: Argentine entrepreneur (b. 1972) whose Aleph Group acts as commercial/advertising partner for platforms such as X, TikTok and Spotify in markets where they don't operate directly. It grew from IMS Internet Media Services (2005); CVC's 2021 minority investment valued Aleph at about $2B. Aleph has since expanded into payments (Aleph Payments, Localpayment).
interesting_fact: He was named EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year 2022 - the first Argentine to win the global award.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding IMS he spent six years at Brazilian internet company UOL's Miami office, leaving in 2004 as head of international operations; by his own account he started IMS in 2005 with about US$5,000, and from 2011 it represented Twitter commercially abroad.
current_role: Founder & CEO, Aleph Group (formerly Aleph Holding), Miami
research_notes: Full name Christian Gastón Taratuta. No press email published on the company site; the company X account is @itsalephdigital.

name: Mathieu Alengrin
profile: French software engineer who was Head of Engineering at Vestiaire Collective before co-founding Ankorstore in Paris in 2019 with Pierre-Louis Lacoste, Nicolas d'Audiffret and Nicolas Cohen. Ankorstore is a European B2B wholesale marketplace connecting independent brands with retailers; it raised a EUR250M Series C in 2022 and reached unicorn status in about two years.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore went from founding in 2019 to unicorn in roughly two years, raising EUR6M seed (2019), EUR25M Series A (2020), EUR84M Series B (2021) and EUR250M Series C (2022).
deep_cut_fact: Ankorstore's founding team paired Alengrin, the engineering lead from luxury resale marketplace Vestiaire Collective, with the founders of the handmade marketplace A Little Market (Nicolas d'Audiffret and Nicolas Cohen) and ex-Etsy Wholesale manager Pierre-Louis Lacoste.
current_role: Co-founder, Ankorstore (listed by Crunchbase as Co-founder and Principal Engineer; not verified on primary source)
research_notes: Technical, behind-the-scenes co-founder with almost no press presence; CEO Pierre-Louis Lacoste is the public face. No published press email found on ankorstore.com.

name: Nicolas Cohen
profile: French e-commerce entrepreneur who co-founded ALittleMarket, a leading French handmade-goods marketplace sold to Etsy in 2014, then worked at Etsy before co-founding Paris-based B2B wholesale marketplace Ankorstore in 2019. Ankorstore became a unicorn in Jan 2022 with a EUR 250M Series C (BOND, Tiger Global) at a EUR 1.75B valuation.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore hit unicorn status only about two years after launch, by which time it connected 200,000 independent retailers with 15,000 brands; Cohen said the mission was 'to swing the balance in favor of independents.'
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Ankorstore came from conversations, while he and Nicolas d'Audiffret were at Etsy after it bought their ALittleMarket, about how hard it was for Etsy sellers to grow from B2C storefronts into wholesale businesses.
current_role: Co-founder of Ankorstore (co-CEO since 2019; current title not confirmed for 2025-26)
research_notes: Common name - be careful with disambiguation. Aggregator profiles conflict on whether he is still co-CEO (one says 2019-2024). No published press email found for Ankorstore this session.

name: Nicolas d'Audiffret
profile: Nicolas d'Audiffret is a French serial marketplace founder. With Nicolas Cohen he co-founded ALittleMarket (2012), France's top handmade-goods marketplace, which Etsy bought in 2014. In 2019 he co-founded Ankorstore, a European B2B wholesale marketplace linking independent brands and shops, which raised over €365M and was valued at more than €1.7B in early 2022. He co-ran it until 2025.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore was born at Etsy. He and Nicolas Cohen worked there after the ALittleMarket sale, noticed Etsy sellers wanted to wholesale to shops, and after staying France-only with their first company, launched Ankorstore internationally from day one.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 2003-2011 as a consultant at Bain & Company in Paris and San Francisco. In 2026 Ankorstore's CEO role passed to another Bain alumnus, Grégoire de Tilly.
current_role: Co-founder, Ankorstore (co-led the company until 2025; Grégoire de Tilly named CEO in 2026)
public_contact: official_website: https://www.ankorstore.com | podcast: Guest episode: 'How To Build A $2 Billion Unicorn In Under 3 Years with Ankorstore's Nicolas d'Audiffret'
research_notes: No longer CEO. Consultor (2026) says he co-led Ankorstore until 2025, and his new activity was not found. Do not confuse him with co-founder Nicolas Cohen. He has done English-language podcasts and interviews. The podcast entry was taken from a search listing and was not opened.

name: Pierre Louis Lacoste
profile: French e-commerce entrepreneur who co-founded Ankorstore in 2019 with Nicolas d'Audiffret, Nicolas Cohen and Mathieu Alengrin. Ankorstore is a wholesale marketplace connecting independent brands with independent shops across Europe. Before that he was a VP at activewear brand Lolë and Etsy's Country Manager for France. Ankorstore raised a €250M Series C in 2022 at unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore is partly a second attempt at an idea Etsy dropped: at Etsy he worked on Etsy Wholesale, which was cancelled when Etsy refocused on consumers. 'I always thought it was a missed opportunity, but also that I would do a few things differently.'
deep_cut_fact: Before building a platform for independent retailers he ran one himself: he owned a multi-brand retail store for several years, and says this taught him how hard it is for shops to find brands and agree terms.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Brand Officer, Ankorstore (Paris B2B wholesale marketplace); current title per MarketScreener, not confirmed on Ankorstore's own site
public_contact: pr_agency: Edifice (Amine Moussaoui) - amine@edifice-communication.com | official_website: https://www.ankorstore.com
research_notes: Nicolas d'Audiffret, not Lacoste, is Ankorstore's CEO. The PR agency contact is from a March 2024 release and may be dated. No recent (2025-26) coverage of Lacoste found.

name: Itai Lahan
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Cloudinary in 2012 with Tal Lev-Ami (CTO) and Nadav Soferman (CPO), whom he met in the IDF's 8200 unit. Its API-based image/video management platform grew for years without VC before Bessemer invested; Hurun values it at ~$2bn, and it now ships AI agents for visual media.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary had paying customers within months of formation and grew organically for years without venture capital, before Bessemer Venture Partners invested to fund expansion.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cloudinary he was an executive at Israeli anti-spam startup Blue Security and at Collactive, founded news aggregator Newsodrome, and in 2009 co-founded Ndivi, a tech consultancy for start-up founders - the gap he noticed there sparked the Cloudinary idea.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Cloudinary
public_contact: press_email: juli@cloudinary.com | official_website: https://cloudinary.com | https://x.com/itail | https://www.linkedin.com/in/itail/
research_notes: Press contact on Cloudinary newsroom: Juli Greenwood, Senior Director Global Communications. Has done developer-podcast interviews (Software Engineering Daily, 'Bootstrapping a SaaS for Developers') - receptive to podcast format.

name: Nadav Soferman
profile: Israeli engineer Nadav Soferman co-founded Cloudinary in early 2012 with Itai Lahan (CEO) and Tal Lev-Ami (CTO), whom he met in the IDF's 8200 unit. Cloudinary's API-first platform optimises, transforms and delivers images and video for the web; it bootstrapped for years before taking growth capital (~$2B valuation). As CPO he leads product.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary was a rare bootstrapped Israeli startup: five years in (2017) it had raised no venture capital, yet had 220,000 developers on its free tier and 5,000 paying customers including eBay and Sky News.
deep_cut_fact: Cloudinary's first version took just four months to build and launched quietly in mid-2012; the idea came from the founders' consulting firm Ndivi, where every new social-network client struggled to render images well on every device and resolution.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Cloudinary
research_notes: Low-profile product-side founder (CEO Itai Lahan is the usual spokesperson). Press contact is Cloudinary's Senior Director of Global Communications (Juli Greenwood) as listed on the newsroom page. He has written for Smashing Magazine on responsive images.

name: Tal Lev-Ami
profile: Israeli developer who co-founded Cloudinary in 2012 with Itai Lahan and Nadav Soferman to fix the tedious work of uploading, transforming and delivering images and video online. The API-first media platform grew profitably without venture funding; a 2022 Blackstone-led secondary deal valued it at $2B. He remains CTO, focusing on AI-powered visual media at scale.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary bootstrapped its way to a $100M annual revenue run rate (2021) without venture capital, before Blackstone's $100M+ secondary investment valued it at $2B.
deep_cut_fact: Cloudinary worked with Google researchers to create the JPEG XL image format, and has since championed JPEG XL support across browsers and Apple devices.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cloudinary
research_notes: Press contact is Juli Greenwood, Senior Director Global Communications, as listed on the Cloudinary newsroom. He gives technical interviews (e.g. TechDogs Dec 2025). Deep-cut fact is about the company he co-founded, not him personally. Fit is CDN/media infrastructure rather than energy.

name: Renaud Heitz
profile: French robotics engineer (Mines Paris-PSL 2006) who worked in robotics software at BA Systèmes and GE Healthcare, then co-founded Exotec in 2015 with CEO Romain Moulin, a longtime colleague. Exotec's Skypod robots climb racks to move in 3D; after first customer Cdiscount it signed clients including Carrefour, Uniqlo and Gap, becoming France's first industrial unicorn.
interesting_fact: In Feb 2026 Exotec opened 'Imaginarium', a 25,000 m² global HQ and production site in Wasquehal, Northern France, with 700+ staff from 60+ nationalities. Heitz said it 'reflects our commitment to build in Europe and our decision to invest for the long term.'
deep_cut_fact: He experienced both Mines Paris-PSL and MIT, calling them two excellent programs with very different academic models, and says his Mines diploma is 'une vraie carte de visite', even with American investors like Goldman Sachs.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Exotec (warehouse robotics, France)
research_notes: No current published press email found. A 2024 release named PR agency Hopscotch for Exotec, but that is dated. CEO Romain Moulin is the more public founder. Pre-Exotec employers come from company job listings and profiles.

name: Romain Moulin
profile: French robotics engineer who co-founded Exotec (Croix/Lille, launched 2015) with longtime friend and GE colleague Renaud Heitz. Exotec's Skypod system uses climbing robots for warehouse automation; a $335M Series D led by Goldman Sachs in Jan 2022 valued it at $2B. Moulin remains CEO, leading global expansion and next-gen Skypod launches.
interesting_fact: Exotec's $335M Series D (Jan 2022, led by Goldman Sachs Asset Management with Bpifrance and 83North) at a $2B valuation made it France's first industrial unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a sales engineer at a small French automated-forklift company, rising to technical manager, then worked on advanced robotic imagers at GE Healthcare, where he says he 'really learned what it takes to build a hardware product.' He has known co-founder Renaud Heitz for 20+ years.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Exotec

name: William Addy
profile: Bill Addy founded Dallas-based ISN Software in 2001. ISN runs the ISNetworld platform, which energy, steel, pharma and other enterprises use to manage contractor and supplier compliance; it served 75,000+ customers in 85+ countries including 170 Fortune 500 firms. He was CEO until about 2015 and then executive chairman. ISN now lists him as Founder, with Brian Callahan as CEO. He is a Dallas philanthropist (The Addy Foundation).
interesting_fact: He and his wife Lydia gave the gift behind Addy Hall, a dormitory in Princeton's new residential colleges. Addy is a Princeton '82 chemical engineering graduate.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012 the Addys created the Addy/ISN North American Low Carbon Emission Energy Self-Sufficiency Fund at Princeton for research on cutting carbon and achieving North American energy self-sufficiency. His senior thesis was 'one part chemical engineering and nine parts economics' on ExxonMobil in western Colorado.
current_role: Founder and board member, ISN Software Corporation (Dallas, TX)
research_notes: A strong fit for an energy podcast: his clients are heavily energy-sector and he funds low-carbon energy research. Blackstone is an ISN investor with a board seat. He also does North Texas philanthropy (search results tie him to KERA public broadcasting, unverified). No published personal email.

name: Alvin Tamsir
profile: Synthetic biologist (BA Molecular & Cell Biology, UC Berkeley; PhD UCSF under Christopher Voigt) who co-founded Pivot Bio in 2011 with lab mate Karsten Temme. Pivot Bio makes nitrogen-fixing microbes that replace part of farmers' synthetic fertiliser; Tamsir led its first commercial corn product, co-authored foundational patents and grew research from under 10 to 200+ scientists.
interesting_fact: Pivot Bio grew out of a 2011 paper by Temme and Dehua Zhao in Voigt's lab on engineering nitrogen fixation - an idea Berkeley dean Paul Ludden suggested to Voigt after a photosynthesis grant proposal was heavily criticised.
deep_cut_fact: As a PhD student he was first author of a 2010 Nature paper, 'Robust multicellular computing using genetically encoded NOR gates and chemical wires', building logic circuits out of communicating E. coli colonies.
current_role: Scientific Fellow and Co-Founder, Pivot Bio (Berkeley, CA)
research_notes: Scientist, low media profile; route via Pivot Bio media team. The source page renders the address as 'media@www.pivotbio.com' (CMS artifact); recent Business Wire releases reportedly use media@pivotbio.com.

name: Karsten Temme
profile: Bioengineer (Iowa BS/MS; UC Berkeley-UCSF PhD) who in Chris Voigt's lab tried to rebuild microbial nitrogen fixation from scratch. In 2011 he co-founded Pivot Bio with Alvin Tamsir to replace synthetic nitrogen fertilizer with nitrogen-fixing soil microbes, serving as CEO until 2023; he now leads innovation focused on 'the Future Acre' (agriculture in 2050).
interesting_fact: He holds over 200 patents or patent applications (90+ granted) and spoke at the TED Countdown Summit in Nairobi in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Originally from Casper, Wyoming, he played trumpet in the University of Iowa's Hawkeye Marching Band, helped design parts for a Mars rover, and as an undergrad founded Xwires Communications to bring internet service to remote farmland.
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Innovation Officer and board member, Pivot Bio (Berkeley, CA)
research_notes: Chris Abbott replaced him as CEO in Aug 2023. Experienced TED speaker; climate/ag-emissions angle (synthetic fertilizer is energy-intensive).

name: Anurag Arjun
profile: Indian technologist who co-founded Matic Network (now Polygon) in 2017 with Jaynti Kanani and Sandeep Nailwal and served as its Chief Product Officer. In 2023 he spun Avail, a data-availability project, out of Polygon Labs and became its 'sole steward'. Avail raised a $27M seed round led by Founders Fund and Dragonfly.
interesting_fact: Avail started inside Polygon in late 2020. In March 2023 Polygon spun it off, and Arjun left Polygon Labs to run it as an independent company with co-founder Prabal Banerjee.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto, he spent years in health-tech product management. At Dexter Consultancy he co-created HealthTrac, a platform that monitored vital signs remotely through wearables, and HealthOne, a free SaaS clinic-management tool for doctors. His first job was programmer analyst at Cognizant in 2006.
current_role: Co-founder, Avail (modular blockchain data-availability network); co-founder of Polygon (formerly Matic Network)

profile: Texas entrepreneur who founded sustainable home-improvement store TreeHouse (2011) before co-founding ICON, which 3D-prints homes and structures. profile: Co-founder and CTO of Austin-based ICON, which builds large-scale robotic 3D printers (Vulcan), materials and software for printing homes and structures, including work for NASA on lunar and Mars construction. profile: Arthur Macedo is listed by MarketScreener as one of five 2013 co-founders of CloudWalk, the Brazilian payments fintech behind InfinitePay (with Luis Silva, Behzad Malek, Bruno Freitas and Eliezer Pimentel), serving as chief commercial officer from 2013 to 2018. No independent press, company or filing source confirming his role or background was found.
interesting_fact: CloudWalk, which he is listed as co-founding, became a unicorn in Nov 2021 when a $150M round valued it at $2.15B, more than incumbents Cielo and Getnet combined according to Brazilian press.
current_role: Listed as CloudWalk co-founder (chief commercial officer 2013-2018 per MarketScreener); current role unknown
research_notes: Only source tying him to CloudWalk is MarketScreener's insider profile (marketscreener.com/insider/ARTHUR-MACEDO-A2AI8G), which also mentions a University of Notre Dame undergraduate link. Tried: English/Portuguese web searches, CloudWalk SEC Form D filings (2019, 2021; list only Luis Silva, James Aviles, Everson Lopes, Bruno Freitas), Wikipedia (en/pt credit only Luis Silva), Brazilian fintech press. Common name; don't use without checking his LinkedIn first.

name: Behzad Malek
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder lists (2022-2024) name Behzad Malek as a founder of CloudWalk, the Brazilian payments fintech founded in May 2013 and valued at about $2B, known for InfinitePay. CloudWalk now runs AI agents for small sellers (JIM, also in the US) and the Pierre finance app. His role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: CloudWalk pitches its products as AI agents: millions of Brazilian sellers use InfinitePay alongside JIM, an autonomous agent that handles payments, credit, storefronts and marketing, which CloudWalk calls one of the largest agentic deployments in commerce.
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of CloudWalk (São Paulo fintech); current role not verified
research_notes: Company facts verified; his founder role and bio not verified (web search quota exhausted; his name does not appear on CloudWalk's pages). Press email reaches CloudWalk, not necessarily him. Check LinkedIn manually.

name: Eliezer Pimentel
profile: Eliézer Pimentel is a co-founder and former executive director of CloudWalk, the Brazilian payments fintech behind InfinitePay (valued at $2.15B in Nov 2021). After leaving, he backed and co-founded Quero 2 Pay with Gabriel Andrade in 2020, turning a pandemic-hit Franca ticketing startup into a card-machine fintech that processed R$1.5B in 18 months.
interesting_fact: Quero 2 Pay grew out of Quero 2 Ingressos, a ticketing startup whose revenue fell to zero when Covid hit. With Pimentel's backing it pivoted to payment terminals ('Queridona Smart') for small merchants, launching in April 2020 and reaching R$100m a month in volume within eight months.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 he told Finsiders Brasil that Quero 2 Pay was 'designing a payment machine for the Metaverse' and planned to launch its own Q2 Bank, a striking ambition for a fintech from Franca, the interior São Paulo shoe-making city.
current_role: Co-founder, Quero 2 Pay (Franca, SP; payment terminals rebranded Monetix in 2024); co-founder and former executive director of CloudWalk. Current title unverified
research_notes: CloudWalk co-founder status per startups.com.br ('cofundador e ex-diretor executivo da CloudWalk') and the MarketScreener founder list (Luis Silva, Arthur Macedo, Behzad Malek, Bruno Freitas, Eliezer Pimentel, 2013). Not on CloudWalk SEC Form D filings (2019/2021), and CloudWalk's own materials credit only Luis Silva as founder. No published personal contact found. Quero 2 Pay brand now Monetix (iDinheiro, 2025).

name: Luis Silva
profile: Brazilian founder of CloudWalk, the AI- and blockchain-heavy payments company behind InfinitePay, which serves 4M+ small merchants in Brazil. CloudWalk reported US$497M revenue for 2024 with tripled net income, and says it passed US$1M revenue per employee thanks to 40+ in-house AI agents. Silva headlined Web Summit Rio 2025 on AI agents and AGI ethics.
interesting_fact: In 2025 CloudWalk raised its internal 'minimum wage' for analysts to R$7,000/month, crediting AI productivity gains; Silva said 'It's only fair that this gain is used to reward CloudWalk's employees.'
deep_cut_fact: CloudWalk's support team built an in-house AI agent named 'Claudio Walker' that handles about 90% of InfinitePay customer interactions with satisfaction comparable to human analysts.
current_role: Founder and CEO, CloudWalk (Brazilian fintech; owner of InfinitePay and JIM)
research_notes: Very AI-forward and publicly vocal (Web Summit, Bloomberg Linea 100 Most Innovative 2024) - strong podcast candidate on AI-native operations. No press email found on CloudWalk's site; route via newsroom or his public talks.

name: John Lafleur
profile: French serial entrepreneur who co-founded Airbyte (2020, YC) with CEO Michel Tricot; the open-source data-integration/ELT platform reached a ~$1.5B valuation in 2021. Earlier ventures: As-App, StreamNation (acquired by SmugMug), CodinGame (COO/CEO) and Anaxi.
interesting_fact: Airbyte started in YC as Daxtarity, a marketing-data tool, and pivoted during COVID after customer interviews revealed teams were hand-building data pipelines.
deep_cut_fact: His entrepreneurial career began in 2008 with As-App, a ski-resort app later acquired by Lumiplan.
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Airbyte (San Francisco)
public_contact: pr_agency: Joe Eckert, Eckert Communications - jeckert@eckertcomms.com (Airbyte media contact) | substack: https://dev.to/johnlafleur
research_notes: Writes about developer marketing/open source; dev.to profile is his own blog, labelled substack type for lack of a better field.

name: Michel Tricot
profile: French data engineer who co-founded open-source data-integration company Airbyte in 2020 with John Lafleur (YC W20); Airbyte's connector platform became one of the most widely used ELT tools and was valued around $1.5B in 2021. Before that he was Head of Integrations/Director of Engineering at LiveRamp and a founding engineering leader at rideOS (later acquired by Gopuff).
interesting_fact: At LiveRamp he spent about seven years building and scaling more than 1,000 data connectors - the pain point that inspired Airbyte's open-source connector model.
deep_cut_fact: His data career began around 2008 as an R&D engineer handling financial data at FactSet in Paris; on YC's profile he says he has 'been working in data since 2007'.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Airbyte (San Francisco)
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker (Airflow Summit, Percona Live, RAISE). Also a venture partner at Flex Capital (per profiles, unverified). Route via Airbyte.

name: Collin Chin
profile: Collin Chin co-founded Aleo in 2019 with Howard Wu, Raymond Chu and others. Aleo is a programmable privacy blockchain built on zero-knowledge proofs; a16z led its 2021 Series A. At Aleo, Chin worked on the developer stack, especially the Leo programming language for private applications.
interesting_fact: Leo, first released in 2020, was one of the first programming languages built specifically for zero-knowledge applications.
deep_cut_fact: He is first author of the 2021 IACR paper 'Leo: A Programming Language for Formally Verified, Zero-Knowledge Applications' (ePrint 2021/651), co-written with Howard Wu, Raymond Chu and formal-methods researchers Alessandro Coglio, Eric McCarthy and Eric Smith.
current_role: Co-founder, Aleo (zero-knowledge privacy L1 blockchain); led teams building developer tooling such as the Leo language and Aleo SDK
public_contact: official_website: https://aleo.org/ | x: https://twitter.com/AleoHQ (Aleo project account, not personal)
research_notes: Low public profile; Howard Wu is Aleo's main public voice. Aleo's author page for him now returns 404, so his current role is unclear. A good angle is the technical depth of the Leo language. I found no personal contact.

name: Howard Wu
profile: Cryptographer Howard Wu co-founded Aleo, a privacy-focused, zero-knowledge layer-1 blockchain, after research at UC Berkeley under Alessandro Chiesa and Dawn Song. He now leads Provable, which builds products for compliant, confidential payments and developer tools for deploying applications on Aleo.
interesting_fact: His Berkeley research, including the Zexe (Zero-Knowledge Executions) and DIZK papers, has been adopted by protocols such as Ethereum and Zcash.
deep_cut_fact: After Zexe was published, Vitalik Buterin asked him to launch it on Ethereum, and DeFi protocols such as Uniswap and Kyber wanted it for decentralized dark pools. That interest led him to take 'a leap of faith' and commercialize the research as Aleo. He calls cryptography 'a fundamental desire to define what trust means.'
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Provable (an Aleo Labs company); co-founder of Aleo
public_contact: official_website: https://provable.com | x: https://x.com/provablehq (Provable company account) | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/provable/ (company page)
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker (CoinDesk Consensus 2025 Hong Kong and Toronto). Aggregators differ on whether he is still Aleo CEO; Provable is his verified current role. Social links are company accounts, not personal.

name: Raymond Chu
profile: Raymond Chu co-founded Aleo Systems in December 2019 with Howard Wu, Michael Beller and Collin Chin. Aleo builds a layer-1 blockchain for private applications using zero-knowledge proofs, rooted in the Berkeley Zexe research, and is backed by investors including a16z. Mainnet launched in September 2024. Chu is an engineering co-founder rather than a public face.
interesting_fact: Aleo was created as 'the first platform for fully private applications', and its name stands for Autonomous Ledger Executions Off-chain. The design grew out of the Zexe zero-knowledge research at UC Berkeley.
deep_cut_fact: He is a hands-on engineer: GitHub shows Raymond Chu (handle raychu86) committing code to Aleo's trusted-setup ceremony software (AleoNet/aleo-setup) in November 2020, ahead of the network's launch.
current_role: Co-founder, Aleo (zero-knowledge privacy blockchain); described as an engineer on Aleo's core node software (snarkVM/snarkOS). Exact current title not verified.
research_notes: Very low media profile; Howard Wu (now CEO of Provable) is Aleo's public spokesperson. His commit email appears in git metadata, but it was not published as a contact and is deliberately excluded.

name: Deepika Bodapati
profile: Co-founded Athelas with Tanay Tandon (Y Combinator), building the Athelas One, an FDA-cleared, internet-connected finger-prick device that measures white blood cell and neutrophil counts at home, and expanding into remote patient monitoring and revenue-cycle software. After Athelas merged with healthcare infrastructure firm Commure in 2023 she became COO of the combined company.
interesting_fact: Athelas One became key for schizophrenia patients on clozapine, who need regular white-cell monitoring; the work led to a partnership with clozapine maker HLS Therapeutics and deployments in California state hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Even as Athelas neared unicorn status she personally read every customer support ticket; persistent emails from Dr. Deanna Kelly of the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center led Bodapati to call her, opening the clozapine use case.
current_role: Co-founder of Athelas; COO of Commure (Athelas merged with Commure in Oct 2023)
research_notes: Route via Commure/Athelas. No published press email found in this session.

name: Tanay Tandon
profile: Silicon Valley founder with a machine-learning background who co-founded Athelas with Deepika Bodapati (YC S16), starting with an in-home blood-testing device and expanding into remote patient monitoring and revenue-cycle software. After Athelas merged with Commure in October 2023 he became CEO of the combined company, with Bodapati as COO; Commure now focuses on AI tools for health systems.
interesting_fact: During Athelas's first clinical trial in 2016 at a hospital in Juárez, Mexico, Tandon spotted a white blood cell count above 40,000 with immature cells - the patient was later confirmed to have leukemia.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Deepika Bodapati met on the high-school science-fair circuit, first bonding on a flight to a competition; Athelas's first Mountain View office was 'a barely refurbished liquor store.'
current_role: CEO, Commure (healthcare technology; merged with Athelas in Oct 2023)
research_notes: Speaks publicly (e.g. Slush 2024 with Initialized: https://blog.initialized.com/2024/11/supercharging-healthcare-with-tanay-tandon-at-slush-2024/). Hurun lists Athelas; the company now operates as Commure. No published press email found on commure.com.

name: Alan Chiu
profile: Alan Chiu co-founded Enya, a startup that took over the OMG Network project, an early Ethereum scaling effort. Under contract with the OMG Foundation, Enya's team built Boba Network, an Ethereum Layer-2 optimistic rollup with 'hybrid compute' (optional off-chain computation). Hurun lists Boba at a $2B peak valuation.
interesting_fact: He said Boba came from his frustration that early DeFi users profited while others were priced out by high gas fees: 'Seeing this inequality made me uneasy, and I was angry.'
current_role: Founder & CEO, Boba Network / Enya Labs (per 2022 sources; current status not re-verified)
research_notes: Aggregator profiles say he holds a Stanford MS in Management, was co-president of Stanford Angels & Entrepreneurs and is a partner at XSeed Capital. I could not verify these from primary pages. The crypto-industry profile and 2022 interview (crypto @ Stanford) are the best context. I did not verify his current activity in 2026.

name: Diogo Frenkel
profile: Brazilian fintech executive listed as co-founder and CFO of Dock, the Sao Paulo-area payments and banking-as-a-service provider that grew out of card processor Conductor (founded 1999). In 2021 Conductor, Dock and Muxi were unified under the Dock brand; Dock reached unicorn status in 2022 (~$1.5B) and serves 400+ companies in 11 Latin American countries.
interesting_fact: Dock started as an in-house project inside card processor Conductor in 2018; it became the name for the whole company in 2021 because it was the only pillar built entirely in-house, and in 2023 Dock became a Central Bank of Brazil-regulated institution.
current_role: Co-founder and CFO, Dock (Brazilian payments/banking-infrastructure company, formerly Conductor) - title as of 2021; current status not confirmed
research_notes: Very low public profile; no personal bio or post-2021 coverage found. CEO Antonio Soares is Dock's spokesperson. Sources conflict on founding history (Conductor 1999 vs Dock 2014/2018). Portuguese-language outreach via Dock press room recommended.

name: Frederico Amaral
profile: Fred Amaral co-founded Brazilian payments and banking-as-a-service infrastructure firm Dock, which became a unicorn, and served as its Chief Product & Technology Officer. He left to found Lerian with his own capital in 2023; it builds Midaz, a source-available core-banking ledger, and raised an R$18M seed led by Maya Capital in 2024 plus a further round reported in 2026.
interesting_fact: With Lerian he is betting that core banking goes open: Midaz's code is public and Lerian plans to earn mainly from hosting and add-on features, building a developer community through developer advocacy and workshops.
deep_cut_fact: He personally pitched Midaz to Brazil's developer community on TabNews, the Brazilian dev forum, in posts like 'Midaz: open source banking ledger com múltiplos conectores'.
current_role: Founder & CEO, Lerian (São Paulo); co-founder and former Chief Product & Technology Officer of Dock
research_notes: Goes by 'Fred Amaral'. Lerian email is the company's general contact, not personal. Aggregator profiles mention earlier stints at Uber, Deutsche Bank, BTG Pactual and Movile (unverified).

name: Marcelo Jacques
profile: Brazilian fintech executive and former investment banker (TMT coverage) who serves as Chief Strategy Officer of Dock, the São Paulo paytech formed when Conductor unified Conductor, Dock and Muxi under one brand in 2021. Dock provides card processing, digital accounts and BaaS infrastructure to 200+ companies across Latin America.
interesting_fact: In 2020 Conductor said it processed more than R$10B in monthly transactions across 100M customer accounts while staying profitable; Jacques: 'we always look for the correct balance between growth and profitability.'
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer, Dock (Brazilian payments & banking-as-a-service platform, formerly Conductor) - title as of 2020-2021; not re-confirmed for 2026
research_notes: Low public profile; CEO Antonio Soares is Dock's main public face. Press room lists both an in-house inbox and an agency inbox.

name: Brad Siegler
profile: Missouri-based co-founder of EquipmentShare, the Columbia, Missouri construction-equipment rental and fleet-technology company started by brothers Willy and Jabbok Schlacks with Siegler, Jeff Lowe and Matthew McDonald. Backed early by Y Combinator (2015), EquipmentShare went public on Nasdaq in January 2026; Siegler was listed as a shareholder in the IPO prospectus.
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare grew out of a 2014 Startup Weekend in Columbia, Missouri, where the Schlacks brothers won first place and $2,000; by 2021 it had about 3,000 employees and 90+ locations.
deep_cut_fact: When EquipmentShare went through Y Combinator in 2015, TechCrunch pitched it as 'Airbnb for construction equipment', a peer-to-peer marketplace letting contractors rent idle gear from one another; Siegler was one of three Missouri-area co-founders who joined the Schlacks brothers.
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder, EquipmentShare (Nasdaq: EQPT); current operating role not confirmed
research_notes: Low public profile. Shareholding confirmed in the 424B4 prospectus (Jan 2026): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1693736/000162828026003334/eqpt-424b4.htm . Wellfound describes him as a UI/UX/web designer and Univ. of Missouri '13 grad (unverified primary).

name: Jeff Lowe
profile: Jeffrey Lowe is one of five co-founders of EquipmentShare, founded in Columbia, Missouri in 2015 with brothers Willy and Jabbok Schlacks, Brad Siegler and Matthew McDonald. EquipmentShare grew from a Startup Weekend-winning contractor equipment-sharing idea into a national construction equipment rental and telematics (T3) platform that filed to go public (S-1/A, Jan 2026, ticker EQPT).
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare's idea won first place and $2,000 at a 2014 Startup Weekend in Columbia, Missouri; the company now has thousands of employees and files with the SEC as EquipmentShare.com Inc (EQPT).
current_role: Co-founder of EquipmentShare (no longer in an active role, per Contrary Research)
research_notes: Very low public profile; Contrary Research says the Schlacks brothers are the only founders still active at the company, and Lowe is not named in the Jan 2026 S-1/A. Common name (do not confuse with the 'Tiger King' Jeff Lowe). An aggregator claims prior work as a freelance web designer and partner at Lowe Constructing (unverified). No contact found. Source: https://research.contrary.com/company/equipmentshare

name: Matthew McDonald
profile: Matthew McDonald is EquipmentShare's technology co-founder. At a Columbia, Missouri Startup Weekend he met the contractors behind the idea, built a prototype and booked a skid-loader rental the same weekend. The team went through Y Combinator, and EquipmentShare grew into a national construction-equipment rental and telematics company that IPO'd on Nasdaq in January 2026 at about a $6B valuation.
interesting_fact: Former co-worker Wade Foster, who went on to co-found Zapier, talked the team into applying to Y Combinator. McDonald admits he first dismissed YC as 'something for Silicon Valley people'.
deep_cut_fact: As founding CTO he grew the engineering team to 11, then with a mentor's help realised he did not enjoy the leadership seat and handed it over. His engineering team was remote from day one because his wife had just taken a job in Maine.
current_role: Co-founder and founding CTO, EquipmentShare (Nasdaq: EQPT). He stepped back from the CTO seat to an engineering role by 2019; current title not confirmed.
public_contact: podcast: Guest on Gun.io 'Frontier' podcast episode 123 (2019) | official_website: https://www.equipmentshare.com (company IR: equipmentshare.gcs-web.com)
research_notes: The SEC filing names only the Schlacks brothers as co-founders, while Startland News lists McDonald among the co-founders (with Brad Siegler and Jeff Lowe). Low profile; his current role at EquipmentShare is unknown. IPO details (23 Jan 2026, $24.50/share, about $6B) come from search snippets of RER/IPOScoop.

name: Ilana Harkavi
profile: New York-based makeup artist who founded the Il Makiage cosmetics brand in 1972; it was known mainly among professional makeup artists. The brand was later bought by siblings Oran Holtzman and Shiran Holtzman-Erel, who relaunched it in 2018 as a digital-first, AI-driven brand under parent ODDITY (Nasdaq IPO 2023). No evidence found that she holds equity or a role in today's ODDITY.
interesting_fact: The brand name is an intentionally simplified spelling of the French word 'maquillage' (makeup).
deep_cut_fact: Under her, Il Makiage was known in professional circles for innovations such as windowed eyeshadow packaging.
current_role: Original founder of Il Makiage (1972); no current role found
research_notes: Likely a list mis-attribution: the $1-2B valuation reflects the post-2018 Holtzman relaunch (ODDITY), not the original founder. Almost no public information on her; alive status unknown. Consider Oran Holtzman (ODDITY CEO) instead if the goal is the unicorn's founder.

name: Shiran Holtzman Erel
profile: Shiran Holtzman Erel co-founded ODDITY with her brother, CEO Oran Holtzman. ODDITY is an Israeli-American, AI- and data-driven beauty and wellness company that owns IL MAKIAGE and SpoiledChild and listed on Nasdaq in 2023. She has been Chief Product Officer since inception and joined the board in November 2022.
interesting_fact: In 2013 she and her brother bought the struggling IL MAKIAGE brand out of receivership for NIS 12M plus NIS 80M of assumed debt, and turned it into a billion-dollar online beauty brand.
deep_cut_fact: She told Calcalist in 2020: 'In Israel, we're a proud retail player; in the U.S., we're 100% online.' This describes IL MAKIAGE's dual model of physical stores at home and a pure-online US business.
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Product Officer and board member, ODDITY Tech (NASDAQ: ODD; IL MAKIAGE, SpoiledChild)
research_notes: Her brother Oran is the public face; she rarely gives interviews. ODDITY runs a biotech lab in Boston (ODDITY LABS) and an R&D centre in Tel Aviv, which could be an AI/data angle. Route through press@oddity.com.

name: Aron Schwarzkopf
profile: Ecuadorian entrepreneur raised in Quito, educated at Babson College (also Singularity University and CUHK), now Miami-based. With Sebastian Castro he built and sold US fintech Leaf (2014), then founded Kushki, a payments acquirer/infrastructure company; its $186M Series B in 2022 made it Ecuador's first unicorn.
interesting_fact: Kushki means 'money' in Ecuadorian Kichwa; its 2022 Series B (Kaszek, SoftBank Latin America Fund, DILA, Clocktower) made it Ecuador's first-ever unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Sebastian Castro, both from Ecuador, met in Boston as college students while watching soccer; he has said 'We never thought that we would return home' to build a company.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kushki (Latin American payments infrastructure)
research_notes: Kushki site only publishes support/security emails (soporte@, seguridad@kushkipagos.com), not press. Listed in Bloomberg Linea 500 (2022) and has a World Economic Forum profile; LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Daniela Espinosa
profile: Ecuadorian banker-turned-founder: 12 years at Citibank (ending as Country Risk Manager for Ecuador), then CFO of large family-owned groups, before co-founding payments platform Kushki in 2016, which became Ecuador's first unicorn. She left Kushki in 2022, founded advisory firm Crakit in 2023 and co-founded UIN (gamification + AI for consumer behaviour) in 2025, while angel investing and advising fintechs.
interesting_fact: She was president of Ecuador's Technology and Innovation Chamber (CITEC) and helped build Kushki, whose payment rails have served clients such as Uber, Cabify and Rappi.
deep_cut_fact: As a child she loved numbers so much she memorized license plates and phone numbers, and her favourite game was Monopoly; she became a Citi country manager by age 29.
current_role: Founder, Crakit (tech advisory & M&A boutique); co-founder, UIN; angel investor
research_notes: No longer at Kushki (2016-2022). No published email or verified own website found; LinkedIn (ec.linkedin.com/in/daespinosa) appears in search but was not verified as hers. Speaks at South Summit Madrid; Spanish-language outreach likely best.

name: Jose Santacruz
profile: Ecuadorian engineer who was part of Kushki's founding core team and served as CTO; Kushki became Ecuador's first unicorn. The company's official site lists Aron Schwarzkopf and Sebastián Castro as co-founders, and later sources name a different CTO, so Santacruz has probably moved on.
interesting_fact: In June 2021, as Kushki CTO, he appeared on Thoughtworks' 'Tecnología y Negocios' podcast to talk about taking a company from start-up to scale-up.
deep_cut_fact: He was one of only five people at Kushki, alongside Sebastián Castro, Aron Schwarzkopf, Daniela Espinosa and Melissa Castro, when the payments startup expanded into Colombia in 2019.
current_role: Payments and fintech engineering leader, Quito (per LinkedIn); former CTO of Kushki. Current employer not confirmed
research_notes: I matched him to Kushki as CTO and early team member, but the 'founder' label comes only from Hurun and is not confirmed by Kushki. His current role is unknown, and Kushki publishes no press email (only support/security addresses).

name: Aaron Matos
profile: Aaron Matos launched Paradox in 2016 in Scottsdale, AZ, building 'Olivia', a conversational AI assistant that screens and schedules candidates by text for employers like Chipotle, 7-Eleven, GM and Nestle. Valued ~$2B (Hurun), it grew 1,000%+ from 2020-24; he handed the CEO role to Adam Godson in 2024, and Paradox is now part of Workday.
interesting_fact: Matos largely self-funded Paradox early on: announcing a $13.34M Series A in 2019 he said the company was backed by 'private family funds and my personal investments' and that 'I've never liked to talk about funding.'
deep_cut_fact: Under Matos, Paradox built an unusual athlete-ambassador roster for an HR-software firm - golfers Cameron Smith, Cheyenne Woods, Jennifer Kupcho and Lydia Ko and NHL great Shane Doan - and in 2022 became one of the only non-golf brands to sign college golfers (Rose Zhang, Rachel Heck) to NIL deals.
current_role: Founder of Paradox (conversational-AI recruiting, Scottsdale, AZ); handed CEO role to Adam Godson in March 2024; Paradox now part of Workday
research_notes: Press email is Paradox CMO Josh Zywien, the media contact on Paradox releases; post-Workday this may route to Workday comms. Matos's current activity after stepping back is not verified (web-search quota exhausted). Fit: AI in hiring, not energy/data centers.
