name: Doron Myersdorf
profile: Israeli engineer (DSc, Technion) who co-founded StoreDot in 2012 to develop extreme-fast-charging (XFC) lithium-ion batteries; backers include Daimler, BP, Samsung, TDK, VinFast and Polestar. Its silicon-dominant XFC cells have been validated by seven OEMs; in 2026 the company is pivoting to licensing deals and says it is preparing for the public markets. It also pitches XFC to data-center operators.
interesting_fact: StoreDot's earliest tech grew out of peptide 'nano-dot' research linked to Alzheimer's studies (Prof. Ehud Gazit's peptide nanocrystals) - the 'dots' still in the company's name - and it demonstrated a 30-second full phone charge in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: Before StoreDot he founded and led SanDisk's SSD business unit, growing it to $100M+ in under three years, and earlier was VP Flash & Operations at Israeli flash pioneer M-Systems; his motto: 'everything is possible, if you approach it with pure credulity.'
current_role: CEO and Co-Founder, StoreDot (Herzliya, Israel)
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.store-dot.com/contact.html | x: https://x.com/StoreDotLtd (company) | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/storedot (company)
research_notes: Talkative founder, good energy-storage guest; company now markets XFC to data-center operators too. Some press (per Wikipedia, Feb 2026) questions StoreDot's runway and long commercialization timeline - handle tactfully.

name: Gil Rosenman
profile: Gil Rosenman co-founded StoreDot in 2012 with Doron Myersdorf and Simon Litsyn. It began with peptide-based displays and storage built on Tel Aviv University research by Ehud Gazit, then pivoted to extreme-fast-charging EV batteries, backed by BP, Daimler, Samsung, TDK, Polestar and VinFast; it was valued at $1.5B in 2022.
interesting_fact: StoreDot started out not in batteries but in bio-organic 'peptide' nanocrystals for phone displays and memory, before becoming known for EV cells designed to add about 100 miles of range in 5 minutes of charging.
current_role: Co-founder, StoreDot (Herzliya, Israel); current operational role not verified
research_notes: Low public profile; StoreDot is fronted by CEO Doron Myersdorf. Sensitive timing: per 2026 press, StoreDot's SPAC deal was cancelled and it is seeking new funding - avoid raising this. Rosenman is widely described as a Tel Aviv University physics/engineering academic, but that was not verified here (web-search budget exhausted).

name: Simon Litsyn
profile: Soviet-trained electrical engineer (PhD, LETI Leningrad 1982) and Tel Aviv University professor since 1991 who was chief scientist at M-Systems/SanDisk (1999-2012). In 2012 he co-founded StoreDot, developer of extreme-fast-charging silicon-based EV batteries backed by BP, Daimler, Samsung and Polestar. He also consults on second-life battery storage (Sparkion).

deep_cut_fact: CHAOS's founding team mixes Epirus and 8VC alumni (Tenet, Bo Marr) with a Palantir/UK Secret Intelligence Service veteran (Gavin Hood) and Brett Cummings of 8VC/Formation 8.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO (sometimes Co-CEO), CHAOS Industries; co-founder of Epirus
research_notes: Now primarily associated with CHAOS Industries rather than Epirus. Titles vary (CEO / Co-CEO).

name: Max Mednik
profile: Max Mednik is listed as a founder of Epirus, the Los Angeles defense-tech company (backed by 8VC) that builds Leonidas, a solid-state high-power-microwave system for defeating drone swarms; Epirus closed a $250M Series D. He does not appear on the current executive team (CEO Andy Lowery since Dec 2023) and his present role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Epirus's Leonidas high-power microwave defeated 100% of a 49-drone swarm in a 2025 live-fire demo, and in Jan 2026 showed it could down fiber-optic-controlled drones that are immune to jamming.
current_role: Listed co-founder of Epirus (not on Epirus's current leadership page; current role unverified)
research_notes: Thin public footprint and web-search budget exhausted before a bio could be found; verify identity/current venture (e.g. LinkedIn) before outreach. Epirus press is only an indirect route since he appears to have left operations.

name: Nathan Mintz
profile: Nathan Mintz is listed as a founder of Epirus, the Los Angeles-area defense-tech startup behind Leonidas, a solid-state high-power-microwave system used to disable drone swarms. Epirus raised $70M (Series B, 2020), $200M (Series C, 2022) and a $250M Series D (March 2025) to scale Leonidas production. His personal background could not be independently verified in this pass.
interesting_fact: Epirus's Leonidas high-power-microwave system was selected for the U.S. Department of War directed-energy pilot program, and the company's $250M Series D in 2025 went to scaling its production for counter-drone defense.
current_role: Co-founder of Epirus (directed-energy/high-power-microwave defense company, Torrance CA); not listed on Epirus's current leadership page, so current role unconfirmed
research_notes: Research cut short by a web-search quota; Mintz's biography, current role and status were not verified - needs a follow-up pass. Epirus press contact is for the company, which he may no longer run day to day.

name: Conor McCarthy
profile: Irish software developer who co-founded Flipdish with his brother James in 2015, after earlier running software firm SawdeeSoft. Flipdish provides online ordering apps, kiosks and POS for takeaway and delivery restaurants; it became an Irish unicorn in 2022 with a $94M Tiger Global-led round at a ~$1.25B valuation, and McCarthy now focuses it on UK and Irish operators.
interesting_fact: He holds both the CEO and CTO titles at Flipdish, and his core business advice is to never do anything 'because it's standard' - everything, contracts included, is negotiable.
deep_cut_fact: He's a keen mountain biker on the Dublin Mountains trails and says it teaches a business lesson: focus on the 'happy path', not the rocks and trees, i.e. on what could go right rather than what could go wrong. His life mantra: 'Live and let live.'
current_role: Co-Founder, CEO & CTO, Flipdish (Dublin)
research_notes: Co-founder brother James McCarthy (CRO/CCO) is more often the commercial face. No published press email found on Flipdish site.

name: James McCarthy
profile: Irish entrepreneur who co-founded Flipdish in 2015 with his brother, CEO Conor McCarthy. Flipdish gives restaurants and takeaways their own branded online-ordering apps, kiosks and POS as an alternative to commission-heavy marketplaces; it became an Irish unicorn in 2022 at a $1.25B valuation after a ~$100M raise led by Tiger Global.
interesting_fact: Flipdish hit unicorn status in Jan 2022 at a $1.25B valuation, raising c.$100M to expand globally as hospitality digitised during the pandemic.
deep_cut_fact: Trained as an architect, he came up with The Christmas Shirt Company in 2011 while working at an architecture firm in Dublin during the recession, pitching Christmas shirts as a cooler alternative to the Christmas jumper and selling via Shopify.
current_role: Co-founder of Flipdish (Dublin); commercial lead (listed variously as COO, CCO and CRO)
research_notes: Conor McCarthy is the public face/CEO. The architect/Christmas-shirt link to the Flipdish co-founder comes via Conor's Business & Finance interview (https://businessandfinance.com/news/there-are-1000s-of-ways-to-achieve-something-and-no-single-correct-way-of-doing-anything-ceo-qa-with-conor-mccarthy-ceo-cto-of-flipdish/); double-check before use.

name: Lawrence Hofmann
profile: Practising interventional radiologist (10 years at Johns Hopkins, ~15 at Stanford, where he was Chief of IR for nearly two decades) who co-founded Grand Rounds with Owen Tripp in 2011-12; Grand Rounds merged with Doctor On Demand in 2021 to form Included Health, the navigation/virtual-care company valued in the billions. He remains a Stanford professor working on AI and digital health.
interesting_fact: He has published 100+ papers on minimally invasive treatment of blood clots (DVT) and cancer, holds two patents and is Global Principal Investigator for the first clinical trial testing a venous stent.
deep_cut_fact: He was the first-ever recipient of The Ohio State University School of Medicine's Early Career Achievement Award (2010), and says he has taken several devices 'from napkin stage to world-wide use'.
current_role: Professor of Interventional Radiology, Stanford School of Medicine; Chief of Industry Partnerships and Medical Director of Digital Health, Stanford Medicine; co-founder of Included Health
research_notes: Goes by 'Rusty'. Hurun lists him under Included Health. Spoke on BackTable podcast ep.100 about building Grand Rounds and gave 2024-25 Stanford Radiology Grand Rounds talk 'Starting a Silicon Valley Health Tech Company to Help Patients'. Academic route via Stanford likely most effective.

name: Owen Tripp
profile: Former Accenture health consultant and eBay data leader who co-founded ReputationDefender/Reputation.com (2006), then co-founded Grand Rounds Health (expert second opinions) with Dr. Rusty Hofmann. He led its 2021 merger with Doctor On Demand, rebranded as Included Health, which now offers navigation, virtual care, an AI assistant 'Dot' and, via the 2026 Firefly Health deal, employer health plans.
interesting_fact: He has a hard line on AI in healthcare: he argues incumbents mostly use AI 'to drive increased profit on existing transactions', while Included Health puts its assistant Dot directly in patients' hands with a clinician watching concerning conversations.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he pioneered eBay's approach to using unstructured data to understand buyer behavior, and co-founded online-reputation pioneer Reputation.com (originally ReputationDefender). He studied Spanish and English literature at Trinity College (Hartford) before a Stanford MBA.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Included Health (San Francisco)
research_notes: Writes guest columns (Fast Company, American Banker). Very active on AI-in-healthcare topics; Included Health published an AI clinical-governance framework June 2026. Education detail (Trinity) is from secondary profiles.

name: Dan Amiga
profile: Israeli Unit 8200 veteran who co-founded Fireglass (remote browser isolation), sold to Symantec in 2017, then co-founded Island with CEO Mike Fey in 2020. Island built the first enterprise browser - Chromium-based with built-in security and IT controls - and was valued at about $5B in 2025; Amiga now pushes its AI-governance products.
interesting_fact: He is credited with inventing two security categories: remote browser isolation at Fireglass and the 'enterprise browser' at Island, backed by Sequoia, Insight, Coatue and Cyberstarts.
deep_cut_fact: At Black Hat USA 2016 (Aug 3, Mandalay Bay) he and Dor Knafo presented 'Account Jumping: Post Infection Persistency & Lateral Movement in AWS', showing how attackers could evade CloudTrail auditing and persist in AWS accounts.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Island (enterprise browser), Dallas/Tel Aviv
public_contact: pr_agency: Andy Shane, Big Valley Marketing for Island: ashane@bigvalley.co | office_email: info@island.io (company general contact)
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker (RSA, Web Summit, Cybertech). Best route is Island's PR agency Big Valley Marketing.

name: Michael Fey
profile: Veteran security executive -- ex-President/COO of Symantec and Blue Coat, CTO of Intel Security and EVP of enterprise products at McAfee, and briefly CEO of D2iQ -- who co-founded Island with CTO Dan Amiga in 2020. Island builds a security-first enterprise browser and now pitches it as the control plane for AI agents; it raised a $400M Series F at a $6.4B valuation in Oct 2026.
interesting_fact: Island was born from an acquisition: Fey met co-founder Dan Amiga when Symantec bought Amiga's browser-isolation startup Fireglass in 2017; after leaving Symantec in 2018 Fey planned to move into private equity before the two decided to rebuild the browser itself.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Engineering Physics and Mathematics at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, co-authored the book 'Security Battleground: An Executive Field Manual', and deliberately built Island in Dallas rather than Silicon Valley.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Island (Dallas-based enterprise browser company)
public_contact: pr_agency: Andy Shane, Big Valley Marketing for Island - ashane@bigvalley.co | official_website: https://www.island.io/press
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker (RSA, Black Hat) and podcast guest; open to media. Strong AI-agents/enterprise-infrastructure angle. Series F source: https://newshub.medianet.com.au/2026/10/islandannounces-400-million-series-f-bringing-valuation-to-6-4-billion/175049/

name: Alex Zaccaria
profile: Melbourne entrepreneur who co-founded link-in-bio platform Linktree in 2016 with his brother Anthony and Nick Humphreys, after spotting the 'one link' problem while running music/digital agency Bolster. Linktree now serves tens of millions of creators and businesses; he is pushing the company into AI and commerce and is also an angel investor.
interesting_fact: Linktree began as an internal fix at Bolster, the digital agency the Zaccaria brothers ran for musicians and festivals, where managing clients' social accounts exposed the single-bio-link limit.
deep_cut_fact: Before Linktree he ran club nights and side businesses, including selling music consumables like guitar strings and drumsticks, and 'Happy Hobo', a mattress that turns a car's back seat into a bed or couch.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Linktree
research_notes: Accessible, media-friendly CEO (podcasts, conference speaker e.g. HumanX). Press email is the best route.

name: Anthony Zaccaria
profile: Australian entrepreneur who, with brother Alex Zaccaria and Nick Humphreys, ran music/entertainment digital agency Bolster before co-founding link-in-bio platform Linktree in Melbourne in 2016. Linktree grew to tens of millions of users (reported 50M+) and a US$1.3B valuation after its 2022 raise; Anthony has focused on commercial/operations roles and also angel invests.
interesting_fact: Linktree spread with almost no advertising; early users included Selena Gomez, Shawn Mendes, TikTok and Red Bull.
deep_cut_fact: He began in artist management for DJs and bands with his brother; Linktree was born from that work: 'there has to be a better way to direct fans to the content we're producing', since Instagram allowed only one bio link.
current_role: Co-founder (Chief Commercial Officer per several profiles), Linktree (Melbourne)
research_notes: Brother Alex Zaccaria (CEO) is the main public face; Anthony keeps a lower profile. Exact current title not confirmed on an official Linktree page.

name: Nick Humphreys
profile: Melbourne designer who co-founded Linktree in 2016 with brothers Alex and Anthony Zaccaria out of their music/entertainment digital agency Bolster, after tiring of constantly updating clients' single bio link. Linktree grew into a $1.3B 'link in bio' platform; he leads design and creative direction.
interesting_fact: Linktree started as an internal fix at Bolster in Collingwood, where the team kept rewriting artists' single social-media bio link.
deep_cut_fact: He spent four years in London designing for brands including Barclays and Manchester United, calls himself a 'brutalist design evangelist', and has two Webby nominations.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Creative Officer, Linktree

name: Felipe Capella
profile: Brazilian-born former corporate/M&A lawyer who co-founded freight-tech company Loadsmart with Ricardo Salgado in 2014. Loadsmart offers AI-driven brokerage, TMS (ShipperGuide), dock scheduling (Opendock) and in 2026 an AI-agent platform; it reached unicorn status in 2022. CEO since 2022 after serving as CPO, COO and co-CEO.
interesting_fact: Loadsmart claims the first fully automated truckload shipment (2016), booked and priced with no human involvement.
deep_cut_fact: He is an amateur photographer who plays guitar, piano and the Brazilian cavaquinho, has visited 47 countries, and holds a US 'Extraordinary Ability in Business' visa.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Loadsmart (New York)
public_contact: press_email: felipe@loadsmart.com (listed as media contact on Loadsmart's 2026 AI-agents release)
research_notes: Frequent podcast guest (Logistics of Logistics, FreightWaves). His own address appears as media contact on a 2026 release; verify before use.

name: Ricardo Salgado
education: Technical University of Lisbon
profile: Georgia Tech-trained engineer and former Goldman Sachs investor (New York, London, Brazil) who co-founded New York-based freight-tech company Loadsmart with Felipe Capella in 2014. Loadsmart automates full-truckload brokerage with instant pricing and booking via API and reached unicorn status in 2022. Salgado led as CEO until Capella took over in May 2022.
interesting_fact: Loadsmart claimed the first nationwide instant pricing and booking for full-truckload shipments and the first enterprise API of its kind; about 45% of its early team were engineers and data scientists.
deep_cut_fact: Before freight, he spent years at Goldman Sachs, including helping set up a capital-structure investing team in Brazil covering Latin American credit and equities - where he first saw how fragmented freight brokerage was.
current_role: Co-founder of Loadsmart; reportedly Executive Chairman since May 2022 (Felipe Capella is CEO)
research_notes: Current title not confirmed by a primary Loadsmart source. FreightWaves speaker page: https://live.freightwaves.com/event-speakers/ricardo-salgado. Route via Loadsmart.

name: Jake Benson
profile: Jake Benson founded the crypto tax and back-office software vendor Libra in 2014 and rebranded it as Lukka in March 2019 to emphasise crypto data as well as software. Lukka later raised from State Street and S&P Global, and its pricing data underpins S&P Dow Jones crypto indices. Benson left in June 2020, and I found no public record of what he has done since.
interesting_fact: Lukka is named after Luca Pacioli, the 15th-century Franciscan friar who helped popularise double-entry bookkeeping. The 2019 rebrand from 'Libra' was meant to position the company as 'a software and data company for the crypto world'.
deep_cut_fact: Under its original name, Libra, the company raised $25M in two equity rounds. Its December 2020 Series C, led by State Street with S&P Global and CPA.com, was its first equity raise after the rebrand.
current_role: Founder and former CEO of Lukka (New York crypto-asset data and software); left the company in June 2020; current role not found
research_notes: He left Lukka in June 2020 (CoinDesk) and has had no public profile since. Lukka's unicorn valuation came after he left. I found no verified current contact; LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Amos Haggiag
profile: Amos Haggiag co-founded Tel Aviv-based Optibus in 2014 with CTO Eitan Yanovsky, a fellow Ben-Gurion University math/CS student. Optibus's cloud and AI platform plans, schedules and runs bus networks for transit operators worldwide. It became a unicorn, and in June 2026 he launched 'Optibus Agent', an AI agent for transit operations.
interesting_fact: He calls mass transit 'a trillion-dollar market that (almost) everyone is ignoring'. Before Optibus he did algorithm design at Microsoft, Collarity and Siemens.
deep_cut_fact: He has never owned a car. He gets around by bus and on personal electric devices such as a Onewheel or electric skateboard, and Optibus gives free e-scooters or e-bikes to employees who use public transit. He says the office sometimes looks 'like a parking lot for electric bikes.'
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Optibus (public-transit planning and operations software)
public_contact: office_email: info@optibus.com (company general inbox) | contact_form: https://www.optibus.com/contact-us/
research_notes: Active public speaker (WEF author page, Smart Mobility Summit May 2026). Still CEO per METRO Magazine (June 2026).

name: Eitan Yanovsky
profile: Eitan Yanovsky studied math and computer science at Ben-Gurion University, where he met Amos Haggiag. He was later an R&D team leader at GigaSpaces. In 2014 the pair founded Optibus to solve bus and transit scheduling with optimization algorithms. Optibus software is used in over 1,000 cities, and the company had raised about $170M by 2022. Yanovsky leads research and technology.
interesting_fact: The idea came from co-founder Amos Haggiag's father, a long-time CFO of Israeli bus company Kavim, who challenged him to write software to plan bus routes. The founders treated it as a traveling-salesman-style puzzle.
deep_cut_fact: Optibus was a side project for nearly a decade: Yanovsky (at GigaSpaces) and Haggiag (at Microsoft Israel) kept 'toying with this idea during our free time', testing it on data from small Israeli bus companies, before quitting to found the company.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Optibus (AI-based public-transit planning and scheduling software, Tel Aviv)
public_contact: office_email: info@optibus.com (company general inbox) | official_website: https://optibus.com/about
research_notes: Optibus's about page confirms him as Co-Founder and CTO. Relevant to the energy angle: Optibus also does electric-bus fleet planning (not checked in detail). CEO Amos Haggiag is the more public co-founder.

name: Gady Shlasky
profile: Israeli co-founder of Optibus, the AI-driven public-transport planning and scheduling platform founded in 2011 with Amos Haggiag (now CEO) and Eitan Yanovsky. Shlasky was the company's early CEO, selling real-time bus rescheduling to operators such as Egged; Hurun lists Optibus as a $1B unicorn. Directory sources say he has since left the company.
interesting_fact: In 2014, as Optibus CEO, he said the startup already managed about 60% of Israel's bus schedules and could save operators 7-10% a year by reassigning buses in real time, helping them avoid municipal fines of up to NIS 10,000 for running late.
deep_cut_fact: Early on, Optibus was enrolled in IBM's Alpha Zone accelerator and named one of seven finalists in Ernst & Young's 'The Pitch' contest; Shlasky flagged airlines as a possible long-term market beyond buses.
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO/President of Optibus (transit-planning software); no longer with the company - current role unknown
research_notes: Left Optibus (per directory sources); current venture not verified. Optibus general contact info@optibus.com is published on optibus.com but is a company address, not his. Has a LinkedIn (il.linkedin.com/in/gadyshlasky) - not verified as active.

name: Kisik Bae
profile: Bae Ki-sik, a Seoul National University electrical engineering graduate and former Samsung Electronics corporate-venture investor, founded RIDI in 2008 betting on smartphone-era content. RIDI became Korea's leading e-book platform and then shifted toward webtoons and web novels; it raised KRW 120B from GIC and others in 2022 at unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: RIDI first tried producing comics with dozens of hired artists, then pivoted to e-books because text only needed digitizing; despite skeptical publishers, he had deals with about 200 publishers by 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding RIDI he worked on Samsung Electronics' corporate venture investment team; in the early days, he says, 'I would visit publishers during the day and develop the service at night with our developers.'
current_role: Founder and CEO, RIDI Corporation (Seoul; e-books, webtoons and web novels)
research_notes: RIDI was selected for the Tokyo Stock Exchange Asia Startup Hub in 2024 and 2025 (https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025092908590212822). No published press email found.

name: Mike Moreno
profile: Mike Moreno co-founded Route with Evan Walker. The Utah company launched in January 2019 and sells package protection, visual order tracking and post-purchase tools to e-commerce merchants. Forbes listed it among the 'next billion-dollar startups', and it later raised a Series C at a reported $1.4B valuation. Data providers list Moreno as co-founder/VP.
interesting_fact: Forbes's list of startups most likely to become unicorns named Mike Moreno and Evan Walker as Route's founders, citing $91M raised and estimated 2020 revenue of $34M.
current_role: Co-founder, Route (Lehi, Utah post-purchase / package-protection platform); listed as VP
research_notes: Very low public profile. Most press coverage features co-founder Evan Walker. A 2025 profile says Eric Kobe is now CEO (not verified). LinkedIn is likely the best route.

name: Brian Denker
profile: Idaho-rooted cloud entrepreneur who cofounded Tackle.io in 2016 with longtime friend Dillon Woods after years working in cloud computing since AWS's 2006 launch. Tackle helps software vendors sell through AWS, Microsoft and Google Cloud marketplaces, became a $1B+ unicorn, and agreed to be acquired by AppDirect in December 2025.
interesting_fact: Tackle's platform supports over $20 billion in cloud hyperscaler marketplace transactions, per AppDirect.
deep_cut_fact: Tackle began with just him and Dillon Woods 'hacking away in a shared office above Goldy's in downtown Boise'; New Relic became their 'lighthouse customer'. He splits his time between Boise, Riggins (Idaho) and Boston.
current_role: Cofounder and longtime COO, Tackle.io (Boise), acquired by AppDirect (announced Dec 2025); current post-deal role unconfirmed
research_notes: Outdoorsy, Idaho-proud founder; friends with cofounder Dillon Woods since the early 2000s. Riggins/Boston detail is from Tackle's company page (via search). No published personal or press email found; post-acquisition role unclear.

name: Dillon Woods
profile: Idaho native and Boise State CS grad (2005) who spent a decade at California data companies (CTO at zData and Alpine Data) before co-founding Tackle.io in Boise in 2016. Tackle helps software vendors sell through AWS/Azure/Google Cloud marketplaces; it raised ~$148m and was acquired by AppDirect in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Tackle turned cloud-hyperscaler marketplaces into a sales channel for SaaS vendors and became a Boise-born unicorn; AppDirect bought it in Dec 2025 to add native hyperscaler-marketplace integration to its B2B subscription-commerce platform.
deep_cut_fact: He minored in philosophy at Boise State and was already 'playing around with starting companies' as a student; Tackle's official HQ sits in downtown Boise above Goldy's, about 50 feet from Boise State's computer-science department at City Central Plaza. His advice: 'solve a problem that you actually have.'
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Tackle.io (Boise, ID) - acquired by AppDirect in Dec 2025; post-acquisition role not confirmed
research_notes: Hurun lists him as founder; John Jahnke was Tackle's CEO. Since the AppDirect acquisition, press goes through AppDirect's PR agency (Bospar). Cloud-marketplace angle rather than energy/data-center hardware.

name: Avi Meir
education: IESE Business School; Paris Descartes University
profile: Serial founder who co-founded Hotel Ninjas (sold to Booking.com in 2014) and then founded TravelPerk in Barcelona in 2015 to bring consumer-grade tech to business travel. Rebranded Perk in Nov 2025 as an AI-native travel and spend platform, it passed $300M annualized revenue with 10,000+ customer companies and moved to dual HQs in London and Boston.
interesting_fact: When COVID made business travel effectively illegal in early 2020, Meir cut costs without layoffs, kept hiring engineers and bought two competitors cheaply; ARR went from ~$20M pre-pandemic to over $300M.
deep_cut_fact: He likens his pandemic playbook to a hibernating bear ('preserve the core, lose the fat'), and says the lesson he took from Booking.com after selling Hotel Ninjas was that 'winning globally means building locally.'
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Perk (formerly TravelPerk)
research_notes: Rebrand announced Nov 4, 2025 (https://www.perk.com/press-release/travelperk-rebrands-to-perk-the-intelligent-platform-powering-real-work/). Talkative, candid interviewee; IPO talk in recent coverage.

name: Javier Suarez
profile: Javier Suarez co-founded Barcelona-based business travel platform TravelPerk in 2015 with Avi Meir and Ron Levin, serving as chief product officer; it later reached a multi-billion-dollar valuation. In 2020 he co-founded Oliva with Sancar Sahin, an employee wellbeing platform offering therapy and workshops used in 27+ countries and 14 languages, backed by Molten Ventures and Stride VC.
interesting_fact: TravelPerk was born from an observation at Booking.com: the founders, both ex-Booking employees, saw that the company focused on leisure travel while business travel was a poorly served market.
deep_cut_fact: Before TravelPerk he worked at Booking.com in business development; his co-founder Avi Meir had joined Booking when it acquired Meir's startup Hotel Ninjas in 2014.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Oliva (workplace mental health platform); co-founder and former CPO of TravelPerk (now Perk)
research_notes: Now focused on Oliva (CEO). He has spoken publicly about founder burnout as Oliva's origin; let him lead on that topic. Sources differ on his Booking.com role (product performance & innovation vs business development). No published press email found.

name: Ron Levin
profile: Technologist who co-founded TravelPerk in 2015 with Avi Meir and Javier Suarez, leading engineering as CTO. The company, now called Perk, is a travel and spend-management platform with dual HQ in Boston and London and a large Barcelona hub; a 2025 Series E ($200M) valued it at about $2.7B.
interesting_fact: Perk raised $409M through its 2022 Series D to reach unicorn status; in January 2025 it raised a $200M Series E led by Atomico (valuing it at $2.7B) and acquired Zurich-based spend-management platform Yokoy.
current_role: Co-founder of Perk (formerly TravelPerk); originally its CTO - current position not confirmed by a primary source
research_notes: Very low public profile. A 2025 Perk press release reportedly names Robin Smith as CTO, so Levin may have stepped back from the role; an aggregator claims he is now at a VC firm but this is unverified. Perk press office is the published route.

name: Ricardo Amper
profile: Mexico City-born serial entrepreneur who founded and sold two earlier companies (one in food, one in chemicals) before moving to the Bay Area in 2015 to start Incode. Incode began as a face-recognition photo-sharing app and pivoted to AI-based identity verification and fraud prevention for banks, fintechs and governments; it was valued at about $1.25B in 2021.
interesting_fact: Incode's origins are in consumer photos: its first app automatically shared pictures with whoever face recognition detected in them, and wrestling with bad, low-light phone photos shaped its later identity-verification tech for low-end phones in Latin America.
deep_cut_fact: Apple took Incode's early photo-sharing app on a roadshow as one of three companies showcasing its on-device machine-learning framework, but the app 'couldn't get traction', prompting the pivot into identity verification.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Incode Technologies
public_contact: office_email: contact@incode.com | contact_form: https://incode.com/contact-us/ | official_website: https://incode.com
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker (e.g. Money20/20) and interviewee; contact@incode.com is the company's general address. Has an active media presence, so a podcast pitch on AI/deepfake fraud is plausible.

name: Brian Barlow
profile: Infrastructure investor with three decades in private markets who led infrastructure investing for Alphabet's urban-innovation arm (Sidewalk Labs), then co-founded SIP, spun out of Alphabet in 2020 with about $400M. SIP builds energy and digital infrastructure businesses, including Verrus (flexible, grid-friendly data centers) and Everyday Electric (residential virtual power plants).
interesting_fact: SIP's portfolio sits right at the AI-power nexus: Verrus builds next-generation flexible data centers, and Everyday Electric (formerly Renew Home) aggregates millions of homes into virtual power plants and acquired Smartcar to add EVs to its VPP.
deep_cut_fact: Earlier in his career he was a senior member of Scion Capital, Michael Burry's hedge fund made famous by 'The Big Short', and he was a managing director at American Infrastructure Funds before joining Alphabet.
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners (SIP)
public_contact: press_email: press@sidewalkinfra.com | office_email: info@sidewalkinfra.com | official_website: https://www.sidewalkinfra.com
research_notes: Excellent fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Did a GrowthCap podcast interview (June 2026) on AI infrastructure. Co-founded SIP with Jonathan Winer (Fortune, 2020: https://fortune.com/2020/05/07/alphabet-vets-infrastructure-funding-400-million/). Best route: press@sidewalkinfra.com.

name: Jonathan Winer
profile: Jonathan Winer is a former Alphabet/Sidewalk Labs executive who co-founded Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners (SIP) with Brian Barlow. SIP spun out of Alphabet in 2020 with a $400M Series A from Alphabet and Ontario Teachers'. It builds tech-enabled infrastructure platforms, and its current companies include Verrus (flexible, grid-friendly data centers) and Everyday Electric (residential virtual power plants).
interesting_fact: SIP's portfolio sits squarely in the energy and data-center space: Verrus builds next-generation data centers designed for flexibility, and Everyday Electric aggregates millions of households into virtual power plants.
deep_cut_fact: In SIP's first-ever interview (Fortune, May 2020) Winer pitched it as building 'unglamorous but sorely needed' infrastructure such as recycling sorting plants, consulting mayors rather than lobbying: 'We're not trying to sell our widgets.'
current_role: Co-founder and former co-CEO, Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners (no longer on SIP's team page, which lists Brian Barlow as Co-Founder and CEO). Current role unknown.
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.sidewalkinfra.com/contact (SIP contact page) | podcast: Guest on HASI 'Climate Positive' podcast E43 (March 2023)
research_notes: Highly relevant to energy and data-center themes (Verrus, VPPs). As of this check he is NOT listed on SIP's team page, so he has likely left SIP, and his new activity was not found; verify before outreach. Aggregators say he founded Nereus Capital, a private-equity firm, in 2010 (not verified here).

name: Michael Delucia
profile: Infrastructure investor (Brown; JPMorgan banking) with 18+ years in project finance: early wind/solar IPP lending at HSH Nordbank, Nereus Capital, and power-project financing at Macquarie Energy. He joined Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs, then the founding team of spin-out Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners, which Hurun counts as a $1B unicorn. Later at Wellington's Climate Innovation Fund, now at Montauk.
interesting_fact: Montauk Capital, where he is a partner, backs the 'Electron Economy'. Its portfolio includes a home energy storage and power retailer, an enhanced-geothermal developer, an off-grid data-center development platform, AI-powered ERP for industrials and data centers, and AI tools for large-load grid interconnection.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career at HSH Nordbank he was an early investor and financier in some of the first wind and solar independent power producers in North America. At Wellington's Climate Innovation Fund he led investments in grid-enhancing technologies.
current_role: Partner, Montauk Capital (NY 'Electron Economy' venture capital and venture studio); adjunct faculty, NYU School of Professional Studies
public_contact: office_email: info@montaukcap.com (Montauk Capital general inbox) | office_email: mrd9717@nyu.edu (NYU SPS faculty directory listing) | contact_form: https://montaukcap.com/contact
research_notes: The 'founder' label is loose: SIP's co-founders are Jonathan Winer and Brian Barlow, and DeLucia was on the founding team (Principal 2019-21, Partner 2021-22). He is not a UHNW founder and has no meaningful personal SIP valuation. Still a highly relevant energy/data-center infrastructure guest and likely approachable.

name: David Leiberman
profile: New York musician, teacher and app builder. He co-founded children's music-app maker Mibblio and then, with his cousin Sammy Rubin, Triller, the AI-powered music-video app (founded around 2015) that later attracted celebrity investors and a reported $1B+ valuation. He later co-founded Console, a Web3 Discord-style community platform, with Chris Castig.
interesting_fact: Triller started as a family project: he co-founded it with his cousin Sammy Rubin, after the two had built Mibblio, a music-making app for toddlers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Triller he helped create the Disney Frozen Karaoke app. He describes himself as a teacher and musician, and also co-founded The Lorca, a contemporary retreat in the Catskills plus a midcentury motel in the Adirondacks.
current_role: Co-founder of Triller, Mibblio and Console; co-founder of The Lorca (hospitality retreats, self-described). Current day-to-day role unclear.
research_notes: No longer prominent at Triller. Avoid Triller's later corporate/financial troubles in outreach. Facts come mostly from his self-written Product Hunt profile. The Lorca's site appears to be thelorca.com, but I could not confirm his link to it independently.

name: Sammy Rubin
profile: New York app developer who, with collaborator David Leiberman, created the kids' music platform Mibblio and the chart-topping 'Disney Frozen: Karaoke' app, then launched Triller in July 2015 with music-video director Colin Tilley. Triller began as an AI auto-editing music-video app and later became a TikTok rival under new owners. His current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Triller launched in July 2015 as a collaboration with director Colin Tilley (known for videos for Kendrick Lamar, Justin Bieber and Nicki Minaj). Its auto-editing tech assembled several takes into a finished music video.
deep_cut_fact: Before Triller, he and Leiberman built Mibblio, a children's music-book app platform, and the chart-topping 'Disney Frozen: Karaoke' app.
current_role: Co-founder of Triller (current role not found)
research_notes: Do not confuse him with UK insurtech founder Sammy Rubin (YuLife, PruProtect), who is a different person; aggregators such as MarketScreener conflate the two. The Triller co-founder keeps a very low profile. Triller (later TrillerNet) went through ownership changes and turmoil, so avoid that topic. No published contact found.

name: Jenn Knight
profile: Salesforce-ecosystem engineer who co-founded Denver-based insurtech AgentSync in 2018 with Niji Sabharwal after building back-office systems at LinkedIn, Dropbox and Stripe. AgentSync automates producer licensing and compliance for insurers; it bootstrapped before raising from Craft Ventures and others and reached a $1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: AgentSync bootstrapped to early product-market fit and only began pitching VCs in March 2020; investors initially said insurance's $1.3 trillion market was 'not cool enough.'
deep_cut_fact: Without a CS degree, she began her tech career as LinkedIn's first Salesforce engineer, building its Salesforce engineering and solutions-architecture team; at Dropbox she migrated the company's ERP before its IPO, and earlier did consulting at Bluewolf.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, AgentSync (per company/podcast materials; latest title not re-verified in 2026)
research_notes: Has done many podcasts (FNO InsureTech ep. 275, The SaaS Podcast #426) - receptive to podcast appearances. No dedicated press email published; company newsroom at agentsync.io/newsroom.

name: Niranjan Sabharwal
profile: Niranjan 'Niji' Sabharwal co-founded AgentSync in 2018 with his wife Jenn Knight, the company's CTO. AgentSync makes insurance producer licensing and compliance software for carriers, agencies, MGAs and insurtechs and became a unicorn in 2021. He was previously CEO and now serves as executive board chair.
interesting_fact: AgentSync grew out of his job fixing Zenefits' agent-licensing compliance crisis. After Zenefits exited insurance, it licensed the intellectual property to him, and that became AgentSync.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zenefits he led sales strategy and operations at LinkedIn. At Zenefits he led the producer licensing and broker compliance response team.
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Board Chair, AgentSync (Denver)
research_notes: The AgentSync site publishes only sales@ and support@ emails, with no press address. Use the contact form or newsroom (https://agentsync.io/newsroom). Goes by 'Niji'.

name: Assaf Resnick
profile: UC Berkeley Haas graduate who started at Moody's on Wall Street, then invested for Sequoia Capital (Israel) before co-founding BigPanda in 2012 with Elik Eizenberg. BigPanda, a unicorn, correlates IT monitoring alerts and automates incident response; in 2025-26 it repositioned around 'agentic ITOps' and an IT knowledge graph.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for BigPanda while at Sequoia, where he saw that as companies moved to the cloud, IT Ops teams were overwhelmed by alert noise from fragmented monitoring tools.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he began his career on Wall Street at Moody's. He says he left to 'marry my passion for tech with my background in investments', and that the 'courage and conviction' of Sequoia's founders inspired him to start BigPanda.
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, BigPanda (agentic AI for IT operations / AIOps)
public_contact: press_email: jbarbour@bigpanda.io (Jenne Barbour, Head of Corporate Marketing, listed as BigPanda contact on July 2026 release) | official_website: https://www.bigpanda.io/leadership/assaf-resnick/
research_notes: Active speaker in 2026 (Emerj AI in Business podcast, July 2026; BigPanda 26 keynote, Atlanta, April 2026). Earlier 2026 releases list Adam Blau (VP Product Marketing) as media contact. bigpanda.io blocked automated fetches (403), so the leadership-page URL is from search results. Data-center angle: IT ops reliability and incident automation.

name: Elik Eizenberg
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded BigPanda (AIOps / IT incident intelligence, backed by Sequoia) in 2012 with Assaf Resnick and served as CTO as it reached unicorn status. He has since founded Scroll AI, focused on reliable, ethical AI that acts as a trusted partner to human leaders.
interesting_fact: He describes 25 years of deploying mission-critical AI across finance, operations and security, and frames his mission around 'the humanist side of technology'.
deep_cut_fact: Before BigPanda he led development of highly scalable data pipelines in the Israeli intelligence service, then designed autonomous trading algorithms for a hedge fund - experiences that made him sceptical of ML vendor hype.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Scroll AI (AI 'mentor' for employees); co-founder and former CTO, BigPanda
research_notes: Name sometimes spelled 'Eisenberg'. No published contact email found for Scroll AI; LinkedIn or Scroll's site are likely routes.

name: Conway Teng
profile: Former McKinsey consultant who held finance and go-to-market roles at Gusto and OrderAhead (acquired by Square), where he managed sales commissions. In 2017 he co-founded CaptivateIQ with college friends Mark Schopmeyer and Hubert Wong (YC 2018) to replace commission spreadsheets with no-code incentive-compensation software; it has raised $164.6M from Sequoia, Accel, ICONIQ and others, and he is now listed as CEO.
interesting_fact: CaptivateIQ says it runs about 8 trillion real-time commission calculations per month for 1,000+ customers.
deep_cut_fact: CaptivateIQ was born when co-founder Mark Schopmeyer, nearly ready to quit over building commission spreadsheets, caught up with college friends Conway and Hubert and found they shared the same frustration; the three quit their jobs to start the company.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, CaptivateIQ (San Francisco)
research_notes: Previously co-CEO with Schopmeyer; company About page now lists Teng as CEO and Schopmeyer as President. A Comparably profile says he co-founded loyalty company Fivestars, but this was not verified.

name: Hubert Wong
profile: Software engineer who co-founded CaptivateIQ in 2017 with Mark Schopmeyer and Conway Teng. The no-code platform designs and calculates sales commissions; it went through Y Combinator (Winter 2018) and reached a $1.25B valuation with a $100M raise in January 2022. Wong leads engineering as CTO.
interesting_fact: CaptivateIQ's backers include Sequoia, Accel and Y Combinator. Its January 2022 round valued the commission-software startup at $1.25B less than five years after launch.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, CaptivateIQ (San Francisco)
research_notes: Low-profile technical founder; co-CEOs Schopmeyer and Teng are the public faces. Profiles say he was previously a senior software engineer at Vungle, and Comparably adds Amazon and founding engineer at Copilot (acquired by OpenTable), but I could not open those pages to verify.

name: Doron Somech
profile: Doron Somech is a Tel Aviv engineer listed as a co-founder of Unit, the embedded-banking platform (founded 2019 with CEO Itai Damti) valued at about $1B. He is no longer on Unit's leadership page; his GitHub now points to Submilli, an open-source WebAssembly sandbox runtime for 'code-mode' AI agents.
interesting_fact: His newest project, Submilli, runs code written by AI agents in isolated WebAssembly sandboxes with no network or file access by default, enforcing permissions on each call with an audit trail.
current_role: Co-founder of Unit (embedded-banking infrastructure, NYC/Tel Aviv); apparently now building Submilli, a secure runtime for AI code agents

name: Itai Damti
profile: Israeli fintech operator who co-founded brokerage-tech provider Leverate (grew to ~160 staff without VC money) and later ran its Asia-Pacific business from Hong Kong. In 2019 he and Doron Somech founded Unit, an embedded-finance/banking-as-a-service platform letting companies launch accounts, cards and lending 'in weeks, not years'; it became a unicorn in 2022 ($100M Series C led by Insight).
interesting_fact: He and CTO Doron Somech had both left Leverate in 2015-16 and reunited about three years later to start Unit, which hit a $1.2B valuation within roughly three years.
deep_cut_fact: Before Unit he was a Fintech Entrepreneur in Residence at 500 Startups and EIR at hardware accelerator HAX, and is a special advisor to Hong Kong investment bank Ion Pacific; he has written guest columns for TechCrunch.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Unit (New York)
research_notes: Active writer/speaker on embedded finance. Route via Unit marketing/press or LinkedIn.

name: Chris Mansi
profile: Newcastle-raised, Cambridge-trained neurosurgeon who operated at Queen Square and King's College hospitals in London before moving to the US for a Stanford MBA. In 2016 he co-founded Viz.ai with ML postdoc David Golan; it won the first FDA clearance for an AI triage platform (stroke) and by its 10th anniversary (July 2026) was in 2,000 hospitals covering ~230M patients with 50+ AI care pathways.
interesting_fact: Viz.ai's software now 'helps one patient every six seconds'; Mansi calls it 'an AI safety net that works consistently across hospital settings'. The idea came from seeing surgeries go well yet patients die or end up disabled because getting them to the OR took too long.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012, while still a neurosurgeon, he started Edusurg, an online exam-prep business for junior surgeons; at Stanford he tinkered with 'every technology I could find', including 3D-printing brains for surgical practice and a cranial-nerve stimulation device.
current_role: CEO and co-founder, Viz.ai (AI disease detection and care coordination, San Francisco)
public_contact: pr_agency: viz.ai@solcomms.co (Caroline Rueve, Viz.ai media contact) | official_website: https://www.viz.ai/ | contact_form: https://www.viz.ai/contact | x: https://twitter.com/viz_ai (company) | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/viz.ai (company)
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker and WEF contributor; accessible via PR agency. Healthcare AI rather than energy; angle could be AI deployment at scale in hospitals.

name: David Golan
profile: Israeli machine-learning researcher (PhD in statistics & ML, Tel Aviv University) who, as a Fulbright postdoc at Stanford applying deep learning to medical imaging and genetics, co-founded Viz.ai in 2016 with Chris Mansi and served as CTO. Viz.ai built the first FDA-cleared AI triage system for stroke (2018), now installed in 800+ hospitals in the US and Europe; he remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Viz.ai's software was the first AI-powered automatic stroke-triage system cleared by the FDA, alerting specialists directly so patients can be treated faster; it runs in 800+ hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Before academia he founded the machine-learning team at Israeli startup b-hive Networks, acquired by VMware in 2008, and later co-authored 20+ scientific papers including three in the journal Science.
current_role: Co-founder and board director, Viz.ai (former CTO); current operating role not found
research_notes: Podcast entry is a past guest appearance (Brains Behind AI episode on building Viz.ai), not his own show; useful as prep. Left day-to-day role at Viz.ai; member of TechAviv founders club. No published personal/press email found; Viz.ai media inquiries via company site.

name: Manoj Ramachandran
profile: London paediatric/young-adult orthopaedic surgeon who co-founded Viz.ai in 2016 with Chris Mansi and David Golan; its FDA-cleared AI care-coordination tools (stroke first, now cardio, vascular, oncology) made it a ~$1bn+ unicorn. He combines NHS practice at Barts with ventures, most recently halfloop (patient data for implant recipients).
interesting_fact: Viz.ai was his fourth business venture; in 2016 he described operating on children on Mondays and 'switching on in the evenings when Silicon Valley wakes up on the West Coast' to build the company.
deep_cut_fact: He became an orthopaedic consultant at a very young age (his self-described career highlight), has a keen interest in medical history - arguing most health solutions 'have been explored at some point in history but now we are adding a technological layer' - and is lead author of a Hodder Arnold basic orthopaedic sciences guide for fellowship exam candidates.
current_role: Co-founder of Viz.ai; Consultant Orthopaedic & Trauma Surgeon (and reported Director of Innovation) at Barts Health NHS Trust, London; CEO & co-founder of halfloop (per profiles)
research_notes: Not a Viz.ai executive (CEO is Chris Mansi), so Viz.ai is an indirect route; halfloop or Barts Health innovation channels may be better. Titles (Professor, Director of Innovation, halfloop CEO) come from aggregator profiles - verify. Textbook detail via search results, not read directly. Personal wealth unconfirmed.

name: Rujul Zaparde
profile: Two-time YC founder who co-founded Zip in 2020 with Lu Cheng and Felix Meng to fix slow enterprise purchasing with an AI 'intake-to-pay' procurement platform. Zip raised $190M at a $2.2B valuation and says its agentic platform processed $355B in spend in 2025; he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: His first company, FlightCar (YC Winter 2013), was pitched as 'the Airbnb of car rentals at airports', letting travellers rent out their parked cars; it operated at 12 US airports with backers including Brian Chesky.
deep_cut_fact: Between FlightCar and Zip he worked at Y Combinator as a Visiting Partner.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Zip (procurement software, San Francisco)
public_contact: press_email: press@ziphq.com | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/rujulz | official_website: https://ziphq.com/about
research_notes: Media-friendly (YC talks with Dalton Caldwell on enterprise sales). Route via press@ziphq.com.

name: Thomas Jermoluk
profile: Veteran tech executive ('TJ'): Bell Labs and HP engineer, then president/COO of Silicon Graphics (1992-96), founding chairman & CEO of broadband pioneer @Home (led the 1999 Excite merger), and a Kleiner Perkins general partner. In 2020 he co-founded passwordless-authentication company Beyond Identity with Jim Clark, serving as CEO before handing over to Jasson Casey.
interesting_fact: At SGI he oversaw 11,000+ employees and drove deals including the MIPS and Cray Research acquisitions; he and Netscape founder Jim Clark reunited to launch Beyond Identity with $30m Series A.
deep_cut_fact: A self-described 'original nighttime hacker', he got into computing in Hawaii when his 11th-grade math teacher had him writing programs on rented computer time, then joined the night-owl computer culture in Virginia Tech's McBryde Hall (CS '78, MS '79).
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Beyond Identity (CEO is now Jasson Casey)
research_notes: Long-time Silicon Valley figure, Virginia Tech alumnus. No published personal or press email found; route via Beyond Identity.

name: Kevin Bennett
profile: Washington, DC-area serial entrepreneur who led MotoRefi, incubated by QED Investors in 2016, as CEO from 2018 and rebranded it Caribou in 2021 as it expanded from auto refinancing into auto insurance; the company reached a $1B+ valuation. He reportedly stepped down as CEO in 2023 and has been building new startups since.
interesting_fact: He has said Caribou was the fifth startup he worked on, pitching it as a 'mission-driven fintech' to help the American middle class save on a $1.4 trillion auto-debt market long untouched by digital innovation.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining the 2021 rebrand from MotoRefi to Caribou on a December podcast, he noted that caribou are also called reindeer - 'seasonally appropriate.'
current_role: Former CEO of Caribou (auto refinance fintech, formerly MotoRefi); reportedly left in Sept 2023 and has since started new fintech/proptech ventures (unverified)
public_contact: podcast: Fintech One-on-One podcast #335 with Kevin Bennett
research_notes: Sources differ on whether he was a founder or joined as CEO in 2018. Post-Caribou ventures (Homezen, Further) only from secondary sources; confirm via LinkedIn.

name: Carolyn Childers
profile: Former Handy and Primary Venture Partners executive who co-founded Chief in New York in January 2019 with ex-Casper VP Lindsay Kaplan. Chief grew from 400 members to 20,000+, became a $1.1B unicorn in 2022 after a $100M CapitalG-led round, and runs clubhouses in New York, Chicago, San Francisco and Washington DC. In 2025 the founders handed the CEO role to Alison Moore.
interesting_fact: Chief grew from 400 members in March 2019 to 20,000 senior women leaders by October 2022; about 70% of members had their membership paid by their employers, and speakers have included Michelle Obama and Indra Nooyi.
deep_cut_fact: Before Chief she worked at venture firm Primary Venture Partners, which then backed Chief as an early investor alongside General Catalyst chairman Ken Chenault, who joined Chief's board. She told Chief's founding story on Masters of Scale in April 2022 ('How Chief became a phenomenon').
current_role: Co-founder, Chief (private network for senior women executives); stepped back from the CEO role when Alison Moore was appointed CEO in January 2025 (current title not confirmed)
public_contact: press_email: press@chief.com | office_email: hello@chief.com (general) | official_website: https://chief.com
research_notes: Her role since the January 2025 CEO transition is not stated in the sources I could access; check before outreach. The deep-cut Primary link combines two Wikipedia statements (her former employer, and Primary as an early investor).
