name: Lindsay Kaplan
profile: American entrepreneur and brand marketer who co-founded Chief, the private membership network for senior executive women, with Carolyn Childers. Chief raised $100M in 2022 at a $1B+ valuation, one of the fastest women-founded companies to unicorn status. She is also an angel investor, an investing partner at Next Wave NYC (2024) and, from 2026, a venture partner at Bullish.
interesting_fact: Before Chief she was Casper's first full-time employee, running communications and brand marketing, and was named one of Business Insider's Most Innovative CMOs.
deep_cut_fact: She started out in publishing at Oxford University Press, Time Out New York and ELLE, and is an Executive Member of the International Academy of Digital Arts and Sciences, serving as an executive judge for the Webby Awards.
current_role: Co-founder, Chief; venture partner at Bullish (2026)
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker (Web Summit, TechCrunch Disrupt, Fast Company Innovation Festival) - likely receptive to podcasts. Web search budget ran out before press contacts could be checked.

name: Christoph Gebald
profile: German mechanical engineer who co-founded Climeworks in 2009 with Jan Wurzbacher while both were PhD students researching CO2 capture at ETH Zurich. Climeworks became the leading direct-air-capture company and an ETH 'unicorn' after a CHF 600M raise in 2022. It runs Orca (2021) and Mammoth (2024) in Iceland, which use geothermal power and store CO2 in basalt with Carbfix.
interesting_fact: Mammoth, launched in May 2024 at Iceland's Hellisheiði geothermal plant, can capture up to 36,000 t of CO2 a year, about 9x its predecessor Orca. The captured CO2 is mineralised into rock underground.
deep_cut_fact: Climeworks took its first outside investment in 2011 to build a modular prototype, two years after spinning out of ETH; it didn't show a working prototype until 2014, five years after founding.
current_role: Co-founder, co-CEO and board member, Climeworks (Zurich)
research_notes: Excellent energy-podcast fit: direct air capture depends on cheap clean power (geothermal in Iceland), and Climeworks is involved in US DAC hubs. Climeworks' site blocked automated reads, so I couldn't extract a press email; use the press page. Co-CEO Jan Wurzbacher is often the company's spokesperson.

name: Jan Wurzbacher
profile: German mechanical engineer who, with fellow ETH Zurich student Christoph Gebald, turned PhD research on capturing CO2 from ambient air into Climeworks, an ETH spin-off founded in 2009. Climeworks became the best-known direct air capture company, running its Orca and Mammoth plants in Iceland that store captured CO2 underground, and reached unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Climeworks' Mammoth plant in Iceland is among the largest direct-air-capture facilities in the world; the company now permanently stores captured CO2 underground rather than selling it.
deep_cut_fact: Climeworks' first commercial plant (Hinwil, 2017) sat on the roof of a waste incinerator using its waste heat, and its captured CO2 was sold to a nearby greenhouse as fertilizer and to Coca-Cola HBC to carbonate Valser sparkling water.
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Climeworks AG (Zurich)
research_notes: Excellent fit for an energy podcast (DAC is very energy-intensive; plants run on geothermal/renewables). Co-CEO Christoph Gebald often handles media. Climeworks site blocks automated fetching, so the press contact wasn't captured; check climeworks.com newsroom manually.

name: Eldon Sprickerhoff
profile: Canadian cybersecurity entrepreneur who founded eSentire in 2001 in the Waterloo region of Ontario. eSentire grew into a managed detection and response (MDR) leader, backed by Warburg Pincus and others, now led by CEO James C. Foster; Sprickerhoff remains on the executive team as founder and advisor.
interesting_fact: eSentire, founded in 2001, now markets 'Controlled Autonomy SecOps', pairing agentic AI operatives with human-judgment controls, and protects thousands of organizations across 35+ industries.
deep_cut_fact: eSentire's own careers page quotes a long-time employee recalling being greeted on her first day by 'the Founder himself, mister Eldon Sprickerhoff', and notes it was the region's only pure-play cybersecurity firm with a local founder.
current_role: Founder and Advisor, eSentire
public_contact: office_email: info@esentire.com (general company inbox) | pr_agency: ZAG Communications for eSentire (Blair Moreland)
research_notes: Low public profile now; no longer CEO. Web-search budget ran out before more personal background could be verified.

name: Deepak Khetan
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of GlobalBees, an Indian house-of-brands roll-up that became a unicorn in December 2021. GlobalBees' own site credits Nitin Agarwal and Supam Maheshwari as co-founders and lists Anuj Jain as CEO; Deepak Khetan does not appear on its About, Board or Executive pages, so his link to the company could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: GlobalBees reached unicorn status in December 2021, its first year, among the fastest Indian startups to do so.
research_notes: Identity unverified - possibly a Hurun attribution error or an early/departed co-founder. Web-search budget ran out before this could be resolved; needs follow-up. Contact listed is the company's general inbox, not his.

name: Nitin Agarwal
profile: Co-founded GlobalBees, an Indian e-commerce brand roll-up that acquires and scales D2C brands, in 2021 with FirstCry founder Supam Maheshwari. GlobalBees became a unicorn in December 2021, one of India's fastest to do so, after buying brands such as The Better Home, andMe, Yellow Chimes and Reach. The company's site now says it is led by Anuj Jain.
interesting_fact: GlobalBees reached unicorn status in December 2021, its founding year, one of the fastest Indian startups to do so.
current_role: Co-founder of GlobalBees (company now led by Anuj Jain; his current role not confirmed)
research_notes: Very common name; identity tied to GlobalBees only. The web-search budget ran out before his current role or a deep-cut fact could be verified (he appears no longer to run GlobalBees). contact@globalbees.com is a general company inbox.

name: Fangjin Yang
profile: Canadian engineer (Waterloo BASc EE, MASc CompE) who worked at Cisco and was a lead engineer at adtech startup Metamarkets, where he co-created open-source real-time database Apache Druid. In 2015 he cofounded Imply with Gian Merlino and Vadim Ogievetsky; it now sells Imply Lumi, an 'observability warehouse' for security and log data.
interesting_fact: He is one of the original authors of open-source real-time database Apache Druid, built at Metamarkets (acquired by Snap in 2017); Imply, founded by Druid's creators, is backed by a16z, Bessemer and Thoma Bravo.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2023 he returned to his alma mater to give a University of Waterloo Engineering talk, 'Getting out of the garage', on taking a startup from idea to scale.
current_role: Cofounder and CEO, Imply Data (Apache Druid-based real-time analytics / observability warehouse)
public_contact: pr_agency: Imply@ink-co.com (Jane Daguio, INK Communications) | contact_form: https://imply.io/contact/ | official_website: https://imply.io/leadership-team/
research_notes: Accessible, technical founder who speaks at conferences (Data Council, O'Reilly, Waterloo). Real-time data infrastructure angle fits data-center/AI theme. Press via Imply's PR agency INK Communications.

name: Gian Merlino
profile: Gian Merlino is an original author of Apache Druid, the open-source real-time analytics database built at Metamarkets, where he led data ingestion after senior roles at Yahoo. In 2015 he co-founded Imply with Fangjin Yang and Vadim Ogievetsky to commercialise Druid (a16z-backed, about $1bn valuation) and remains its CTO.
interesting_fact: Druid powers real-time analytics at large internet companies. Merlino was the Apache Druid project's first PMC (Project Management Committee) chair after it entered the Apache Software Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.S. in Computer Science from Caltech. He still gives hands-on technical talks, for example 'Swimming in the Data River, or When Streaming Analytics Isn't' at Data Council 2025, about where streaming analytics fits.
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer, Imply Data
research_notes: Engineer-founder who speaks regularly at data conferences (Data Council/AI Council, Strata, Databricks Data+AI Summit), so he is likely open to technical podcasts. No published press email found on imply.io; the contact form and the company X account are company channels, not personal.

name: Vadim Ogievetsky
profile: Stanford CS master's graduate who, at Metamarkets (later acquired by Snap), was one of the original authors of the Apache Druid real-time analytics database. In 2015 he cofounded Imply with Fangjin Yang and Gian Merlino to commercialise Druid; it became a $1B+ unicorn backed by a16z. As CXO he leads Imply's product experience and UI, including its Druid console.
interesting_fact: He is one of the original authors of Apache Druid, the open-source real-time analytics database used by companies like Netflix, Airbnb and Salesforce.
deep_cut_fact: Before databases, he was in Stanford's Data Visualization group, where he contributed to Protovis and was one of the co-authors of D3.js, the JavaScript library behind much of the web's interactive data journalism.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Experience Officer (CXO), Imply Data
research_notes: Strong data-infra/visualisation podcast angle (D3 + Druid). No press email found on imply.io (press/contact pages timed out). Fallback is Imply's site contact form. Druid's named enterprise users are commonly cited in Druid materials and were not separately verified here.

name: Chris Caulfield
profile: Nurse and co-founder of IntelyCare, the Quincy, Mass.-based AI-driven nurse-staffing platform launched in 2016. A $115M Series C in 2022 valued it at $1.1B; Matthew Levesque became CEO in 2024 and in January 2026 IntelyCare acquired CareRev to build a broader health-system workforce platform.
interesting_fact: Caulfield, IntelyCare's Chief Nursing Officer, and CTO Ike Nnah met in 2015 while working together at a hospital, then recruited David Coppins in 2016; the three won EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2022 New England.
deep_cut_fact: IntelyCare's first customer contract, signed in 2016 alongside its first mobile app, was with Pope Rehabilitation & Skilled Nursing Center in Massachusetts.
current_role: Co-founder, IntelyCare (Chief Nursing Officer as of 2022; current title not confirmed)
public_contact: pr_agency: Joe Casados, Bospar PR - prforintelycare@bospar.com | official_website: https://www.intelycare.com
research_notes: PR agency contact is from a 2022 release and may be stale. Company general email careteam@intelycare.com is on the About page. Low personal media profile.

name: David Coppins
profile: Boston-area entrepreneur who co-founded IntelyCare in 2016 with Ike Nnah and Chris Caulfield, building an app-based per-diem nurse staffing platform for post-acute care that reached unicorn status. Earlier he co-founded college-savings rewards company Upromise (1999) and was president of Virgin Pulse. Reported to have moved to executive chairman in 2023.
interesting_fact: He and his IntelyCare co-founders were named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2022 New England award winners.
deep_cut_fact: Long before healthcare, he co-founded Upromise in 1999, the program that turned everyday purchases into college-savings rebates, and later served as president of Virgin Pulse, part of Richard Branson's Virgin Group.
current_role: Co-founder; Executive Chairman (formerly CEO), IntelyCare
research_notes: Executive-chairman transition comes from a secondary source; confirm before outreach. Has written columns for MedCity News (https://medcitynews.com/author/dcoppins/).

name: Ike Nnah
profile: Ike Nnah is listed as a founder of IntelyCare, the Boston-based app/platform matching nurses (RNs, LPNs, CNAs) with shifts and jobs at healthcare facilities, which Janus Henderson valued at $1.1B in a $115M 2022 round. IntelyCare named Matthew Levesque CEO in 2024 (co-founder David Coppins is executive chairman) and acquired acute-care staffing platform CareRev in January 2026.
interesting_fact: IntelyCare's 2022 $115M round, led by asset manager Janus Henderson, valued the nurse-staffing app at $1.1B.
current_role: Listed co-founder of IntelyCare (current role not publicly documented)
public_contact: pr_agency: Jenny Edelston, 120/80 MKTG - jenny.edelston@120over80mktg.com (media contact on Jan 2026 IntelyCare/CareRev release; may represent CareRev side) | contact_form: https://www.intelycare.com/about-us/ (Contact Us)
research_notes: Not mentioned on IntelyCare's own newsroom pages; no bio found before web-search budget ran out. Verify identity/role (LinkedIn) before outreach. David Coppins is the company's public co-founder.

name: Prince Nnah
profile: IntelyCare is a Massachusetts-based healthcare talent platform that uses software to connect nursing professionals with care facilities for per-diem and permanent shifts, valued around $1B+. Prince Nnah is listed as a founder in the input data, but no IntelyCare page or verifiable biography naming him was found in this pass.
current_role: Listed as an IntelyCare founder in the source data; not named on IntelyCare's current website pages
public_contact: contact_form: careteam@intelycare.com (general care-team contact, not press)
research_notes: Identity unverified - IntelyCare's public face is founder/CEO David Coppins; confirm Nnah's role (e.g. via the Forbes/Crunchbase listing) before outreach. Research cut short by a web-search quota.

name: Smita Deorah
profile: Former Procter & Gamble finance/treasury/strategy leader (nine years in Singapore and India) who co-founded LEAD with Sumeet Mehta in 2012. LEAD provides an integrated curriculum, teacher training and tech system to affordable private schools in India's small towns; it reached a $1.1B valuation in Jan 2022 after a $100M Series E.
interesting_fact: LEAD began in 2012 as a single school on the outskirts of Ahmedabad with 14 students and grew into a system serving thousands of affordable private schools across India.
deep_cut_fact: Before LEAD, she and Sumeet Mehta started Sparsh, an NGO for Mumbai's Anganwadis, implementing a 'pre-school in a box' in 16 Anganwadi centres to prepare children for school and reduce dropouts.
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, LEAD Group (LEAD School), Mumbai
research_notes: Regular speaker (ASU+GSV Summit 'Power of Women' honoree, DNA Changemaker in Education 2024). No published press email found.

name: Sumeet Mehta
profile: IIM Ahmedabad (PGP 1999) and PEC Chandigarh alumnus who spent 8 years running P&G businesses across Asia-Pacific and then was CEO of Zee Learn, growing it from a Rs 20 Cr preschool franchisor to a Rs 100 Cr NSE-listed education company. In 2012 he and wife Smita Deorah co-founded LEAD, a school-edtech system for affordable private schools in small-town India; it became a unicorn in 2022 ($1.1B).
interesting_fact: LEAD started in 2012 with a single school of 14 students in a village on the outskirts of Ahmedabad and grew into a network serving over a million students across thousands of partner schools.
deep_cut_fact: At Zee Learn he led the development of the iLLUME (preschool) and Litera Octave (school) pedagogies; he grew up in a small town with both parents working as teachers, which he credits for his drive to close India's small-town education gap.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, LEAD Group (LEAD School), Mumbai
research_notes: Co-founded with wife Smita Deorah (co-CEO). Regular Entrepreneur India columnist and ASU+GSV speaker; appeared on Chetan Bhagat's 'Deep Talk' podcast. Only published LEAD email is partner@leadschool.in (school partnerships), not a press line.

name: Ghazal Alagh
profile: Chandigarh-raised entrepreneur who co-founded Honasa in 2016 with Varun Alagh, starting with toxin-free baby products under Mamaearth and growing into India's largest digital-first beauty and personal-care house (Mamaearth, The Derma Co, Aqualogica, BBlunt, etc.), which listed in 2023. She leads new product innovation and was a 'Shark' investor on Shark Tank India season 1.
interesting_fact: Known as the 'Mama Shark', she was one of the original investor-judges on Shark Tank India (2021-22).
deep_cut_fact: Her first job was as an NIIT corporate trainer teaching software to companies like Infosys; she is also a trained painter who did an intensive figurative-art course at the New York Academy of Art in 2013 and earlier ran a diet start-up, dietexpert.in.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Innovation Officer, Honasa Consumer Ltd (Mamaearth parent; NSE/BSE-listed)
research_notes: High-profile in India (TV, Instagram). Honasa is listed, so investor-relations channels also exist via honasa.in. Her quote on the Honasa page: 'Your current best consumers got you here. Your future consumers will fuel your next stage of growth.'

name: Varun Alagh
profile: Delhi College of Engineering electrical engineer and XLRI MBA who spent years in FMCG at Hindustan Unilever, Diageo and Coca-Cola before co-founding Honasa Consumer with Ghazal Alagh in 2016. Honasa grew Mamaearth into a house of brands (The Derma Co, Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's, BBlunt) and listed in India in Nov 2023. In Jan 2026 he joined Shark Tank India Season 5 as a Shark.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he joined Shark Tank India (Season 5, Sony TV) as one of the Sharks, alongside Ghazal Alagh who was a Shark in earlier seasons.
deep_cut_fact: During his corporate career he was instrumental in launching Coke Zero in India, and won Diageo's 'I am Diageo' and 'Above and Beyond' awards.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Honasa Consumer Ltd (Mamaearth parent; NSE/BSE listed)
research_notes: High public profile in India (TV, LinkedIn). Honasa is a listed company, so IR/stock-exchange filings also available. Avoid child-related origin story in outreach.

name: Abhishek Agrawal
profile: Princeton electrical engineer and Harvard MBA who was an early product leader at Dropbox and an engineer at Microsoft Research. In 2017 he co-founded Material Security with ex-Dropbox colleagues Ryan Noon and Chris Park to protect Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 email, files and accounts; the company passed a $1B valuation (Andreessen Horowitz, Elad Gil backers).
interesting_fact: Material was inspired by the 2016 US election email hacks -- notably the breach of Clinton campaign chair John Podesta's Gmail -- and the idea that attackers will win round one, so the job is to make the 'second round' (what they can do with a compromised mailbox) much harder.
deep_cut_fact: Before settling on email security, he and his co-founders reportedly listed about 25 startup ideas, narrowed them to four and tried selling each before committing. At Dropbox he shipped collaboration products as well as core infrastructure and analytics.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Material Security (CEO since April 2023; previously CTO)
research_notes: Podcast-friendly (has appeared on The Desi VC, Duo Decipher). The '25 ideas' detail is from a podcast summary and is less firmly sourced. No published press email on the Material site.

name: Chris Park
profile: UC Berkeley EECS graduate who worked on data privacy at Google, was the first engineer at Parastructure (acquired by Dropbox) and then led Dropbox infrastructure teams, before co-founding email and cloud-workspace security company Material Security in 2017 with Abhishek Agrawal and Ryan Noon. Material protects Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace and reached a ~$1B valuation.
interesting_fact: All three Material co-founders came out of Dropbox; the company was started in 2017 in the wake of the 2016 election email-hacking incidents, to protect sensitive data sitting in mailboxes.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Material he was the very first engineer at Parastructure, the startup co-founded by his future Material co-founder Ryan Noon, which Dropbox acquired; earlier he led data-privacy and authorization projects at Google.
current_role: Co-founder and VP of Engineering, Material Security (Redwood City, CA)
research_notes: Engineering-focused, low public profile; CEO Abhishek Agrawal is the public face. No press email found on Material's site (disclosure@material.security exists but is for security reports). 'First engineer at Parastructure' is from profile aggregators; Material's page confirms Parastructure/Dropbox/Google.

name: Ryan Noon
profile: Stanford-trained security engineer (BS CS; MS computer networks and security) who co-founded Material Security in 2017 with Abhishek Agrawal and led it as CEO before becoming Chairman in 2023. Material secures Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace email and files; Noon previously led engineering teams at Dropbox and Ayasdi.
interesting_fact: Material Security protects cloud email and productivity suites (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace) and reached unicorn status; Noon handed the CEO role to co-founder Abhishek Agrawal in 2023 and became Chairman.
deep_cut_fact: His previous startup, Parastructure, was acquired by Dropbox (2014), where he went on to lead engineering teams.
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Material Security (CEO until 2023)
research_notes: Has appeared on security podcasts and written for SC World. No published email found; LinkedIn or Material's site likely best.

name: Alfonso De los Rios
profile: Mexican entrepreneur from Monterrey who co-founded Nowports in 2018 with Uruguayan Maximiliano Casal; the YC-backed digital freight forwarder combines logistics with trade finance and software and became a unicorn when he was about 23. He led it as CEO until April 2025 (Fernando Poitevin succeeded him; Casal returned as CEO in Oct 2026).
interesting_fact: Nowports reached a US$1B+ valuation in 2022, making De los Ríos one of Latin America's youngest unicorn founders at around age 23; the company has raised roughly US$250M in equity.
deep_cut_fact: He started coding at 11, and his first 'build' was a modification of Minecraft; he left university in his first semester, which took him to Silicon Valley where he met co-founder Max Casal.
current_role: Co-founder of Nowports (Monterrey digital freight forwarder); moved from CEO to President in April 2025 (current title after Oct 2026 CEO change unconfirmed)
research_notes: Role change sources: April 2025 (https://www.descubre.vc/noticia/nowports-anuncia-relevo-en-su-direcci-n-general-2025-04-22) and Oct 2026 Casal return (https://clusterindustrial.com.mx/maximiliano-casal-vuelve-como-ceo-de-nowports-para-impulsar-una-nueva-etapa-ai-native/). Nicknamed 'Poncho'. Received Nuevo León's Entrepreneurial Merit Medal. No published press email found.

name: Maximiliano Casal
profile: Uruguayan systems engineer (Universidad ORT) and ex-iOS developer who co-founded digital freight forwarder Nowports with Mexico's Alfonso de los Rios in 2018; it went through YC and became a unicorn after a $150M Series C in 2022. He later left the COO role and is building a new AI-related company.
interesting_fact: He met co-founder Alfonso de los Rios at a Stanford-run software development seminar in 2017; Nowports made him only the third Uruguayan unicorn founder after dLocal's founders.
deep_cut_fact: Before logistics he was a hands-on mobile engineer: senior iOS developer and team lead at Moove-it, iOS developer at Globant, and co-founder/CTO of Croway.
current_role: Co-founder & former COO, Nowports; building a new AI company
research_notes: Early-career details come from TheOrg (aggregator).

name: Guan Dian
profile: Guan Dian studied management information systems at the National University of Singapore. In 2007 she co-founded Patsnap with fellow NUS student Jeffrey Tiong, starting with a S$50,000 NUS Enterprise grant. Patsnap became a unicorn after a $300M round led by SoftBank and Tencent, and it serves more than 10,000 customers in over 50 countries with AI-powered patent and innovation analytics. She runs marketing and the Asia-Pacific business.
interesting_fact: Patsnap began with a S$50,000 (about US$37,700) grant from NUS Enterprise, and the founders spent two years building their data capabilities before expanding globally.
deep_cut_fact: As an NUS undergraduate she interned in Silicon Valley at a video-streaming company. NUS later gave her its Outstanding Young Alumni Award in 2019.
current_role: Co-founder, CMO and APAC General Manager, Patsnap (Singapore-founded AI patent and R&D intelligence platform), per Vertex Ventures, Feb 2024
public_contact: official_website: https://www.patsnap.com/about-us | podcast: Hard Truths by Vertex, Series 2 Ep 8 (Feb 2024): 'How Guan Dian built a Tech Unicorn from Ground up'
research_notes: Female co-founder, featured in Vertex's women-founder series. The Vertex episode covers why she left a 'cushy job' to join the startup, a good conversation hook. CEO Jeffrey Tiong is the main press voice. I found no published press email. Her Stanford education appears in some bios but was not verified.

name: Manish Taneja
profile: IIT Delhi electrical engineer Manish Taneja, who passed the CFA exam in 2010, left an investments job at Fidelity to start beauty e-tailer Purplle around 2011-12 with ex-flatmate Rahul Dash; Suyash Katyayani joined soon after. Backed by Blume, Verlinvest, Goldman Sachs, Kedaara and Premji Invest, it has built its own brands since 2017.
interesting_fact: The founders chose beauty over furniture because it needed less capital and offered high gross margins and repeat purchases. They started with about $100,000 in combined savings.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Faridabad he wanted to be a cricketer. At IIT he was inspired by a talk from Sunil Bharti Mittal on how Airtel stayed focused on telecom, and he counts Rajiv Vij's 'Inside Out Leadership' among his favorite books. His motto: 'Being nice to other people is a superpower.'
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Purplle (Indian beauty e-commerce and brands, Mumbai)
research_notes: Podcast-friendly: he has appeared on Blume's X-Unicorns and Z47's Unstarted. The only published Purplle email found is customercare@purplle.com (customer service, not press). Blume transcript is AI-generated, but details are consistent with other sources.

name: Rahul Dash
profile: Rahul Dash is an IIT Kharagpur graduate who then went to IIM Ahmedabad and worked at Tata, where the Purplle idea took shape. He co-founded Purplle with Manish Taneja (CEO) and Suyash Katyayani (CTO). The trio pooled about Rs 40 lakh of savings to start it. Purplle sells beauty products online and through its own brands, and became a unicorn valued at about $1B.
interesting_fact: Purplle's three co-founders started the company by pooling just Rs 40 lakh (about $50k) of their own savings. It later became a ~$1B (about Rs 8,200 crore) beauty unicorn competing with Nykaa.
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Purplle (Indian online beauty retailer and brand house, Mumbai); role as reported in 2023
research_notes: Sources conflict on his pre-Purplle employer: DNA says Tata (aggregators say Tata Power strategy and business development), while indiacsr.in says McKinsey. Left out of the deep-cut for that reason. If Tata Power is confirmed, it is a natural energy-podcast hook. CEO Manish Taneja is the public face. Current role not re-verified after 2023.

name: Frank Wolf
profile: German entrepreneur who spent years as a consultant building enterprise intranets before co-founding Staffbase in Chemnitz in 2014 with Martin Böhringer and Lutz Gerlach. Staffbase launched what it calls the world's first employee app and now serves 1,500 customers and 16.5M users; it is still founder-led and was valued at over €1B (OMR, 2022).
interesting_fact: Staffbase's founding idea came from Wolf's frustration that the big enterprise intranets he built as a consultant were complex, expensive and used by only a fraction of the workforce - so they designed for 'the hardest-to-reach employee'.
deep_cut_fact: Wolf championed Dresden as Staffbase's 'kind of second headquarters', moving there largely to recruit software talent from TU Dresden; by end-2020 the Dresden office had 62 staff.
current_role: Co-founder, Staffbase (Chemnitz-based employee communications platform); listed as President & Co-Founder on recruiter profiles - current title unverified
research_notes: Staffbase is headquartered in Chemnitz, East Germany - a notable non-Berlin unicorn story. CEO is Martin Böhringer; Wolf is lower-profile.

name: Lutz Gerlach
profile: German former academic (doctorate in business/managerial economics, senior researcher at Chemnitz University of Technology) who co-founded productivity app Hojoki in 2011 and then Staffbase in 2014 with Martin Böhringer and Frank Wolf. Staffbase grew into a leading employee-app and intranet platform, reaching unicorn valuation with Series D (2021) and E (2022) rounds.
interesting_fact: Staffbase is headquartered in Chemnitz, eastern Germany, a rare unicorn outside Berlin/Munich, and grew out of the same founding team as the earlier Hojoki startup.
deep_cut_fact: Before Staffbase he was a senior researcher at Chemnitz University of Technology (doctorate in business/managerial economics), then co-founded and served as COO of productivity-app startup Hojoki, founded in Chemnitz in March 2011.
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Staffbase (employee communications platform, Chemnitz, Germany)
research_notes: Role sourced from Staffbase recruiting pages and MarketScreener; CEO Martin Böhringer is the more public face.

name: Martin Bohringer
profile: Martin Bohringer — wealth from Staffbase (founder; company valued $1B)

name: Balaji Srinivasan
education: Stanford University
profile: Balaji S. Srinivasan (b. 1980; Stanford EE PhD) co-founded Counsyl (sold to Myriad for $375m), was an a16z general partner, co-founded 21 Inc/Earn.com (sold to Coinbase in 2018, where he became first CTO) and relocation start-up Teleport (2014, sold to Topia). He now runs the Network School (now in Kazakhstan) and the Balaji Fund.
interesting_fact: His self-published 2022 book 'The Network State: How To Start a New Country' hit No. 2 on the Wall Street Journal's e-book bestseller list, and in 2017 the Trump administration considered him for FDA Commissioner.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he taught Stanford's 'Startup Engineering' online course, which Business Insider ranked in 2014 as the sixth most popular free online course for professionals; his genomics papers have 5,000+ citations.
current_role: Founder, The Network School; founder, Balaji Fund; author of 'The Network State'
research_notes: IDENTITY CAVEAT: Hurun lists him as founder of a $1bn cloud unicorn 'Teleport' - that is almost certainly Gravitational/Teleport (founders Ev Kontsevoy et al.), not Balaji's 2014 relocation start-up teleport.org (sold to Topia). Treat the Hurun attribution as an error. Very active on X; reachable publicly. Renounced US citizenship in 2023.

name: Silver Keskküla
profile: Estonian engineer-entrepreneur Silver Keskküla was the first researcher on Skype's core team, then co-founded Teleport (2014, with Sten Tamkivi and Balaji Srinivasan), a data-driven relocation search engine for 'digital nomads' later acquired by MOVE Guides/Topia (2017). He then founded AI startup Supervaisor and now builds AI-safety and LLM-brand-monitoring tools.
interesting_fact: Teleport, which he co-founded with ex-Skype executive Sten Tamkivi and Balaji Srinivasan, began as a search engine to help people pick cities to live and work in, and was acquired by global-mobility firm MOVE Guides (now Topia).
deep_cut_fact: At Skype he used machine learning to optimise the peer-to-peer network topology, shipping neural networks to hundreds of millions of computers years before the deep-learning boom; he says he is most inspired by bio-mimetic algorithms, from evolutionary computation to neural nets.
current_role: CEO, ScamGuardian.AI (deepfake-scam defence); also runs trackAIanswers.com; CDL-Estonia associate
research_notes: Identity confirmed as Teleport co-founder, but the input's claim that Teleport was a $1B 'unicorn' is doubtful: it was a modest exit to MOVE Guides/Topia, so the Hurun listing may be an error. Not a UHNW profile. Approachable startup founder; also raised what was described as Estonia's largest solo-founder angel round for Supervaisor.

name: Sten Tamkivi
education: Miina Härma Gymnasium; Stanford University; University of Tartu
profile: Estonian entrepreneur and investor who spent 8+ years as an early Skype executive through its $8.5B sale to Microsoft. As an EIR at Andreessen Horowitz he co-founded Teleport, a tool for remote workers and digital nomads that pivoted to B2B and was acquired by Topia in 2017; he stayed as Topia's CPO through a $48M Series C. He now invests as a partner at Plural.
interesting_fact: Teleport was co-founded while he was an entrepreneur-in-residence at Andreessen Horowitz, after his Skype years spanning startup to the $8.5B Microsoft exit.
deep_cut_fact: He started his entrepreneurial career in 1996, aged 18, by founding the first digital media agency in Estonia.
current_role: Partner, Plural (European founder-led VC platform); Founding Partner, Creative Destruction Lab Estonia
research_notes: Very accessible and public: active on X and LinkedIn, gives interviews (ERR, Estonian World, Seedcamp). Founders Pledge member. Hurun lists him via Teleport, but his wealth is mainly from Skype/Teleport exits. Good podcast guest candidate.

name: Anthony Watson
source_of_wealth: The Bank of London (founder; company valued $1B)
profile: London-born technology executive (CBE, 2023) who was CIO of Barclays' retail bank (launching the Pingit app) and Nike's CIO in 2014, then co-founded crypto platform Uphold in 2015. He conceived The Bank of London in 2016 and launched it in November 2021 as a UK clearing, correspondent and wholesale bank, serving as CEO until September 2024.
interesting_fact: The Bank of London launched on 30 November 2021 as the UK's sixth clearing bank; Watson is also a prominent LGBT advocate - GLAAD board member since 2013, Stonewall ambassador and founder of The Watson Pride Foundation.

profile: German entrepreneur, ex-Goldman Sachs investment professional and Rocket Internet executive, who founded Berlin tech-rental/subscription platform Grover in 2015 and grew it into a unicorn that raised about $2B. name: Brynne Rojas
profile: Brynne McNulty Rojas, a Miami-born, Harvard MBA, ex-Goldman Sachs real estate investor and ex-McKinsey consultant, co-founded Habi in Bogotá in 2019 with Merqueo co-founder Sebastián Noguera. Habi uses algorithmic pricing to buy, renovate and resell used homes and became Colombia's second unicorn (2022, US$200M round); in March 2026 it acquired Mexican broker-tech startup Pulppo.

name: Sebastian Noguera Escallón
profile: Colombian entrepreneur who co-founded Bogota proptech Habi with CEO Brynne McNulty around 2019; it buys and sells homes for Latin America's middle class and became Colombia's second unicorn. Earlier he was Chief Digital Officer at Banco de Bogota and co-founded online grocer Merqueo.

profile: IIT Madras computer-science graduate who co-founded Hasura with Rajoshi Ghosh. He started as CTO and later became CEO; Hasura's open-source GraphQL Engine has passed 600M downloads and reportedly runs under half the Fortune 500. deep_cut_fact: Hasura began as an internal tool. While building a food-delivery venture in Chennai with Rajoshi Ghosh, he wrote a database platform called procrust.es. He also helped create and teach IIT Madras's 'Introduction to Modern Application Development' course.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, PromptQL (AI data-agent/AI-native workspace spun out of Hasura); co-founder of Hasura

name: Glenn Luk
profile: Glenn Luk co-founded HealthCare.com in 2014, an online marketplace that makes individual health and Medicare insurance easier for consumers to understand and buy, and sits on its board. He previously spent about a decade in Investcorp's technology investment group in New York. He has since been involved with blockchain, edtech and internet companies.
interesting_fact: He is a widely followed analyst of the Chinese economy, U.S.-China competition and China's high-speed rail. Steve Hsu's Manifold podcast (ep. 58, April 2024) featured his work on China's GDP and HSR.
deep_cut_fact: After college he joined Deutsche Bank in Hong Kong for about three years, doing M&A for Chinese state-owned oil & gas and power companies, before returning to New York in 2004 to join Investcorp. current_role: Co-founder and board member, HealthCare.com (HealthCare Inc.); investor and writer on China's economy
public_contact: x: https://x.com/GlennLuk | substack: https://www.readwriteinvest.com (reading, writing & investing)

name: Howard Yeh
profile: Howard Yeh is a Penn graduate who started as a Merrill Lynch media investment banker and was a VC at VantagePoint. He co-founded BrokersWeb, an insurance ad network that made the Inc. 500 twice and was acquired by Vantage Media in 2011. He then co-founded HealthCare.com, a health-insurance marketplace that has raised $200M+ across Series A to C, and he still blogs on ACA, Medicare Advantage and insurtech.
interesting_fact: BrokersWeb, his first insurance company, grew revenue from $16M in 2010 to $55M in 2011 before Vantage Media acquired it. It was twice on the Inc. 500.
deep_cut_fact: Between BrokersWeb and HealthCare.com he co-founded ContactUs.com (2012-2015), a SaaS tool for better website contact forms and lead capture. He describes its sale to WorkWave in 2015 as a 'bite-sized acquisition'. He also writes on his blog about Asian American leadership and entrepreneurship.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer, HealthCare.com (New York). His roles there went Co-Founder, then CEO, then COO, then CRO.
research_notes: Very accessible: he runs an active personal blog (posts through March 2026) on healthcare markets, AI and founder stories, which is a natural hook for outreach. NYC-based. Don Loonam became HealthCare.com CEO in March 2021.

name: Jeff Smedsrud
profile: Health-insurance marketing veteran who co-founded HealthCare.com, the health-coverage shopping and lead-generation company (Hurun lists it at a $1B valuation), and founded Pivot Health, an Arizona-based designer and marketer of short-term and supplemental health plans that HealthCare.com later acquired. Pivot Health products are sold through HealthCare.com sites such as Healthcare Insider.
interesting_fact: HealthCare.com both publishes consumer guides (e.g. Healthcare Insider) and manufactures its own short-term and supplemental health insurance products under the Pivot Health brand that Smedsrud founded.
current_role: Founder & CEO, Pivot Health (short-term/supplemental health insurance products, now part of HealthCare.com); co-founder of HealthCare.com

name: Jose Vargas

name: Dan Littman
profile: Dan R. Littman is a leading immunologist best known for cloning the CD4 and CD8 T-cell genes. He has been at NYU since 1995 and an HHMI investigator since 1987, and is a member of the National Academy of Sciences and National Academy of Medicine. He is a scientific co-founder and advisory board member of Immunai (AI and single-cell immune profiling) and Vedanta Biosciences, and sits on Pfizer's board.
interesting_fact: As a postdoc in Richard Axel's Columbia lab he cloned CD8 and, within months, CD4, the genes that define the two main types of T cells. CD4 later turned out to be HIV's receptor, and his lab's HIV work contributed to identifying CCR5 as a drug target, which Pfizer's maraviroc now blocks.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Bucharest in 1952. His family waited years to emigrate, finally leaving Romania in 1962, and spent six months in Rome while his father passed the US medical licensing exam before they came to the US with help from HIAS.
current_role: Helen L. and Martin S. Kimmel Professor of Molecular Immunology, NYU Grossman School of Medicine; HHMI Investigator; Pfizer board member; scientific co-founder of Immunai
public_contact: official_website: Littman Lab, NYU (saturn.med.nyu.edu/research/mp/littmanlab) | official_website: Pfizer board bio
research_notes: Primarily an academic scientist; Immunai is one of several company affiliations. The best route is his NYU lab. 'Pfizer's maraviroc' is my identification: the transcript says only 'Pfizer makes a drug' targeting CCR5.

profile: Software engineer named among MinIO's co-founders in 2015 coverage (Nov 2014 founding, after he was a senior principal engineer at Red Hat and CTO of GridX); MinIO's own site now credits three other founders. current_role: Cloud-native security / zero-trust architect and open-source leader; SPIFFE Steering Committee member (current employer not confirmed; TheOrg lists HumanForm Technologies)

name: V.R. Govindarajan
profile: Indian software entrepreneur (IISc Bangalore engineering; MS in CS in the US; database work at DEC and IBM) who co-founded IT product-engineering firm Aztecsoft, sold to MindTree in 2008. With Debasish Chakraborty he then founded Perfios, which pivoted from consumer personal-finance software to B2B credit-underwriting and financial-data analytics for banks and became a unicorn after a 2022 Warburg Pincus-led round.
interesting_fact: Perfios started as a web-based personal finance management tool for retail consumers before pivoting to serve lenders; today its software can read data from 250+ financial institutions and returns credit decisions in under a minute.

name: Amit Bareket
profile: Israeli cybersecurity entrepreneur and IDF Unit 81 veteran who, after engineering stints at IBM XIV Storage and BigBand Networks, co-founded consumer VPN SaferVPN with Sagi Gidali (sold to J2 Global) and then Perimeter 81, a cloud network-security/SASE platform. Check Point agreed to acquire Perimeter 81 for about $490M in August 2023, after it had been valued at $1B in 2022.

current_role: Co-founder & former CEO, Perimeter 81 (acquired by Check Point); reportedly VP of SASE at Check Point Software (verify)

name: Sagi Gidali

public_contact: press_email: adore@rothys.com (Anna Doré, Senior Director of Communications, as of Jan 2024)
research_notes: Spent ~20 years in M&A/investment banking before Rothy's (directory profiles also list Duke undergrad and Wake Forest law degree; unverified). Press contact is from a Jan 2024 release; may be stale.

name: Jiang Hua
education: Tsinghua University
profile: Career GAC Group executive (joined 1997) who has led Ruqi Mobility as CEO since June 2019, when GAC and Tencent launched it as a Guangzhou ride-hailing platform. Ruqi raised a ~$153M Series A, then listed in Hong Kong in July 2024 positioning itself as a robotaxi operator, with Pony.ai as a strategic shareholder and partner.
interesting_fact: Ruqi was co-founded by carmaker GAC and Tencent and marketed its Hong Kong IPO as an autonomous-driving operations story, running robotaxi services in the Greater Bay Area.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ruqi he spent two decades inside GAC: general manager of GAC Business/Trading (广汽商贸) 2008-2018, then head of GAC's mobility project team (2018-19) that spawned Ruqi; he holds a business-management BA from Beijing Technology and Business University (1994) and a Sun Yat-sen University MBA (2003).
current_role: Executive Director & CEO, Ruqi Mobility (如祺出行 / Chenqi Technology, HKEX: 9680), Guangzhou

name: Johnny Mitrevski
profile: Shellharbour-born engineer (UOW telecoms engineering, 2000) who spent over a decade at Nortel Networks in Wollongong and later was a technology manager at Commonwealth Bank. In 2019 he co-founded Scalapay with CEO Simone Mancini after spotting a lack of BNPL options in Italy; it became Italy's first fintech unicorn in Jan 2022 and in 2025 secured €70M from the EIB.
interesting_fact: Scalapay hit unicorn status in January 2022, under three years after founding, and was dubbed the 'Wollongong-founded' unicorn because its tech team was built in the Illawarra while the business runs from Milan.
deep_cut_fact: He calls himself 'a child of the public education system' and spent over a decade commuting by local train to Nortel Networks' office on the University of Wollongong campus - where he met future Scalapay engineering colleagues.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Scalapay (Milan-based buy-now-pay-later fintech)
research_notes: Splits time between Wollongong and Milan. No published press email found; Simone Mancini is the public face. University of Wollongong alumni relations has profiled him and could be a warm route.

name: Simone Mancini
profile: Tuscan-born, raised in Darwin, Australia, Mancini co-founded Scalapay in 2019 with CTO Johnny Mitrevski after earlier startups and product roles in Sydney. Scalapay became an Italian-founded BNPL unicorn after a $497M Series B in 2022 (Tencent, Tiger Global) and now serves 13M+ users and 12,000+ brands; it reported monthly break-even in 2025, took a €70M EIB venture loan and expanded via Stripe to 30+ countries in 2026.
interesting_fact: Mancini said Scalapay reached monthly break-even during 2025 and expected to finish 2026 in profit, after the EIB granted it a €70M Scale Up Debt loan.
deep_cut_fact: Before Scalapay he took a sewing course and launched his own online fashion brand, then in 2015 co-founded with Mitrevski EatTonight (a Sydney marketplace for home-cooked meals) and Sweetly (a platform for cake-decorating artists). His parents were lay Catholic missionaries sent from Empoli to Darwin.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Scalapay (Milan/Dublin buy-now-pay-later fintech)
research_notes: Speaks Italian with a Tuscan accent; gives interviews to Italian business press (EconomyUp, Milano Finanza, Fortune Italia 40 Under 40). No published press email found on scalapay.com.

name: Christian Floerkemeier
profile: Cambridge-trained electrical engineer with an ETH Zurich computer-science PhD who was Associate Director of MIT's Auto-ID Lab, part of the team behind RFID tech now used in major supply chains. In 2009 he co-founded Scandit with fellow ETH PhDs Samuel Mueller and Christof Roduner; its smartphone computer-vision barcode/'smart data capture' software made it a $1B unicorn in 2022.
interesting_fact: Scandit was bootstrapped for three and a half years, only raising its first round in 2013; he did all the early product, algorithm and computer-vision work himself and jokes that he once did the jobs of everyone who now reports to him.
deep_cut_fact: Within his first week as a PhD student he joined a Walmart-MIT research collaboration on the 'next-generation barcode'; he also co-founded Fosstrak, the leading open-source RFID software platform.
current_role: Co-founder, CTO and VP Product, Scandit (Zurich)
research_notes: Technical co-founder, comfortable with media (writes bylines, speaks at NRF). Fosstrak detail confirmed on Scandit management page.

name: Christof Roduner
profile: Swiss computer scientist and co-founder (2009, with Samuel Mueller and Christian Floerkemeier) of Scandit, the Zurich-based smart data capture company whose smartphone-camera barcode scanning and computer vision is used in retail and logistics; it reached unicorn status in 2022. He leads Scandit's software engineering and research organisation.
interesting_fact: Scandit grew out of ETH Zurich/MIT Internet-of-Things research, aiming to bridge physical objects and digital information just as smartphone cameras became capable enough.
deep_cut_fact: Before research he founded a company that built and sold a CRM system and ran the internet business at a Zurich IT firm; as an ETH/MIT researcher he co-founded Fosstrak, the leading open-source RFID platform implementing the EPC Network spec, used by SAP and Orange.
current_role: Co-founder, CIO and VP Engineering, Scandit (Zurich)
research_notes: Studied CS and business at University of Zurich and Uppsala. Appeared on Swisspreneur podcast ep. 249 (2022). Samuel Mueller (CEO) is the main public face.

name: Samuel Mueller
profile: Swiss computer scientist (PhD ETH Zurich; MSc CS and MA financial economics, University of Zurich) who co-founded Zurich-based Scandit in 2009 with Christian Floerkemeier and Christof Roduner. Scandit sells smartphone-based barcode, ID and label scanning plus store-intelligence software powered by computer vision and AI to retailers, logistics and airlines.
interesting_fact: Scandit started from the idea of bridging physical objects and digital information, using barcodes as the entry point just as phone cameras were becoming ubiquitous.
deep_cut_fact: Before Scandit he was a corporate researcher at IBM Zurich Research Lab, earning three IBM Invention Achievement Awards and an IBM Research Division Award; his ETH PhD was in computer science and temporal logics.
current_role: CEO and Co-founder, Scandit
research_notes: Regular conference speaker and podcast guest; press email is the best route.

name: Sachin Nayyar
profile: Serial identity-security entrepreneur who founded Vaau (acquired by Sun Microsystems, where he became Chief Identity Strategist), then Securonix (SIEM; US$1B+ Vista-led growth investment in 2022) and Saviynt. He stepped back to executive chairman at Saviynt in 2018 and returned as CEO in 2023; in Dec 2025 Saviynt raised US$700M led by KKR at about a US$3B valuation.
interesting_fact: Saviynt's US$700M Series B (Dec 2025), led by KKR with Sixth Street Growth, TenEleven and Carrick Capital, valued the identity-security company at roughly US$3B and was pitched as making identity 'the foundation for the AI era'.
deep_cut_fact: He served five years as Board Chair of the Health Information Sharing & Analysis Center (H-ISAC), the healthcare sector's cyber-threat-sharing body; per CEO Magazine he sold his first company, Vaau, to Sun Microsystems at age 28.
current_role: Founder, CEO & Chairman, Saviynt (identity security, El Segundo, CA)
research_notes: Founded both Saviynt and Securonix. PR handled by agency Inkhouse. Vaau-at-28 detail from https://digitalmag.theceomagazine.com/sachin-nayyar/ (page blocked to fetch; seen in search summary).

name: Tanuj Gulati
profile: Cybersecurity entrepreneur and investor. A founding member of identity-governance firm Vaau (sold to Sun Microsystems), he co-founded SIEM company Securonix with Sachin Nayyar and served as CTO, growing ARR past $100M. Nayyar also founded Saviynt; I found no primary source naming Gulati as a Saviynt co-founder.
interesting_fact: He is part of the ownership group of MLS club Austin FC; a lifelong soccer fan, he played varsity soccer at school and still plays.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BS in computer applications and an MBA from Oklahoma State University, and serves on the boards of the Miracle Foundation and Austin Speech Labs.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Securonix; part of Austin FC ownership group
research_notes: Hurun lists him under Saviynt; documented roles are Vaau, Oracle/Sun, Securonix. Verify the Saviynt link before outreach.

name: Michael Gilbert
profile: Canadian chemist (PhD, UBC) who founded Semios in 2010 to bring pheromone-based mating disruption and wireless orchard sensors to growers, reducing pesticide use. Semios grew into an ag-data platform covering 100M+ acres.
interesting_fact: Semios pairs aerosol pheromone dispensers with a wireless sensor network, confusing pests like codling moth so they can't mate instead of killing them with sprays.
deep_cut_fact: He told the Georgia Straight that pheromones, though well understood, were used on 'less than one per cent of the farms that could be using them' - and that 'farmers are always environmentalists'.
current_role: Founder, Semios (Vancouver); CEO until Amie Thesingh's appointment in late 2025 - current title unconfirmed
research_notes: Common name; confirmed via Semios coverage. The Semios Group named Amie Thesingh CEO (Sept/Oct 2025).

name: Laura Behrens Wu
profile: German-born entrepreneur who left her University of St. Gallen master's to co-found Shippo in San Francisco (2013-14) with Simon Kreuz; the multi-carrier shipping API/platform serves 100,000+ e-commerce merchants and was valued at $1B in 2021. In 2026 she is still CEO, pushing AI-driven shipping analytics ('Shippo Intelligence').
interesting_fact: Shippo was born after she and Simon Kreuz ran an online shop as students and found shipping was the problem they couldn't solve; she was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 and Inc.'s Female Founders 100.
deep_cut_fact: She came to the US for a compulsory master's internship intending to stay just three months ('Ich hatte die Absicht, nur drei Monate zu bleiben'); she was named HSG (St. Gallen) Founder of the Year in 2015.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Shippo (San Francisco)
public_contact: pr_agency: Mike Bradshaw, Connect Marketing - Mikeb@connectmarketing.com
research_notes: Media contact listed on Shippo's Oct 2026 press release. Speaks German; featured in the German government's 'Makers of Tomorrow' series.

name: Max M. Diez
profile: Zurich-based serial B2B software entrepreneur, listed with Laura Behrens Wu and Simon Kreuz as a 2013 co-founder of Shippo, the San Francisco multi-carrier shipping API later valued at over $1B. He then co-founded Assaia, whose ApronAI uses existing apron cameras to manage aircraft turnarounds in real time for customers such as Alaska Airlines, Southwest and Fraport. He was CEO until January 2024, when he became chairman.
interesting_fact: On handing over Assaia's CEO role in 2024, he predicted that around 80% of airlines and airports would buy turnaround-optimisation technology within a few years, a category Assaia says it created.
deep_cut_fact: Assaia began as computer-vision technology without a use case. Diez and co-founder Nikolay Kobyshev ran workshops to find one, and Swissport's head of innovation saw a demo and said, in effect, 'if this actually worked' it would change apron operations.
current_role: Chairman & Co-Founder, Assaia (Zurich AI/computer-vision platform for aircraft turnarounds); co-founder of Shippo
public_contact: office_email: info@assaia.com (Assaia general contact) | official_website: https://www.assaia.com/company
research_notes: Rarely in the press about Shippo, where Laura Behrens Wu is the public face; his early Shippo CTO title appears only in aggregator profiles. Assaia also pitches sustainability benefits (cutting APU use and taxi time), which could interest an energy podcast.

name: Simon Kreuz
profile: German-born Simon Kreuz co-founded Shippo with CEO Laura Behrens Wu, whom he met at business school in Switzerland. Shippo gives e-commerce merchants and platforms a single API and app to compare carriers, buy labels and handle customs, an 'abstraction layer for the shipping network' in his words. It reached a ~$1B valuation.
interesting_fact: Shippo started when he and Behrens Wu ran a side-project online store and found that importing products in bulk from South Africa and shipping them around Europe was the hard part. The company sold its first label on February 14, 2014.
deep_cut_fact: He chose the name because hippos are herd animals that protect their group and can travel on land and water. He's bugged when people call the company 'Goshippo', and Shippo still didn't own shippo.com, so he offered a bonus to anyone who could help get it. Favorite reads include Cixin Liu's 'Remembrance of Earth's Past' trilogy.
current_role: Co-founder and President, Shippo (multi-carrier shipping API/platform, San Francisco). Title per 2020 Shippo Q&A; current status not re-verified.
research_notes: Self-described as preferring to work outside the spotlight, and very few interviews exist. No 2025-26 mentions found, so confirm he is still active at Shippo. Fun icebreaker: he'd rather chat over a German beer and would most like to meet Arnold Schwarzenegger.

name: Gaurab Chakrabarti
profile: Gaurab Chakrabarti is a physician-scientist (Forbes 30 Under 30; author on 20+ publications and patents). In 2016 he co-founded Solugen with MIT chemical engineer Sean Hunt. Solugen's 'Bioforge' plants combine enzymes and metal catalysts to turn corn sugar into chemicals such as hydrogen peroxide and organic acids that normally come from petroleum. It is building a second Bioforge in Marshall, Minnesota.
interesting_fact: In June 2024 Solugen got a conditional commitment for a $213.6M DOE Loan Programs Office loan guarantee for Bioforge Marshall. It is a ~500,000 sq ft plant next to an ADM corn facility, which DOE called its largest single bioindustrial manufacturing investment since the 2022 biotech executive order.
deep_cut_fact: Solugen started on a $10,000 MIT grant meant to cover salaries, rent and equipment, in a $150/month space near the Houston airport. Chakrabarti jokingly called himself 'the Heisenberg of hydrogen peroxide'. Seed investor Seth Bannon of Fifty Years called it one of the 'sketchiest' labs he had seen.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Solugen (Houston chemicals-from-biology company)
research_notes: Strong fit for the energy and decarbonization angle. Secondary sources (search results only) say he and Hunt met at a poker game in Texas while Hunt was visiting from MIT. Whether the DOE loan guarantee has closed was not verified.

name: Sean Hunt
profile: MIT chemical engineer (SM '13, PhD '16) who co-founded Solugen in 2016 with physician-scientist Gaurab Chakrabarti. Solugen makes hydrogen peroxide and other commodity chemicals from sugar using engineered enzymes and metal catalysts instead of petrochemicals; Hunt leads the chemienzymatic process technology behind its Bioforge plants. Forbes 30 Under 30.
interesting_fact: Solugen's first lab was leased for $150/month near the Houston airport in a facility TechCrunch said made it possibly 'the first legitimate multi-million-dollar company to start out in a meth lab'; Chakrabarti calls himself 'the Heisenberg of hydrogen peroxide'.
deep_cut_fact: Their first customers were float-spa owners: one saw the MIT $100K pitch video and shared it in a Facebook group of ~400 US float spas. Hunt then spent $7,000 at Home Depot building a pilot reactor - 'this little PVC bubble column' - and fed it 55-gallon drums of sugar. He calls himself a 'recovering biotech skeptic'.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Solugen (Houston chemicals company using enzymes + metal catalysis - 'Bioforge' plants)
research_notes: Great fit for energy/industrial podcast: Solugen now pitches its Forges as dual-use for energy systems and defense. Hunt has appeared on podcasts (e.g. MCJ 'Inevitable' ep.175 with Chakrabarti, The Chemical Show).

deep_cut_fact: In 2009 he founded Denver Cyberknife (later Anova Cancer Care), personally guaranteeing over $6M of bank debt - 'the alternative to success was personal insolvency' - and sold it, returning 12x to his outside investor.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SonderMind (Denver behavioral-health platform)

Vayyar's radar-on-chip is used for elder-care fall detection (Vayyar Care), in-car occupant and child-presence sensing, and robotics. He brings over 30 years in signal processing, radio systems and antennas.
interesting_fact: Vayyar's single-chip millimetre-wave radar can 'see' through walls and sense people without cameras. That makes privacy-preserving uses possible, such as detecting falls in seniors' bathrooms and children left in cars.
deep_cut_fact: Chayat is a graduate of Talpiot, the IDF's elite R&D programme (BSc in physics and maths at Hebrew University), and rose to Chief Engineer in an IDF R&D department. Before Vayyar he was Chief Scientist of BreezeCOM/Alvarion, an early broadband-wireless pioneer, and represented it in IEEE 802.16 (WiMAX) work.
current_role: Co-Founder and CTO, Vayyar Imaging (Yehud, Israel)

name: Raviv Melamed
profile: Raviv Melamed (BSc/MSc EE, Ben-Gurion University) joined Intel through its acquisition of startup Envara and rose to VP of the Intel Architecture Group and GM of its mobile wireless group. In 2011 he co-founded Vayyar, which makes low-cost 4D mmWave radar-imaging chips for in-cabin automotive sensing, elder care and more. It became a unicorn after its Series E.
interesting_fact: Vayyar began as a breast-cancer imaging project: Melamed asked why radio waves couldn't look inside the body if cheap RF silicon and MIMO radar made imaging affordable. The same sensor then spread to in-wall imaging, food contaminant detection, cars and elder-care fall detection.
deep_cut_fact: Melamed says he 'started life as an engineer at 13', building electronics and trying to sell them. Vayyar's core idea came from his army work using radio waves to see through walls, which he later reapplied to medical imaging.
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Vayyar Imaging (Yehud, Israel)

BeZero rates the quality of carbon credits for buyers, investors and developers, raised a $50M Series B, and has applied for ESMA recognition as a ratings provider.

name: Sebastien Cross
profile: UK economist who started his career at the Bank of England and then did fixed-income research at Bank of America, before co-founding BeZero Carbon with CEO Tommy Ricketts in 2020. BeZero publishes credit-rating-style quality ratings for carbon-offset projects, bringing capital-markets research methods to the voluntary carbon market. As CIO he focuses on regulation, market structure and product.
interesting_fact: BeZero applies a bond-market idea to climate: like an S&P or Moody's for carbon credits, it rates how likely each offset is to deliver the tonne of CO2 reduction it claims.
deep_cut_fact: Before carbon markets he was an economist at the Bank of England, where he began his career; he holds a BA in Economics from the University of Sheffield and an MSc in Finance & Economics from Warwick Business School.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Innovation Officer, BeZero Carbon (London carbon-credit ratings agency)

name: and George Danezis
profile: Computer scientist (b. 1979; Cambridge BA/PhD) known for privacy and anonymous-communications research. He worked at KU Leuven and Microsoft Research before becoming a UCL professor. current_role: Co-founder & Chief Scientist (part-time), Mysten Labs (Sui blockchain); Professor of Security and Privacy Engineering, UCL

name: Hayden Adams
profile: Former Siemens mechanical engineer (Stony Brook grad) who taught himself Solidity in 2017 and launched Uniswap, the automated-market-maker decentralized exchange on Ethereum, in November 2018. As CEO of Uniswap Labs he leads development of the Uniswap protocol, wallet and the Unichain layer-2 network.
interesting_fact: Uniswap was inspired by a Vitalik Buterin blog post on automated market makers; it launched on Ethereum mainnet on November 2, 2018 and became the largest decentralized exchange.

research_notes: Very active on X (@haydenzadams); that is the most direct public route. Media inquiries via media@uniswap.org.

name: Jonathan Ellis
profile: Co-founder and former CTO of DataStax and first chair of the Apache Cassandra project. He and Matt Pfeil left Rackspace in 2010 to found Riptano in Austin (renamed DataStax), the commercial Cassandra company later pivoted to real-time data for AI and acquired by IBM in 2025. He now runs Brokk, building static-analysis and review tooling for AI coding agents.

deep_cut_fact: Before Cassandra, around 2005 he built a multi-petabyte storage system for backup service Mozy using Reed-Solomon encoding; a PyCon talk about it led Rackspace to hire him, where evaluating NoSQL databases drew him to Cassandra.

name: Zhoujie Zhou

In 2021 he co-founded Magic Eden with Jack Lu, Sidney Zhang and Zhuoxun Yin; it became Solana's dominant NFT marketplace and a unicorn within months. The company has since gone multi-chain, launched the $ME token, and in 2025 bought the Slingshot trading app.

We didn't know how long the revenue was going to last.' The first six people all worked from six different addresses with no office.

He co-founded Blockstream in 2014, which builds Bitcoin infrastructure (Liquid sidechain, Jade wallet, mining). PhD in distributed systems from Exeter.
interesting_fact: He invented Hashcash (1997), the proof-of-work function at the heart of Bitcoin mining.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1990s anti-ITAR crypto-export protests, his 'RSA in 3 lines of Perl' signature was printed on a 'munitions' T-shirt that was technically illegal to export from the US. His first computer was a Sinclair ZX81.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Blockstream
public_contact: press_email: press@blockstream.com | official_website: http://www.cypherspace.org/adam/ | x: https://x.com/adam3us
research_notes: Very active on X (@adam3us). Avoid leading with the Satoshi speculation; he has denied it.

name: Hans Robertson
education: Chalmers University of Technology
profile: MIT-trained (BS/MS computer science) serial founder who co-founded Meraki and was its COO for almost a decade, helping design the first cloud-managed enterprise Wi-Fi, firewall and switching products before Cisco bought it for $1.2B in 2012. In 2016 he co-founded Verkada, the cloud-based physical-security (cameras, access control, 'physical AI') company, now 2,200+ employees, 30,000+ customers and valued at $5.8B; he runs daily operations with CEO Filip Kaliszan.
interesting_fact: He has co-founded two cloud-managed hardware unicorns: Meraki (networking, sold to Cisco for $1.2B in 2012) and Verkada (security cameras/access control, $5.8B), which started with just four employees in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before Meraki he was an early employee at VMware and a product manager at EMC, and began his career as a business analyst at McKinsey; he also sits on the boards of Pilot and industrial-maintenance AI startup Tractian.
current_role: Executive Chairman & Co-founder, Verkada
research_notes: Good fit for a hardware/infrastructure angle (cloud-managed devices, physical AI). Verkada's 2021 camera breach is a known topic - avoid in outreach.

name: Doss Cunningham*
profile: Austin-born Texas A&M finance grad who joined struggling supplement maker Cellucor as a student around 2003-04, took it over (buying out founder Poul Bodholt in 2007) and built it into Nutrabolt, maker of C4 Energy, Cellucor, XTEND and a stake in Bloom. Nutrabolt passed $1B in sales; Keurig Dr Pepper paid $863M for a 30% stake in late 2022.
interesting_fact: He turned Cellucor's C4 pre-workout powder into a zero-sugar carbonated energy drink around 2017, moving the brand from GNC shelves into grocery and gas-station coolers nationwide.
deep_cut_fact: He had a Deloitte job offer in hand when his roommate invited his new boss, Poul Bodholt, to a barbecue. Cunningham agreed to do some freelance bookkeeping, found the company was months from insolvency, and fixed cash flow by paying salespeople commission only when customers actually paid.
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Nutrabolt (Austin, Texas); co-founder/chairman FitJoy Nutrition; runs family office LivWell Ventures
research_notes: Hurun lists the name with an asterisk ('Doss Cunningham*'). Media-friendly: has appeared on Taste Radio, Kara Goldin and CEO Magazine. No published press email found on nutrabolt.com. Has been a guest on Kara Goldin's podcast (https://karagoldin.com/podcasts/doss-cunningham/).

name: Huang Dongxu
profile: Huang Dongxu (Ed Huang) is the Beijing-born engineer who co-founded PingCAP in 2015 with Max Liu and Cui Qiu and is chief architect of the open-source TiDB database and TiKV key-value store (a CNCF graduated project). PingCAP, now headquartered in Silicon Valley and backed by Sequoia, GGV and Coatue, sells TiDB Cloud and is pushing into AI-agent and vector workloads.
interesting_fact: Before PingCAP he worked at Wandou Labs (Wandoujia), where he built and open-sourced Codis, a Redis clustering tool; frustration with sharding led him to build TiDB, inspired by Google's Spanner and F1 papers.
deep_cut_fact: A former metal fan, he picked Pink Floyd's 'Dark Side of the Moon' as his desert-island track on the Kubernetes Podcast from Google, insisting the whole album counts as one song.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, PingCAP (maker of the TiDB distributed SQL database)

name: Brandon Millman
profile: Former Twitter engineer who moved into crypto in 2017, helping build the 0x protocol and the Matcha DEX aggregator before co-founding Phantom in 2021 with Chris Kalani and Francesco Agosti. Phantom became the dominant Solana wallet, expanded to Ethereum, Bitcoin, Base and Sui, acquired Bitski, and was valued at $3B in a $150M Series C (Jan 2025).
interesting_fact: Phantom grew to 3M+ users within about six months of launch; Millman's thesis was that a wallet is most people's first crypto experience, so 'a great wallet can 100x how many people we onboard'.
deep_cut_fact: He says he left Twitter after becoming 'disillusioned with the typical web2 growth loops (A/B tests, time spent, etc)' and started diving into Ethereum in 2017, which led to building 0x and Matcha with his future Phantom co-founders.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Phantom (self-custody crypto wallet), San Francisco
research_notes: Active on X and frequent crypto-podcast guest (CoinGecko, Solfate, Lightspeed). Note Phantom warns of impersonation scams - use only official channels. Sometimes misspelled 'Brandon Miller'.

name: Jason Warner
profile: American technologist, ex-CTO of GitHub (through the Microsoft acquisition) and earlier engineering leader at Heroku and Canonical. After a stint as a VC at Redpoint he co-founded Poolside with Eiso Kant in 2023 to build foundation models for coding and, ultimately, AGI; Poolside has raised billions and was reported valued around $12B.
interesting_fact: Poolside went full-stack into energy and compute: in Oct 2025 it announced Project Horizon, a self-powered 2-gigawatt AI campus on ~568 acres in West Texas's Permian Basin, fuelled by on-site natural gas and planned in eight 250MW phases.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Thomaston and Southbury, Connecticut, he got into tech via a high-school co-op at IBM's Southbury office, carrying printers and hooking up Token Ring networks, while also working at McDonald's; he only started programming at ~17 and first planned to study mechanical/aerospace engineering at Penn State.
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Poolside (frontier AI lab for software engineering; co-leads with Eiso Kant)
research_notes: Penn State CS alumnus; very active publicly on AI/compute. Strong fit for data-center/energy angle (Project Horizon). Some 2026 reports say the CoreWeave anchor-lease arrangement for Horizon changed - check current status before referencing. Media route: press@poolside.ai.

name: Eiso Kant
profile: Dutch-born software entrepreneur who co-founded Poolside in 2023 with ex-GitHub CTO Jason Warner. Poolside trains its own foundation models for agentic coding and was valued at about $12B after Nvidia agreed in Oct 2025 to invest up to $1B. He previously co-founded Tyba (a talent marketplace), source{d} (ML on source code) and Athenian.
interesting_fact: Poolside is building Project Horizon, a 2-gigawatt AI data-center campus in Pecos County, Texas, with CoreWeave. Phase one began in Oct 2025. Kant argues energy and compute will decide the AGI race.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 op-ed for El Adelantado de Segovia, Kant wrote that he had been programming since age 12. He said he was one of three friends from around Europe (he came from the Netherlands) who went to IE University in Segovia in 2009 and started Tyba while they were still students.
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Poolside (AI foundation models for coding); earlier described as CTO
research_notes: Very relevant for an energy/data-center show: Poolside's 2GW Texas campus, plus his podcast appearance 'Intelligence Isn't Enough: Why Energy & Compute Decide the AGI Race' (The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck). Active on X. Warner and Kant first met in 2017 when GitHub tried to acquire source{d}. No published press email was found.

name: Keone Hon
profile: Former high-frequency trader (quant at GETCO, then ~8 years leading a futures trading team at Jump Trading, then Jump Crypto) who in early 2022 co-founded Monad Labs with James Hunsaker and Eunice Giarta to build Monad, a high-performance parallel-execution EVM layer-1. The company (renamed Category Labs) raised ~$244M+ incl. a $225M Paradigm-led round; Monad mainnet launched 24 Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Monad's MON public sale in Nov 2025 was the first-ever token sale run through Coinbase's Token Sales platform, ahead of mainnet on 24 Nov 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He earned three MIT degrees by 2011 - a B.S. in Computer Science and Math, a Master of Finance and an M.Eng in Computer Science - before building ultra-low-latency trading systems at GETCO and Jump.
current_role: Co-founder of Monad; co-founder & general manager, Monad Foundation (formerly co-founder & CEO of Monad Labs, now Category Labs)
research_notes: Very active on X and crypto podcasts (Edge Podcast, Unlayered, CryptoNews); X handle widely cited as @keoneHD but not verified here. HFT-systems-to-blockchain-infrastructure angle fits a data-center/compute podcast. Title per IQ.wiki (Dec 2024 move to Foundation) - confirm.

name: James Hunsaker
profile: University of Iowa CS/maths graduate who worked at Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan, then spent eight years at Jump Trading building ultra-low-latency HFT systems and working on crypto trading and Pyth. In 2022 he co-founded Monad Labs with Keone Hon and Eunice Giarta to build Monad, a high-performance parallel-EVM Layer 1; the team rebranded to Category Labs in Dec 2024 and Monad mainnet launched in 2025.
interesting_fact: Monad applies HFT-style low-latency engineering to Ethereum compatibility - a parallel-execution EVM chain aiming for ~10,000 transactions per second while remaining portable for Ethereum apps.
deep_cut_fact: He started programming in elementary school by typing code printed in magazines into Apple II computers at school, as he recalled on Munjal Shah's Unfiltered Podcast (2023).
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Category Labs (formerly Monad Labs, developer of the Monad blockchain)
research_notes: Category Labs' team page lists him as CEO (older sources say CTO). Active in crypto podcasts/X; no published press email found.

name: Eunice Giarta
profile: MIT computer-science graduate who co-founded Monad Labs in 2022 with Keone Hon and James Hunsaker to build Monad, a high-performance parallel-EVM layer-1 blockchain. As COO she ran business development and ecosystem; when Monad Labs became Category Labs in Dec 2024 (valued ~$3B), she moved with Keone Hon to the new Monad Foundation, which handles ecosystem, governance and developer relations.
interesting_fact: She took a famously non-linear route into crypto: MIT (CS, minor in finance), a rates-derivatives trading internship at Bank of America Merrill Lynch, product/business-development roles at Broadway Technology and senior PM at Shutterstock, before co-founding Monad.
deep_cut_fact: Between Shutterstock and Monad she reportedly worked as a chef de partie in Jean-Georges Vongerichten's restaurant group (2019-2020), and she ran her own design studio, Euna Creative; at MIT she was a Media Lab research assistant, which is where she met co-founder Keone Hon.
current_role: Co-founder of Monad (Monad Labs, renamed Category Labs in Dec 2024); now with the Monad Foundation (co-founder/general manager per profiles)
public_contact: x: https://twitter.com/0x_eunice | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/eunicegiarta/ | official_website: https://www.monad.xyz
