name: Yotam Segev
profile: Israeli Talpiot and Unit 8200 veteran who, with CTO Tamar Bar-Ilan, built and ran the cloud security division of Unit 8200 before co-founding data-security platform Cyera in 2021. Cyera discovers, classifies and protects data across cloud, SaaS and on-prem; backed by Sequoia, Accel, Coatue and others, it raised at a $6B+ valuation in 2025 and ~$9B later, among the fastest-growing cyber companies ever.
interesting_fact: Cyera went from founding in 2021 to a $3B valuation (Series D, $300M) in 2024 and over $6B in 2025, a trajectory Calcalist compared only to Wiz; it also acquired Trail Security for $162M.
deep_cut_fact: He met co-founder Tamar Bar-Ilan in the IDF's Talpiot program, where he later served as a Senior Class Commander; on Cyera's Cyber Inspiration podcast he said 'We wanted to build something that will outlast us.'
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Cyera (AI-native data security)
research_notes: Frequent podcast/conference speaker (RSAC, SC World, Dark Reading contributor). Route via Cyera press office.

name: Tamar Bar-Ilan
profile: Israeli engineer (BSc physics and computer science, Hebrew University) and Talpiot graduate who co-founded AI-native data security company Cyera in 2021 with CEO Yotam Segev. Cyera, based in New York and Tel Aviv, discovers and classifies sensitive data across clouds and has become one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity unicorns; she leads product and engineering.
interesting_fact: She and Yotam Segev met in the IDF's elite Talpiot program and together founded, built and ran the cloud security division of Unit 8200.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the army in early 2020 she and Segev spent most of that year as 'independent entrepreneurs in our living rooms, learning how to set up a company' - Cyera is her first job after military service.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cyera
research_notes: Rare example of a female cybersecurity unicorn co-founder/CTO; press route via press@cyera.io.

name: Don Burnette
profile: Autonomous-vehicle engineer (UF electrical engineering, CMU robotics master's) who was a software tech lead on Google's self-driving project (now Waymo), co-founded self-driving truck startup Otto (bought by Uber in 2016), and founded Kodiak in 2018. Kodiak went public via SPAC in 2025 and runs customer-owned driverless trucks hauling frac sand in the Permian Basin for Atlas Energy Solutions.
interesting_fact: Kodiak's trucks run fully driverless for Atlas Energy Solutions in the Permian Basin, hauling frac sand to wellsites around the clock; Atlas plans to grow the driverless fleet to 100 trucks by mid-2027.
deep_cut_fact: Before Kodiak he co-founded Otto, described in Kodiak's investor materials as the first self-driving truck startup, after starting as a software tech lead on Google's self-driving car project; he holds a robotics master's from Carnegie Mellon.
current_role: Founder, CEO & Director, Kodiak AI (Kodiak Robotics; autonomous trucking, Mountain View; Nasdaq: KDK)
research_notes: Excellent energy-podcast fit: driverless trucking in oilfield logistics (Permian frac sand). Frequent speaker at CES, FreightWaves and SAE events. First Kodiak/Atlas driverless delivery: Jan 2025 (https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/24/kodiak-has-made-its-first-driverless-truck-deliveries-to-customer-atlas-energy).

name: Kavitha Subramanian
profile: Indian fintech co-founder who, with Ravi Kumar and Shrini Viswanath, built Upstox (RKSV), a Mumbai discount broker backed by Tiger Global and Ratan Tata that became a unicorn in 2021 with 10M+ users. IIT Bombay electrical engineer and Wharton MBA, formerly at McKinsey and private-equity firms Actis and LeapFrog.
interesting_fact: She is one of relatively few women co-founders of an Indian fintech unicorn; Upstox scaled past 10 million users during the 2020-21 retail investing boom.
deep_cut_fact: Before Upstox she was an associate director at impact investor LeapFrog Investments and an investment principal at emerging-markets PE firm Actis.
current_role: Co-founder, Upstox (growth, strategy, finance and customer experience)
research_notes: Frequently quoted on women investors and financial literacy (Zee Business).

name: Shrini Viswanath
profile: Co-founded RKSV Securities in 2009 with Ravi Kumar and Raghu Kumar; it moved into flat-fee online retail broking in 2012 and launched the Upstox trading platform in 2016. Upstox, backed by Tiger Global, grew into one of India's largest discount brokers with 10M+ users and a ~$3.5B valuation (2021). Viswanath led technology until an external CTO was hired in 2021.
interesting_fact: More than 80% of Upstox's new customers come from India's tier 2 and tier 3 cities, per Viswanath.
deep_cut_fact: RKSV was set up in 2009 purely as a proprietary trading firm; only in 2012 did it pivot to retail broking with an online-only, flat-fee unlimited trading plan.
current_role: Co-founder, Upstox (RKSV Securities), Mumbai; former CTO, now in a strategic role
research_notes: Lower profile than CEO Ravi Kumar. Undergraduate degree from University of Illinois per MarketScreener (aggregator, unverified). Route via Upstox corporate comms.

name: Shiv Rao
profile: Cardiologist Dr. Shiv Rao, a Pittsburgh native, ran UPMC Enterprises' health-tech investments (2013-19). In 2018 he founded Abridge with CMU professor Zachary Lipton to end doctors' nightly note dictation. Its ambient AI scribe turns clinical conversations into notes. Fortune valued it at $2.75B in Feb 2025; Hurun lists $5B.
interesting_fact: Rao still practices cardiology while running a multibillion-dollar AI company: he is on call Thursdays and takes one weekend shift a month. Emory Healthcare CEO Joon Lee calls him 'a doctor first.'
deep_cut_fact: He was a high-school skateboarder into Fugazi and Minor Threat. At Carnegie Mellon he deejayed in art museums and made avant-garde electronic music with virtual synths (he admires Aphex Twin and Autechre). One of his 'side quests' was tracking down Rick Rubin, whom he persuaded to give an interview at an Abridge event.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Abridge (generative-AI clinical documentation); practicing cardiologist at UPMC
public_contact: press_email: press@abridge.com | official_website: https://www.abridge.com/bio/shiv-rao | x: https://twitter.com/AbridgeHQ (company account)
research_notes: Very media-friendly; has appeared on Masters of Scale, the Voicebot podcast and HLTH. He says 'Pittsburgh is a part of our founding DNA' (Axios, March 2025). Music is a great rapport topic.

name: Nathaniel Bennett
profile: Protein-design scientist (Nate Bennett, PhD) trained at the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design under Nobel laureate David Baker, where he worked on generative deep-learning models for designing binding proteins, including RFdiffusion. He co-founded Xaira Therapeutics with Baker and Joseph Watson; Xaira launched in 2024 with over $1B in funding and licenses IPD technology.
interesting_fact: He was co-lead author of the 2025 Nature paper 'Atomically accurate de novo design of antibodies with RFdiffusion' - AI-designed antibodies created from scratch - technology Xaira has licensed.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining why de novo antibodies matter, he noted that many diseases have no approved medicines because they are driven by molecules with vulnerable sites that small-molecule drugs can't reach - 'Computer-generated antibodies could target these sites directly.' The RFantibody code was released openly on GitHub.
current_role: Co-founder, Xaira Therapeutics (AI drug discovery; South San Francisco/Seattle) - employed there per 2025 Nature paper disclosures
research_notes: Scientist-founder rather than the business lead (Xaira launched with ex-Genentech executives in leadership, per BioSpace headline). info@xaira.com is the company's general contact.

name: Justas Dauparas
profile: Machine-learning protein-design researcher, formerly a project scientist in David Baker's lab at the UW Institute for Protein Design, who led ProteinMPNN (Science 2022) and LigandMPNN (Nature Methods 2025). Xaira, launched in 2024 with $1B+ under CEO Marc Tessier-Lavigne, was founded to build on IPD models including RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN.
interesting_fact: ProteinMPNN, the sequence-design model he led at the Baker lab, runs in about one second - over 200x faster than the previous best software - and its designs were more likely to fold as intended in lab tests.
deep_cut_fact: On building ProteinMPNN he said: 'Neural networks are easy to train if you have a ton of data... We had to go in and identify which features in these molecules are the most important.'
current_role: Protein-design scientist; Hurun lists him as a Xaira Therapeutics founder, but no Xaira source confirms his current role
research_notes: GeekWire (2024) describes him as one of the scientists behind ProteinMPNN in its Xaira coverage (https://www.geekwire.com/2024/inside-the-seattle-labs-of-xaira-the-ai-powered-startup-launched-with-1b-from-investors/); I couldn't open the article to confirm his Xaira title. An academic, not a typical founder-CEO; route via Xaira.

name: David Baker
profile: Biochemist David Baker shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for computational protein design. He directs UW's Institute for Protein Design, whose Rosetta software, Rosetta@home and Foldit pioneered protein modelling, and has co-founded more than a dozen biotechs including Icosavax (acquired by AstraZeneca), Sana, Lyell and AI drug-discovery company Xaira Therapeutics, which launched with $1B+.
interesting_fact: His lab turned protein folding into crowd science: Rosetta@home lets volunteers donate computer time, and Foldit is a video game in which players solve protein structures.
deep_cut_fact: A Seattle native and Garfield High School graduate, his lab designed Top7, the first artificial protein with a fold not seen in nature; he also gave a 2019 TED talk, '5 challenges we could solve by designing new proteins'.
current_role: Director, Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington; co-founder of Xaira Therapeutics
public_contact: press_email: communications@ipd.uw.edu | office_email: contact@ipd.uw.edu | press_email: info@xaira.com
research_notes: Nobel laureate; heavy media demand, so go via IPD communications. AI-for-science and compute angle (protein design models) fits a data-center podcast. Not to be confused with other David Bakers.

Umoja develops in vivo CAR-T therapies that engineer a patient's immune cells inside the body rather than in a lab; Crisman oversees technical operations and manufacturing, including its Colorado site.
interesting_fact: Before Umoja he was executive director of the Gates Biomanufacturing Facility at CU Anschutz, building out and staffing a protein and cell-therapy CDMO that delivered many first-in-human therapeutic products.
deep_cut_fact: At Juno Therapeutics he led the CMC (manufacturing) program for JCAR017, the CAR-T product later approved as Breyanzi, and was Juno's head of late-stage process development; earlier he held scientific roles at ZymoGenetics and CMC Biologics.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technical Officer, Umoja Biopharma (Seattle)
research_notes: Company general inbox (not personal). Researched from Umoja's own site (web search budget exhausted). The Breyanzi naming of JCAR017 is general knowledge, not on the cited page.

name: Gary D. Glick
profile: Chemist and serial biotech founder. He started Lycera from his academic research, built IFM Therapeutics (program sales worth $750M so far, potentially $4.7B+) and launched Scorpion Therapeutics, which Eli Lilly bought for up to $2.5B in 2025. He founded Odyssey in 2021, which IPO'd on Nasdaq in May 2026 and is in Phase 2 for an ulcerative colitis drug (OD-001).
interesting_fact: IFM, which he founded and ran, was the first company to target the NLRP3 inflammasome and STING pathways, two of the hottest immunology targets of the last decade.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his Ph.D. in organic chemistry at Columbia and did an NIH postdoc at Harvard. While running Odyssey in Boston he also chairs London-based Charm Therapeutics, using the transatlantic time difference to handle Charm work outside Boston hours.
current_role: Founder, President and CEO, Odyssey Therapeutics (Nasdaq: ODTX); also Executive Chairman and interim CEO of Charm Therapeutics
public_contact: press_email: media@odysseytx.com | ir_email: investors@odysseytx.com | official_website: https://odysseytx.com
research_notes: Formerly a University of Michigan chemistry professor (general knowledge, not verified this pass). Comms lead is Benjamin Navon, Senior Director, Communications. Not to be confused with NFL player Gary Glick (died 2015).

name: Cynthia Chaerunissa
profile: Indonesian entrepreneur who co-founded Kopi Kenangan in 2017 with Edward Tirtanata and James Prananto, starting from a single outlet in Jakarta with about Rp150M of capital. Kopi Kenangan popularised affordable palm-sugar milk coffee, reached a ~$1B valuation, and now runs over 1,000 outlets, expanding abroad as Kenangan Coffee (Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, Australia, Taiwan).
interesting_fact: The signature drink 'Kopi Kenangan Mantan' roughly means 'memories of an ex' - the name was chosen so customers would remember the coffee the way they remember past lovers. In April 2022 the chain set an Indonesian MURI record by opening 26 outlets in 13 cities in one week.
deep_cut_fact: Edward, James and Cynthia opened the first outlet in Standard Chartered Tower, Jakarta, in 2017; by the third day the queue spilled into the building lobby and the coffee sold out within 90 seconds, per the company's own history page.
current_role: Co-founder, Kopi Kenangan / Kenangan Brands (Jakarta); exact current title not verified

name: Victor Cui
profile: Edmonton-born sports executive who co-founded ONE Championship in Singapore with Chatri Sityodtong in 2011 and was its CEO for its first eight years, building it into Asia's largest sports media property (valued $1B+, broadcast in 150+ countries). He left in 2022 to run the CFL's Edmonton Elks, and now advises sport startups, leads APAC for Shaun White's Snow League and sits on the Canadian Olympic Committee (Class B member, 2025).
interesting_fact: Before ONE he ran 'Martial Combat', a promotion staging two shows a month at Resorts World Sentosa in 2010, after senior roles at ESPN Star Sports and the PGA Tour and work on the X Games, Olympics and Commonwealth Games.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Edmonton to Filipino parents (Chinese ancestry on his father's side), he moved with his family to West Africa at age five and returned to Edmonton at 13; his Chinese name is 崔伟德. He's also a founding partner of Inzdr, an AI athlete 'digital twin' platform built with two-time F1 champion Mika Hakkinen.
current_role: Sport-business advisor/entrepreneur; Head of Asia-Pacific, The Snow League; founding partner, EPIC World Championship (pickleball); co-founder of ONE Championship
public_contact: personal_email: victor@victorcui.com | official_website: https://victorcui.com/ | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/victorcui/ | instagram: https://www.instagram.com/victorcui/
research_notes: Very reachable - his own site invites founders to 'Get in Touch' and lists speaking/press pages. Motto on his site: 'Create new value rather than compete for value created by others.' No longer at ONE Championship (left Feb 2022).

ONE has been valued at over $1B and broadcasts to global audiences, including a weekly US prime-time slot.

name: Tyler Shaddix
profile: Engineer who co-founded ed-tech company GoGuardian (founded 2014 as Liminex Inc.), whose software helps K-12 schools filter content, manage classroom devices and flag students at risk of self-harm. GoGuardian was acquired by Sumeru Equity Partners in 2018, merged with Pear Deck in 2020 and was valued at ~$1B+; Shaddix has served as Chief Product Officer and now Chief Innovation Officer.
interesting_fact: Within months of launch GoGuardian was picked by Los Angeles Unified School District for its 1:1 device rollout, and by mid-2015 it was installed in 1,600+ US school districts.
deep_cut_fact: Before GoGuardian he spent about five years (2008–2013) as a software developer at NetFile, Inc., while studying computer science and engineering at UC Merced.
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Innovation Officer and Board Member, GoGuardian (El Segundo / Los Angeles)
research_notes: GoGuardian's student-monitoring products have drawn privacy criticism—avoid as an opener. Low personal public profile.

It was founded in 2014 and was the first to offer remote monitoring of orthodontic treatments via smartphone scans, backed by 80+ patents. interesting_fact: DentalMonitoring says its founders left other successful companies in 2014 to build 'DentalMind', and that it became the first company to offer remote monitoring for orthodontic treatments, protected by 80+ patents.

name: Christopher Altchek
profile: Serial founder who runs Cadence, which partners with health systems to remotely monitor patients with chronic conditions such as heart failure, hypertension and diabetes. Clinical teams track vitals, coach, and titrate medications; Cadence reached a ~$1B+ valuation. He previously co-founded the millennial news site Mic (originally PolicyMic) in 2011.
interesting_fact: He argues that care teams' jobs (monitoring vitals, coaching, titrating meds, ordering labs) will each 'be done by an agent' in the future. Cadence's HypertensionOS software was selected for the FDA's TEMPO program.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he co-founded PolicyMic in 2011 with high-school friend Jake Horowitz; it was rebranded Mic in 2014, and both made Forbes 30 Under 30 that year.
current_role: Founder & CEO, Cadence (remote patient monitoring for chronic disease), New York

profile: Serial data-integration entrepreneur: co-founded Informatica with Diaz Nesamoney in 1993 and took it public, then founded SnapLogic in 2006, building it into an AI/'agentic integration' platform with $100M+ ARR. He stepped down as CEO in August 2025 to become chairman and adviser.
interesting_fact: Informatica, the company he co-founded and left as CEO in 2004, was acquired by Salesforce in 2025 for about $8 billion — some 20 years after his departure; Fortune ran a piece on what that felt like.

name: Stefan Kukman
profile: Slovenian founder and CEO (Štefan Kukman) of CargoX, founded in 2018, which runs a blockchain-based platform for transferring trade documents such as electronic bills of lading. CargoX is the authorised blockchain document-transfer gateway for Egypt's NAFEZA single window (Advance Cargo Information), and in 2025 it went live with the UAE's MPCI programme; it also serves carriers such as Evergreen and HMM.
interesting_fact: CargoX's platform was approved by the International Group of P&I Clubs in February 2020, and it underpins Egypt's national Advance Cargo Information system for import documents.
deep_cut_fact: CargoX demoed its 'Smart B/L' on the public Ethereum blockchain at the International Logistics Congress in Portorož in April 2018, then issued its first commercial one in July 2018 for a shipment from Shanghai to the Slovenian port of Koper.
current_role: CEO, CargoX (Ljubljana, Slovenia)

name: Neha Palmer
profile: Energy and infrastructure executive with 20+ years building energy supply and energy-intensive infrastructure - from early work as an engineer in natural gas to developing energy-hungry data centers at Google. She co-founded Terawatt Infrastructure about five years ago to build and operate charging depots for electric trucking, rideshare and autonomous-vehicle fleets; it won a $63.8M federal EV-charging grant.
interesting_fact: Before Terawatt she developed data centers at Google - a direct bridge between the podcast's energy and data-center themes. She holds a Kellogg MBA in Finance and a Cal Poly San Luis Obispo civil-engineering BS.
deep_cut_fact: In her 'Teraversary' essay she recalls that right after Terawatt's first public announcement, one of the first customer calls came from a friend at an autonomous-vehicle company - and AV fleets have since become a major Terawatt focus. Outside work she spends winters 'chasing snow'.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Terawatt Infrastructure (San Francisco)
research_notes: Top-priority fit for an energy/data-center podcast (ex-Google data-center energy, now EV/AV fleet charging). LinkedIn listed is the company page. Writes her own company blog posts.

Earlier he was president/CEO of Y Combinator-backed referral-marketing company Talkable. He moved to a board role in late 2023 and has a newer venture, Real.Photos.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he co-founded and ran Talkable, a YC-backed company building refer-a-friend programs for e-commerce brands; he holds a BA in political science from Emory University.

profile: Luke Kervin co-founded PatientPop in 2014 with Travis Schneider, a practice-growth and digital-marketing platform for independent healthcare providers. In November 2021 PatientPop merged with Kareo (founded 2004 by Dan Rodrigues) to form Tebra, an Irvine-based practice-management, billing and patient-engagement software company valued at over $1B.
interesting_fact: Tebra was born from a merger: Kareo's clinical and financial software combined with PatientPop's patient-acquisition platform to serve independent medical practices end to end.

profile: Israeli SaaS operator who moved to New York with the early Datorama team, helped scale it to its 2018 acquisition by Salesforce and led post-merger integration as a Salesforce VP. He joined CHEQ (go-to-market security: blocking bots and fake users from ad funnels, sites and data) around 2019 as COO, was named President & COO and added to the co-founding team after a $150M Tiger Global-led Series C valued CHEQ at ~$1B in 2022.

name: Raffi Garabedian
profile: Raffi Garabedian co-founded Electric Hydrogen (with ex-First Solar CTO David Eaglesham), which builds large-scale PEM electrolyzer plants to make low-cost green hydrogen. Before that he joined First Solar in 2008 and served as its CTO from 2012, running its technology platform and product development. He has also sat on the board of ESS Inc.
interesting_fact: He is named on about 30 issued U.S. patents and holds electrical-engineering degrees from Rensselaer (B.S.) and UC Davis (M.S.).
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he spent 15+ years in MEMS, building products from automotive engine-control sensors to fiber-optic telecom switches, and was founding CEO of two startups that were acquired: Micromachines Inc. (by Kavlico) and Touchdown Technologies (by Agilent/Verigy).
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Electric Hydrogen Co.
research_notes: No published press email found; company site has an on-page contact section (eh2.com/#contact). Personal LinkedIn is linked from the company team page. Regular CERAWeek / energy-podcast speaker — strong fit for an energy podcast.

name: David Eaglesham
profile: Materials physicist (PhD Bristol). He spent years at Bell Labs on semiconductors, then managed at Lawrence Livermore and Applied Materials, and as First Solar's VP Technology/CTO (2006-12) saw revenue grow from ~$50M to ~$4B. He co-founded Electric Hydrogen (c.2020) out of Breakthrough Energy Ventures to build low-cost 100MW-class PEM electrolyzer plants.
interesting_fact: EH2's Massachusetts gigafactory is designed for 1.2 GW/yr of PEM electrolyzers, one of the largest in the world. Its 100 MW plant is the core of Infinium's Project Roadrunner e-fuels site in Pecos, Texas.
deep_cut_fact: He is a past president of the Materials Research Society, and in that role called for a 'Manhattan Project' for renewable energy. In a 2012 interview at an Ypsilanti brewery he argued that the hunt for earth-abundant PV materials was 'working on the wrong problem' because efficiency matters more.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Electric Hydrogen (EH2), Devens/Natick, Massachusetts
research_notes: info@eh2.com is the company's general contact (not press-specific). CEO Raffi Garabedian (his First Solar colleague) is the usual public face. Between First Solar and EH2 he worked at magnesium-battery startup Pellion Technologies. Strong fit for an energy podcast.

name: Derek Warnick
profile: Derek Warnick is co-founder and CFO of Electric Hydrogen, which builds large, low-cost PEM electrolyzer plants for green hydrogen. A clean-energy finance specialist, he previously held executive roles at Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Tank Utility and Infinite Cooling. EH2 raised $380M in 2023 and is now supplying 100MW+ projects in Texas, Europe and Australia.
interesting_fact: Electric Hydrogen's 2023 $380M Series C was one of the largest climate-tech raises of that year, aimed at scaling its 100MW electrolyzer plants and Devens, Massachusetts factory.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups, Warnick began his career as a technical consultant at the World Bank.
current_role: Co-founder and CFO, Electric Hydrogen (EH2)

Spoke at Aspen Ideas: Climate 2023.

name: Byung Joon Han
profile: Dr. BJ Han spent 1999-2019 at STATS ChipPAC, serving as CTO, CEO and chairman, and grew the chip packager from about $100M to $4.3B in revenue. In 2021 he co-founded Silicon Box with Marvell founders Sehat Sutardja and Weili Dai. The company does chiplet integration and panel-level advanced packaging in Singapore and is building a €3.2B plant in Novara, Italy.
interesting_fact: Silicon Box's Singapore fab, which it calls the world's largest panel-level packaging facility by capacity, shipped its 100 millionth unit in Oct 2025. The company says it beat Han's long-standing record of 99.7% wafer-scale yield.
deep_cut_fact: Han holds over 300 patents. His teams drove commercial adoption of the quad flat no-lead (QFN) package, now shipped at over 100 billion units a year. He received the 2025 Leonardo International Prize for contributions to Italy's tech landscape. PhD, Columbia.
current_role: Co-founder, Board Director and CEO, Silicon Box (Singapore)
public_contact: press_email: janice.yeo@silicon-box.com | contact_form: https://www.silicon-box.com/contact | official_website: https://www.silicon-box.com
research_notes: Good fit for the AI/data-center hardware angle (chiplets and advanced packaging for AI/HPC). Mike Han is Head of Business. Route media requests via the Silicon Box press contact or the site's Media Enquiries form.

name: Eric Vreeland
profile: Crypto marketing and strategy executive who joined Polyhedra Network in 2024 as Chief Strategy Officer after leading marketing at LayerZero Labs, with earlier roles at People Data Labs and Jobr. Polyhedra builds ZK-proof infrastructure including zkBridge (connecting 25+ chains) and 'verifiable AI'; he is a frequent podcast spokesperson for the company.
interesting_fact: He argues that 'ZK-proofs are the only way blockchain can realize its true vision', and promotes Polyhedra's push into verifiable AI using zero-knowledge proofs.
current_role: Chief Strategy Officer, Polyhedra Network (zero-knowledge proof / zkBridge infrastructure)
research_notes: Hurun lists him as a founder, but CB Insights/Crunchbase name James Zhang (Abner Zhang) as Polyhedra's founder and Vreeland as CSO who joined in 2024 - he is likely an executive, not a co-founder, and may not be UHNW. Princeton economics / Berkeley Haas MBA appear only in a podcast bio (unverified).

name: Tiancheng X
profile: Tiancheng Xie (listed by Hurun as 'Tiancheng X') earned a UC Berkeley PhD in computer science researching zero-knowledge proofs, then co-founded Polyhedra Network in 2022 from the group's zkBridge research. Polyhedra builds ZK proof systems (deVirgo, Expander), the zkBridge cross-chain interoperability protocol and verifiable-AI tooling; backers include Polychain and Binance Labs.
interesting_fact: Polyhedra grew directly out of a 2022 academic paper on zkBridge that Xie co-authored during his Berkeley PhD; he calls the April 2023 zkBridge testnet launch his favourite memory at the company.
deep_cut_fact: He is first author of 'Libra: Succinct Zero-Knowledge Proofs with Optimal Prover Computation' (CRYPTO 2019, with Jiaheng Zhang, Yupeng Zhang, Charalampos Papamanthou and Dawn Song) - the first ZK proof system with both optimal prover time and succinct proofs.
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Polyhedra Network (zero-knowledge proof infrastructure; ZKJ token)
research_notes: Name in input is truncated ('Tiancheng X'); identified as Tiancheng Xie via Polyhedra Network. Academic-cryptographer founder; CEO Abner Jia is the business face. No published press email found.

name: James Zhang

Polyhedra was founded in 2022 by cryptography researchers from UC Berkeley, Stanford and Tsinghua, raised about $75M privately and has since pivoted toward zk-verified AI ('verifiable intelligence').
interesting_fact: zkBridge grew out of an academic paper the founders published in 2022; Zhang described it as using 'zero-knowledge proof constructions to verify the validity of the consensus between two blockchains' -- trustless bridging without external assumptions.
current_role: Co-founder, Polyhedra Network (exact current title unclear)

name: Abner Jia
profile: Co-founder and CEO of Polyhedra Network, a zero-knowledge proof infrastructure company spun out of UC Berkeley cryptography research (co-founders Tiancheng Xie, Jiaheng Zhang, Yuncong Hu). Polyhedra built zkBridge, the Expander proof system and EXPchain, and raised ~$75M at a $1B post-money valuation from Polychain, Binance Labs, Animoca Brands and others.
interesting_fact: Polyhedra's zkBridge, the first cross-chain bridge secured by zk-SNARKs, has processed 21M+ cross-chain transactions and became the default verifier (DVN) for 10 chains in the LayerZero ecosystem.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Polyhedra Network (zero-knowledge proof infrastructure)
research_notes: Very little public biographical info on Jia himself (no interviews found); CTO Tiancheng Xie is the more visible founder. Company HQ variously listed as Berkeley/Singapore. No press email found.

name: Danny Jenkins
profile: Irish-born cybersecurity entrepreneur who started in IT in 1997, co-founded Dublin email-security SaaS MXSweep (sold to j2) and led Sirrustec (sold to Censornet in 2014). In 2017 he co-founded ThreatLocker in Orlando with Sami Jenkins and John Carolan, built around 'default deny' allowlisting; it serves 50,000+ businesses and raised a US$190M Series F in 2026, bringing total funding to nearly US$500M.
interesting_fact: ThreatLocker was born after he witnessed a phishing attack that nearly destroyed a company, leading him to build a 'default deny' model where nothing runs unless explicitly approved.
deep_cut_fact: Long before ThreatLocker he co-founded MXSweep, a Dublin-based email and internet security SaaS provider later sold to j2, and was CEO of white-label email-security firm Sirrustec, sold to Censornet in 2014.
current_role: CEO & Co-founder, ThreatLocker (zero-trust endpoint security, Orlando, FL)
research_notes: Frequent podcast guest and keynote host at ThreatLocker's Zero Trust World conference. Has said in interviews he left school at 15 for an IT apprenticeship (seen in search summaries of interviews, e.g. https://www.scworld.com/podcast-episode/3596-how-to-start-a-company-when-you-dont-want-to-a-journey-from-founder-to-cto-to-ceo-danny-jenkins-fs-9; not independently verified).

name: Sami Jenkins
profile: Co-founder and COO of Orlando-based Zero Trust endpoint security company ThreatLocker, launched in 2017 with Danny Jenkins and John Carolan. With ~20 years in IT starting in tech support and sysadmin work, she oversees operations, product, engineering, sales and support and global expansion.
interesting_fact: She led ThreatLocker through an 83% headcount increase in 2024; its 'Cyber Hero' support team answers requests in about a minute on average.
deep_cut_fact: Before ThreatLocker she co-founded email-security developer Sirrustec and founded PRD Technology, an IT management and software services firm; she was a finalist in CRN's inaugural Women of the Year awards (2023).
current_role: Co-founder & COO, ThreatLocker

name: John Carolan
profile: Co-founded zero-trust endpoint security company ThreatLocker in 2017 with Danny and Sami Jenkins; the company launched with application allowlisting ('default deny') and now protects 50,000+ businesses, reaching a $1B+ valuation. He leads quality assurance.
interesting_fact: ThreatLocker's default-deny model blocks every application action unless explicitly allowed - the opposite of traditional antivirus.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief of Quality Assurance, ThreatLocker (Orlando)

profile: Brazilian fintech founder. After 11 years as co-founder/CEO of credit fund manager Quatá Investimentos, he founded QI Tech in 2018 as banking/credit-as-a-service infrastructure; it became a unicorn in 2024 and in 2025 ANBIMA ranked it Brazil's largest FIDC administrator and custodian.
interesting_fact: QI Tech was the first Sociedade de Crédito Direto (SCD) licensed by Brazil's Central Bank (Dec 2018), and its 2021 R$270M round from GIC was billed as LatAm's largest fintech Series A.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, he spent five years at Standard & Poor's in Transaction Services for Latin America, managed funds at Link Corretora and co-founded Sorse Asset Management; he studied Business Administration at Ibmec.
current_role: Founder and CEO, QI Tech (São Paulo, Brazil)
research_notes: Company press inbox is comunicacao@qitech.com.br. QI Tech has publicly discussed an eventual IPO.

name: Marcelo Bentivoglio
profile: Co-founder and CFO of QI Tech, the Brazilian financial-infrastructure (banking/credit-as-a-service) unicorn, which he joined as CFO around its 2018 founding (one Insper report says 2021). He leads fundraising, including rounds from GIC and General Atlantic.
interesting_fact: On IPO plans (South Summit Brazil, Apr 2025): 'Hoje, eu não tenho nada a fazer com o dinheiro... Seria um IPO por ego' - he views an IPO purely as a financial transaction.
deep_cut_fact: His fundraising philosophy, from a 2025 interview: 'Muita gente olha para a captação como um prêmio, eu olho como um compromisso' (many see a raise as a prize; I see it as a commitment).
current_role: Co-founder and CFO, QI Tech (Brazil)
research_notes: Not listed among founders on QI Tech's own About page (which lists Mac Dowell, Buosi, Emilio Moreira), though press calls him co-founder.

name: Marcelo Buosi
profile: Co-founder and COO of QI Tech, the Brazilian banking/credit-as-a-service infrastructure unicorn founded in 2018. Before that he worked with Pedro Mac Dowell at credit fund manager Quatá Investimentos in operations and fund management; QI Tech grew out of Quatá's own infrastructure needs.
interesting_fact: QI Tech reports R$494B in Pix transactions, R$107B+ in credit issued and R$190B+ under management.
deep_cut_fact: An economist from USP's FEA, he started out in the economics department of Barclays Bank before joining Quatá Investimentos.
current_role: Co-founder and COO, QI Tech (Brazil)

name: Alex Bradford
profile: Founded Rain in 2019 to offer earned wage access and financial-wellness tools integrated with employers' payroll (Workday, etc.). Rain raised a $75M Series B led by Prosus (2025) and $300M in financing from Clear Haven. Stanford undergrad and HBS MBA, with brief stints at Goldman Sachs and McKinsey.
interesting_fact: Rain is his third fintech company; he got the idea in late 2018 after learning of a European employer-integrated finance company.
deep_cut_fact: At Stanford he was a teaching assistant for a Social Entrepreneurship course focused heavily on microcredit.
current_role: CEO and Founder, Rain (earned wage access platform, rainapp.com)
research_notes: Check Hurun's $2B valuation: it may conflate with Rain (rain.xyz), a separate stablecoin-card company. No press email found on rainapp.com.

name: George Brooks
profile: Hurun lists him as a founder of Rain (valued $2B). Rain's own press materials name Alex Bradford as CEO and founder and do not mention George Brooks; I could not confirm his role.
current_role: Not verified; listed by Hurun as a Rain founder
research_notes: Verify which 'Rain' Hurun means (EWA company rainapp.com vs stablecoin-card Rain) and his role before outreach.

name: Isaiah Taylor
profile: Isaiah Taylor, 27, dropped out of high school at 16, ran an auto-repair shop in northern Idaho and a software company, then founded Valar Atomics in 2023 to build small, passively safe nuclear reactors on a factory line. Valar raised a $130M Series A in late 2025 and is bringing its first reactor online at a site in Orangeville, Emery County, Utah.
interesting_fact: His great-grandfather, Ward Schaap, was a Manhattan Project nuclear physicist at Oak Ridge, Tennessee; Taylor's grandmother was born in the Army field hospital there.
deep_cut_fact: He learned to code at about age 10 after a software engineer at his church introduced him to a kids' programming language; by 16 he had decided to start Valar, but chose to build other companies first to gain experience. In Feb 2026 Valar's 5 MW reactor was airlifted to Utah aboard three Air Force cargo planes.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Valar Atomics (El Segundo, CA; small modular / micro nuclear reactors)
public_contact: press_email: press@valaratomics.com | office_email: info@valaratomics.com | x: https://x.com/isaiah_p_taylor | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/isaiahptaylor | official_website: https://www.valaratomics.com
research_notes: Very media-accessible (TBPN, Limitless and other podcasts; active on X). Note that some outlets wrongly call Ward Schaap his grandfather - he is his great-grandfather. Some critical press exists about the company's investors; avoid. Good fit for energy/data-center podcast.

name: Bar Winkler
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Wonderful in early 2025 with CTO Roey Lalazar to build AI agents for enterprise customer service, especially in non-English markets. Previously founded procurement startup Approve.com (sold to Tipalti, 2021). Wonderful raised $150M at a $2B valuation (2026 Series B) and then $550M at ~$5B (Sept 2026).
interesting_fact: Wonderful went from founding in early 2025 to a ~$5B valuation in under two years and ~650 employees across 35+ markets, deploying local teams alongside its AI agents.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Approve.com, Winkler was an early employee at ironSource, the Israeli app-monetization company that later went public at an ~$11B valuation.
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Wonderful (enterprise AI agent platform)
research_notes: Hurun lists the industry as Agriculture, but this is Wonderful the Israeli AI company (wonderful.ai), not The Wonderful Company. Valuation is now ~$5B, not $2B. No personal press email found; use company channels.

name: Roey Lalazar
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded Wonderful in early 2025 with CEO Bar Winkler. Wonderful builds AI agents and an 'AI operating system' for enterprise customer service and back-office workflows, focusing on non-English markets. It raised $150M at a $2B valuation (Series B, 2026), then $550M at ~$5B in September 2026, and has ~650 staff.
interesting_fact: Wonderful planned to grow from 350 to ~900 employees in a single year to serve enterprises in 30+ countries across Europe, the Middle East, APAC and Latin America, pairing its AI agents with local deployment teams.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wonderful, Lalazar founded Kaps, an AI-based localization platform. That language work foreshadows Wonderful's focus on non-English-speaking markets.
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Wonderful (enterprise AI agent platform)
research_notes: Low personal media profile; CEO Bar Winkler does most of the press. Hurun's $2B valuation is outdated (now ~$5B). Some outlets misspell his name as 'Lalzar'/'Royel'.

name: Michael Grinich
profile: Software founder who previously co-founded email-API company Nylas, then launched WorkOS in March 2020 to give developers plug-in enterprise features (SSO, SCIM directory sync, audit logs, permissions). In March 2026 WorkOS raised a $100M Series C at a $2B valuation led by Meritech and Sapphire. Customers include OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Cursor and Perplexity, and it is pushing into auth for AI agents.
interesting_fact: WorkOS sells 'enterprise readiness' to AI labs: OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Cursor, Perplexity and Replit all use it. Grinich argues that as software becomes autonomous, 'trust becomes the constraint.'
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 WorkOS bought Modulz, maker of the popular open-source Radix UI framework. Angels in that $80M Series B included Hollywood super-agent Michael Ovitz, Guillermo Rauch and Jack Altman.
current_role: Founder & CEO, WorkOS (San Francisco)
public_contact: x: https://x.com/grinich | office_email: hello@workos.com (company) | podcast: Crossing the Enterprise Chasm (WorkOS podcast featuring Grinich): https://workos.com/podcast | official_website: https://workos.com
research_notes: Very reachable founder: active on X (@grinich, ~15.7K followers, and grinich.com redirects there) and runs a B2B podcast, so it is a natural fit for a podcast invite. The Nylas background is from general knowledge; no fetched source was re-checked because web-search quota ran out.

name: Jonathan Hurst
profile: Carnegie Mellon-trained roboticist (BS, MS, PhD) who joined Oregon State in 2008 and ran its Dynamic Robotics Lab. In 2015 he co-founded Agility Robotics with Damion Shelton and Mikhail Jones to commercialise his legged-locomotion research; its humanoid Digit targets logistics/warehouses. Agility has raised 640M+ USD and is valued around 2.5B USD; renamed Agility in March 2026.
interesting_fact: Agility's robots descend from his lab's spring-mass biped ATRIAS (modelled on how a pogo stick works) and the ostrich-like Cassie, unveiled in 2017 and sold to university research groups, before the humanoid Digit.
deep_cut_fact: He was Oregon State University's first robotics professor (2008); the legged-locomotion program he built grew into an OSU robotics MS/PhD program, which he says was only the third such program in the US.
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Robot Officer, Agility (formerly Agility Robotics); Professor of Robotics, Oregon State University
public_contact: press_email: media@agilityrobotics.com | contact_form: https://agilityrobotics.com/press | official_website: https://mime.oregonstate.edu/people/hurst
research_notes: Frequent conference speaker (RoboBusiness, AI Infra Summit, CMU Yata lecture) and podcast guest - receptive to media. Press contact Tim Smith (Element PR) via media@ address. Title variously listed as CTO in older sources; current is Chief Robot Officer.

name: Damion Shelton
profile: Carnegie Mellon robotics PhD who co-founded Agility Robotics in 2015 as a spinout of Jonathan Hurst's OSU legged-locomotion lab and served as CEO until 2024 (Peggy Johnson succeeded him; he then served as president). He now chairs Agility's board and runs CMU's Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship, mentoring founders.
interesting_fact: His founder advice: 'build something that's useful to someone rapidly, as opposed to having it be an indefinite science project' - the approach he used to take Agility from research robots to warehouse humanoids.
deep_cut_fact: Before Agility he co-founded threeRivers 3D, where as CTO he designed a low-cost, high-volume laser scanner for novice users in healthcare; he describes himself as a 'jack-of-all-trades roboticist' who left academia to build products.
current_role: Co-Founder & Chairman of the Board, Agility (Agility Robotics); AVP & Executive Director, Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship, Carnegie Mellon University
research_notes: Now based at CMU (Pittsburgh); CMU Swartz Center may be a better route than Agility. Has written for TechCrunch (author page exists) and spoken at TC Disrupt. Exact end dates of CEO/president roles vary across sources.

name: Mikhail Jones
profile: One of three co-founders of Agility Robotics (2015, with Jonathan Hurst and Damion Shelton), spun out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Lab where he had been a research engineer. Agility builds the Cassie biped and the Digit humanoid for logistics and manufacturing and is valued around 2.5B USD.
interesting_fact: Agility grew out of OSU research on spring-mass bipedal walking (ATRIAS), leading to the ostrich-like Cassie in 2017 and the humanoid Digit.
current_role: Co-Founder, Agility (Agility Robotics); last listed as VP of Software (unverified profile)
research_notes: Very low public profile; not listed on Agility's current leadership page, so his current role is unclear (theorg.com, unverified, lists VP of Software and prior OSU Faculty Research Assistant). Best route is via Agility press or co-founders. Research cut short by web-search quota.

name: Boris Sofman
profile: Carnegie Mellon robotics PhD who co-founded consumer-robotics company Anki (Anki Drive, Cozmo) in 2010, then spent ~5 years at Waymo leading its autonomous trucking program. In 2024 he co-founded Bedrock Robotics, which retrofits excavators with sensors and ML to run autonomously; it raised a 600M USD Series C in Oct 2026 at a 4.1B USD valuation.
interesting_fact: Data centers are a priority market for Bedrock: Sofman cites roughly 170B USD/yr of US data-center construction, much of it on remote, off-grid sites that need massive earthworks - Inc. framed it as 'The AI boom has a dirt problem'.
deep_cut_fact: His 2010 CMU PhD thesis, 'Online Learning Techniques for Improving Robot Navigation in Unfamiliar Domains' (advisors Drew Bagnell and Tony Stentz), taught off-road robots to predict terrain traversal costs from overhead imagery - a direct ancestor of today's autonomous dirt-moving.
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Bedrock Robotics (San Francisco)
research_notes: Very media-friendly (MCJ/Inevitable, Automate podcast ep. 66 Nov 2026). Strong data-center/energy angle. Quote: 'If you're too soon, there's no prize for being there 10 years early.' Avoid dwelling on Anki's 2019 shutdown.

name: Kevin Peterson
profile: Robotics engineer who co-founded sidewalk-delivery-robot company Marble (acquired by Caterpillar in 2020), then led perception for Waymo's autonomous trucking division. In 2024 he co-founded Bedrock Robotics with Boris Sofman and others; as CTO he leads its autonomous excavator system, now valued at 4.1B USD after a 600M USD Series C (Oct 2026).
interesting_fact: In July 2026 a Bedrock-equipped Caterpillar 352 excavator dug to grade and loaded a dump truck for hours with no one in the cab and no remote intervention; by Aug 2026 driverless excavators were working on three commercial sites in Texas and Nevada.
deep_cut_fact: His earlier startup Marble was acquired by Caterpillar in 2020 - and Bedrock's autonomy kit now runs on Caterpillar excavators such as the Cat 352.
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, Bedrock Robotics (San Francisco)
research_notes: Lower profile than CEO Sofman; route via Bedrock press. A Kevin Peterson completed a CMU Robotics MS (2009, advisor Red Whittaker) but it is unconfirmed this is the same person. Data-center construction is a Bedrock target market (e.g. Haydon partnership).

name: Ajay Gummalla
profile: Former Waymo engineering leader who co-founded Bedrock Robotics in 2024 with Boris Sofman, Kevin Peterson and Tom Eliaz. Bedrock retrofits excavators and other heavy construction equipment with autonomy kits; it emerged from stealth in July 2025 with ~$80M and has since raised large later rounds (Hurun: $2B+ valuation).
interesting_fact: Bedrock emerged from stealth in July 2025 with about $80M in seed and Series A funding to automate construction equipment, founded by a group of ex-Waymo self-driving engineers.
current_role: Co-founder & VP of Engineering, Bedrock Robotics (San Francisco)
public_contact: press_email: press@bedrockrobotics.com | official_website: https://bedrockrobotics.com | x: https://x.com/bedrockrobotics (company)
research_notes: Low public profile; no personal socials found. Patent databases list a prolific RF/antenna inventor of the same name (Rayspan, Broadcom, Google patents) - likely him but not confirmed, so not used as deep-cut. Best route: Bedrock press email.

name: Tom Eliaz
profile: Software engineering leader who co-founded Bedrock Robotics (autonomy retrofits for excavators and heavy construction equipment) in 2024 with ex-Waymo leaders Boris Sofman, Kevin Peterson and Ajay Gummalla. Previously spent ~5 years at Segment/Twilio, rising to VP of Engineering (Twilio Engage, high-scale computation and AI efforts). Penn computer science graduate.
interesting_fact: Unlike his ex-Waymo co-founders, Eliaz came from data infrastructure rather than self-driving: he was VP of Engineering at Twilio, leading multiple products plus high-scale computation and AI efforts.
deep_cut_fact: Before Segment he was an early employee at Anki, the AI robot-toy startup, where he led cloud platforms - and earlier founded a healthcare technology company focused on improving care for patients with chronic conditions.
current_role: Co-founder & VP of Engineering, Bedrock Robotics
research_notes: Speaks at engineering-leadership events (ELC San Francisco) - an engineering-culture angle may resonate. Location reported as NY or SF depending on source.

name: M.N. Srinivasu
profile: Indian payments pioneer who co-founded BillDesk in 2000 with fellow Arthur Andersen consultants Ajay Kaushal and Karthik Ganapathy. A commerce graduate and IIM Ahmedabad MBA, he spent nearly a decade at ITC before consulting. BillDesk grew into one of India's largest online payment gateways (FY21 revenue ~Rs 2,124 crore); a planned $4.7B sale to PayU was called off in 2022.
interesting_fact: BillDesk started as 'one convenient bill payments aggregation platform', deliberately avoiding competing with banks (its customers) in trading or lending.
deep_cut_fact: The founders spent four years persuading state telecom BSNL to sign on as a biller, finally landing it in early 2006 - a breakthrough account. Srinivasu: 'The DNA of the company is such that we've never had to play up what we do.'
current_role: Co-founder & Director, BillDesk (IndiaIdeas.com Ltd), Mumbai
research_notes: Very low-profile founders; BillDesk rarely does press ('never had to play up what we do'). No press email published on the BillDesk site (only support/sales addresses). Current exact title not confirmed (search budget exhausted).

name: Arjun Prakash
profile: Cornell-trained engineer who spent about eight years at Palantir, where he helped build the commercial business, expand it into Europe and create the Foundry platform. In 2022 he co-founded Distyl AI with fellow Palantir alum Derek Ho to build AI systems inside large enterprises' core workflows. Distyl raised a $175M Series B at a $1.8B valuation in Sept 2025, led by Khosla and Lightspeed.
interesting_fact: Distyl's pitch is to make companies 'AI-native' by embedding forward-deployed teams with customers, a Palantir-style model. At its 2023 seed, Prakash said the biggest LLM value was in information retrieval, not generative apps: cutting a call-center agent's hold time from ten minutes to two seconds.
deep_cut_fact: Before Palantir he held research and leadership roles at Siemens Research, BlackRock and Snorkel AI. His degree is in Electrical & Computer Engineering from Cornell.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Distyl AI
public_contact: press_email: media@distyl.ai | office_email: inquire@distyl.ai | x: https://x.com/distylai
research_notes: inquire@distyl.ai is Distyl's general business-inquiry address (company, not personal). media@distyl.ai is the company's published press address. Prakash is an author on World Economic Forum stories. The company says it is working on its New York expansion (2026).

name: Derek Ho
profile: Former Palantir colleague of CEO Arjun Prakash, with whom he co-founded Distyl AI in 2022 to embed LLM systems into Fortune 500 workflows (an OpenAI services partner). Distyl raised a $7M seed (Coatue, Dell Technologies Capital), then a $175M Series B at a $1.8B valuation in Sept 2025 led by Khosla and Lightspeed. Crunchbase lists a UPenn education and an earlier VP role at Mendel.ai.
interesting_fact: Distyl is often described as a 'Palantir for generative AI': it sends forward-deployed engineering teams into large enterprises, and reached a $1.8B valuation within about three years of founding.
deep_cut_fact: In an April 2023 seed-round interview he said GPT-3.5's two new capabilities, question answering and information retrieval, were the trigger: enterprises were 'less interested in the generative aspect' than in getting information to make decisions, and 'Arjun and I realized that this was the enterprise moment for AI.'
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Distyl AI (New York / San Francisco)
public_contact: press_email: media@distyl.ai | office_email: inquire@distyl.ai | official_website: https://www.distyl.ai
research_notes: Low public profile; CEO Arjun Prakash is the usual spokesperson. inquire@distyl.ai is a general company inbox (not personal). Hurun's $2B figure vs. reported $1.8B Series B valuation.

name: Sam Perkins
profile: Princeton alum who co-founded Nourish with childhood friend Aidan Dewar (CEO) and Stephanie Liu (CTO). Nourish connects patients with registered dietitians via insurance-covered telehealth; 94% of patients pay $0 out of pocket, it has 10,000+ dietitians in all 50 states, and it reached a ~$2B valuation after large 2025-26 rounds ($70M Series B, $100M raise).
interesting_fact: Nourish says 500k+ people have been helped by its dietitians, and it is backed by founders of Headway, Spring Health, Oscar, Notion and Flatiron among others.
deep_cut_fact: Nourish is a friendship company: Perkins and CEO Aidan Dewar are childhood friends, and CTO Stephanie Liu became close friends with Perkins at Princeton before the three co-founded it.
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Nourish (telehealth nutrition / registered dietitians)
research_notes: Nourish's public face is CEO Aidan Dewar (Forbes 30 Under 30; Wharton Pulse podcast). TechCrunch notes the founders' personal motivations - avoid health specifics in outreach. No press email published on site (only support@).

name: Stephanie Liu
profile: Stephanie Liu co-founded Nourish in 2021 with Aidan Dewar and Sam Perkins and leads its technology as CTO. Nourish connects patients with registered dietitians covered by insurance; it raised a $70M Series B (2025, reported >$1B valuation) and a $100M Series C led by Menlo Ventures in May 2026 at a reported $1.75B valuation.
interesting_fact: Nourish was reported to be profitable at the time of its 2025 Series B, a rarity for a fast-growing digital-health startup; the 2026 Series C brought total funding to about $215M.
deep_cut_fact: Liu met co-founder Sam Perkins while they were both studying at Princeton; Perkins then brought her together with his childhood friend Aidan Dewar to start Nourish.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Nourish (virtual dietitian / nutrition-care platform, New York)
public_contact: press_email: britta.franson@usenourish.com | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/nourish/ | official_website: https://www.usenourish.com
research_notes: Low public profile; few interviews. Press contact (Britta Franson, PR for Nourish) appears on Business Wire releases 2024 and Feb 2026 (could not load the page directly; confirmed via search snippets). Company LinkedIn/site are company-level, not personal.

name: Aidan Dewar
profile: Aidan Dewar co-founded Nourish in 2021 with childhood friend Sam Perkins and Stephanie Liu, and runs it as CEO. Nourish matches patients with insurance-covered registered dietitians via telehealth; it raised a $70M Series B led by J.P. Morgan Growth Equity in 2025 (reported >$1B valuation) and a $100M Series C led by Menlo Ventures in May 2026 at a reported $1.75B valuation.
interesting_fact: Nourish was reported to be profitable at the time of its 2025 Series B, unusual for a fast-growing digital-health startup; its 2026 Series C was framed around supporting patients on GLP-1 treatments.
deep_cut_fact: Dewar and his co-founder Sam Perkins are childhood friends; the third co-founder, CTO Stephanie Liu, was Perkins' friend from Princeton.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nourish (virtual dietitian / nutrition-care platform, New York)
public_contact: press_email: britta.franson@usenourish.com | official_website: https://www.usenourish.com | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/company/nourish/
research_notes: Founder story is personal (he has spoken about his own chronic condition motivating Nourish) - let him raise it. Unverified aggregator claims: Harvard economics (2018), prior consulting, co-founded 'Feed The Frontlines SF' - not confirmed. Has appeared on podcasts (e.g. PodRocket episode on going $0 to $1B).

name: Christian Cantrell
profile: Christian Cantrell spent 17 years at Adobe (2005-2022), ending as Director of Experience Development and head of Adobe Design Prototyping, then was VP of Product at Stability AI (2022-23), launching DreamStudio 1.0 and the Stability API. In March 2023 he founded Reve AI, maker of the Reve image-generation model, where he runs product, design and marketing. He is also a published novelist.
interesting_fact: He is a thriller/sci-fi novelist: his novel 'Scorpion' (Random House) began as the short story 'The Epoch Index', optioned by FOX, and he has a series ('Brainbox') developed at Hulu; Publishers Weekly and Kirkus both gave Scorpion starred reviews.
deep_cut_fact: At Macromedia (2002-05) he built and maintained Macromedia's first blog and RSS aggregation platforms; he started his career as a Java developer at Amazing Media, holds a Creative Writing and Literature degree from George Mason, and was named an Adobe Distinguished Inventor in 2022 (22 patents).
current_role: Founder and Chief Product (and 'Prompt') Officer, Reve AI (foundation-model and creative-tooling startup, Palo Alto)
public_contact: personal_email: christian.cantrell@gmail.com | official_website: https://christiancantrell.com | x: https://x.com/cantrell | linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/christiancantrell | official_website: https://cantrell.medium.com (Medium)
research_notes: His site invites email ('Feel free to email me') but shows the address scrambled behind a decode slider (simple letter-shift of 'inxoyzogt.igtzxkrr@msgor.ius'); the decoded address above is what the slider reveals. Ideal podcast guest: technology + storytelling. Reve co-founders: Michael Gharbi, Taesung Park.

name: Michaël Gharbi
profile: French computer-vision and graphics researcher (Ecole Polytechnique; PhD at MIT CSAIL under Fredo Durand) who was a Research Scientist at Adobe Research before co-founding image-generation startup Reve with Christian Cantrell, Taesung Park, Jon Watte and Mike Speiser, serving as Founder and Chief Scientist. His own site now lists him as a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI.
interesting_fact: He co-authored 'Deep Bilateral Learning for Real-Time Image Enhancement' (SIGGRAPH 2017, with Google researchers) and the one-step diffusion 'Distribution Matching Distillation' papers (CVPR 2024 / NeurIPS 2024); a 2025 SIGGRAPH Asia paper he co-wrote won Best Paper.
deep_cut_fact: Outside graphics, he co-authored a 2018 Science Advances paper applying a convolutional neural network to earthquake detection and location (with Thibaut Perol and Marine Denolle), and contributed to the learned autoscheduler for the Halide image-processing language.
current_role: Member of Technical Staff, OpenAI (previously co-founder and Chief Scientist, Reve)
research_notes: Now at OpenAI per his personal site (date of move not stated) - his Reve stake/'founder' status may be outdated. Pure researcher, low media profile. His site lists a phone number - deliberately not recorded. Site notes the economist Sarah Gharbi is a different person.

name: Taesung Park
profile: Taesung Park is a generative-imaging researcher (Stanford BS Math / MS CS; UC Berkeley PhD under Alexei Efros) who was a Research Scientist at Adobe Research, where he built the upscaling pipeline for Adobe Firefly, before co-founding Reve with Christian Cantrell and Michael Gharbi. Reve develops its own image models and editing tools.
interesting_fact: He is a co-author of landmark image-synthesis work including CycleGAN/pix2pix code and GauGAN (SPADE), the sketch-to-photo tool named one of Popular Science's 100 Greatest Innovations of 2019.
deep_cut_fact: GauGAN grew out of his summer 2018 NVIDIA internship with Ming-Yu Liu; his PhD was funded by a Samsung Scholarship and he received an Adobe Research Fellowship in 2020. His Swapping Autoencoder research became Photoshop's Landscape Mixer.
current_role: Co-founder, Reve (AI image-generation startup, Palo Alto)
research_notes: Researcher-founder with low media profile; his personal site publishes the email above. Fellow Reve co-founder Michael Gharbi's site says Gharbi has since moved to OpenAI - check Reve's current status before outreach.

name: Jon Watte
profile: Veteran systems/graphics engineer and one of five co-founders of Reve, the Palo Alto AI image company behind Reve Image (with Christian Cantrell, Michael Gharbi, Taesung Park and Mike Speiser). Earlier he ran Be Inc.'s media group, built avatar/networking tech at There.com, was CTO of Forterra Systems, worked on IMVU and Roblox engineering, and co-founded Observe Inc.
interesting_fact: Reve relaunched in Sept 2025 with a code-like 'layout representation' that breaks images into editable components; Reve 2.0 later ranked near the top of the Arena text-to-image leaderboard (June 2026).
deep_cut_fact: At Be Inc. he took over the media group, working on the low-latency, multiprocessing foundations of BeOS; after Be was sold to Palm he helped build avatar, networking and simulation tech for the virtual world There.com, then became CTO of Forterra Systems.
current_role: Co-founder, Reve (Reve AI, Inc., Palo Alto AI image-generation startup)
research_notes: Hurun lists him under 'Telecommunications' but he is the Reve (AI image) co-founder. Low public profile; no personal accounts verified. Only published Reve email is support@reve.com (customer support, not press). One unverified report mentioned Reve sunsetting; June 2026 coverage shows it active - check current status.

name: Bob Badal
profile: Healthcare executive who co-founded Strive Health (Denver value-based kidney-care provider, valued ~$2B) in 2018. Before that he spent 12+ years at DaVita running health-plan and provider network contracting and strategy (a $2.5B+ revenue portfolio) and served as President of DaVita Kidney Care's Latin America operations. Now also an a16z Bio + Health advisory partner and board member at several health companies.
interesting_fact: At DaVita he was President of Latin America Operations for DaVita Kidney Care, after a decade-plus in health-plan network development and hospital administration.
deep_cut_fact: Studied economics and law at Trinity University in San Antonio before his USC Marshall MBA; in 2017, a year before Strive, he co-founded WaveHealth, an electronic patient-reported-outcomes (ePRO) company.

name: Bernt Øivind Børnich

name: Xavier Orr

current_role: Founder, Anitron (humanoid robot AI); board director & advisor, Advanced Navigation
research_notes: Stepped back from Advanced Navigation for a family matter (do not raise). Anitron (pre-seeded 1M USD by Orr; Unitree G1-based beta trials, shirt-folding demo) is the most current topic. No Anitron contact found.

name: Chris Shaw
profile: UWA electrical-engineering graduate who co-founded Advanced Navigation with Xavier Orr in 2012, building the hardware for its AI-based inertial navigation systems. The ~1B USD-valued firm supplies navigation for drones, ships, defence vehicles, satellites and a NASA CLPS lunar lander, with customers in 70+ countries. He became sole CEO after Orr stepped back in 2024.

current_role: CEO & Co-Founder, Advanced Navigation (Sydney)

name: Cristian Zamfir

name: George Candea

He served as Cyberhaven's CEO and later Chief Scientist and now focuses on his EPFL lab.

name: Radu Banabic
profile: Romanian computer scientist (BSc Technical University of Cluj-Napoca; EPFL PhD 2015 under George Candea) who co-founded data-security company Cyberhaven in 2016 with Candea and fellow lab members. Cyberhaven, now led by CEO Howard Ting, sells data-lineage-based data loss prevention and was valued at $1B+.
interesting_fact: His EPFL PhD thesis, 'Techniques for Identifying Elusive Corner-Case Bugs in Systems Software', included Achilles, a tool that hunts for 'Trojan messages' in distributed systems.
deep_cut_fact: As an undergraduate research assistant in Cluj he built a model for detecting automobile window pillars in live images for a project with Volkswagen AG, and graduated with a 9.92/10 GPA; he also interned at IBM Research Zurich (2012) on a distributed storage algorithm.
current_role: Co-founder & VP of Engineering, Cyberhaven (per EPFL DSLAB alumni listing)
research_notes: Very low public profile engineer. Current title from EPFL lab alumni page; not confirmed on Cyberhaven's site. Old EPFL email on his CV is likely inactive — not listed.

name: Vitaly Chipounov
profile: Computer scientist (EPFL PhD 2014, George Candea's lab) and the lead author of S2E, the open-source selective-symbolic-execution platform. He co-founded data-security company Cyberhaven in 2016 with Candea and fellow lab members and serves as its Chief Architect; Cyberhaven sells data-lineage-based data loss prevention and is valued at $1B+.
interesting_fact: His PhD thesis 'S2E: A Platform for In-Vivo Multi-Path Analysis of Software Systems' produced a tool security researchers have used to find Windows, Linux and Android kernel CVEs.
deep_cut_fact: Cyberhaven built the 'Galactica' system on S2E for the DARPA Cyber Grand Challenge finals (CodeJitsu team, with UC Berkeley and Syracuse); S2E drew 'first blood' by exploiting 7 binaries before anyone else and launched 392 successful attacks — about twice as many as Mayhem.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Architect, Cyberhaven (per EPFL DSLAB alumni listing)
public_contact: press_email: press@cyberhaven.com | official_website: http://s2e.systems/ (S2E project site, his PhD work)
research_notes: Deeply technical; S2E/Cyber Grand Challenge are the best conversation hooks. Title from https://dslab.epfl.ch/people.

name: Volodymyr Kuznetsov
profile: Security researcher (EPFL PhD 2016 under George Candea; previously a researcher at UC Berkeley) who co-founded data-security company Cyberhaven in 2016 and was its first CEO, moving to CTO when Howard Ting became CEO in 2021. Cyberhaven sells data-lineage-based data loss prevention and is valued at $1B+.
